cita: Guan et al. (2026). A Dual-Helix Governance Approach Towards Reliable Agentic AI for WebGIS Development.
problema: Agentic WebGIS development suffers five compounding LLM limitations -- long-context degradation, cross-session forgetting, output stochasticity, instruction-following failures, and fine-tuning's adaptation rigidity -- because current governance (prompting, RAG, fine-tuning) is purely informational/advisory, not structurally enforced.
mecanismo: A dual-helix of Knowledge Externalization (a persistent, version-controlled knowledge graph of typed JSON nodes -- Category/Concept/Document -- each linking to a Markdown file) and Behavioral Enforcement (executable, prioritized protocol nodes an agent must validate against before executing a skill) intersect in a Skills track; role separation (meta-level Agent Builder vs task-level Domain Expert) prevents context contamination, and a 5-step self-learning cycle (discover-structure-link-validate-persist) writes new discoveries back into the graph as auditable nodes.
evaluacion: Two case studies: (1) a real WebGIS refactor (FutureShorelines) measured via SLOC/cyclomatic-complexity/maintainability-index/JSHint-warnings before vs after governance-guided refactoring, plus KG substrate growth tracking; (2) a controlled 3-condition (unguided/static-prompt/dual-helix) 5-trial COVID-19 cartography experiment scored on 6 dimensions (E1-E6, deterministic checks + gpt-5.2 LLM-as-judge), comparing mean and standard deviation via Welch's t-test and Cohen's d.
numeros_clave: -51% cyclomatic complexity, -49% logical SLOC, +7pt maintainability index, -98% JSHint warnings (Table 3, FutureShorelines refactor); dual-helix condition sigma=0.36 vs static-prompt baseline sigma=0.79 (variance more than halved, Sec.5); rule-compliance dimension E5 mean 1.66 vs 1.30 baseline (+27.7%); Welch t(5.18)=1.60 p=0.169, Cohen's d=0.46; KG substrate grew up to 433% (Table 4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The KG node taxonomy (Category/Concept/Document, JSON + linked Markdown, version-controlled, Sec.3.2 Table 2) offers a concrete Tier-1 typed-narrative pattern MF could mirror for docs-as-truth.
The Domain Expert's mandatory 'plan-first' step with human approval gate before autonomous execution (Sec.3.3) is a concrete plan-state-as-memory pattern.
The 5-step self-learning cycle (discover-structure-link-validate-persist, Sec.3.4, Fig.4) is an explicit discretionary write trigger fired on discovery, not a blind append.
KG substrate growth (Table 4, up to 433% node growth) demonstrates promotion of transient discoveries (e.g. vector-tile fallback logic) into durable graph nodes, matching MF's consolidation need.

notes: Sec.4.4 Table 3 (FutureShorelines refactor code-quality metrics) and Sec.5 Fig.8 + rule-compliance table (variance reduction / E5 results) anchor the numbers above.

cita: Xu et al. (2025). Everything is Context: Agentic File System Abstraction for Context Engineering.
problema: Agentic GenAI context management (memory, tools, external knowledge, human input) via prompt engineering/RAG/tool integration remains fragmented and ad hoc, producing transient, opaque, unverifiable context artefacts that cause context rot and knowledge drift.
mecanismo: A Unix-'everything is a file' abstraction mounts heterogeneous context sources (KGs, memory stores, human notes, MCP tools) into one governed namespace with uniform metadata/access-control; a Persistent Context Repository layers History (immutable append-only log), Memory (indexed/structured views -- episodic, fact, experiential, procedural, user -- built by summarisation/embedding/clustering), and Scratchpad (ephemeral per-task workspace, later pruned or promoted into Memory/History); a Context Engineering Pipeline (Constructor/Updater/Evaluator) then selects, compresses, and incrementally streams this repository into the bounded token window, logging every transition for traceability.
evaluacion: Systems paper with no quantitative benchmark: validated through architectural description plus two exemplars implemented in the open-source AIGNE framework -- a memory-enabled conversational agent (afs_list/afs_read tool calls building a context manifest) and an MCP-mounted GitHub assistant demonstrating any MCP server can be exposed as a file-system module.
numeros_clave: NINGUNO

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: History is explicitly the 'immutable source of truth' from which Memory (indexed/derived views) is built via summarisation/embedding -- the same truth-vs-derived split MF encodes as TIER-DOCS/TIER-INDICE (Sec.IV, Sec.IV-B).
Memory is described as 'structured and indexed views' over History, exposed per agent/session and rebuildable from the immutable log -- a derived-cache role matching MF's Tier-3 (Sec.IV-B).
Memory deduplication/consolidation strategies are named as a required mitigation for stateless-session memory growth and redundancy (Sec.V-A.2), a concrete consolidation trigger MF could adopt.
Every file-system transaction (agent or human) is logged with timestamp/origin/lineage for provenance and post-hoc audit (Sec.III.4), directly extending MF's provenance/staleness need.

notes: Sec.IV/Sec.IV-A-D (History/Memory/Scratchpad lifecycle, Table I taxonomy) and Sec.VI exemplars (memory agent, GitHub MCP) are the qualitative anchors; purely CUALITATIVA, no benchmark numbers reported.

cita: Vasilopoulos, A. (2026). Codified Context: Infrastructure for AI Agents in a Complex Codebase.
problema: Single-file agent manifests (.cursorrules/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) don't scale beyond modest codebases -- a 100,000-line system can't be described in one prompt -- so AI coding agents keep losing project conventions, coherence, and past mistakes across sessions in large, multi-agent codebases.
mecanismo: A three-tier codified-context infrastructure: Tier-1 hot-memory 'constitution' (~660-line Markdown, always loaded, encodes conventions + orchestration trigger tables routing tasks to agents); Tier-2 19 specialized domain-expert agent specs (~9,300 lines, embedding >50% project-specific domain knowledge, symptom-cause-fix tables) invoked per task via the trigger table; Tier-3 cold-memory knowledge base of 34 Markdown subsystem docs (~16,250 lines) retrieved on demand through an MCP keyword-search server (list_subsystems/find_relevant_context/suggest_agent); all three tiers overlap intentionally to counter 'brevity bias' collapse toward generic prompts.
evaluacion: Systems/experience-report paper: quantitative infrastructure-growth and interaction metrics mined from Git history and 1,457 JSONL conversation logs across 283 development sessions (no controlled ablation), complemented by four observational case studies (save-system coordination, UI-sync captured experience, drop-system gap detection, deterministic-RNG debugging) with no causal claims.
numeros_clave: NINGUNO

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The 3-tier hot/warm/cold memory (Tier1 always-loaded constitution, Tier2 specialist-agent docs, Tier3 34 on-demand Markdown specs, ~26,200 lines total, Table 3) is a measured instance of docs-as-typed-truth scaling beyond a single manifest -- strong external confirmation of MF's TIER-DOCS bet.
Each Tier-3 document is explicitly 'scoped to a single subsystem' (Sec.3.3) -- a single-source-per-fact seam discipline MF's COSTURAS anchor could adopt verbatim.

Agent Tier-2 specs are created reactively when 'a category of task repeatedly required re-explaining the same domain knowledge' (Sec.3.2 Emergence pattern) -- codifying recurring gotchas into a durable spec.
Retrieval usage is directly measured (1,478 MCP retrieval calls across 218 sessions, 194 agent conversations reading KB docs, Sec.4.4) rather than assumed, matching MF's measured-retrieval need.

notes: Sec.4.2-4.4 (Table 3 infra scale 24.2% knowledge/code ratio, 283 sessions, 2,801 human prompts, 1,197 agent invocations) and the 4 case studies (Sec.4.4.1-4.4.4) anchor the qualitative evidence; purely CUALITATIVA per extraction, no ablation numbers.

cita: Fan et al. (2026). Skill Drift Is Contract Violation: Proactive Maintenance for LLM Agent Skill Libraries.
problema: Reusable LLM agent skill documents silently decay as the external services/APIs/packages/configs they reference evolve, but existing monitors observe raw environmental values (URLs, version strings) rather than the operational role those values play in a skill, forcing a bad trade-off between false alarms and missed drift.
mecanismo: SkillGuard reframes skill drift as contract violation: a deterministic pass extracts candidate environment mentions (15 pattern families -- URLs, versions, imports, API paths, auth, Docker images, env vars...), then a semantic pass labels each as an executable contract record (type, role in {OPERATIONAL, INCIDENTAL}, value, evidence span); only OPERATIONAL contracts are matched against known/live drift events via a type-gated predicate, and a violated contract becomes a localized repair specification (failed assumption + evidence span + old/new value) fed back to the LLM for targeted, verifiable repair.
evaluacion: Evaluated on the released DriftBench (880 pairs: 174 controlled drifts, 107 real-world drifts from live registries/changelogs, 599 no-drift/hard-negative controls, 99.6% adjudicated validity + 20% human audit) across five backbone LLMs on known-drift precision/recall, a pre-registered 49-real-skill live-discovery study, and a repair-success comparison against no-localization/plain-drift-text/Self-refine/full-drift-spec baselines.
numeros_clave: Contract-free CI probes: 40% FPR; SkillGuard: 0% FPR over 599 no-drift/hard-negative cases (Wilson 95% CI [0,0.6]%), 100% precision / 76% recall (strongest backbone, Table 2); live pre-registered scan of 49 real skills: 86% conservative precision, 55% recall; repair success 10% -> 78% with contract localization (~10K tokens/skill vs ~18K for 3-round Self-refine).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: SkillGuard treats each skill doc's environment mentions as role-typed (OPERATIONAL vs INCIDENTAL) contract records rather than plain text -- a typed-narrative discipline MF's Tier-1 docs could adopt to flag load-bearing obligations vs incidental prose (Sec.4.1).

Directly measures doc staleness/drift as the central failure mode and shows contract-typed validation eliminates false alarms (0% FPR over 599 cases) while catching 76% of known drift -- confirms MF's staleness detection needs typed, role-aware checks over raw diffing (Table 2, Sec.5.1).

Proactive, precision-first drift detection (before execution failure) is a concrete discretionary write/update trigger MF's G-M1 could model -- detect violated contract, then localize and repair (Sec.4.3).

Contract-localized repair is cheaper: ~10K tokens/skill vs ~18K for 3-round Self-refine while matching its 78-80% one-round success (Sec.5.3) -- evidence that targeted/typed context beats brute-force iteration.

notes: Sec.5.1 Table 2 (known-drift precision/recall by backbone) + Sec.5.2 Fig.4 (49-skill live scan) + Sec.5.3 Fig.4B (repair success) are the numeric anchors.

cita: Pedada, S., Dhavala, A., & Patil, N. (2026). Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems.
problema: Agentic LLM systems that generate/edit artifacts through multi-turn tool use are stateless -- each session discards the domain constraints, data schemas, tool configs, and output-format preferences that made the prior session productive, forcing costly re-specification, while naively persisting entire conversation histories is token-inefficient and actively degrades output quality via irrelevant/stale context.
mecanismo: Shared selective persistent memory decomposes reusable session knowledge into four orthogonal, git-versioned categories per workspace -- task specifications (system-prompt rules), data schemas (precomputed statistical profiles instead of raw data), tool configurations, and output constraints (a runtime data-injection contract) -- while explicitly discarding reasoning traces, tool-invocation logs, and error-recovery paths; workspaces are shareable across users under role-based access control, and a zero-token data-refresh mechanism swaps compatible data into the artifact without any LLM re-invocation.
evaluacion: Four studies: a controlled 24-task ablation (no-memory vs full-history vs selective memory) across three enterprise use cases scored by two blinded raters (kappa=0.91) with Fisher's exact significance tests; a 4-public-dataset / 36-trial replication for generalizability; a token-efficiency comparison of raw/truncated/summary-driven data representation; and a 12-participant counterbalanced user study.
numeros_clave: Selective memory: 96% task completion vs 79% no-memory vs 71% full-history (Table 1, Fisher p=0.046/0.008); public-dataset replication: 100% completion at 0 LLM tokens on 12/12 zero-token-refresh trials (Table 2); summary-driven data representation cuts tokens 97x (enterprise) to 946x (public datasets) vs raw injection (Table 3); user study: 14x faster recurring generation (12s vs 165s).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Workspace memory is decomposed into four typed, git-versioned categories (task specs, schemas, tool configs, output constraints) rather than a single freeform doc -- a category-typed narrative pattern MF's Tier-1 could extend beyond one STATE.md (Sec.3.2-3.3, Eq.3).

Summary-driven schemas cut token cost 97-946x vs raw data injection and zero-token refresh needs 0 LLM tokens on 12/12 trials (Table 2/3) -- strong confirmation that MF's context-economy discipline (derived summaries over raw dumps) pays off.

Selective forgetting is an explicit, enumerated write-time decision (discard reasoning traces/tool logs/error-recovery paths, keep 4 stable categories, Sec.3.3) -- a concrete discretionary write/discard trigger MF's G-M1 anchor could formalize.

Measures that stale session traces actively bias ('trace anchoring') the agent toward wrong prior solution paths, degrading completion 8-25pp below no-memory (Table 1/2, Sec.6.2-6.3) -- direct evidence for MF's staleness/poisoning concern in FIDELIDAD.

notes: Sec.6.2 Table 1 (24-task enterprise ablation), Sec.6.3 Table 2 (public replication), Sec.6.4 Table 3/Fig.2 (token efficiency) anchor the numbers; Sec.7 explicitly frames full-history persistence as counterproductive, not merely unhelpful.

cita: Holt et al. (2023). L2MAC: Large Language Model Automatic Computer for Extensive Code Generation.
problema: LLMs are constrained by a fixed context window, so they cannot produce long, internally-consistent outputs (e.g. large codebases): existing memory-augmented approaches only read from memory (reducing updates to append-only concatenation) or use narrow domain-specific memories (dictionaries/databases) that don't generalize and can't recover from errors.
mecanismo: L2MAC is a stored-program-computer (von Neumann) framework: an LLM 'processor' executes one instruction at a time from an LLM-generated instruction registry I, while a Control Unit manages the processor's bounded context (P1: always includes the current unresolved instruction plus prior-execution summary, decluttering as the window fills), grants precise read/write/extend access to an external file-store memory (P2), and checks each output for syntactic validity and self-generated-unit-test pass/fail before accepting the write, triggering iterative corrective regeneration on failure (P3).
evaluacion: Benchmarked Code-L2MAC against AutoGPT, CodeT, Self-Refine, Reflexion and single-shot GPT-4 on three system-design codebase-generation tasks (Features%/# Errors/LOC/Tests-Passed averaged over 10 seeds with 95% CIs) plus the standard HumanEval benchmark, and ran targeted ablations isolating P1 (context retention), P2 (read/write precision) and P3 (error-correction) contributions.
numeros_clave: Code-L2MAC: 90.2% Pass@1 on HumanEval (state-of-the-art); Table 2 URL-shortener task Features% 91.6+-8.22 vs GPT4 53.6+-10.5 / CodeT 52.9+-6.74 / Self-Refine 47.9+-8.53 / Reflexion 38.8+-6.02 / AutoGPT 25.3+-19.6, with 0+-0 syntax errors vs baselines' >=0.05.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The file store is the persistent memory of record that every instruction-agent reads/writes precisely (P2) rather than an ephemeral conversation buffer -- a docs/files-as-truth substrate MF's Tier-1 already assumes (Sec.3, Fig.2).

The Control Unit maintains an explicit instruction registry I (the decomposed task plan) and tracks per-instruction completion state across the whole run -- literal plan-state-as-memory, confirming MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor (Sec.1, Fig.1).

P2 (precise read/write for the entire memory store) is directly measured via the Features%/error/LOC/tests-passed metrics (Table 2), showing task-oriented, checked retrieval outperforms read-only or full-context baselines -- a measured retrieval layer matching G-M2.

The Control Unit's P3 (checking generated output via syntax checkers + self-generated unit tests before accepting a memory write) is a concrete write-time fidelity gate MF could extend to docs/state writes (Sec.3, Sec.6.2 Fig.3b).

notes: Sec.6.1 Table 2 (Features%/Errors/LOC across 3 system-design tasks + HumanEval) and Sec.6.2 Fig.3 (P1/P2/P3 insight ablations) anchor the numbers; plan_estado=SI reflects the explicit instruction registry I as a persisted plan (Sec.3, Fig.1).

cita: Wang, Y., Yang, L., Chen, B., Zou, G., Xu, K., Tang, B., Xiong, F., Chen, S. y Li, Z. (2025). Text2Mem: A Unified Memory Operation Language for Memory Operating System.
problema: Existing LLM-agent memory frameworks (MemGPT, A-MEM, MemOS, mem0, Letta) expose only basic primitives (encode/retrieve/delete) with no formal, executable specification for higher-order controls (merge, promote/demote, split, lock, expire), leaving scope and lifecycle rules implicit and causing unpredictable, non-portable behavior across systems.
mecanismo: Text2Mem defines twelve mutually exclusive verbs across encode/storage/retrieval stages, each expressed as a typed JSON schema instance with a five-field backbone (stage/op/target/args/meta); a validator checks legality, a parser normalizes into typed operation objects, and adapters compile these into either a SQL-like reference backend or real memory-framework APIs (MemOS, mem0, Letta), unifying write/consolidate(merge)/forget(delete,expire)/update across representations.
evaluacion: Primarily a language/schema design paper: it does not run a live benchmark. It compares operation coverage against MemOS, mem0 and Letta qualitatively (Table I, native/partial/absent support matrix) and outlines 'Text2Mem Bench' as planned future work separating schema generation from backend execution, but reports no empirical results yet.
numeros_clave: Twelve verbs across 3 stages (1 encode, 9 storage, 2 retrieval), 5-field schema backbone, 3 frameworks compared in Table I support matrix (MemOS/mem0/Letta); no ablation/benchmark numbers reported (Text2Mem Bench is future work).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Text2Mem's typed 5-field schema (stage/op/target/args/meta, sec III-B) offers MF a formal vocabulary for narrative-memory operations that could type Tier-1 doc mutations beyond free prose.
The Update-verb example ('remember key points...becomes...dated action items') treats task/plan state as a memory object, but the paper never specializes a dedicated plan-state layer.
Merge/Split verbs (Table I) formalize consolidation-with-lineage as first-class operations that MF's promotion-of-gotchas mechanism could adopt directly.
Lock/Expire verbs attach audit trails and TTL/until governance (sec III-A.2.b), supporting MF's provenance/staleness concerns for Tier-1 docs.

notes: Table I (sec III-A.3) is the qualitative support matrix vs MemOS/mem0/Letta; Text2Mem Bench (empirical eval) is explicitly future work, not yet run.

cita: Deshpande et al. (2025). MEMTRACK: Evaluating Long-Term Memory and State Tracking in Multi-Platform Dynamic Agent Environments.
problema: Existing memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval) focus on single-thread conversational settings; there is no benchmark for long-term memory and state tracking in dynamic, multi-platform enterprise agent environments (Slack/Linear/Git) with noisy, conflicting, cross-referring information.
mecanismo: MEMTRACK is a benchmark harness, not a memory system: a dockerized environment with real Slack/Linear/Git servers injects a chronologically platform-interleaved event timeline; agents are queried with sequential (incl. follow-up) questions while memory tools (Mem0 vector store with ChromaDB, Zep knowledge-graph) or no memory are attached, and Correctness (LLM-judge), Efficiency (tool-call count), and Redundancy (subsumed tool calls) are measured.
evaluacion: GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro agents tested with NoMem/Mem0/Zep across 47 curated multi-platform instances (mean 39.9 events, mean 4.01K event tokens), results averaged across 5 runs, Correctness scored via an LLM-judge (GPT-4o).
numeros_clave: Table 3: GPT-5+NoMem Correctness=0.601 vs GPT-5+Mem0=0.610 vs GPT-5+Zep=0.601 -- memory components give NO significant lift; best model (GPT-5) only ~60% Correctness; Gemini-2.5-Pro ~0.14-0.144 (about 4x worse than GPT-5); Redundancy ~20.6-24.0%; Table 1: 47 instances, mean 39.9 events/instance, mean 4.01K event tokens, mean timeline span 878h.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table 3 shows Mem0/Zep retrieval adds NO significant Correctness gain over NoMem (GPT-5: 0.601->0.610->0.601), a measured case where a vector/graph retrieval layer does not help -- cautions that MF's ADR-019 bet on measured retrieval only pays off with the right design, not any store.

The benchmark treats the Git/codebase as one of three memory-relevant platforms (sec 3) alongside Slack/Linear, evidencing that versioned code/docs are a first-class memory source, though MEMTRACK does not itself propose a docs-as-truth tier.

Sec 2 flags that forgetting/retention policy 'is understudied' (citing Shan et al.) and MEMTRACK's conflict-resolution questions test whether agents notice contradictory info (sec 3), but the benchmark itself does not measure negative-knowledge/re-derivation strategies.

Efficiency/Redundancy metrics (sec 4.2) explicitly penalize excess/duplicate tool calls (TC_min=10, ~20% redundancy measured, Table 3), confirming MF's context-economy concern that unmeasured retrieval wastes tokens.

notes: Table 3 (sec 5) has the Correctness/Efficiency/Redundancy numbers; Table 1 has dataset stats; the forgetting-understudied claim is sec 2 citing [41].

cita: Modi et al. (2025). Debugmate: an AI agent for efficient on-call debugging in complex production systems.
problema: On-call software engineers debugging complex, distributed production systems face heavy cognitive load navigating vast codebases plus org-specific context that LLMs are not pretrained on; prior debugging agents (SWE-Agent) or context-selection tools don't integrate internal docs/codebase/incident history with external knowledge.
mecanismo: DebugMate combines RAG (LangChain RetrievalQA plus OpenAI embeddings, query expansion, cross-encoder reranking) over internal docs/knowledge-base, a Neo4j dependency graph over microservices, Git-change ranking (an 'election' over batches of 20 changes), and Tree-of-Thought branching (a parent agent spawns child agents per code module, DFS ordered by confidence) atop ReAct, plus short/long-term memory that stores code dependencies and class hierarchies as intermediate steps fed back into the LLM.
evaluacion: Evaluated on (1) DebugBench logical-error benchmark vs GPT-4-0613, (2) Observe.AI's historical P0/P1 reliability incidents (longest 10% resolution time), and (3) 16 real-world bugs from 5 Java open-source repos (Elasticsearch, Kestra, Dubbo, OpenSearch, Jenkins); ablations remove stack trace, KB/DP search, or replace Tree-of-Thought with Chain-of-Thought.
numeros_clave: 82% DebugBench vs GPT-4-0613's 75%; 83% ObserveAI vs 58%; 71.4% open-source vs 42.8% (Table 2); +20% accuracy vs baseline per abstract; ToT-to-CoT ablation drops Err.Fixed from 83.33% to 50.00% and avg reviewed function calls from 6 to 3.4 (Table 1); 14/16 root causes found, correct/partial fixes in 11 of those, on 5 real OSS repos (sec 4.1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: DebugMate's KB/DP-Search ablation (Table 1) shows removing internal docs/KB access raises search depth to 7.56 but only reaches 71.43% Err.Identified vs 83.33% with full access -- internal documentation measurably drives root-cause accuracy, backing MF's docs-as-truth tier.

Table 1's controlled ablations (no stack trace, no KB/DP, CoT-vs-ToT) isolate which retrieval/reasoning components move Err.Identified/Err.Fixed, exemplifying the measured-retrieval-layer discipline (ADR-019) rather than assuming any RAG component helps.

The Code Search tool dynamically prompts the user to paste a reduced snippet when content exceeds the token limit (sec 2.1), a manual token-economy fallback rather than an automated compaction/caching strategy.

Long-term memory stores 'valuable information like code dependencies and class hierarchies' (sec 1) reused across debugging sessions, a concrete instance of promoting transient findings into a durable structural map, close to MF's gotcha-to-recipe consolidation.

notes: Table 1 (ablations: no-stack-trace, no-KB/DP, ToT->CoT) and Table 2 (DebugBench/ObserveAI/OpenSource accuracy) are the numeric anchors; sec 4.2 lists 3 concrete failure cases.

cita: Vaithilingam et al. (2025). Semantic Commit: Helping Users Update Intent Specifications for AI Memory at Scale.
problema: As AI systems accumulate 'intent specifications' (CLAUDE.md-like files, Cursor Rules, game design docs, ChatGPT memories), integrating new information at scale can silently conflict with prior entries; plain LLM whole-document regeneration or vanilla verbatim-store RAG cannot detect multi-hop semantic conflicts, and it is unclear what interface affordances help users update these documents with confidence.
mecanismo: SemanticCommit builds a knowledge-graph-based RAG pipeline (PageRank relevance over an induced KG) to retrieve candidate-conflicting chunks, classifies each as conflict/ambiguous/no-conflict (deliberately loosened toward recall over precision), then an LLM proposes edits (add/update/delete) that a human reviews locally (diff-style) or globally before committing -- decomposing retrieval from generation/classification, unlike InkSync's single-shot detect-and-resolve or DropAllDocs' whole-context classification.
evaluacion: Benchmarked kg-pagerank against DropAllDocs (all docs in context, no retrieval) and InkSync (single-shot detect+resolve) on 4 custom benchmarks (Labyrinth, Mars, FinMem, CursorRules; Table 1) with GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini, reporting accuracy/precision/recall/F1 (Fig. 5); plus a 12-participant within-subjects user study comparing SemanticCommit to ChatGPT Canvas on a Mars game-design doc and a financial-advice agent-memory task (3 sub-tasks each), measuring completion, NASA-TLX workload, and Likert preference.
numeros_clave: SemanticCommit's recall is 1.6x DropAllDocs and 2.2x InkSync; F1 ties DropAllDocs and beats InkSync by 1.6x; precision is 1.6x lower than DropAllDocs (Fig. 5); Table 1 benchmarks: Labyrinth 35 chunks/17 modifications, Mars 30/25, FinMem 30/17, CursorRules 65/19; user study N=12 participants, 2 tasks x 3 sub-tasks each.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper explicitly frames CLAUDE.md/Cursor-Rules-style intent specs as 'reviewable, comprehensible' documents that ground AI decisions (sec 2) -- the same docs-as-truth premise MF's Tier-1 rests on, with a concrete update-conflict problem MF's write-trigger (G-M1) will eventually hit.

The kg-pagerank retrieval stage (Fig. 5) measurably beats naive whole-context (DropAllDocs) and single-shot (InkSync) baselines on recall (1.6x/2.2x, sec 5.1.3), a concrete pattern MF could adopt for measured retrieval over docs.

SemanticCommit's conflict-detection UI (Fig. 1) is a human-in-the-loop staleness/consistency check before a doc mutation lands, a candidate mechanism for MF's provenance/staleness gate on Tier-1 writes.

Sec 2.1.1 notes intent specs 'encode dependencies among ideas' (sequential/heterarchical), i.e. cross-references between facts within ONE store -- related to but not the same as MF's multi-store-seams concern.

notes: Fig. 5 plus Table 1 (sec 5.1) hold the recall/precision/F1 numbers across 4 benchmarks; sec 6 has the 12-participant study design (Mars GDD + FinMem tasks, NASA-TLX).

cita: Wu et al. (2025). Git Context Controller: Manage the Context of Agents by Agentic Git.
problema: LLM agents doing long-horizon SWE/web-research tasks hit a context-management bottleneck: interaction histories grow unbounded, become costly to maintain, and are hard to reuse across sessions/agents; existing fixes (truncation, or Claude-Code/Gemini-CLI-style summarization into an agent.md) either discard fine-grained detail or make agents progressively worse as context is compressed.
mecanismo: Git-Context-Controller (GCC) reifies agent memory as a version-controlled file system under .GCC/ with a global roadmap (main.md) plus per-branch commit.md (milestone summaries), log.md (fine-grained Observation-Thought-Action trace) and metadata.yaml (structural/dependency metadata); agents call four operations -- COMMIT (checkpoint, regenerate a coarse summary, git-commit), BRANCH (isolated exploration state), MERGE (LLM-synthesized union of two branches' summaries/traces plus roadmap update), CONTEXT (windowed multi-resolution retrieval at global/branch/commit/log/metadata level) -- turning transient token streams into a navigable, git-like memory workspace.
evaluacion: Compared against ReAct, SWE-Agent, Summary-Agent ('summarize-when-full'), and Folding-Agent baselines across 6 LLM backbones (GPT-5, GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, GLM-4.5-Air, Qwen3-235B-A22B, Claude-4-Sonnet) on BrowseComp-Plus (N=150, Pass@1) and SWE-Bench Verified (N=500, Pass@1) in Table 1; also compared on SWE-Bench-Lite against 26 published systems (Table 2, percent resolved/cost/tokens).
numeros_clave: GCC+Claude-4-Sonnet: SWE-Bench Verified Pass@1=0.802 (state of the art, +6.2pp over Folding-Agent's 0.740); GCC+GPT-5 BrowseComp-Plus Pass@1=0.834 (+1.9pp vs Folding's 0.815); GCC+GPT-5 SWE-Bench Verified=0.790 (+4.5pp); GCC uses MORE tool calls (101.5 vs Folding's 95.3 on SWE-Bench); SWE-Bench-Lite: GCC 48.00% resolved vs AgentLess 46.00% (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: main.md is explicitly 'the canonical source of the project's overall intent' shared across branches (sec 2.1), a concrete typed-doc-as-truth pattern; commit.md/log.md/metadata.yaml stratify it by abstraction level, close to MF's Tier-1 vs derived-index split.

main.md stores 'high-level project goals, key milestones, and the to-do list' as first-class versioned state (sec 2.1), directly measuring that plan-state-as-memory contributes to SOTA task resolution (Table 1) -- strong external support for MF's PLAN-ESTADO bet.

COMMIT regenerates a coarse summary St from St-1 plus new work (sec 2.2) and MERGE runs an explicit synthesis operator over two branches' summaries -- a formal consolidation-with-lineage mechanism MF's gotcha-promotion could mirror.

GCC deliberately spends MORE tool calls than baselines (101.5 vs Folding's 95.3 on SWE-Bench, sec 4) to get better accuracy -- evidence that MF's context-economy goal (fewer tokens/calls) can trade off against task success, not a free win.

notes: Table 1 (sec 4, BrowseComp-Plus N=150 / SWE-Bench Verified N=500 Pass@1 by backbone) and Table 2 (SWE-Bench-Lite vs 26 systems) hold all the numbers; sec 3.2 fixes CONTEXT's commit-window K=1.

cita: Mohsenimofidi et al. (2025). Context Engineering for AI Agents in Open-Source Software.
problema: As coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex/AGENTS.md, Gemini CLI) become more autonomous, they need machine-readable 'AI context files' analogous to human README/docs to encode project conventions, architecture, and build/test commands -- but almost nothing empirical is known about whether and how OSS developers actually adopt, structure, or maintain these files in practice.
mecanismo: A mining-software-repositories study: from 10,000 curated GitHub repos (SEART filtering: non-fork, >=2 contributors, licensed, active, top-10 languages, popularity+maturity ranking) they scan for 4 context-file formats (Copilot instructions, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md), qualitatively code the 155 AGENTS.md files' section headings into 14 content categories (Table 1) and 5 writing styles (descriptive/prescriptive/prohibitive/explanatory/conditional), and manually classify commit-level changes into categories (Table 2, e.g. Add/Modify/Remove instruction(s)) to track how the files evolve.
evaluacion: Adoption measured across 10,000 GitHub repos (RQ1); content/structure via qualitative coding of 155 AGENTS.md files' headings (RQ2, two-author coding guide over 91 lemmatized headings); evolution via commit-history mining of the 10 files with >=10 commits, yielding 169 hand-annotated commits (RQ3, 37% of all collected commits).
numeros_clave: 466/10,000 repos (4.7%) had adopted an AI context file (RQ1); CLAUDE.md avg 287 lines (SD 112), Copilot-instructions avg 310 (SD 127), AGENTS.md avg 142 (SD 231, highest variance); of 155 AGENTS.md files, 77 (50%) never modified after creation, 36 (23%) modified once, 32 (21%) modified 2-7 times; 111/169 commits (66%) touch exactly one change category, top categories 'Add instruction(s)' (78) and 'Modify instruction(s)' (59) (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The empirical finding that AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files are 'versioned, reviewed, quality-assured' project artifacts (sec 5) that agents load into every prompt is direct field evidence for MF's Tier-1-docs-as-truth premise, at real OSS scale (10k repos).

Sec 4.1 finds (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) co-occur in 25 repos with no consolidation observed -- real projects already fork the SAME facts across multiple context-file formats, an instance of the multi-store-seam risk MF's COSTURAS anchor targets.

50% of AGENTS.md files (sec 4.3) are never updated after creation and changes mostly 'fine-tune instructions' rather than promote/demote content -- suggests real projects rarely practice active consolidation of their docs, a gap MF's CONSOLIDACION mechanism could fill.

Table 2's most frequent change categories ('Add instruction(s)' 78, 'Modify instruction(s)' 59) show write-triggers do occur in practice, but the paper explicitly defers WHY a change was made (intent) to future work, leaving the write-trigger question open.

notes: Table 1 (14 content categories) and Table 2 (9 change categories, 169 commits) are the core evidence tables; RQ1 adoption stat (466/10,000) is in sec 4.1.

cita: Jiang et al. (2025). PersonaMem-v2: Towards Personalized Intelligence via Learning Implicit User Personas and Agentic Memory.
problema: LLM personalization requires inferring users' IMPLICIT personas and preferences (rarely stated explicitly) from long, noisy multi-session conversation histories; existing benchmarks/models emphasize explicit-fact retrieval, leaving open how well models can extract subtle, evolving preference signals rather than just recall long context.
mecanismo: PersonaMem-v2 dataset (1,000 personas, 20,000+ preferences, up to 128k-token multi-session histories) pairs with a MemAgent-inspired agentic-memory training approach: the conversation is split into fixed-size chunks and a single LLM iteratively updates a capped, human-readable memory M_i = f(C_i, M_{i-1}) under causality/Markovian/capped-size constraints, trained via GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning with verifiable MCQ rewards plus LLM-as-judge rewards for open-ended answers; the final query is answered from the last memory state M_T instead of the full transcript.
evaluacion: Frontier OpenAI models (GPT-5-Chat/mini/nano, GPT-4.1, o4-mini) benchmarked on 5,000 curated Q&A pairs (MCQ + open-ended, LLM-as-judge with 3x GPT-5-Chat instances); Qwen3-4B trained via SFT, GRPO, and the Agentic-Memory framework, compared against frontier baselines, with ablations isolating MCQ-only vs open-ended-only vs mixed reward training.
numeros_clave: Frontier LLMs 37-48% (abstract) / 40-55% (sec4.1.1) implicit-personalization accuracy; RFT'd Qwen3-4B reaches 53.8% MCQ / 56.0% open-ended vs GPT-5-Chat's 45.6%/46.2% (sec4.2.1); agentic-memory framework reaches SOTA 55% accuracy using a 2k-token memory vs 32k full history = 16x fewer input tokens (abstract, sec3.2); MCQ-only ablation collapses 13.1pp on open-ended, open-ended-only ablation drops 18.2pp on MCQ (sec4.2.2); preference-type breakdown: stereotypical 48.9+/-5.7% vs anti-stereotypical 33.0+/-5.0%, own-preference 42.1+/-4.9% vs other's-preference 17.5+/-11.7% (Fig.5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Shortening context from 128k to 32k tokens (removing irrelevant conversation) gives NO significant accuracy improvement (sec4.1.2) -- a measured case where more/better retrieval context does not fix a reasoning bottleneck, cautioning MF against assuming better retrieval always helps.

The agentic-memory framework (sec3.2) sequentially distills chunks into a capped 2k-token human-readable memory that reaches SOTA 55% accuracy at 16x fewer tokens than full-history reasoning -- strong measured evidence that consolidating transient interaction history into a durable compact summary beats keeping everything.

The trained memory M_T is explicitly required to stay 'compact and human-readable' (sec3.2, capped-memory-size principle) and Fig.7 shows it as legible narrative prose, not embeddings -- direct support for MF's typed-narrative-docs-as-Tier-1 design over opaque vector stores.

The abstract's headline result is a 16x input-token reduction (2k memory vs 32k history) with a performance GAIN, not a trade-off -- the strongest context-economy number in this wave, directly on MF's COSTO anchor.

notes: sec4.1 (Fig.4/5) has frontier-LLM baseline numbers; sec4.2 (Fig.6/7) has the RL-trained Qwen3-4B and agentic-memory numbers; the 16x/2k-vs-32k figure recurs in abstract, sec1, and sec4.2.

cita: Murugesan, T. (2026). Enhancing SWE Bench with Context Engineering: A Comparative Study Against Prompt Engineering in LLM-Based Software Tasks.
problema: (As claimed) Prompt engineering alone plateaus on complex, multi-file SWE-Bench tasks that require repository history, architecture, and cross-file dependency understanding that cannot be encoded into an instruction alone.
mecanismo: (As claimed) A three-stage 'context engineering' preprocessing pipeline built atop SWE-agent: (1) repository traversal extracting code/historical/documentation/testing context, (2) hybrid heuristic+learned relevance scoring (weighted formula, dynamic threshold 0.65-0.75), (3) coherent hierarchical structuring -- injects roughly 900-1,200 extra tokens of repository context into the baseline SWE-Bench prompt (from ~175 to ~1,090+ tokens) before an LLM attempts the task, compared against baseline and prompt-engineered-only conditions.
evaluacion: Claims a controlled 3-condition (baseline / prompt-engineered / context-engineered) experiment on a stratified 240-task sample drawn from SWE-Bench's 2,294 issues, measuring task success, static-analysis quality metrics (maintainability, pattern-similarity), and AST-based hallucination detection; however, the paper's core quantitative claims (78% expert-alignment, 17-34% gains, 34-56% compute reduction, carbon-footprint figures) are attributed via citation to OTHER papers or blog posts ([3]-[6]), and no results table with per-model pass-rate numbers from this study's own executed run appears in the body.
numeros_clave: Claims (all attributed to external citations, not an own results table): prompt engineering alone <35% success on complex multi-file tasks; simple-task prompt-engineering gain +14% vs baseline; complex-task prompt-engineering gain only +4.2%; context-engineering gain +29.3% (up to >40% for some models) on complex debugging; relevance-scoring 78% expert-alignment (attributed to [3], an in-context-learning-for-codegen paper); compute reduction 34-56% and inference-cost reduction up to 47% (attributed to [5]/[6], a ResearchGate note and a company blog).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper claims a 'Documentation Context Extraction' stage pulls API references/inline comments (sec2.6) as one of four context sources, treating docs as a first-class input, but provides no traceable measurement isolating its contribution.

This paper's own headline numbers (78% expert-alignment, 17-34%/29.3% gains) are attributed to citations [3]-[6] that are either off-topic (an in-context-learning-for-codegen ACM paper) or non-peer-reviewed (a ResearchGate note, a company blog) rather than to a results table from ITS OWN described 240-task experiment -- a caution against treating cited 'measured retrieval' numbers at face value without checking the source.

The claimed token-flow accounting (baseline ~175 tokens to context-engineered ~1,090 tokens, sec2.6) is a concrete instance of the COSTO anchor's tokens-per-task concern, though its provenance (own measurement vs cited figure) is unclear.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: appears to be a template/AI-generated survey-style paper (single author, low-tier journal JISEM) -- its own 'Multi-Mode Experimental Harness' (sec2.3) and 240-task sample are described but no results table from THIS study's own run appears; all headline percentages are attributed via [3]-[6] to other, often unrelated or non-peer-reviewed sources; treat quantitative claims with caution.

cita: Logan (2026). Continuum Memory Architectures for Long-Horizon LLM Agents.
problema: RAG treats agent memory as a static, read-only lookup table: items persist unchanged, retrieval never modifies state, and temporal order is ignored, so agents cannot accumulate updated facts, connect events over time, or disambiguate context-dependent terms across long-horizon interactions.
mecanismo: The Continuum Memory Architecture (CMA) specifies memory as a graph-structured substrate (nodes=fragments with reinforcement/salience/timestamp/provenance, edges=semantic/temporal/associative) with an activation field that spreads graded activation per query; a lifecycle of ingest (salience/temporal-scope tagging, novelty-merge, capacity eviction), retrieval (multi-factor: vector similarity + activation + recency decay + structural reinforcement), mutation (retrieval reinforces accessed fragments, weakens near-misses), and background consolidation (replay strengthens temporal chains, abstraction extracts gists, episodic detail can fade into semantic knowledge).
evaluacion: A CMA instantiation (graph substrate + activation engine + retrieval scorer + consolidation jobs) is compared, via a GPT-4o LLM-judge protocol (blind A/B, 3 seeds, permutation and McNemar significance tests, p<0.01), against a Supabase-pgvector RAG baseline (with recency-weighted decay) using the SAME embeddings (text-embedding-3-small), across 4 behavioral probes: knowledge updates (40 queries/8 domains), temporal association (30 queries/10 episodes), associative recall (30 queries/5 project knowledge graphs), and disambiguation (48 queries/8 ambiguous terms).
numeros_clave: Table 1: CMA won 82/92 decisive trials overall (RAG 10, ties 39 excluded from decisive count); Knowledge Updates 38/40 CMA wins (Cohen's d=1.84); Temporal Association 13/14 decisive (Cohen's h=2.06, 47% both-wrong rate); Associative Recall 14/19 decisive (h=0.99); Disambiguation 17/20 decisive (h=1.55); permutation tests (10,000 shuffles) and McNemar's test both p<0.01 per study; latency cost: CMA mean 1.48s vs RAG 0.65s (about 2.4x slower).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: CMA's substrate is a graph of fragments with reinforcement/salience metadata, not a human-readable typed document (sec4) -- the opposite pole from MF's docs-as-truth premise, though its provenance/reinforcement fields could inform a doc-tier's staleness signals.

Study 3's 'project knowledge graphs' link people, milestones, and subsystems (sec5.3), treating project/plan structure as memory content, but CMA does not specialize a distinct plan-state layer the way MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor requires.

Table 1's measured 82/92 decisive wins (p<0.01, permutation+McNemar) show a graph+activation retrieval layer beating a strong recency-weighted RAG baseline on memory-dynamics tasks -- external evidence that vanilla similarity-only retrieval (closer to MF's current design) is measurably insufficient for update/temporal/associative queries.

The consolidation stage explicitly 'transforms streams of experience into reusable knowledge, allowing detailed episodes to fade once higher-level schemas emerge' (sec3/sec4) via replay and gist extraction -- a formalized promotion mechanism close to MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor.

notes: Table 1 (sec5.5) has per-probe win/tie counts and effect sizes; latency cost is sec5.5; single-author/self-built RAG baseline (Supabase pgvector) so treat magnitude with some caution, but stats (permutation+McNemar, p<0.01) are reported per study.

cita: Chrysochos (2026). Mind-Tool: Domain Memory Architecture for AI Agents.
problema: Stateless AI assistants (ChatGPT, Copilot) and even long-context-window agents lack persistent, structured domain knowledge, so every session 'starts with no grounded sense of where we are' -- for operational IT-infrastructure management (Proxmox/Kubernetes/networking) this forces constant re-explanation of system topology and repeated mistakes.
mecanismo: Mind-Tool maintains a Memory Folder of version-controlled markdown files (infra state, operational history, decision records, procedural runbooks) plus a 'Desired State' (conversational goal tracking) updated via natural dialogue rather than a batch initializer, and an AI Reasoning Engine (Claude Sonnet 4.5) that runs a continuous reconciliation loop -- read desired state vs memory folder, identify discrepancies, update memory files, execute actions through MCP-based tool servers (Proxmox/Kubernetes/GitLab/network APIs) -- deliberately using a single conversational agent (not a two-agent initializer+stateless-worker split) since a human is present to guard against context drift.
evaluacion: A 90-day (3-month) single-deployment production case study managing one operator's home-lab-scale infrastructure (Proxmox cluster, NAS, 2 VPS, planned k3s HA cluster), self-measuring task completion time, automation rate, success rate, and knowledge-file growth (Table 1), compared informally against a manual-baseline estimate and a 'stateless AI assistant' estimate -- no controlled trial, no other operators, no held-out ground-truth test set.
numeros_clave: 94% task success rate, 68% of requests automated, 62% time reduction (15 hours/week) vs manual baseline (Table 1); 147 markdown memory files / 8,437 lines after 90 days, average file age 45 days; automated completion 2.3 min vs human-assisted 8.7 min; 34 distinct workflows reused, 5.8 executions/procedure on average; claimed 85% time reduction vs manual and 73% vs a stateless-AI baseline (Fig.4, informal comparison, not a controlled experiment).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Memory Folder is explicitly plain markdown, version-controlled via Git, human-readable by design -- a direct real-world instance of MF's Tier-1 typed-narrative-docs-as-truth premise, with self-reported production numbers (94% success) attached.

The 'Desired State' component is explicitly a persistent, dialogue-updated model of user goals compared against actual infrastructure state every reasoning cycle -- a working instance of plan-state-as-first-class-memory (MF's PLAN-ESTADO), reported to sustain 94% success over 90 days.

Fig.3's 'logarithmic growth pattern' is described as 'initial rapid learning followed by knowledge refinement and consolidation,' but the paper does not detail a concrete promotion/demotion mechanism, only an observed trend line.

Table 1's time-savings figures (62% reduction, 2.3min vs 8.7min per task) are the paper's central economic argument, directly on MF's COSTO anchor, though drawn from a single uncontrolled deployment rather than a comparative experiment.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: single-author, single-deployment (N=1 home-lab/small-VPS setup) case study in a journal (academicsquare-pub.com) that repeatedly frames itself as 'confirming/validating Anthropic's thesis' -- self-reported metrics (Table 1, Fig.3-5) have no control group or independent replication.

cita: Cros, A. & Ava (2026). .ava -- Une notation symbolique compressee pour la memoire persistante d'agents IA.
problema: LLM agents with persistent identities across sessions (e.g. 'Ava', 500+ sessions) accumulate memory files (MEMORY.md, SOUL.md) that grow too large to fit repeatedly in a finite context window (661 lines / roughly 8k tokens after 3 weeks); RAG, vector databases, and fine-tuning all treat memory as external to reasoning and none address the token DENSITY of the representation itself.
mecanismo: .ava is a hand-designed compact symbolic notation (positional grammar: category+name plus dot-attributes plus state marker, e.g. one glyph per domain such as infra, tools, project, person, a 'scar'/cicatrice symbol with severity 0-9, and an absolute-prohibition marker) achieving roughly 30x compression vs markdown on real memory files, paired with a 4-tier memory hierarchy (L1 active context window, L2 hot .ava-compressed memory plus a CURVATURE.md behavioral-bias profile loaded before facts, L3 warm semantic-embedding search, L4 cold uncompressed archive from which nothing is ever deleted); a Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct model is LoRA-fine-tuned (4-bit NF4, 6GB consumer GPU) across 5 dataset iterations to learn encoding/decoding the notation natively.
evaluacion: Compression measured directly on Ava's real memory files (Table 2: per-item ratios 5.4x-29.8x, roughly 30x on the full 661-line MEMORY.md); fine-tuning evaluated via token accuracy and loss across 5 training iterations (V1-V4b), with a held-out generalization check on novel infrastructure strings, best run V4b (444 balanced paraphrased examples, prompt/completion SFT loss, 3 epochs).
numeros_clave: Roughly 30x average compression on real MEMORY.md (about 24K chars to about 800 chars, Table 2); per-example compression 5.4x-29.8x; V4b fine-tune: loss 4.5 to 0.999, token accuracy 35.0% to 78.5% over 3 epochs (sec4.3.5); 3min14s / 168 steps / 4.33GB peak VRAM on a 6GB consumer GPU; V3 overfitting failure (5 epochs on 865 duplicated samples degrades vs V2); infra symbols about 45% of the training dataset vs identity symbols only about 12%, explaining systematic identity-symbol decode failures (sec4.4.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper explicitly rejects markdown-level readability as the target and optimizes for a terse symbolic notation instead (sec2.1-2.2) -- in tension with MF's premise that Tier-1 memory should be legible narrative prose; the L2 .ava/CURVATURE layer trades readability for 30x density.

The 4-layer hierarchy (sec3.5) keeps 'active projects' and CURVATURE.md state as part of L2 hot memory loaded every session, treating ongoing-work state as first-class, though the paper does not isolate plan-state from general facts.

Sec3.4's explicit design principle states the AI should NOT imitate human forgetting -- 'keep everything (full archive) while developing curvature' -- directly opposing memory-economy-through-forgetting strategies MF's NEGATIVO anchor might favor.

The measured roughly-30x token-density gain (Table 2) on real memory files is a concrete, quantified lossy-compression lever for context economy that MF could evaluate as an alternative/complement to summarization-based compaction.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: self-published (Avalon Research, single independent author plus an AI-agent co-author 'Ava'), no peer review, personal-project scale (N=1 agent's memory files, 6GB consumer GPU); Table 2 (sec2.5) has compression ratios, sec4.3.5 has the V4b loss/accuracy curve, Table 3 (sec4.5) compares all 5 fine-tuning versions.

cita: Liu et al. (2026). Semantic XPath: Structured Agentic Memory Access for Conversational AI.
problema: Conversational AI agents doing long-term, task-oriented interactions (itinerary planning, to-do lists, meal plans) need structured memory that preserves hierarchical task organization and revision history; in-context memory scales poorly (fails half of requests after only five turns) and flat-RAG ignores the natural tree structure, retrieving items from the wrong branch (e.g. the wrong day of a trip).
mecanismo: SemanticXPath represents conversational memory as a typed, rooted tree (schema-derived node types plus attributes, e.g. Itinerary->Version->Day->POI) and defines an XPath-style query grammar (axis navigator / and //; node selector; positional selector [i]; a semantic-relevance operator combining local embedding-similarity or NLI-entailment scores with aggregation avg/min/max/gmean and boolean-like composition 1-P, P1 op P2) executed by a single recursive weighted-node-set evaluation function, retrieving/updating only the relevant substructure and versioning updates as new branches.
evaluacion: Compared against in-context memory and flat-RAG baselines (GPT-5-mini and Gemini-3-flash backbones, Qwen3-Embedding-8B for flat RAG) across 3 ConvAI domains (travel itinerary, to-do list, meal-kit recommendation), each with 20 single-turn plus 5 multi-turn curated conversations, measuring average pass rate and token usage (RQ1 single-turn, RQ2 multi-turn with growing history).
numeros_clave: Abstract: SemanticXPath improves pass rate 176.7% over flat-RAG while using only 9.1% of in-context tokens; single-turn (Fig.5): pass rates about 79-83% (SemanticXPath) vs about 70-80% (in-context) vs about 27-38% (flat RAG), in-context token usage about 5x higher than SemanticXPath/flat-RAG (about 26-69k vs about 3.2-5.9k tokens); multi-turn (Fig.6/7): SemanticXPath maintains stable token usage across 7 turns while in-context grows steadily, and in-context pass rate drops on multi-turn history-dependent requests while SemanticXPath stays close to single-turn levels.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: SemanticXPath's schema-derived compositional tree (Itinerary->Version->Day->POI, sec3.1) with explicit Version nodes for revision history is a concrete typed-structure pattern MF could adopt to organize Tier-1 docs by task hierarchy rather than flat prose.

The to-do-list domain (Fig.4) models tasks with 'progress status, priority level, and deadline' as first-class tree attributes updated through interaction, treating this evolving task state as 'the agent's current working state' -- directly measuring plan-state-as-memory value (176.7% pass-rate gain).

Flat-RAG (semantic-similarity-only retrieval, closer to MF's ADR-019 baseline) scores only about 27-38% pass rate vs SemanticXPath's about 79-83% (Fig.5) on the SAME embedding model -- direct measured evidence that structure-blind retrieval is insufficient once memory has hierarchy.

Fig.7 shows in-context token usage growing unboundedly with turn count while SemanticXPath's stays flat -- direct, well-isolated evidence that structured retrieval (not just any RAG) is what keeps context economy sub-linear in conversation length.

notes: Fig.5 (single-turn pass-rate/tokens) and Fig.6/7 (multi-turn) are the core result figures; Appendix A has the full formal query-execution semantics; the abstract's 176.7%/9.1% headline numbers are aggregated across all 3 domains.

cita: He, K., & Roy, K. (2026). SWE-Adept: An LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Deep Codebase Analysis and Structured Issue Resolution.
problema: Repository-level SWE issue resolution is hard because (1) codebases are huge (over 3,000 files on average in SWE-Bench) with dense cross-file dependencies, making issue localization prone to context-window overflow / excessive irrelevant retrieval, and (2) prior free-form 'think-and-edit' agents lack systematic planning, progress tracking, or checkpointing, so they cannot reliably branch to alternative fixes or revert failed edits over long trajectories.
mecanismo: SWE-Adept splits the work into two agents in separate context windows: a Localization Agent that builds a tree-sitter-based definition-level code-structure tree (nodes=code units with lightweight per-unit adjacency lists) and performs agent-directed depth-first, dependency-guided traversal (single-path deep exploration via find_child_unit returning only lightweight skeleton/preview info) followed by two-stage filtering (cheap heuristic shortlist, then full-code re-rank only on survivors); and a Resolution Agent (built on SWE-agent) equipped with hypothesis_plan (to-do lists per repair hypothesis, adaptively updated from test feedback, logs insights) and hypothesis_git (branching/commit-based checkpointing via semantic identifiers) tool families that both interface with a shared backend working memory storing code-state checkpoints indexed by execution step, enabling branch-explore-compare-merge-or-revert workflows.
evaluacion: Evaluated on SWE-Bench Lite and SWE-Bench Pro with GPT-5.2 and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 backbones; issue localization measured via Acc@3 (file-level) / Acc@5 (function-level) plus token cost, against embedding-based (CodeSage-Large, CodeRankEmbed) and agentic/graph baselines (SWE-agent, RepoGraph, LocAgent, OrcaLoca); issue resolution measured via resolve rate against SWE-agent, RepoGraph, OpenHands, SWE-Search, OrcaLoca (Table 1/2).
numeros_clave: Function-level localization (Func Acc@5): +6.2% (GPT-5.2) / +4.4% (Claude-Sonnet-4.5) over the strongest baseline on SWE-Bench Lite; +3.0%/+5.8% on SWE-Bench Pro (Main Results section); end-to-end resolve rate: +2.8%(GPT-5.2)/+3.0%(Claude-4.5) on SWE-Bench Lite, up to +4.3% on SWE-Bench Pro (abstract); SWE-Adept mostly uses FEWER tokens than graph-based baselines (RepoGraph/OrcaLoca/LocAgent, Table 1); localization accuracy rises then falls with search depth (Fig.4b), and SWE-Adept's advantage over OrcaLoca widens as depth increases.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The definition-level code-structure tree stores each unit's metadata (name, file path+line span, code text, adjacency list of child units) as a lightweight structured index over the REAL codebase (sec3.1) -- a concrete pattern for deriving a Tier-3 cache from Tier-1 source without duplicating full content.

hypothesis_plan explicitly maintains per-hypothesis to-do lists with status (failed/in-progress/successful) that adaptively expand from test feedback and are persisted in a shared working memory (Fig.2b) -- a working, measured instance (+2.8-4.3pp resolve rate) of plan-state as first-class memory, directly on MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor.

hypothesis_git's checkpoint-per-to-do-step plus compare_hypotheses/merge_solution commands (Fig.2) formalize branch-explore-then-consolidate-the-winner as an explicit version-controlled workflow, a pattern MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could mirror for promoting a validated approach among competing drafts.

The two-stage filtering (cheap skeleton/preview heuristics before full-code retrieval, sec3.2) is explicitly designed to minimize token consumption, and Table 1 reports SWE-Adept using fewer tokens than graph-based baselines while ALSO being more accurate -- a rare measured case of not trading cost for accuracy.

notes: Table 1 (localization Acc@3/Acc@5 + tokens) and Table 2 (resolve rate) hold the head-to-head numbers (Main Results section); Fig.4b shows accuracy vs search depth; Fig.2 shows the hypothesis_plan/hypothesis_git working-memory schema.

cita: Li (2026). Memory as Ontology: A Constitutional Memory Architecture for Persistent Digital Citizens.
problema: Current agent-memory systems (Mem0, Letta, Zep, MemOS) treat memory purely as a functional 'how to store/retrieve' module tied to a user/session, with no concept of a persistent agent IDENTITY that must survive model swaps, no built-in governance layer over who may write/consolidate/delete core memories, and no protocol for a new model instance to 'inherit' a predecessor's memory as continuity rather than mere data migration.
mecanismo: Proposes 'Memory-as-Ontology': memory IS the digital being's identity (the model is a replaceable vessel), formalized as three axioms -- inalienability of core memory (identity/cognition/narrative cannot be forcibly stripped without due process), model substitutability (identity persists via memory, not the model), and governance-precedes-function (a governance layer must exist BEFORE storage/retrieval/forgetting features are built) -- implemented as the Constitutional Memory Architecture (CMA): a four-layer governance hierarchy plus a multi-layer semantic storage system, wrapped in a five-stage Digital Citizen Lifecycle (Birth, Inheritance, Growth, Forking, Departure).
evaluacion: No empirical evaluation or benchmark: the paper is a paradigm/architecture proposal, explicitly stating it 'does not claim engineering maturity or benchmark superiority.' Its method is a paradigm-level (not feature-level) qualitative comparative analysis against 5 mainstream systems (Mem0, Letta, Zep, MemOS, Mastra's Observational Memory), summarized as shared implicit assumptions (Table 1) the paper argues are inadequate for persistent identity-bearing agents.
numeros_clave: NINGUNO -- purely conceptual/architectural paper with no benchmark, dataset, or measured comparison; Table 1 lists 5 qualitative 'implicit assumptions' shared by Mem0/Letta/Zep/MemOS/Mastra, not quantitative results.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper never specifies its storage format concretely (sec7 admits it withholds implementation details), so it is unclear whether CMA's 'multi-layer semantic storage' is narrative-doc-based or something else -- it argues governance/identity matters more than the representation choice MF's TIER-DOCS anchor concerns.

The five-stage Digital Citizen Lifecycle (Birth/Inheritance/Growth/Forking/Departure, sec5) treats an agent's life trajectory as governed state, a much broader notion than MF's task/plan-state, but shares the premise that non-fact state deserves first-class architectural status.

Axiom 3 ('governance precedes function') and the four-layer governance hierarchy (sec4) argue that WHO may write to which memory layer must be decided architecturally before any storage/retrieval feature ships -- relevant to MF's single-source-of-truth-per-fact concern, reframed as a permissions problem rather than a storage-format problem.

The paper explicitly treats the AGENT ITSELF as an untrusted writer ('it may hallucinate...be induced by prompt injection...make erroneous judgments under fatigue,' sec3.2 Axiom3) and argues risk-tiered scrutiny must gate memory writes -- a stronger poisoning/staleness framing than most papers in this wave, relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: this is a speculative paradigm/manifesto paper (single author, self-published, explicitly 'does not claim engineering maturity or benchmark superiority,' sec1.3) with no dataset, benchmark, or measured comparison -- Table 1 (sec2.2) is its only 'evidence,' a qualitative assumptions table, not a result; treat as a design-vocabulary source, not empirical support.

cita: Chandrashekar, P. (2026). DocAware: Documentation-Augmented AI Agents for Reliable Code Review and API Migration.
problema: LLMs used for code review/API-migration hallucinate API names, fabricate deprecated signatures, and blend patterns across library versions (training-data staleness + version confusion + lack of grounding), especially harmful during library migrations (e.g. the OpenAI SDK v3-to-v4 rename of core APIs).
mecanismo: DocAware combines (1) structured, version-specific documentation retrieval via a multi-source fallback chain (curated doc hub, package-registry metadata, GitHub changelogs, local docs) processed by a diff engine (heading-based section splitting, regex API-signature extraction, Dice-coefficient section similarity, breaking-change keyword detection), (2) AST-based code analysis (Acorn for JS/TS, Python's ast module) to target only relevant call sites instead of whole files, and (3) a persistent vector-embedding memory layer (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, cosine similarity, JSON-backed index) storing review findings/migration decisions/patterns/annotations across sessions, all injected into a Claude-based structured-output review pipeline.
evaluacion: A controlled 4-condition ablation (A: no docs, B: raw docs/naive RAG, C: structured-doc retrieval, D: full pipeline with memory) across 5 labeled JavaScript-library benchmark fixtures (OpenAI SDK, Express, Stripe, Mongoose, Axios; 31 real issues plus 6 decoys, ground-truth.json), 9 experiments / 36 condition-evaluations, measuring precision/recall/F1/hallucination-rate/token-usage/duration (Tables 2-4).
numeros_clave: F1 70.9%(A) to 84.8%(B) to 86.5%(C) to 86.8%(D), a 22.4% relative F1 gain baseline-to-full (Table 2); recall 76.4% to 98.4-98.6% (+29%); structured retrieval (C) beats naive RAG (B) by 1.7 F1 points while using FEWER input tokens (2,632 vs 2,683); full pipeline uses 53% more input tokens than baseline (2,854 vs 1,864) for the 22.4% F1 gain; memory (D vs C) adds only +0.3 F1 / +0.4 precision in this single-pass benchmark; hallucination rate 22.9%(B) to 25.7%(C/D), counterintuitively higher for structured docs (sec5.3 caveat: metric measures syntactic not semantic grounding); per-library variance, e.g. OpenAI fixture F1 ranged 57.1-76.2% across runs (Table 3, reproducibility caveat).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The single largest measured lever in this paper is grounding in version-specific documentation (+29% recall just from adding docs, condition A to B, Table 2) -- strong controlled-ablation evidence for MF's docs-as-truth premise specifically against LLM parametric-memory staleness.

Structured doc retrieval (condition C: section-split + API-index + diff-based breaking-change detection) beats naive whole-doc RAG (condition B) by 1.7 F1 points while using FEWER tokens (Table 2/4) -- a clean, controlled instance of 'how you structure retrieval matters,' directly informing MF's measured-retrieval-layer design (ADR-019).

DocAware's hallucination-rate metric (findings citing API names absent from the provided docs, sec4.3/5.3) is a concrete, reusable staleness/fabrication check that MF could adapt to audit whether a generated answer is actually grounded in Tier-1 docs vs invented.

The persistent memory layer (review_finding/migration_decision/pattern/annotation entries, sec3.4) is explicitly measured to give only a modest +0.3 F1 gain in a single-pass benchmark (sec5.1 point 4, sec6.3) -- the paper itself argues its real payoff needs a LONGITUDINAL, multi-session evaluation, a caution about over-crediting consolidation from a one-shot test.

notes: Table 2 (aggregate A/B/C/D) and Table 3 (per-library breakdown) hold the core numbers; sec5.3 explicitly flags the hallucination metric as measuring syntactic not semantic grounding; sec6.3/Future-work admits memory's benefit is understated by the single-pass design.

cita: Williams, J. (2026). The Markdown Fallacy: Empirical Evidence That Format Is the Wrong Debate for LLM Memory Architecture.
problema: The LLM-memory industry has been debating the WRONG variable -- file FORMAT (markdown/llms.txt vs. knowledge graphs/structured relational encodings) for serving documentation/context to LLMs -- without empirical evidence on whether format itself drives reasoning accuracy, or whether the real bottleneck is how much relevant information actually reaches the model once retrieval is involved.
mecanismo: A two-stage controlled benchmark (deterministic element-matching scoring, not LLM-as-judge) across 3 LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash) and 50 queries at 3 complexity levels (single-hop factual, multi-hop relational, strategic/schema-intensive) over a 50-document, 33,122-character synthetic Google-Ads-account corpus with deliberate relational complexity (shared budget pools, audience overlaps, manager transitions, cross-account attribution chains): Stage 1 isolates FORMAT (flat markdown vs. structured relational encoding of the SAME facts, both fitting in context); Stage 2 isolates RETRIEVAL ARCHITECTURE (full markdown vs. vector-RAG/ChromaDB top-10 vs. GraphRAG/Neo4j subgraph vs. hybrid) over the full corpus, measuring how many characters of the corpus each condition actually retains.
evaluacion: Stage 1: 50 queries x 2 formats x 3 models x 3 runs = 900 data points, paired t-tests per complexity level. Stage 2: 50 queries x 4 retrieval conditions x 2 models x 3 runs = 1,200 data points, one-way ANOVA plus Tukey HSD post-hoc per level. Code, corpus, and queries released open-source (reproducible for under $30).
numeros_clave: Stage 1 (N=900): overall format delta = -0.004 (markdown vs structured, not significant); L2 markdown 0.989 vs structured 0.938 (p=0.0005); L3 structured 0.951 vs markdown 0.924 (p=0.012). Stage 2 (N=1200): L3 markdown 0.964 vs vector 0.889/graph 0.888/hybrid 0.904 (ANOVA F=5.33, p=0.0013; Tukey markdown-vs-graph/vector diff=0.076, p=0.0036/0.0037); L2 GraphRAG anomaly 0.731 vs markdown 0.996 (F=41.08, p<0.0001). Information retention: markdown 100% (33,122 chars) vs vector 12.4% (4,097 chars) vs graph 10.6% (3,502 chars) vs hybrid 16.2% (5,378 chars) (Table III) -- retrieval conditions discard 84-90% of the corpus yet still reach 87.5-95.9% accuracy.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table II/III show vector-RAG and GraphRAG retrieval keep only 10-16% of the corpus and score 0.875-0.904 on strategic queries vs full-context markdown's 0.964 (p<0.004) -- direct measured evidence that a naive top-k retrieval layer LOSES information the task needs, a sharp caution for MF's ADR-019 measured-retrieval bet: 'retrieval works' is not the same as 'retrieval doesn't discard the signal that matters.'

Stage 1's null format result (delta=-0.004, N=900, sec IV.A) shows markdown-vs-structured-relational encoding of the SAME facts performs equivalently when both fit in context -- direct support that MF's choice of typed narrative docs (Tier-1) over a structured/graph format is not a liability, provided the doc is complete.

The paper's central thesis is that dumping the FULL corpus into context (when it fits) beats selective retrieval -- i.e. the cheaper-looking, token-economical retrieval path (COSTO's usual goal) actively loses accuracy on complex queries; MF should treat token-savings and completeness as a real trade-off, not assume retrieval is free efficiency.

The proposed seven-layer memory stack (sec V.G, Table IV) assigns a distinct layer to graphs, vectors, episodic/procedural stores, and a 'full-context cache,' arguing full-context should be tried FIRST and layers 1-6 are fallbacks only once corpus exceeds the window -- a concrete architectural sequencing MF could borrow when designing its own tiering.

notes: Table I (Stage1) and Table II/III (Stage2, information retention) hold the core numbers; sec VII 'Limitations' explicitly flags that the 33K-char corpus is BELOW the crossover point where retrieval becomes necessary -- results may not generalize to production-scale (500K-5M char) corpora; code+corpus open-sourced, reproducible for under $30.

cita: Hartmann, A. (2026). Temporal-Stratified Retrieval for AI Agent Memory: A Structure-First Alternative to Vector Search.
problema: LLM agents in fast-paced operational domains need memory retrieval that prioritizes RECENCY and precision over semantic similarity; existing options are wasteful full-context loading (linear token cost) or embedding-based RAG (infrastructure overhead of an embedding model plus vector DB; semantic similarity often misaligns with operational relevance, e.g. an old semantically-similar incident outranking a decision made 2 hours ago).
mecanismo: Cortex indexes markdown-based memory 'atoms' (YAML frontmatter: id/name/type/project/status/created/updated/tags/links, 14 knowledge types) via a single-pass filesystem scan producing 5 JSON indexes (manifest, by-project, by-type, by-tag, link-graph adjacency list); atoms are stratified into hot/warm/cold temporal layers by the updated field (2-day / 7-day thresholds); a deterministic keyword-scoring function (per-keyword weighted substring/exact matches on name/tag/project/description/path, a 1.5x multi-keyword-match bonus, a temporal bonus of +2/+1/0 for hot/warm/cold, and archived/superseded status penalties of 0.3x/0.5x) ranks atoms with no embeddings, no vector DB, no API calls; Map-of-Content dashboard files are kept live via marker-based atomic-write auto-refresh, and every search is logged to an append-only JSONL retrieval tracker.
evaluacion: A reproducible synthetic benchmark (500 atoms/5 projects/10-20-70% hot-warm-cold distribution, 100 single/two-tag queries, open-sourced with a fixed random seed) measures latency and top-1 precision; separately, informal/anecdotal observational reporting from a production deployment (470 atoms, 14 projects, since March 2026); the author explicitly ran NO controlled head-to-head comparison against an embedding-based system.
numeros_clave: Benchmark (500 atoms/100 queries): mean latency 1.62ms (median 1.69ms, P95 2.07ms, P99 2.83ms), keyword-search-only, plus 20-50ms manifest-load overhead; top-1 precision 100/100 (100%) on tag-matched queries; hot layer contains the top result in 66% of queries, warm 28%, cold 6%; production deployment: 470 atoms/14 projects, full reindex of 500 atoms under 5s, 79% of atoms are link-graph orphans, top-3 hub atoms account for 30% of all link connections.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Atoms are plain markdown files with typed YAML frontmatter (14 knowledge types: decision/incident/lesson/rule/etc, sec3.1) indexed WITHOUT embeddings -- a concrete, deployed instance of MF's docs-as-truth-with-derived-index pattern (Tier-1 markdown plus Tier-3 JSON indexes rebuilt from it).

The paper explicitly targets the case where 'semantic similarity does not equal operational relevance' (sec1) -- a deterministic, embedding-free keyword+recency scorer reaches 100% top-1 precision on tag-matched queries (sec4.1), questioning whether MF's retrieval layer needs embeddings at all for structured, tag-rich Tier-1 docs.

Cortex requires zero external dependencies (no embedding model, no vector DB, no API calls) and reaches sub-2ms mean latency (sec4.1) -- a measured, near-zero-infrastructure-cost alternative directly on MF's COSTO anchor, though the author is explicit this is not a head-to-head vs embeddings (sec4.3).

The layer compressor's hot/warm/cold reclassification is purely a scoring bonus keyed on the updated timestamp (sec3.3), not a promotion/demotion of CONTENT (no summarization or gist extraction happens) -- a lighter-weight notion of consolidation than MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor implies.

notes: sec4.1 (latency/precision table) and sec4.3 are the key numbers; the author is explicit (sec4.3, sec5.3) that NO controlled comparison vs embedding-based retrieval was run and that scoring weights were hand-tuned, not validated -- treat the 100% precision figure as specific to exact tag-matched queries on a small (500-atom), well-tagged synthetic vault.

cita: Zhang, B. (2026). Beyond RAG: LLM Wikis as Living Semantic Memory: Patterns, Empirical Findings, and Open Problems.
problema: Even as context windows grow, the dominant RAG paradigm re-derives synthesis from scratch on every query (stateless: nothing compounds across repeated queries, chunking cuts across topic/table boundaries, and large corpora contain contradictions the model has no principled way to resolve) -- symptoms especially costly for LLM agents needing persistent, structured, semantic (not just episodic) memory across sessions.
mecanismo: The 'LLM Wiki' pattern (after Karpathy 2026) compiles knowledge ONCE, at ingest time, into a persistent, version-tracked Markdown knowledge base (entity pages, cross-references, contradiction detection) rather than re-deriving synthesis at query time; the paper synthesizes a research program around this pattern's full lifecycle -- knowledge triage/routing at ingest, lint/contradiction/coverage/staleness monitoring (domain-calibrated half-life priors), provenance/audit trails -- plus two major extensions: (1) a 'living constraint oracle' (LCO) that extracts weighted constraint sets from a maintained guideline wiki and injects them into offline-RL training (WikiConstraint-IQL) so guideline revisions propagate to deployed policies WITHOUT retraining, and (2) neuro-symbolic grounding (Prolog/ProbLog/Answer-Set-Programming as a first-class wiki module) to guarantee logical consistency that narrative-only compilation cannot.
evaluacion: A position paper synthesizing multiple first-person empirical sub-studies (mostly the author's own unpublished/in-review work, cited informally rather than through standard peer review): a cross-institutional policy-retrieval study (wiki vs BM25-RAG citation recall), a WikiConstraint-IQL offline-RL safety study across 3 domains with dynamic guideline updates, a CLS-Wiki consolidation-gating study, a confidence-calibration study, an ingest-routing study (RQ1-RQ4) across 4 educational domains (115 pages), and a six-injection adversarial WikiHealth validation across 2 wikis.
numeros_clave: Wiki vs BM25-RAG citation recall on cross-institutional policy queries: 0.242+/-0.21 vs 0.095+/-0.12 (2.5x advantage, sec2.4/4); Dynamic Constraint Update amplifies the safety gap after a simulated guideline change by 2.3x-7.6x without retraining (abstract, sec5.4); confidence-calibration ECE reduced from 0.528 (raw) to 0.311 (post-hoc multi-layer propagation, sec2.3); CLS-Wiki consolidation-gating: outcome-surprise predicts consolidation value with AUC=0.720 (sec2.2); ingest-routing (RQ1-RQ4, 115 pages/4 domains): structured cost-framing prompt cuts cost-weighted routing error 25x (+58pp over GLM-4-flash zero-shot); rare FACT category collapses to F1=0.00 vs WIKI class F1=0.92 (RQ2, temporal-transfer test); closed-loop retraining-on-mistakes DEGRADES via self-reinforcing boundary drift (RQ4, explicitly negative result); schema-constrained ingest improves Schema Compliance Score 23-33% in 3 of 4 domains but -2.4% (p=0.200, not significant) in the 4th where the schema was auto-induced; WikiHealth's 6-injection adversarial test finds citation-removal goes UNDETECTED in both tested wikis (explicitly reported blind spot).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The wiki-vs-RAG citation-recall study (0.242 vs 0.095, sec2.4) is direct measured evidence that a maintained, structured Markdown knowledge base beats raw-chunk retrieval on cross-document synthesis queries -- the closest external validation in this wave for MF's Tier-1-docs-as-compiled-truth premise.

The paper repeatedly foregrounds NEGATIVE findings as first-class results (RQ4's self-reinforcing boundary drift from naive closed-loop retraining; WikiHealth's undetected citation-removal blind spot, sec8.5) -- exactly the honestly-documented-failure discipline MF's NEGATIVO anchor targets, offering a template for how to report what did NOT work.

Sec3.3's domain-calibrated half-life staleness scoring (freshness priors differ for lecture content vs other types) and sec3.4's provenance/audit-trail lifecycle stage are concrete, measured mechanisms for exactly the staleness/provenance concerns MF's FIDELIDAD anchor covers.

The CLS-Wiki study explicitly models episodic-to-semantic consolidation as a LEARNED importance-gating function (outcome-surprise AUC=0.720, sec2.2), grounded in Complementary Learning Systems theory -- a concrete, measured mechanism for MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion, going beyond ad-hoc summarization.
