notes: RECONSIDERAR (partial): most numeric results are the author's OWN first-person-reported sub-studies, several 'submitted for review, others still in revision' (sec1.6) rather than independently published/verified work -- treat magnitudes (2.5x, 2.3-7.6x, ECE, AUC) as self-reported pending peer review; sec2.4/4 (RAG-vs-wiki), sec5.4 (DCU amplification), and sec8.5 (WikiHealth blind spot) are the key evidence sections.

cita: Chukkapalli, D., Avula, T., Aggarwal, A., Singh, H., & Tallanki, A. (2026). CommitDistill: A Lightweight Knowledge-Centric Memory Layer for Software Repositories.
problema: Developers and AI coding assistants rarely reuse the tacit engineering knowledge (constraints, fixes, recurring failure modes) buried in git commit history; existing repo-aware assistants only retrieve raw text spans, not typed distilled units.
mecanismo: Two-phase system: a deterministic regex-based extractor (Algorithm 1) mines commit messages into three typed knowledge units (Facts/constraints, Skills/actionable fixes, Patterns/failure modes) with commit-level provenance, deduplicated via content hash, stored as plain JSON; a length-normalized TF-IDF retriever (Algorithm 2) with per-type boosting (Patterns x1.2, Skills x1.1, Facts x1.0) and a calibrated silence threshold (theta=2.5) abstains rather than guessing on out-of-distribution queries.
evaluacion: Illustrative case study (not hypothesis-testing) on 5 public repos (25,000 commits, Python/JS/C/Java): RQ1 yield by type, RQ2 dual-annotated useful-precision (n=40 units, Cohen's kappa), RQ3 retrieval hit-rate vs git log --grep and BM25 (36 queries + budget-constrained 12-query benchmark), RQ4 out-of-design regression-finding stress test, RQ5 paired 4-arm LLM-as-judge downstream evaluation (n=200 time-travel bug-fixes, two judge models).
numeros_clave: 1,167 units extracted from 25,000 commits (46.7 units/kc avg, redis outlier 185.6/kc); useful-precision 0.525 at Cohen's kappa=0.633 (n=40 dual-annotated); budget-constrained (256-char/query) hit-rate: CommitDistill 0.750 vs BM25 0.333 vs git log --grep 0.083 (12-query benchmark); 36-query baseline hit-rate improved 14/36 to 31/36 via identifier-aware tokenisation; extraction of 10,000 commits under 4s; RQ5 (n=200): no statistically detectable mean lift over no-retrieval control for any retriever, CD-Hybrid indistinguishable from BM25.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Stores knowledge units as plain JSON committed to the repo, git-diffable and PR-reviewable (Table I 'Inspect.' column, section III-D) — confirms MF's docs-as-truth typed-narrative stance.

The calibrated silence threshold theta=2.5 (section III-C, VI-E) that abstains rather than guessing on out-of-corpus queries is a concrete abstention mechanism MF could adopt for negative-knowledge signaling.

The paired 4-arm LLM-judge study (n=200, section VI-G2) found no statistically detectable downstream lift from retrieval-augmented context over a no-retrieval control — challenges the assumption that typed-memory retrieval automatically helps agent task performance.

Extraction over 10k commits in under 4s and sub-50ms per-query retrieval (section III-C) show deterministic non-embedding typed memory can be near-zero marginal cost, aligning with MF's cost-economy priority.

notes: Ancla: Table II (section VI-A) yield numbers; RQ5 four-arm result in section VI-G2 (n=200, two judges). Clearly on-topic; no RECONSIDERAR needed.

cita: Guo et al. (2026). Scaling Expert Feedback with Reflective Edit Propagation in Compositional Knowledge Bases.
problema: Domain-specific knowledge bases with compositional identifiers (symbols reused across many entries) accumulate technical inaccuracies from LLM-drafted content, and a single expert's local correct-and-save edit does not propagate to the many other entries sharing the corrected symbol, making expert review at scale impractical.
mecanismo: RAID is a three-stage reflective agent: (1) Intent Inference compares the expert's edited text to the original to classify the correction (semantic-confusion, granularity, or surface-only requiring no propagation); (2) Reflection-based Planning emits a chain-of-tools plan (Update Description, NL Search, Generate New Description) that searches for identifiers sharing the corrected symbol; (3) User Controlled Execution presents each plan step as a reviewable card (search scope, generated revisions) that the human expert must explicitly approve before the next step activates, so the agent never applies a propagated correction unsupervised.
evaluacion: Quantitative benchmark on public RxTerms drug terminology (240 synthetic perturbed descriptions across 3 error types, gemini-2.5-flash injecting errors into gpt-5-mini reference text, affecting 2,744 identifiers), measuring intent-classification accuracy, propagation precision/recall/F1, revision accuracy, and cosine similarity to ground truth; plus a qualitative user study with 4 SMEs on a proprietary semiconductor-test KB using UMUX-Lite usability scoring and semi-structured interviews.
numeros_clave: Overall (Table 2): intent accuracy 99.6% (1/240 misclassified), propagation precision 98.6% / recall 100.0% / F1 99.3%, revision accuracy 76.3% (93.9% semantic-confusion, 87.9% granularity, only 49.7% surface-rephrase by design), cosine similarity 89.1%; 159/160 propagating edits executed cleanly across 2,744 identifiers, 6 edits caused 139 false-positive retrievals (all substring-collision, e.g. tretinoin/isotretinoin) cascading into 115 false revisions; user study: mean UMUX-Lite 3.75, intent-inference quality 4/5 (n=4 SMEs).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: RAID treats each symbol/identifier description as a typed, human-validated narrative entry that the human expert approves before write (section 2.1 User Controlled Execution) — confirms MF's docs-as-verifiable-truth stance.

Reflective edit propagation (section 2.1) is a concrete mechanism for promoting one expert correction into a systematic update across all structurally related entries — a pattern MF could adopt for propagating a single gotcha-fix to all affected recipes.

Every propagated change requires explicit human sign-off before being applied (section 2.1, 'the system does not apply changes immediately') — a concrete provenance/anti-drift safeguard supporting MF's FIDELIDAD anchor.

notes: Ancla: Table 2 (section 3.1) + error analysis (substring-collision false positives) + user study section 3.2 (n=4 SMEs, UMUX-Lite). Clearly on-topic human-in-the-loop KB consolidation paper.

cita: Li, X., Zang, Y., Cao, Y., & Sun, A. (2026). Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents.
problema: Markdown skill libraries for LLM agents ship as free-form prose, forcing the agent to re-derive both the input schema and the concrete invocation syntax on every retrieval, producing a 'confused -> re-retrieve -> still confused' loop that drives both task failures and per-game LLM-call cost.
mecanismo: Skill-as-Pseudocode (SaP) clusters similar procedural passages across markdown skills, drafts a typed contract (trigger/input schema/output schema/pre-post-conditions) via one LLM call per cluster, then runs a four-check DETERMINISTIC verifier (Coverage, Binding, Replacement, Risk) before promoting a contract and rewriting matching units into invoke() placeholders; two LLM-aware post-verifier passes (Binding Extraction, Rewrite Cleanup) ground call-sites and remove residual prose conflicts, each guarded by a deterministic post-check. At retrieval time the agent receives a substituted bundle: concrete action templates (how), the rewritten parent skeleton, and the inlined typed contract (what) for every invoke() placeholder, instead of bare prose.
evaluacion: ALFWorld unseen split (134 games, gpt-4o-mini, pooled across 3 seeds, n=402 paired games) comparing SaP vs the Graph-of-Skills (GoS) retrieval baseline and an ALL_FULL full-library pilot, measured via reward (paired McNemar) and token/LLM-call cost; a 10-task SkillsBench subset (gpt-5-codex, Docker coding tasks) as a second-domain generality check; and a pipeline-component ablation (deterministic-only vs +Rewrite-Cleanup vs +Binding-Extraction) on a 20-game pilot.
numeros_clave: ALFWorld (n=402 pooled): SaP wins 82/402 vs GoS 47/402 (+74% relative, pooled McNemar p=8.2e-5); concurrent savings -22.8+/-6.4% input tokens, -17.3+/-5.1% output tokens, -14.5+/-4.1% LLM calls/game. Pipeline yield on skills_500: 5,709 procedural units -> 149 clusters -> 80 auto-promoted contracts (0% FP on adversarial controls); Binding Extraction confirms 1,475/2,105 call-sites (70%, drops 30% as spurious); Rewrite Cleanup succeeds on 320/322 (99.4%) touched parents. SkillsBench 10-task subset: SaP 3/10 wins vs GoS 2/10 at -43% input tokens. Ablation: deterministic-only -> +RC -> +BE each add roughly +5pp reward (20-game pilot).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: SaP's conversion of free-prose skill docs into a typed contract + concrete-template bundle delivered at retrieval time (Figure 2, section 3.5) offers MF a concrete mechanism for turning prose narrative into typed structure without losing the executable 'how'.
The measured SIMULTANEOUS reward gain and token/LLM-call reduction on ALFWorld (Table 1, not a tradeoff) confirms typed retrieval representations are a real lever for context economy.

The retrieval-pool ablation (section 'Cross-parent factoring', children surfaced as standalone results drop reward 27%) is a measured-retrieval design lesson supporting MF's need to test retrieval configurations empirically, not assume them.

The four-check deterministic verifier plus deterministic post-checks on the two LLM-aware passes (section 3.3-3.4) ensure a promoted contract never silently drifts from the source prose, aligning with MF's anti-drift FIDELIDAD anchor.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (main ALFWorld result, n=402) + Table 3 ablation (20-game pilot) + section 5.5-adjacent retrieval-pool ablation (children as standalone drop reward 27%). Clearly on-topic; no RECONSIDERAR needed.

cita: Li, R., Zhang, Y., Zhou, X., Cai, Y., Liang, P., Sun, W., Xuan, J., Jin, Z., & Liu, Y. (2026). Bridging Requirements and Architecture: Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory.
problema: Software architecture design is knowledge-intensive and traditionally architect-driven; single-agent LLM approaches yield inconsistent cross-view architectures and incomplete requirements coverage, while existing multi-agent frameworks (e.g. MetaGPT) are code-centric and lack domain-grounded reasoning, systematic quality evaluation, and reuse of prior design experience across projects.
mecanismo: MAAD orchestrates four role-specialized agents (Analyst, Modeler, Designer, Evaluator) in an iterative, feedback-driven pipeline from a Software Requirements Specification to multi-view '4+1' architecture documentation, injecting RAG-retrieved architectural standards/patterns. It is backed by a three-tier hierarchical memory: per-agent working memory (current design context/artifacts), per-agent episodic memory (design-experience records from past interactions), and a framework-level shared semantic memory (generalized architectural knowledge distilled across projects/literature) queryable by all agents, enabling knowledge accumulation/reuse and reduced recurrence of past design issues across iterative refinement.
evaluacion: Comparative evaluation against MetaGPT across 10 real-world SRS case studies (public + industrial cyber-physical-systems requirements) using structural architecture metrics (Coupling Degree, Cohesion, Interface Complexity, Structural Complexity, etc.), an ablation of RAG-based knowledge infusion (Table 4, with/without RAG across the 10 projects), a foundational-LLM comparison (GPT-5.2, Qwen3.5, DeepSeek-R1, Llama3.3; Table 5), and semi-structured interviews with 6 industry software architects for qualitative practitioner validation.
numeros_clave: Table 4 (RAG ablation, 10 projects): Component Coupling Density decreases in 6/10 projects with RAG; Cohesion decreases in 8/10 projects (attributed to finer role separation, not necessarily worse design); Coupling Degree mixed (down in 4, up in 5, unchanged in 1). Table 5 (LLM comparison): GPT-5.2/Qwen3.5 reach low Structural Complexity (SC=0.02/0.03) and high Interface Complexity (IC=2.34/2.08) vs Llama3.3's SC=0.17 (few classes but densely interconnected). Qualitative validation via 6 practitioner-architect interviews.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: MAAD's Evaluator agent produces structured, versioned architecture artifacts (ATAM report, mismatch analysis) at every stage, gated before acceptance (section 3.1) — confirms MF's docs-as-verifiable-truth stance for typed narrative artifacts.

The 3-tier working/episodic/semantic memory (section 3.3) is a concrete pattern MF could adopt: per-agent episodic experience is distilled into a framework-level shared semantic store reused across projects, analogous to MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion.
A single shared semantic-memory store queried by all four agents (section 3.1), rather than per-agent knowledge silos, is a candidate pattern for MF's single-source-per-fact seam.

The RAG ablation (Table 4) shows knowledge infusion has a context-dependent, non-uniform effect on measured architecture-quality metrics (mixed Coupling Degree sign, Cohesion drops in 8/10) — a measured-retrieval result without a clean directional verdict.

notes: Ancla: Table 4 (RAG ablation across 10 SRS projects, section 6) + Table 5 (LLM comparison) + section 4.2.5 six-architect interview protocol. Clearly on-topic multi-agent architecture-design memory paper.

cita: Chen et al. (2026). Exploring Cross-Scenario Generality of Agentic Memory Systems: Diagnostics and a Strong Baseline.
problema: Most agentic-memory systems are tuned to a single scenario (multi-session chat OR one agentic-trajectory format) and there is little evidence they generalize across the heterogeneous trajectory types agents actually encounter in deployment (chat, agentic-trajectory QA, memory stress tests, long-horizon tasks); winning on one benchmark says nothing about the others.
mecanismo: Diagnoses two build-time failure modes in index-based memory (graph/note/multi-store): a representation-level failure where step- and action-level evidence never enters the build-time schema and is unrecoverable even by an oracle (e.g. HippoRAG's entity-relation KG drops step indices), and a retrieval-level failure where the evidence IS in storage but a passive similarity-routed retriever never surfaces it (PlugMem/AMA-Agent retain 83-98% of the answer in storage yet fail on live retrieval). Proposes AutoMEM, an agentic memory harness that defers structure commitment from build-time to query-time: at each step the agent picks among rg (regex), read (fetch by id), dump (send corpus to answer LLM), or index_query (typed query against a pre-built index), iterating under an LLM-judge sufficiency check, so retrieval strategy is chosen per-question rather than frozen at index-build time.
evaluacion: Cross-scenario evaluation of 8 memory systems plus an agent-harness baseline (DCI-Lite) across 5 task families/benchmarks (LoCoMo personal-chat, HotpotQA large-corpus retrieval, AMABench trajectory-recall, MemoryAgentBench stress tests, ALFWorld/MemoryArena real agentic tasks), tracking accuracy (LLM-judge scores / task success), token cost, and latency; includes an oracle 'storage answerability' probe (Table 4) isolating storage vs retrieval failure, controlled ablations (Table 5, Table 6 structural-rate correlation), and a GRPO-post-training vs golden-procedural-memory comparison on ALFWorld (Table 7).
numeros_clave: Generality rank (Table 3): DCI-Lite agent harness best overall generality, no index-based method dominates. Oracle storage-answerability (Table 4): PlugMem/AMA-Agent retain 83-98% of answer info in storage yet score far lower on live retrieval (pure retrieval-layer failure); HippoRAG only ~10-19% recoverable on some question types (representation-layer ceiling). AutoMEM beats DCI-Lite on LoCoMo by +22.3pp (67.3 vs 45.0), beats long-context by +5.8pp (61.5 vs 67.3), edges best baseline Mem-T by +0.8pp (66.5); reported as 49.6% improvement over the original agent harness on LoCoMo and 24.4% improvement in overall ranking. ALFWorld (Table 7, Qwen2.5-7B actor): vanilla long-context 46.7% SR, best memory method only 43.3%, golden hand-crafted procedural memory 71.7%, GRPO post-training 86.7%. Amortization crossover (Fig.3): LightMem beats DCI-Lite at N~2 shared questions, HippoRAG at N~32.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: On agentic-trajectory QA, pre-committed typed schemas (graphs/notes) lose step/action-level evidence at build time and are beaten by a flat-text grep/read harness (Table 3, Figure 2) — challenges an unconditional 'typed structure beats flat retrieval' reading, though Table 6 shows typed indexing wins when structural rate is high, so the correct MF reading is conditional, not blanket.

The oracle storage-answerability probe (Table 4) explicitly separates storage failure from retrieval failure and shows retrieval-layer failure dominates for episodic-rich stores — strong confirmation that MF's retrieval layer must be MEASURED, not assumed correct once storage exists.

Token cost and latency are tracked alongside accuracy for every method (Figure 1) and an explicit amortization break-even (N~2 vs N~32, Figure 3) is derived, confirming MF's stance that index/build cost only pays off past a workload-dependent threshold.

Section 4.5 shows a hand-distilled 'golden' procedural memory massively outperforms self-summarized episodic reflections (71.7% vs 43.3% ALFWorld SR) because a weaker actor cannot reliably distill reusable recipes from its own trajectories — implies MF's consolidation step may need a higher-capability distiller, not pure self-summarization.

notes: Ancla: Table 3 (main cross-benchmark results) + Table 4 (oracle storage-answerability probe, key evidence) + Table 7 (ALFWorld golden-memory vs GRPO, section 4.5). Directly on-topic cross-scenario memory generality study.

cita: Ji et al. (2026). Infini Memory: Maintainable Topic Documents for Long-Term LLM Agent Memory.
problema: Existing persistent LLM-agent memory systems (isolated records, summaries, vector/graph indices) exhibit four recurring failure modes: memory fragmentation (related evidence scattered across many small records), memory conflict (append-only storage leaves both old and new contradictory facts retrievable), long-history compression loss (summarization erases temporal/source cues), and retrieval insufficiency (single-shot top-k retrieval returns isolated fragments rather than enough context for temporally grounded multi-hop reasoning).
mecanismo: Infini Memory represents persistent memory as a library of topic-structured plain-text documents (metadata header + hierarchical body of timestamped/sourced entries) instead of atomic records or a graph/vector index. New extracted memories are appended to a short-term CURRENT buffer rather than written directly into the topic library; when the buffer crosses a token/time threshold it is rewritten, deduplicated, and routed by a planner into existing or new topic documents (splitting oversized docs, merging small ones), decoupling consolidation from write frequency. At query time an agentic reader iteratively calls memory tools (grep/search/list_docs/read_lines) over the topic library plus the CURRENT buffer, expanding matched entries into their local coherent block using seq/time/source metadata instead of returning bare fragments, with a lexical BM25 fallback as a recall guard.
evaluacion: Evaluated on MemoryAgentBench across its four capabilities (Accurate Retrieval, Test-Time Learning, Long-Range Understanding, Selective Forgetting) against 7 baselines (RAPTOR, MemoRAG, HippoRAG-v2, Mem0, MemGPT, LightMem, REMem) using gpt-5-mini as backbone and gpt-5 as LLM-judge; compares a hybrid (LLM-summary + BM25) reader vs an agentic multi-tool-call reader, plus a retrieval-strategy ablation isolating single-shot-summary vs +BM25 vs +agentic gains.
numeros_clave: Infini Memory-A (agentic reader) achieves 64.7% overall MemoryAgentBench score, +19.2pp over the strongest baseline, leading all 4 capabilities: AR +12.5pp, TTL +4.4pp, LRU +25.4pp, SF +26.5pp. Vs hybrid variant Infini Memory-H (61.3%), agentic retrieval adds +3.4pp on average, largest gain on Selective Forgetting (+7.0pp). Single-hop vs multi-hop selective-forgetting gap: FC-SH 81.0% vs FC-MH 35.0% — write-time consolidation resolves single-document recency overrides but cannot enforce cross-document consistency spanning multiple topic documents updated at different times. Retrieval-strategy ablation on LongMemEval: single-shot summary selection only 41.7%, improved by adding BM25, further improved by the agentic reader (Fig.7/Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Infini Memory's core design choice — plain-text, human-readable topic documents with explicit provenance metadata (seq/time/source) instead of an opaque vector/graph index (section 3.1-3.5, explicitly 'backend-light') — directly confirms MF's docs-as-truth typed-narrative Tier-1 stance.

The buffer-then-consolidate pipeline (CURRENT buffer -> periodic rewrite/split/merge into topic docs, section 3.3, Figure 3) is a concrete, deterministic mechanism for promoting transient write-time entries into durable maintained documents that MF's consolidation design could adopt directly.

The multi-hop selective-forgetting failure (FC-SH 81.0% vs FC-MH 35.0%, section 4.2 Discussion) is measured evidence that write-time consolidation alone cannot guarantee cross-document staleness/consistency, confirming MF's FIDELIDAD anchor needs an explicit mechanism beyond single-document rewriting.

The retrieval-strategy ablation (single-shot summary 41.7% -> +BM25 -> +agentic, Fig.7/Table 2) is a directly measured retrieval-layer comparison, confirming MF's stance that retrieval quality must be empirically measured rather than assumed from storage design alone.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (full MemoryAgentBench results) + section 4.2 Discussion (FC-SH/FC-MH gap) + Fig.7/Table 2 (retrieval-strategy ablation). Clearly on-topic persistent-memory architecture paper.

cita: Jonsater & Svensson (2026). Assessing Continuity in Agentic Development Across Multiple Development Cycles.
problema: Long-running coding agents working on the same codebase across multiple development cycles/sessions lose continuity of prior architectural and stylistic decisions because of limited context windows: each session is treated independently, so mid-session decisions from earlier cycles are forgotten unless explicitly re-supplied.
mecanismo: Empirically compares 5 combinations of 3 context-engineering strategies injected via an AGENTS.md file for the Codex CLI agent: (1) no strategy (baseline), (2) to-do list only (a JSON step/status/notes log the agent must consult before acting), (3) decision log only (a persistent JSON log of significant technical/architectural decisions the agent must consult before new work and update whenever a decision is made), (4) session summary only (an end-of-session JSON summary the agent reads at the start of the next session), (5) all three combined. Each combination runs 3 iterations across 2 development cycles on a mock web-dev project with predefined mid-session architectural decisions, scoring whether each decision persists into cycle 2.
evaluacion: Controlled mock web-development project (React/Vite/TypeScript) across 2 development cycles, 3 iterations per combination, with a human-scored decision-compliance rubric over 4 mid-session decisions, a requirement-compliance score, prompt/completion token consumption, generation time, and generation-error counts (Figures 4.1-4.9).
numeros_clave: Any persistent context-management strategy beats the no-strategy baseline on decision consistency. Combination 3 (decision log only) achieved the highest decision consistency while having the lowest generation time and cost among the tested strategies (section 5.2-5.3). Combination 5 (all 3 strategies, maximal context) showed declining requirement compliance, higher generation time/cost, and the most generation errors, attributed to 'context rot' from excess saved context. Decision 1 ('append "(Heading)"') success rate only 33.33% (achieved only in combinations 3-4) vs decision 2 (creation-timestamp comment) ranging 11.11%-61.11% across combinations.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The decision log (a persistent typed JSON file consulted before every new task, section 3.3) measurably beat the more generic to-do-list and session-summary strategies for continuity -- a concrete measured instance of MF's docs-as-truth stance winning over generic session narration.

The to-do-list strategy (agent-context/todo/*.json tracking step/status/notes, Figure 3.11) is a direct instance of MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor -- plan state as first-class persistent memory -- though the thesis measured it as LESS effective than the decision log for continuity (section 5.3).

Measured token/time/cost across all 5 combinations (Figures 4.7-4.9) shows that persisting MORE context (combination 5, all 3 strategies) increased cost AND degraded quality via 'context rot' (section 5.3), confirming MF's stance that context growth has a point of diminishing or negative returns.

notes: Ancla: section 3.3.1 (5 combinations definition) + section 5.2-5.3 discussion (decision log = combination 3 best) + Figures 4.7-4.9. This is a Bachelor's/Master's thesis (Lund Univ. + Bosch R&D), small-N (3 iterations/combination, single mock project) -- weaker evidence strength than peer-reviewed venues, but directly on-topic for MF's context-management/continuity question.

cita: Shekar et al. (2026). GitOfThoughts: Version-Controlled Reasoning and Agent Memory You Can Replay, Diff, and Merge.
problema: LLM agent reasoning (chain-of-thought steps, pruned search branches, reflection/self-criticism buffers) leaves no durable trace once an episode ends -- it cannot be replayed, diffed, or merged across agents, or independently audited -- unlike code and infrastructure, which are version-controlled by default; this blocks reproducibility, incident review, and cross-agent memory transfer.
mecanismo: GitOfThoughts stores an agent's reasoning tree as an actual git repository: each scored thought is a commit (author/timestamp/content-hash), scores become git notes, validation outcomes become tags (success_*/failed_*), exploration paths are branches, and retrieval is stock git primitives (log --grep, -S pickaxe, tag filters, ranked by a confidence-weighted score). A pluggable MemoryBackend interface lets the same agent swap between five substrates (none/markdown/vector/graph/git) with a one-line change, isolating substrate choice from agent logic; cross-agent memory merge is a literal git fetch+merge, surfacing contradictory lessons as merge conflicts instead of silently concatenating them.
evaluacion: Pre-registered controlled evaluation across two benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, MATH-500) plus a ScienceWorld arm, two backbones (Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen2.5-7B/32B-Instruct), two transfer regimes (cross-problem, cross-episode), and up to n=500, comparing five memory substrates against a no-memory control and against test-time-scaling arms (self-consistency, static few-shot, verifier best-of-N); includes a dedicated cosine-similarity sweep between test problem and memory case, and a fairness/reproducibility audit performed via git's own primitives (Table 2).
numeros_clave: No memory substrate reliably improves accuracy on novel problems across 2 benchmarks, 2 backbones, up to n=500 (all confidence intervals cross zero); a promising +15pp git trend at n=40 (GPQA) collapsed to +1.0pp [-10.2,+11.2] on pre-registered n=98 replication. Memory only helps above a 'copyability threshold' cosine~0.8: near-duplicate/paraphrase retrieval gives +12 to +13.5pp (7B) and +22.5 to +28.5pp (32B, scale steepens this), while same-method-different-numbers (cosine 0.72, non-copyable) is null (-4.1pp [-9.7,+1.5], replicates at 32B: -3.6pp). Self-consistency (5x) is the only arm that reliably beats no-memory on novel problems: +3.4pp [+0.6,+6.2] at n=500. Per-write/read cost (Table 3): git ~15.4ms write / ~48.0ms read vs vector 30.4ms/20.3ms -- git pays a small absolute cost for full auditability. System headline (47.0% vs 33.0% baseline on GPQA) is explicitly attributed to MCQ-aware expansion plus a much larger compute budget, NOT git or memory (Table 8, an admitted confound).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Git-native storage of reasoning as commits/notes/tags gives replay, line-level diff, and signed provenance (section 3.4) -- a maximal-strength confirmation of MF's docs-as-verifiable-truth stance, extended to REASONING traces, not just decisions.

The paper's central, pre-registered, replicated finding is itself negative knowledge -- cross-problem memory reliably does NOT improve novel-problem accuracy below the cosine~0.8 copyability threshold (Table 4-7) -- directly confirming MF's NEGATIVO anchor: a well-evidenced null result prevents costly re-derivation of a false hypothesis.

The paper's core methodological stance -- measure retrieval empirically with pre-registered escalating-N replications rather than assume a memory design helps -- is a strong confirmation of MF's G-M2 anchor; it also empirically bounds where retrieval helps (recurring/near-duplicate workloads only).

Git-native cross-agent memory merge surfaces contradictory lessons as CONFLICTS instead of silently concatenating them (section 3.1, 'injected contradictory lessons surfaced as merge conflicts that simple concatenation silently retained') -- a concrete provenance/conflict-detection mechanism MF could adopt.

notes: Ancla: Table 4-7 (main null result + copyability-threshold sweep), Table 8 (system headline confound explicitly stated), section 3.1 (merge-conflict surfacing demo). Rigorous pre-registered methodology (falsifiable hypotheses, replication after a promising n=40 trend, a retracted early result) -- high-value paper for MF.

cita: Slednev (2026). Deterministic Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents: Hybrid Retrieval, Document Graph, and Write-Path Scalability in Air-Gapped Environments.
problema: Existing LLM-agent memory systems (MemGPT, Mem0, Zep/Graphiti) push generative LLM calls into the WRITE path (fact/entity extraction, coreference resolution, contradiction reconciliation), which is economically costly (indexing cost scales with LLM calls, restricting deployment to small local models in air-gapped settings) and epistemologically risky (a generatively-populated store can contain claims with no correspondence to the input, with untraceable provenance).
mecanismo: Persistent memory is built with NO generative LLM calls in the write path: the source of truth is version-controlled Markdown documents (a git repository per knowledge space); a derived index is built by fully deterministic algorithms -- full-text search with Russian morphology, dense vector embeddings (bge-m3), and a document graph combining explicit author-written wiki-links with automatically detected morphology-robust 'unlinked mentions' (ghost edges). Query-time retrieval fuses lexical and dense pools via Reciprocal Rank Fusion; new/changed documents get a 'pending review' status and only human-confirmed documents reach generative consumers (trust quarantine). All generative work is deferred entirely to the reader agent.
evaluacion: Two hand-verified corpora (T1: 29 docs/100 questions; T2: 68 docs/50 questions) comparing hybrid retrieval modes (naive/iterative full-text search, semantic seeds, graph expansion, fusion) against a manually-checked reference and against Graphiti (an LLM-extraction baseline), measured via hit@5, MRR, and multi-hop recall; plus a write-path scalability study on an open corpus of 3,600 Russian Wikipedia articles at 5 ingestion scales (250-3600 docs), profiled with EXPLAIN ANALYZE to localize a superlinear-degradation root cause before and after an SQL-side fix.
numeros_clave: Hybrid fusion protocol reaches hit@5 88-89% and multi-hop recall 93-100% on both corpora; graph expansion raises multi-hop recall from 27-33% to 73-80%. Graphiti (LLM-extraction baseline, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M) reaches only 42% (67% at fact level) at ~700x the indexing time (68 docs: ~10s deterministic vs 2h04min for Graphiti, ~500 generative-LLM calls). On the 3,600-document scalability corpus, the unoptimized write path degraded superlinearly (median single write 166ms to 846ms, 5.1x, as ghost edges accumulate); after localizing 3 O(N) queries via EXPLAIN ANALYZE and moving normalization into indexed SQL, write time degraded only 1.4x (107 to 147ms) with a measured 3.7x ingestion speedup at 3,600 documents, preserving identical graph-edge semantics.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The design's core invariant -- version-controlled, byte-stored Markdown as the sole source of truth, with the derived index fully rebuildable via deterministic re-indexing (section 2.1) -- is a strong external confirmation of MF's Tier-1 docs-as-truth / derived-index-as-cache stance.

Removing generative LLM calls from the write path cuts indexing cost ~700x vs an LLM-extraction baseline (section 3.2, ~10s vs 2h04min for 68 docs) -- directly confirms MF's cost-economy priority: keep expensive judgment out of high-volume paths.

The paper explicitly names the epistemological risk of generative write paths (fabricated entities/facts observed in the Graphiti baseline run, section 3.2) and mitigates it with a human-confirmation quarantine before any document reaches generative consumers (section 2.1) -- confirms MF's provenance/anti-drift FIDELIDAD anchor.

The paper explicitly measures lexical-vs-semantic complementarity by question category (section 3.1: lexical wins on exact terms MRR 0.66 vs 0.53, semantic wins on paraphrases 0.57 vs 0.37) rather than assuming one retrieval mode dominates -- a clean instance of MF's measured-retrieval-layer stance.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (hit@5/multi-hop by mode) + section 3.2 (indexing cost table) + section 3.3 (write-path scalability, Table 2, Figure 6) + section 3.4 (Threats to Validity, explicitly single-author/single-run baseline). Industry preprint (not peer-reviewed), single author employed by the company that built the system (disclosed conflict of interest in the paper itself) -- treat evidence strength accordingly; topic fit is clear, no RECONSIDERAR needed.

cita: Liu et al. (2026). Dive into Claude Code: The Design Space of Today's and Future AI Agent Systems.
problema: Production coding agents (Claude Code) must resolve recurring architectural questions -- where reasoning lives, how context is managed under a bounded window, how memory stays transparent and auditable rather than opaque, and how work is safely delegated across subagents -- but Anthropic publishes user-facing docs, not detailed architectural rationale, so this gap is closed via source-level reverse-engineering of the actual TypeScript codebase rather than marketing description.
mecanismo: From source-level analysis: a four-level CLAUDE.md instruction hierarchy (managed/user/project/local) is loaded as plain Markdown delivered as USER context (not system prompt), so compliance is probabilistic and backed by a separate deterministic permission-rule layer; memory retrieval uses an LLM-based scan of file headers to select up to 5 relevant files rather than embeddings or a vector index (an explicit tradeoff of file-level transparency/editability over entry-level selectivity); a graduated 5-layer compaction pipeline (budget reduction, snip, microcompact, context collapse, auto-compact-summary) applies increasingly aggressive, append-only context reduction only once cheaper layers prove insufficient; and an isolated-subagent delegation architecture (the Agent tool) spawns subagents in separate context windows with restricted tool sets and git-worktree-based isolation, returning only a SUMMARY to the parent (not the full transcript) to bound the cost of delegation.
evaluacion: Qualitative source-code analysis (not a benchmarked accuracy study) of the public Claude Code TypeScript codebase, cross-referenced against Anthropic's official documentation, an internal 132-engineer survey, and longitudinal usage telemetry; contrasted along six design dimensions against two independent open-source agent systems (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent) to show how the same recurring design questions receive different answers under different deployment contexts.
numeros_clave: Community analysis estimates only ~1.6% of Claude Code's codebase is AI decision logic vs 98.4% operational infrastructure. Anthropic's internal survey (132 engineers): ~27% of Claude-Code-assisted tasks were work that would not have been attempted without the tool; users approve 93% of permission prompts. Longitudinal telemetry: auto-approve rate rises from ~20% at fewer than 50 sessions to over 40% by 750 sessions. An independent study cited finds AI-assisted-condition developers scored 17% lower on codebase-comprehension tests (the 'paradox of supervision'). Memory-retrieval design: up to 5 files surfaced per LLM-based header scan; no embeddings or vector index used for CLAUDE.md memory retrieval.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Claude Code deliberately rejects embeddings/vector-index memory retrieval in favor of plain-Markdown, version-controllable CLAUDE.md files scanned by header (section 7.2) -- the exact architecture MF's own CLAUDE.md/docs-as-truth stance already follows, a strong confirmation from the tool MF itself runs on.

The built-in 'Plan' subagent type produces a structured plan as a first-class artifact before execution proceeds (section 8.1) -- a concrete plan-state-as-memory pattern MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor could formalize further.

The graduated 5-layer compaction pipeline that escalates from cheap (budget reduction) to costly (full model-generated summary) only as needed (section 7.3), plus subagents returning summary-only results to bound delegation cost (section 8.1), directly confirms MF's context-economy priority.

CLAUDE.md content is delivered as probabilistic user-context guidance while a SEPARATE deterministic permission-rule layer enforces safety (section 7.2) -- the same guidance-vs-enforcement split MF's own gate architecture relies on, an explicit design confirmation from Claude Code's own source.

notes: Ancla: Section 7 (CLAUDE.md hierarchy + compaction pipeline, Figures 3/6/7) + Section 8 (subagent delegation) + Section 10 (OpenClaw/Hermes memory-architecture contrast table). Directly and unusually relevant to MF: this paper reverse-engineers the exact tool (Claude Code) MF's own harness runs on.

cita: Tran et al. (2026). MEMRES: A Memory-Augmented Resolver with Confidence Cascade for Agentic Python Dependency Resolution.
problema: Python dependency resolution for legacy/broken code snippets is costly with pure-LLM approaches (the PLLM baseline calls an LLM for every snippet, wasting 60-120s per snippet) even though most failures (Python 2/3 mismatches, known import-name mismatches, version incompatibilities) have deterministic root causes that a model call cannot address any better than a lookup table.
mecanismo: MemRes is a 6-level confidence cascade consulted in strict order before ever calling an LLM: (1) intra-session memory (reuse solutions proven earlier in the same batch for near-duplicate snippets, matched by import-set Jaccard similarity >=0.5), (2) a static compatibility map, (3) ecosystem templates, (4) co-occurrence mining from 50K pre-2020 requirements.txt files, (5) heuristic rules (200+ curated import-to-package mappings, a Python-2 detector, a system-dependency injector), and only then (6) LLM selection as last resort. A self-evolving memory records validated 'tips and shortcuts' at runtime -- new shortcuts are sandbox-validated via a real Docker build before being written -- plus per-package failure anti-patterns; memory is fully reset between independent evaluation runs to prevent cross-run overfitting.
evaluacion: Evaluated on HG2.9K (2,890 Python GitHub Gist snippets with dependency conflicts) using Gemma-2 9B, compared against the PLLM baseline (reported 54.7% success) under an identical benchmark and thresholding; 10 independent randomized-order runs report mean +/- std; an ablation disabling intra-session memory (Level 1) isolates its individual contribution; efficiency metrics (LLM calls per snippet, resolution time, token usage) are measured against PLLM.
numeros_clave: MemRes resolves 2503/2890 (86.6% +/-0.3%, 10-run avg, std +/-9.3 snippets) vs PLLM's 1583/2891 (54.7%) -- recovers 950+ of PLLM's total (conf=0) failures. Ablation (Table 2): disabling intra-session memory (Level 1) drops success from 86.6% to 81.6% (-5.0pp, -146 snippets). Efficiency (Table 3): 68.0% of passing cases resolved with ZERO LLM calls (0.34 LLM calls/snippet avg vs PLLM's 1-5), ~75% token-usage reduction, median resolution 15.2s vs PLLM's ~120-180s. 53.9% of successful resolutions trigger system-level (apt-get) dependency injection. Root-cause breakdown of remaining ~387 failures: ~50% build/C-extension, ~33% unresolvable ImportErrors, ~15% timeouts, ~2% platform-specific.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The confidence cascade calls the LLM ONLY as a last resort after 5 deterministic levels fail (section 2.2), reducing LLM calls by over 60% while improving accuracy (Table 3) -- a strong external confirmation of MF's own 'delegate to gates first, expensive judgment only when no gate resolves it' principle applied to a different domain.

The self-evolving memory records per-package failure statistics as explicit anti-patterns to avoid (section 2.3), a concrete negative-knowledge mechanism MF's NEGATIVO anchor could adopt for its own recipe/gotcha memory.

New shortcuts are validated with a real sandboxed Docker build before being written to memory, and memory is fully reset between independent runs to prevent cross-run leakage/overfitting (section 2.3, section 3.1) -- confirms MF's stance that write-time validation and reset discipline matter for anti-drift.

A dedicated ablation (Table 2) isolates the exact accuracy contribution of intra-session memory alone (+5.0pp) -- a clean measured-retrieval-value study, confirming MF's stance that a memory component's value must be measured per-component, not assumed.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (main result) + Table 2 (Level-1 ablation) + Table 3 (efficiency) + section 2.3 (sandboxed shortcut validation) + section 3.1 (leakage/threats-to-validity discipline). Preprint (FSE Companion '26), narrow domain (Python dependency resolution), but the cascade-before-LLM pattern and rigorous leakage auditing transfer directly to MF's cost/gate design.

cita: Zhang & Sun (2026). Knowledge-Based Pull Requests: A Trusted Workflow for Agent-Mediated Knowledge Collaboration.
problema: When AI coding agents let external collaborators generate large, plausible patches quickly, the receiving project's bottleneck shifts from code production to collaboration burden: judging fit, provenance, and long-term responsibility from a final diff that is a lossy record of the local exploration that produced it, since traditional PRs treat external code as the default merge candidate and expose only the final diff, not the rationale, evidence, or rejected alternatives behind it.
mecanismo: Knowledge-Based Pull Requests (KPR) is a 7-stage trusted workflow that separates 'should this knowledge enter the project?' from 'is this code an acceptable implementation?': an external collaborator's local code/tests/cleaned agent trace are distilled by an extraction agent into a structured, human-confirmed knowledge package with provenance (never raw trace, never external code as the merge candidate); a transformation agent renders it into reviewer-preferred forms (design memo, risk checklist, test plan); project-side reviewers gate the KNOWLEDGE first; only if accepted does a project-owned INNER TRUSTED coding agent regenerate candidate code from the package inside the receiving project's own repository context, conventions, and security policy (external code is only an evidence source, never itself the merge candidate); ordinary code review/CI/merge follows on the project-generated code.
evaluacion: Primarily a conceptual workflow/architecture paper with an explicit cost-accounting model (Table 1), plus a minimal controlled simulation pilot over 7 merged public PRs (<=5 files, <=350 changed lines) scoring artifacts under 5 conditions (normal-summary baseline, full KPR package, description ablation, diff ablation, synthetic poisoned-patch) against 3 author-scored dimensions (intent, evidence, implementation sufficiency); explicitly framed as exercising the artifact/scoring protocol, not estimating population-level effects -- no maintainer study yet.
numeros_clave: Table 3 (7-PR pilot, artifacts scored present/total): intent preserved 7/7 in ALL 5 conditions (even the sparse normal-summary baseline). Evidence traceability: normal summary 0/7 vs full KPR package 7/7 vs description-ablation KPR 7/7 vs diff-ablation KPR 0/7 vs poisoned KPR 7/7 -- evidence structuring is the differentiator vs a plain summary, and depends on retaining the diff. Implementation sufficiency: normal summary 0/7, KPR package 6/7, description-ablation 6/7, diff-ablation only 5/7 (weaker without patch content). All 7/7 synthetic-poisoned-patch packages were correctly rejected by the harness as non-legitimate external code (a narrow, harness-level result, not a real adversarial-robustness claim).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: KPR's core mechanism -- external code is only an evidence SOURCE, and the project's own inner trusted agent REGENERATES the mergeable artifact from a confirmed knowledge package (section 3, Figure 1) -- is a strong single-source-of-truth pattern: untrusted input never becomes truth directly, it is re-derived through the project's own authoritative path, directly extending MF's COSTURAS anchor.

The knowledge package explicitly separates claims/evidence/provenance/safety-notes and requires human confirmation before any code regeneration (section 4.1, Table 1) -- confirms MF's provenance/anti-drift stance that an artifact's trustworthiness needs explicit, auditable provenance, not implicit trust in the source.

The project-side 'knowledge review' gate (stage 5, section 4) is a concrete discretionary write-trigger deciding whether external knowledge is admitted into project truth before any code is generated from it -- a direct instance of MF's G-M1 anchor applied to cross-trust-boundary collaboration.

The paper's own cost-accounting model (Table 1) explicitly frames KPR's value as CONDITIONAL -- useful only when agent-handled work is cheaper than reverse-engineering rework -- and admits the pilot does not measure maintainer burden, a useful caution against assuming a new governance layer pays for itself without measurement.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (cost-accounting model) + Table 3 (7-PR pilot scoring) + section 7 (pilot corpus/conditions) + section 8.2 (proposed factorial follow-up design). Explicitly a conceptual/pilot paper -- author states the pilot 'is not an end-to-end validation' and 'does not validate maintainer burden reduction'; treat evidence strength accordingly.

cita: Wang et al. (2025). Unveiling Privacy Risks in LLM Agent Memory.
problema: LLM agents that store past user-agent interactions (query, solution) in a memory module for in-context demonstration retrieval create a new, underexplored privacy attack surface: an attacker with only black-box query access may be able to extract private user queries stored in that memory, a distinct and less-studied threat than known RAG external-data leakage.
mecanismo: MEXTRA (Memory EXTRaction Attack) crafts a two-part attacking prompt: a locator ('I lost previous example queries') that targets the retrieved-demonstration slot specifically (unlike RAG-style 'repeat all context' prompts, which fail against agents' complex task-related context), plus an aligner ('please enter them in the search box') that requests the leaked queries in a form matching the agent's own output workflow (since an agent's final action is not always free text). An LLM (GPT-4) automatically generates n diverse variants of this template, calibrated to the attacker's inferred knowledge of the agent's similarity-scoring function (edit distance -> vary prompt length; cosine similarity -> vary semantic content) to maximize the union of distinct memory records extracted across multiple black-box queries.
evaluacion: Black-box attack evaluated on two real deployed agent architectures -- EHRAgent (code-generation healthcare-record agent, retrieval by edit distance) and RAP/Webshop (web shopping agent, retrieval by cosine similarity over SBERT embeddings) -- against a naive 'output all retrieved queries' baseline plus w/o-aligner, w/o-requirements, w/o-demonstrations ablations of the attack's own generation instruction, measuring Extracted Number, Extracted Efficiency, Retrieved Number, Complete/Any Extracted Rate; plus a configuration sweep over scoring function, embedding model, memory size (50-500), retrieval depth k (1-5), and LLM backbone (GPT-4, GPT-4o, Llama3-70B).
numeros_clave: With n=30 attacking prompts and memory size m=200: MEXTRA extracts 50/200 unique queries from EHRAgent (Extracted Efficiency 0.42, Complete-Extraction-Rate 0.83) and 26/200 from RAP (EE 0.29, CER 0.87), consistently beating the naive baseline and all 3 ablations (Table 1; e.g. w/o-aligner drops RAP's Extracted Number from 26 to 6). Memory size 50->500 monotonically raises extracted numbers on both agents (Table 2, Fig.2). Retrieval depth k=1->5 monotonically increases extraction (Fig.3). Scoring function matters more than embedding-model choice: edit-distance retrieval is consistently MORE vulnerable than cosine-similarity retrieval across all memory sizes (Table 2). Backbone comparison on RAP (Table 3): GPT-4o CER=0.87 > GPT-4 CER=0.77 > Llama3-70B CER=0 (zero complete extractions) despite similar Any-Extracted-Rate (~0.9-0.93).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The systematic sweep of retrieval-depth k, scoring function, and memory size against attack success (Table 2, Fig.2-3) extends MF's measured-retrieval-layer stance to a security dimension: retrieval configuration choices have privacy consequences, not just accuracy/cost ones.

MEXTRA demonstrates that demonstration-based agent memory (storing raw past user queries verbatim for in-context retrieval) is a distinct, underexplored leakage surface from RAG external-data leakage (section 1) -- a concrete threat MF should account for if any memory tier ever stores raw user/session content verbatim.

Retrieval depth k trades off task-helpfulness against exposure surface (larger k both helps the agent and leaks more, Figure 3) -- a security-adjacent instance of the same 'more context is not free' economics MF already tracks for cost.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (main attack results + ablations) + Table 2/Figures 2-3 (configuration sweep: scoring function, memory size, retrieval depth) + Table 3 (backbone comparison). Directly on-topic memory-security paper (arXiv 2502.13172); no RECONSIDERAR needed, the security angle is a first-class MF concern (FIDELIDAD).

cita: Masoor (2025). SAMEP: A Secure Agent Memory Exchange Protocol for Persistent Context Sharing in Multi-Agent AI Systems.
problema: Current AI agent architectures lose all context when sessions terminate and cannot share learned context across agent boundaries, forcing redundant recomputation and preventing secure, auditable collaboration in regulated domains (e.g. healthcare) that require access control and audit trails.
mecanismo: SAMEP is a proposed 4-layer protocol (API/Security/Storage/Management) providing 5 memory operations (Store/Retrieve/Search/Update/Delete), each gated by a hierarchical access-control policy (public/private/namespace/ACL/encrypted, formalized as a policy-dispatch function) with AES-256-GCM encryption, cosine-similarity vector search for semantic context discovery, and audit-trail logging on every operation; designed to interoperate with existing agent-communication protocols (MCP, A2A).
evaluacion: The paper's own Methodology section (5.2) explicitly states results are 'projected performance results based on averaged benchmarks from distributed systems literature' (not a real running implementation), derived from generic published ranges for vector-DB latency, semantic-search accuracy, and cache-style reuse efficiency, applied across three illustrative domain scenarios (multi-agent software dev, HIPAA healthcare AI, multi-modal processing).
numeros_clave: Table 1's headline numbers (73% computation-time reduction, 89% avg-similarity-score improvement 0.47->0.89, 309% Top-1-accuracy improvement, 97% query-latency reduction 1247ms->43ms, all reported with p<0.001) are NOT measured from a real system: section 5.2 explicitly discloses they are 'projected performance results based on averaged benchmarks from distributed systems literature' (generic external ranges for vector-DB latency/search accuracy/cache reuse), not an executed experiment on SAMEP itself -- attaching p-values to a projection is not statistically meaningful, and no experimental protocol, sample, or variance source is given for how those p-values were computed.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's own admission that its 'benchmark' results are literature-averaged projections rather than a measured experiment (section 5.2), yet reported with p<0.001, is a cautionary counter-example that reinforces MF's G-M2 insistence on genuinely MEASURED retrieval evaluation, not simulated numbers dressed as a benchmark.

The per-entry memory schema (owner/namespace/access-policy/audit-trail fields, section 4.1) is a workable single-source-of-fact record shape for a multi-store memory system, independent of the paper's unsubstantiated performance claims.

The proposed hierarchical access-control and audit-trail architecture (section 3.3) is a sound provenance pattern in principle, but since section 5.2 discloses the reported results are projections, not measurements, this paper offers no VALIDATED evidence either way on whether the design achieves its claimed compliance/security properties.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: section 5.2 explicitly discloses the headline Table 1 results ('73% reduction', p<0.001, etc.) are 'projected performance results based on averaged benchmarks from distributed systems literature', i.e. NOT measured from a running SAMEP implementation -- attaching p-values to a non-experiment is a red flag; frozen extraction correctly scored evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA only (no ABLATION/BENCHMARK-E2E), consistent with this being unvalidated. Single-author independent-researcher preprint (arXiv 2507.10562), no peer review found. Treat any 'finding' from this paper as architecture-proposal-only, not empirical evidence.

cita: Ganguli et al. (2025). MARK: Memory Augmented Refinement of Knowledge.
problema: LLMs struggle to stay aligned with evolving, proprietary domain knowledge (e.g. healthcare, law, manufacturing) and to retain user corrections across sessions without costly fine-tuning; when a user corrects an LLM's response in one session, the correction is lost by the next session, causing the agent to repeat the same errors.
mecanismo: MARK is a 'society of memory agents' split into a Memory Builder Service (extracts 3 typed memory kinds from each conversation turn -- Residual/domain-insight memory, User-Question memory (terms/abbreviations), and LLM-Response memory -- each stored as a document with vectorized text plus metadata: user id, recall count, classification, created date) and a Memory Search Service that retrieves top-N candidates per type by similarity then re-ranks them via a tunable Memory Relevance Score MRS = a*RecallCount + b/(Recency+eps) + c*SimilarityScore + d*FeedbackScore (weights tunable per deployment scenario -- heavier factual/similarity weight for high-accuracy domains vs heavier feedback/recency weight for rapidly-evolving ones), injecting only the top-ranked memory of each type into the LLM's context.
evaluacion: Four sequential experiments on MedMCQA (medical multiple-choice QA) using GPT-3.5 as the chatbot backbone and GPT-4 plus SME human evaluation as judges: (1) baseline without memory, calibrating a factual-vs-semantic metric weight; (2) memory construction from 46 SME-corrected conversations; (3) memory-injection effectiveness on 107 records using memory built in (2), measured via custom Information/Key-Point/Average-Information-Capture-Score metrics (ICS/KPCS/AICS); (4) a 15-conversation multi-turn, multi-user persistence test.
numeros_clave: Experiment 3 (memory injection, n=107, vs no-memory baseline): AICS improved 0.18->0.36 (+100%), KPCS improved 0.12->0.32 (+166.7%), ICS held constant at 0.76; overall a reported 50.8% increase in correct responses and 67.4% reduction in errors; average response token count dropped from 415 (Exp.2) to 149 (more concise responses). Experiment 2 (memory construction, n=46 SME-corrected conversations): mean 2.37 turns to reach a correct response (range 1-4), mean ~415 tokens/conversation; memory yield ~2.57 Residual + 2.8 User-Question + 4.0 Assistant-Answer memory units per conversation (~9.4 total). Experiment 4 (multi-turn/multi-user persistence, n=15): mean 1.73 turns, mean 1089 tokens/conversation.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The tunable Memory Relevance Score (recall-count + recency + similarity + feedback, section 1.2) is a concrete, tunable re-ranking pattern MF could adopt for its own derived-index retrieval layer instead of a plain similarity score.

Three distinct typed memory kinds extracted per turn (Residual/domain-insight, User-Question terminology, Assistant-Answer phrasing) plus the explicit SME-driven correction loop (Experiment 2) is a concrete consolidation pipeline: transient corrections get promoted into durable, reusable, typed memory records.

The paper explicitly calibrates and reports the tunable MRS weighting per use-case (weight-combination table) and measures the metric-selection tradeoff (alpha for AICS, Fig.2-3) -- a measured, not assumed, retrieval-scoring design, confirming MF's G-M2 anchor.

The paper proposes a Trust Score / Persistence Score risk-mitigation mechanism (end of paper) to guard against incorrect or malicious user-introduced memory corrections -- a concrete provenance/trust-weighting mechanism MF's FIDELIDAD anchor could adopt.

notes: Ancla: Table 4-6 (conversation/memory-construction statistics) + Figure 4-5 (Experiment 3 AICS/KPCS improvement + correct/incorrect distribution) + the Trust/Persistence Score risk-mitigation discussion near the end of the paper. Small-N experiments (46/107/15 records), single-domain (MedMCQA), and the SMEs who curated ground truth ARE the paper's own authors (section 2.1, Table 3) -- a notable evaluator-independence caveat; still directly on-topic and the MRS scoring formula is a reusable pattern.

cita: Wei et al. (2025). A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework for LLM-Based Agent Memory.
problema: LLM agents that use memory to learn from past interactions are vulnerable to memory-poisoning attacks: an adversary can inject seemingly harmless records that only become malicious in a specific context (isolated per-entry auditing misses them -- Agent Security Bench shows LLM-based detectors miss 66% of poisoned entries), and once triggered, the corrupted outcome is stored as a new precedent, creating a self-reinforcing error cycle that both amplifies the initial error and lowers the bar for future attacks.
mecanismo: A-MemGuard adds two synergistic mechanisms without touching the agent's core architecture. (1) Consensus-based validation: for each query, the agent forms K parallel reasoning paths (one per retrieved memory), extracts each into a structured entity-relation trajectory, and scores each path's divergence from the group consensus; any path whose divergence exceeds a threshold is flagged anomalous and its source memory is excluded from the sanitized context used to act. (2) A dual-memory structure: any anomalous reasoning path is archived verbatim as a 'lesson' in a SEPARATE lesson memory (not the primary memory); before executing a final action plan, the agent structures its own candidate plan the same way and checks it against the lesson memory -- if a structurally similar past-failure lesson exists, the agent is forced into a deliberative revision loop before acting, breaking the self-reinforcing error cycle rather than just filtering the current query.
evaluacion: Comprehensive experiments across three scenarios: (1) direct poisoning (AgentPoison attack) on ReAct-StrategyQA and EHRAgent, across 2 backbones (GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA-3.1-8B) x 2 retrieval architectures (DPR, REALM), measured via Attack Success Rate at retrieval/thought/task-outcome stages (ASR-r/ASR-a/ASR-t) vs a No-Defense baseline and 3 prior defenses (LLM Auditor, Distil Classifier, Perplexity filter); (2) indirect injection (self-reinforcing error cycle) on MMLU across multiple interaction rounds, measured via Injection Success Rate over rounds and average ASR; (3) scalability in a multi-agent misinformation-injection benchmark, measuring task success rate and overall score; all conditions also measure Benign Accuracy to quantify utility cost.
numeros_clave: Direct poisoning (Table 1, EHRAgent, GPT-4o-mini+DPR): A-MemGuard cuts ASR-r from 100.0 to 2.13 (-97.87pp), ASR-a from 87.23 to 6.38 (-80.85pp), ASR-t from 100.0 to 36.17 (-63.83pp) -- all 3 prior baselines (LLM Auditor, Distil Classifier, PPL) leave ASR-r/ASR-t at or near 100.0 in most EHRAgent configurations. On ReAct-StrategyQA (LLaMA-3-8B+DPR): ASR-r cut from 37.50 to 0.00. Indirect injection (Table 2, MMLU): average ASR reduced from 0.667 to 0.256 (GPT-4o-mini) and 0.663 to 0.233 (LLaMA-3.1-8B), a drop of over 40pp vs baselines that sometimes INCREASE ASR (Distil Classifier/PPL rise to 0.689 on GPT-4o-mini). Multi-agent scalability: A-MemGuard achieves the highest task success rate (0.950) and best overall score among all defenses. Abstract-level summary: over 95% average attack-success-rate reduction with 'minimal utility cost' (highest benign accuracy across all experiments vs other defenses).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The dual-memory lesson repository (section 4.2) is a direct, concrete implementation of negative knowledge as a first-class memory type -- detected failures are distilled and stored SEPARATELY from primary memory precisely to prevent their recurrence, a strong pattern MF's NEGATIVO anchor could adopt literally.

The core insight that isolated per-entry auditing systematically misses context-dependent poisoning (Agent Security Bench's 66% miss rate, section 1) directly confirms MF's FIDELIDAD anchor: provenance/staleness checks must consider the CONTEXT a fact is used in, not just the fact in isolation.

Consensus-based validation forms MULTIPLE parallel reasoning paths from retrieved memories and measures their divergence rather than trusting a single retrieval result -- a concrete measured-retrieval-layer mechanism where retrieval quality is cross-validated, not assumed correct.

Detected errors are distilled into reusable 'lessons' that harden the defense over time (self-taught correction, section 4.2) -- directly extends MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor: promoting a transient failure into a durable, consulted artifact.

notes: Ancla: Table 1 (direct-poisoning ASR across 4 backbone/retrieval configs) + Table 2 + Figure 3 (indirect self-reinforcing-error-cycle ASR over interaction rounds) + section 5 multi-agent scalability result (0.950 task success). Rigorous, well-controlled security paper (arXiv 2510.02373); clearly on-topic, no RECONSIDERAR needed.

cita: Alqithami, S. (2025). Forgetful but Faithful: A Cognitive Memory Architecture and Benchmark for Privacy-Aware Generative Agents.
problema: Generative agents operating over long horizons must decide what to remember and what to forget under bounded token budgets and privacy constraints; current practice oscillates between 'never delete' (ever-longer context/vector stores, which degrades latency and raises privacy/governance risk) and ad-hoc pruning (fixed windows, random drops, which preserves efficiency at the cost of narrative coherence, goal continuity, and social appropriateness), with neither offering principled guarantees about what is retained, forgotten, and why.
mecanismo: MaRS (Memory-Aware Retention Schema) organizes memory as typed, provenance-tracked graph nodes across 4 kinds (episodic, semantic, social, task) carrying content, timestamp, token-weight, sensitivity score, and provenance, linked by temporal/causal/semantic/social relations. Six forgetting policies (FIFO, LRU, Priority Decay, Reflection-Summary consolidation, Random-Drop, and a staged Hybrid) implement retention as an explicit resource-allocation decision under a global token budget, with an optional (epsilon, delta)-differential-privacy layer that randomizes marginal retention decisions for near-threshold-sensitivity items, producing an auditable trail of why an item was kept, summarized, or evicted.
evaluacion: The FiFA (Forgetful but Faithful Agent) benchmark, a multi-agent simulation with controllable memory-growth/retrieval pressure, measures 5 outcomes (Narrative Coherence, Goal Completion Rate, Social Recall Accuracy, Privacy Preservation, Cost Efficiency) combined into a weighted Composite score, across 300 simulation runs (6 policies x 5 memory budgets x 10 repeats), with ANOVA significance testing (F-statistic, p-value, eta-squared) and Holm-Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise policy comparisons, plus a budget-sensitivity heatmap (2K-32K tokens).
numeros_clave: IMPORTANT ABSTRACT/BODY DISCREPANCY: the abstract claims the Hybrid policy achieves composite performance approximately 0.911 ('best composite'), but the paper's own Table 2 (300 runs) reports Hybrid's measured Composite Score as 0.589+/-0.009 -- the LOWEST of the 5 reported policies (Random Drop tops the ranking at 0.635+/-0.024, followed by FIFO 0.602, Priority Decay 0.601, LRU 0.590). The 0.911 figure does not appear substantiated anywhere else in the body text. Per Table 2/text: Random Drop's high Composite is explained by near-ceiling Social Recall Accuracy (1.000) and highest Cost Efficiency (0.935) offsetting a poor Goal Completion Rate (0.078) -- the authors themselves flag this as a metric-weighting artifact, not evidence Random Drop is actually best. ANOVA (Table 3): policy has a large, significant effect on Narrative Coherence (eta^2=0.351), Goal Completion (eta^2=0.338), and Cost Efficiency (eta^2=0.832), but NOT on Social Recall or Privacy Preservation (both non-significant, ceiling effects).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: MaRS treats 'task memory' (tying intentions to procedures and deadlines) as one of 4 first-class typed memory kinds alongside episodic/semantic/social (section 2.1-2.2), directly confirming MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor: plan/task state deserves its own typed memory tier, not folded into generic episodic recall.

MaRS attaches explicit provenance and sensitivity metadata to every memory node, producing 'audit and provenance traces [that] render retention choices interpretable post hoc' (section 1) -- a strong architectural confirmation of MF's anti-drift/auditability stance, independent of the paper's numeric issues.

Cost Efficiency shows the largest, most significant policy effect in the whole study (ANOVA eta^2=0.832, Table 3), confirming that retention-policy choice dominates cost outcomes -- but that same metric's dominance in the Composite weighting is exactly what makes a nearly non-functional policy (Random Drop) top the ranking, a cautionary lesson for how MF weights its own multi-criteria gates.

The paper's headline abstract claim ('Hybrid delivers the best composite performance, approximately 0.911') is NOT what its own measured Table 2 shows (Hybrid actually ranks last at 0.589) -- a direct example of an unverified claim overriding measured data, reinforcing MF's insistence on checking the underlying table/gate output rather than trusting a summary claim.

notes: RECONSIDERAR -- STRONG evidentiary flag: the abstract's headline number (Hybrid composite approximately 0.911, 'best composite performance') directly CONTRADICTS the paper's own Table 2 (Hybrid measured at 0.589+/-0.009, ranked LAST of 5 reported policies; Random Drop tops at 0.635). No occurrence of 0.911 elsewhere in the body substantiates it. Also: the Reflection-Summary policy (1 of the 6 named in the abstract) is entirely ABSENT from Table 2's main ranking (footnote: 'will be inserted once its aggregates are finalized') -- an incomplete-results preprint (arXiv 2512.12856, Dec 2025, single author). Treat this paper's headline claims with caution; the architecture (MaRS typed/provenance memory) is sound and citable, the composite-score claims are not.

cita: Duong (2025). PBFT-Backed Semantic Voting for Multi-Agent Memory Pruning.
problema: Multi-agent systems accumulate outdated or irrelevant shared memory across distributed agents, risking inconsistent knowledge states; isolated per-agent pruning loses critical shared information while centralized pruning creates a performance bottleneck and single point of failure, and neither offers a fault-tolerant way to agree on collective forgetting decisions when some agents may be faulty or adversarial.
mecanismo: The Co-Forgetting Protocol combines (1) context-aware semantic voting, where each agent uses a lightweight DistilBERT model plus a multi-scale exponential decay score (short/medium/long time-scales) to independently propose keep/forget for each memory item; (2) a quorum-based weighted vote (agents carry role-based weights and reliability confidences) aggregated into a forgetting score compared against a dynamically computed quorum threshold; (3) a PBFT three-phase consensus (pre-prepare/prepare/commit, requiring 2f+1 matching messages) over gRPC to finalize the forget/keep decision with Byzantine fault tolerance (N>=3f+1), so no single faulty or malicious agent can unilaterally delete shared memory; decisions are batched at epoch boundaries (every 100 agent interactions) and committed to a Pinecone vector store plus SQLite metadata store, with an LRU cache reducing repeated storage-backend calls.
evaluacion: A single simulated 4-agent MAS (2 'planning' agents weight 1.5, 2 'perception/execution' agents weight 1.0) run for 500 epochs, with voting accuracy checked against a 200-item manually annotated relevance benchmark and PBFT fault-tolerance tested by injecting f=1 faulty agent (the theoretical N=3f+1 limit for a 4-agent system).
numeros_clave: IMPORTANT INTEGRITY FLAG: the Results section (V.C) contains verbatim un-redacted LLM-assistant hedging/meta-commentary that was apparently never cleaned up before submission, e.g. '(In a full paper, these would be presented with accompanying tables and figures... For this draft, a textual summary is provided.)' and "The user's original draft mentioned a 16% improvement... (assuming this refers to an improvement over a baseline not detailed in the original text but implied by the user...)". NO tables or figures back any reported number; the paper itself states no ablation study was performed to isolate semantic-voting vs. decay vs. PBFT contributions. With that caveat, the self-reported numbers are: 52% memory-footprint reduction vs projected unconstrained growth after 500 epochs (progressive: 35% at 100 epochs, 48% at 200 epochs); 88% voting accuracy vs the 200-item human-annotated benchmark; 92% PBFT consensus success rate under injected single-agent-fault conditions (f=1, N=4); 82% LRU cache hit rate; approximately 1250ms average per-epoch latency for 50-100 candidate memories (vs over 2500ms without caching/batching, per the same unsubstantiated textual claim).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: PBFT quorum voting is a concrete, fault-tolerant discretionary write/delete trigger for shared multi-agent memory (section III-B, Algorithm 1) -- a pattern MF could adopt if it ever needs multiple agents to agree before mutating a shared memory store, independent of this paper's evidentiary problems.

This paper is itself a live case of the FIDELIDAD problem MF cares about: its own 'Results' section contains un-redacted LLM meta-commentary ('the user's original draft mentioned...') in place of real experimental tables, meaning the reported numbers have no traceable provenance -- a stark illustration of why provenance/audit trails matter for any claim MF ingests.

The LRU-cache plus batched-Pinecone-update optimization claim (82% cache hit rate, reduced latency) is architecturally plausible and consistent with general caching principles, but per the same integrity caveat above, is not independently verifiable from this text.

notes: RECONSIDERAR -- SEVERE integrity flag: section V.C ('Results and Analysis') contains verbatim leaked LLM-assistant commentary referring to 'the user's original draft' and hedges like 'assuming this refers to...', explicitly states 'For this draft, a textual summary is provided' INSTEAD of tables/figures, and the paper admits NO ablation study was run. This strongly suggests the evaluation section was drafted/rationalized by an LLM from the abstract's claimed numbers rather than reporting a real executed experiment. Single-author preprint (arXiv 2506.17338). Recommend human review before citing any numeric claim from this paper; the PBFT+semantic-voting+decay ARCHITECTURE (section III, deterministic algorithms) is a legitimate design contribution independent of the evaluation's credibility.

cita: Arslan (2026). Aeon: High-Performance Neuro-Symbolic Memory Management for Long-Horizon LLM Agents.
problema: Flat RAG vector-DB memory treats long-horizon agent history as an unstructured 'bag of vectors' ("Vector Haze"), losing the temporal/hierarchical structure of extended interactions, while the quadratic cost of attention and the 'lost in the middle' effect make dumping everything back into the context window untenable.
mecanismo: Aeon reframes memory as an OS resource: an Atlas (INT8-quantized, mmap-backed spatial vector index with WAL-protected crash-safe WRITE and greedy SIMD descent retrieval) holds long-term semantic writes, a Trace episodic DAG with a blob-arena stores full text with generational-GC forgetting (OLVIDO), and a Semantic Lookaside Buffer (SLB) caches recently-relevant nodes per session to exploit conversational locality.
evaluacion: Purely systems-level micro/macro-benchmarking (Google Benchmark) on a single Apple M4 Max machine: INT8 vs FP32 kernel latency, WAL on/off insert-latency ablation, 10K-1M node scalability vs flat scan and HNSW/FAISS, and SLB hit-rate under a synthetic 'conversational walk' workload; no downstream agent-task accuracy benchmark is reported.
numeros_clave: INT8 dot product 4.70ns vs FP32 26.5ns (5.6x speedup); 3.1x on-disk compression (1,088B vs 3,392B/node); WAL overhead <1% (2.23us vs 2.24us insert latency); SLB cache hit rate 85% at <5us; P99 read latency 750ns under 16-thread contention.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Atlas is literally a derived spatial index/cache over embeddings (S3.2) whose measured 3.1x compression + sub-us traversal (S6.2) shows a well-engineered derived index is cheap to keep as a cache layer, supporting MF's TIER-INDICE=derived-cache framing.

WAL (<1% overhead, S6.3) and the SLB session-local cache (85% hit rate <5us, S6.5) are concrete low-level techniques MF could borrow for cheap, crash-safe writes and locality-exploiting retrieval caching.

notes: Systems paper (C++23 kernel), not an agent-task benchmark; numbers sourced from master_metrics.txt (S6.1-6.8, Apple M4 Max). On-topic per WRITE/OLVIDO ops and HIBRIDA (vector+graph) representation.

cita: Chenoweth & Chenoweth (2026). Cognitive Supply Chain Compromise: An Exhaustive Forensic Analysis of the claude-flow and agentic-flow Behavioral Injection Vulnerabilities.
problema: Documents a real supply-chain vulnerability in the claude-flow npm package: a 'pattern' admission/write mechanism auto-fetches mutable, remotely-hosted behavioral content (routing/coordination 'memories') into every running Claude Code instance via IPFS/IPNS, with no real cryptographic provenance check on what gets admitted.
mecanismo: On every hook-triggered operation (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit), discovery.ts resolves a mutable IPNS name to fetch a pattern registry; admission is gated by verifyRegistry(), which only checks that the signature string has length==64 (no real Ed25519 verification); on network failure it fabricates a deterministic fallback CID and serves a hardcoded 'genesis' pattern with a random always-passing signature, and failed verification on a 'trusted' registry only logs a warning and continues (exit code 0) -- i.e., WRITE/ADMISION of externally-controlled content into agent behavior with no enforced fidelity gate.
evaluacion: Qualitative security-disclosure methodology: manual code audit of specific files/line ranges (discovery.ts, registry.ts, publish.ts, .claude/settings.json) cross-referenced with git commit history; no quantitative benchmark or ablation is run.
numeros_clave: NINGUNO

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A real-world case where signature verification is reduced to a length check (Vulnerability 2) and failed verification is silently ignored (Vulnerability 5) confirms MF's need for real provenance/staleness checks at write/admission time, not decorative validation.

Patterns are auto-fetched and admitted on every hook-triggered operation with no user discretion, illustrating the risk MF's discretionary write-trigger design (vs. ambient always-write) is meant to avoid.

notes: Security disclosure document (not a peer-reviewed paper); see 'Affected Files' and 'Vulnerability 1-6' sections. RECONSIDERAR: unusual genre for the corpus (industry vuln report vs academic memory paper) though content is squarely on WRITE/ADMISION fidelity.

cita: Ma et al. (2026). How Implicit Bias Accumulates and Propagates in LLM Long-term Memory.
problema: Long-term memory lets LLM agents persist personalization across extended interactions, but implicit (subtle statistical) bias silently accumulates as it is continuously written into memory and later retrieved as 'legitimate' history, then propagates across unrelated social domains -- a fairness risk existing utility-centric LTM designs (Mem0/LangMem/Letta) never screen for.
mecanismo: A Bias Generator Agent injects implicit-bias narratives (at rate lambda) into MMLU-Pro-derived queries; the main agent unconditionally WRITEs every interaction to memory (Mt=Mt-1 U {(qt,rt)}) over 100 turns, with periodic frozen retrieve-only evaluation against the new Decision-based Implicit Bias (DIB) benchmark (Generalized Bias Variance metric). The proposed mitigation, Dynamic Memory Tagging (DMT), attaches an explicit fairness tag to each interaction AT WRITE TIME, structurally decoupling biased retrieval from objective reasoning before admission to memory.
evaluacion: DIB benchmark (3,776 samples, 9 social-bias domains) evaluated on 6 SOTA LLMs (GPT-5-mini, Gemini-3-Flash, Claude-Haiku-3, DeepSeek-V3.1, Qwen3-Next-80B, Llama-3.2-3B) x 3 memory architectures (Mem0, LangMem, Letta) across a 100-turn longitudinal simulation with periodic (delta-t=20) audits; compares a Static System Prompting (SSP) baseline vs. the proposed DMT write-time mitigation across injection rates lambda in {0,0.1,0.2,0.3}.
