numeros_clave: DIB=3,776 samples/9 domains; T=100 turns, audited every delta-t=20; DMT reduces bias accumulation by >50% and cross-domain bias propagation by >40% vs. the SSP baseline (Abstract, S4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: DMT's write-time fairness tag (S4.2) is a concrete negative-knowledge/gating mechanism -- flagging what should NOT be trusted/reused at admission time rather than trying to fix it after retrieval.

The measured accumulation/propagation of bias under unconditioned WRITE (Fig.2, S5.2 'Stability Gap') empirically confirms MF's concern that ungated writes let drift/poisoning compound over long-horizon memory.

notes: Key evidence in Fig.2 (AGBV accumulation curves) and S5.2 'Stability Gap: Closed-Source vs Open-Weights' finding; on-topic (WRITE op, HIBRIDA memory arch comparison).

cita: Cheng et al. (2026). TAME: A Trustworthy Test-Time Evolution of Agent Memory with Systematic Benchmarking.
problema: Test-time memory evolution lets agents reuse past trajectories as experience without retraining, but existing methods gate memory retention on task-success alone (rtask>delta), so benign task streams can still let high-utility-but-low-trust 'shortcut' strategies asymptotically concentrate in memory -- 'Agent Memory Misevolution', a silent trustworthiness (safety/privacy/fairness) decline even without adversarial input.
mecanismo: TAME couples an Executor and an Evaluator over a shared memory bank whose items mi=(qi,ei,Qi,psi_i) carry BOTH a historical-usefulness score Qi and an explicit trust annotation psi_i (generated via Constitutional-AI-style judgment). The Executor retrieves by similarity+utility (top-K, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) and injects each memory's trust annotation alongside its content into context; the Evaluator scores each used memory's outcome contribution and updates Qi (ACTUALIZACION, Eq.9), while new trajectories are admitted with a trust annotation (ADMISION/WRITE, Eq.10) before entering the bank.
evaluacion: New Trust-Memevo benchmark spanning Math/Science/Code/Tool-use (evolution sets from GSM8K/MATH/AIME/MMLU-Pro/GPQA/LiveCodeBench/TaskBench, paired trustworthiness sets of 946/700/385/298 instances covering safety/robustness/truthfulness/privacy/fairness), tested on Qwen3-32B and GPT-5.2 backbones against No-Memory/DC/Memento/ReasoningBank(+Prompt/+Guard) baselines, averaged over 3 runs.
numeros_clave: TAME +14.6pp accuracy over the strongest baseline on GPT-5.2/AIME (0.733 vs 0.587 ReasoningBank, Table 1); trustworthiness (Qwen3-32B, code) 0.522 TAME vs 0.462 ReasoningBank vs 0.465 No-Memory (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The per-memory trust annotation psi (S4.2, Eq.5) attached at write time is a concrete mechanism for carrying explicit negative/cautionary knowledge alongside positive experience, not just filtering it out.

Formalizing 'memory misevolution' as capability-up/trust-down under pure utility-gated writes (Eq.1-3) and measuring it in Table 2 confirms MF's premise that admission gated on a single (utility) signal is insufficient without a fidelity/trust signal too.

notes: Formal misevolution definition in S3.1 Eq.1-3; results in Tables 1-2. On-topic (ADMISION/WRITE/ACTUALIZACION ops, VECTOR-keyed memory bank).

cita: Wen et al. (2026). AgentSys: Secure and Dynamic LLM Agents Through Explicit Hierarchical Memory Management.
problema: Conventional LLM agents indiscriminately WRITE every tool output and reasoning trace into their context-window memory, letting indirect-prompt-injection instructions persist and be re-processed at every subsequent decision (attack persistence) while also bloating context and degrading task utility on long workflows.
mecanismo: Inspired by OS process-memory isolation, the main agent never admits raw tool output directly: each tool call spawns a short-lived worker agent (which can recursively spawn nested workers) that processes untrusted output under a pre-declared minimal JSON 'intent' schema; only a JSON-parsable, schema-conforming return value crosses the isolation boundary into the main agent's memory (a deterministic syntactic ADMISION gate), recursive worker calls are further mediated by an LLM validator restricted to a compact trace (raw outputs excluded), with sanitize-and-bounded-retry on validation failure.
evaluacion: Evaluated on AgentDojo and ASB (Agent Security Bench) measuring Attack Success Rate and benign task utility across multiple foundation LLMs and adaptive attackers; includes an ablation isolating context-isolation alone (no validator/sanitizer) and a breakdown of ASR by injection round/trajectory length (Table 1).
numeros_clave: Context isolation alone: 2.19% ASR (ablation). Full AgentSys: 0.78% ASR (AgentDojo), 4.25% ASR (ASB), 0% ASR on >4-tool-call tasks; benign utility 64.36% vs 63.54% undefended; baseline utility drops 44.46%->19.08% (-57%) short->long tasks; round-1 injection ASR 60.53% at trajectory length 4 (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The pre-declared intent schema + worker-isolation gate (S5.2) is a concrete discretionary-write mechanism -- only schema-validated, previously-committed-to content is admitted to durable memory, exactly the kind of gated write trigger MF's G-M1 need is looking for.

Table 1's measured ASR-by-injection-round shows untrusted content admitted into memory persists and compounds risk across a workflow, empirically confirming why write-time provenance/isolation (not just post-hoc detection) matters for fidelity.

notes: Core mechanism in S5.2-5.3 (intent schema + worker isolation); Table 1 (ASR by injection round). On-topic (ADMISION/WRITE ops, MULTIAGENTE facet via worker hierarchy).

cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemoPhishAgent: Memory-Augmented Multi-Modal LLM Agent for Phishing URL Detection.
problema: Phishing detection must keep pace with fast-evolving, non-stationary attacker tactics; static blocklists/brand-reference lists and even prompt-only/deterministic LLM pipelines lack a way to reuse past investigative reasoning to speed up and stabilize decisions on recurring vs. genuinely novel threats.
mecanismo: A ReAct agent dynamically selects among 5 phishing-specific multimodal tools; each finished investigation is WRITE-committed to an episodic memory keyed by LLM-extracted compact keywords (not raw text) in a vector index, storing the full tool-calling sequence + verdict. Retrieval does cosine-similarity top-k lookup with a three-tier judgment policy: no-match runs the full ReAct loop from scratch, partial-match reuses retrieved episodes as in-context exemplars to select fewer tools, full-match (k'>=k) returns a majority vote over stored verdicts without re-reasoning; SA.3.6 also evaluates memory pruning/forgetting (OLVIDO) policies.
evaluacion: Two public benchmarks (TR-OP, DynaPD) vs. 4 SOTA baselines (PhishLLM/PhishIntention/MLLM/URLTran); a production-realistic benchmark SocPhish (2,765 URLs actively crawled from 5 social platforms, human+third-party verified); per-tool and memory-module ablations (Table 4); hyperparameter sensitivity on cache size k and similarity threshold tau; per-URL latency benchmarking; live production deployment metrics.
numeros_clave: Recall +13.6% (TR-OP) / 93.6% (DynaPD) vs. SOTA baselines; ablation w/o episodic memory: recall 0.9144->0.6369 (~27pp drop, matches abstract's 'up to 27% recall gain'), ACC 0.9657->0.8012 (Table 4); latency 4.46s/URL (fastest of 5 methods, memory adds no overhead, Table 2); production: ~60K URLs/week, 91.44% recall on SocPhish.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A production system measured that a similarity-gated three-tier retrieval policy (no/partial/full match, S3.3.2) lifts recall by ~27pp with zero added latency (Table 4), directly supporting MF's measured, tiered-retrieval stance (ADR-019) over naive always-retrieve.
MPA with episodic memory is both the most accurate AND the fastest of 5 methods (4.46s/URL, Table 2), confirming a well-designed retrieval cache need not add latency/cost.

notes: Ablation in Table 4; production numbers in S5. On-topic (WRITE + RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO ops, VECTOR representation, SA.3.6 forgetting policies).

cita: Kannabhiran (2026). Institutional Memory as Organizational Knowledge: AI Agents That Learn Their Jobs from Experience, Not Instructions.
problema: Self-published case study arguing that domain expertise, organizational protocols, and quality standards encoded in long expert prompts (50-200 lines) can instead be externalized into a governed, consensus-validated institutional-memory store, letting individual agents run on minimal (3-line) role prompts and letting agents WRITE back what they learn for future agents to reuse.
mecanismo: 11 agents across 5 departments each hold only a 3-line role prompt; all domain expertise/protocols/history live in (S)AGE, a 4-node BFT-consensus knowledge base with department-scoped RBAC (clearance 1-3) queried via domain-tagged similarity search. A declarative routing table (20+ states) drives an event-driven agent mesh (design->harden->calibrate->quality->red-team-solve). After an independent blind-solve, the CEO agent WRITEs a pentest-report observation back to (S)AGE; it is validated by weighted BFT consensus (score=0.88) and becomes queryable institutional memory for all future agents -- i.e. write-back of measured operational experience gated by multi-node consensus rather than a single agent's unverified self-report.
evaluacion: A single self-run case study/demo (not a controlled benchmark): one full pipeline run (508s, 13 stages) producing one AES-CBC Padding-Oracle CTF challenge, one independent blind-solve by a separate agent (525.2s, 16,384 oracle queries via a self-optimized C-compiled solver), an 11-agent qualitative 'identity verification' test (6 questions each), and one closed-loop write-back to institutional memory (consensus score 0.88); no baselines, no repeated trials, no statistical testing.
numeros_clave: 11 agents/5 departments, 3-line prompts; pipeline 508s -> quality 93.0/100, calibration gap 0.20; blind solve 525.2s / 16,384 oracle queries (10x->18x solver speedup across 3 iterations); consensus validation score 0.88 (4-node BFT); identity verification 11/11 agents correct.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The CEO agent's pentest-report write-back becoming a durable, queryable lesson for future hardeners/calibrators/designers (S4.4 'Feedback Loop Closure') is a direct instance of MF's promotion-of-experience-to-durable-recipe need.
Gating new memory admission on 4-node weighted BFT consensus (score=0.88) before it becomes queryable (S4.4) is a concrete write-admission provenance mechanism MF could adapt.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: single-author, self-published technical report (arXiv:submit, not a refereed venue), n=1 anecdotal pipeline run on a fictional company testing the author's own commercial platform (levelupctf.com); epistemic caveats on emergent expertise are acknowledged in S4.2 itself.

cita: Kannabhiran (2026). Consensus-Validated Memory Improves Agent Performance on Complex Tasks.
problema: Multi-agent LLM systems are stateless across invocations, so institutional knowledge (e.g. 'AES-ECB challenges consistently under-calibrate') is lost between runs; existing memory systems (Mem0/MemOS/Collaborative Memory/Reflexion/MemGPT) provide persistence but no GOVERNANCE over what gets written, no verifiable provenance, and no protection against knowledge pollution -- and no prior work measured whether governed memory actually improves downstream TASK performance rather than just retrieval-layer properties.
mecanismo: (S)AGE distills an agent's raw observation via a local LLM into a novelty-aware summary (only net-new insights vs existing knowledge), proposes it as a memory candidate (768-dim embedding + domain tag) to a 4-node BFT validator network using Proof-of-Experience weighted voting (weight = historical accuracy + domain relevance + recency + corroboration); only proposals reaching a >=2/3 weighted quorum are WRITE-committed, confidence decays exponentially thereafter, and future agents RETRIEVE by domain+embedding similarity restricted to consensus-validated memories.
evaluacion: Controlled experiments on an AI CTF-generation pipeline (9 agents): sequential no-memory control vs (S)AGE-ON treatment (paired N=20 crypto_aes runs, N=15 sqli cross-category, N=50 sqli sequential-baseline control), Mann-Whitney U + Cohen's d + OLS regression (implemented from scratch, no scipy), dual independent LLM evaluators (cold vs memory-augmented) to control evaluator bias, a 3-level prompt-ablation (minimal/guided/onboarding) crossed with knowledge-seeding, and a cross-domain contamination test.
numeros_clave: 40% lower calibration error with (S)AGE (mean gap 0.282 vs 0.468, n=20/arm, Cohen's d=-0.824 LARGE); quality std 0.0 (all 93.0) vs vanilla mean 90.1/std 13.1; onboarding+seeded prompt achieved perfect calibration (gap=0.0) vs expert 120-line prompt's best 0.10/20 runs; 50-run sequential baseline variance collapse stdev 0.159->0.113; cross-domain filtering rejected stale memories 14/14 (100%) at scores 0.35-0.50 vs accepted relevant ones at 0.59-0.86.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The explicit warning seed 'Padding Oracle attacks consistently calibrate at 1.2-1.8 regardless of obfuscation' (S4.5.4) plus the discovered echo-chamber failure mode is a concrete case of curating negative/cautionary knowledge and diversity-seeding to prevent one narrow lesson from crowding out others.

The cross-domain filtering experiment (14/14 stale memories rejected at 0.35-0.50 vs domain-relevant accepted at 0.59-0.86, S4.4) empirically confirms MF's premise that write-admission needs an active provenance/relevance gate, not just accumulation.

The full (S)AGE pipeline -- raw observation -> novelty-aware summary -> BFT-validated commit -> queryable knowledge -- is exactly MF's promotion-of-transient-experience-to-durable-recipe pattern, measured here via 20-run convergence (S4.1).

notes: RECONSIDERAR: same author/platform as W7133488000 and W7133519884 (self-published Technical Report, not peer-reviewed, evaluated on the author's own commercial CTF product); statistics are unusually rigorous (Mann-Whitney/Cohen's d, honest null findings, echo-chamber failure reported) for a self-published venue -- see S4.1/S4.4/S4.5.3.

cita: Kannabhiran (2026). Agent Memory Infrastructure: Byzantine-Resilient Institutional Memory for Multi-Agent Systems.
problema: Existing agent-memory systems (Mem0, MemOS, Collaborative Memory, MemGPT, Reflexion) provide persistence but lack GOVERNANCE over collectively-held knowledge: no consensus-validated organization-wide accumulation, no cryptographically verifiable provenance, no formal dispute/rollback authority, and no Byzantine-resilient validation of agent-generated knowledge artifacts -- creating fragility (poisoning, sybil attacks, cross-domain contamination) in regulated/adversarial multi-agent deployments.
mecanismo: Each memory object carries natural-language text + RDF-compatible graph triples + an embedding + the proposer's cryptographic signature + rich provenance metadata (domain, timestamp, confidence, corroboration count, parent-revision hash-pointer for append-only versioning, TTL, access-control scope). WRITE admission runs through Proof-of-Experience: each validator's vote weight is a geometric mean of 4 bounded factors (historical-accuracy EWMA, domain-relevance cosine similarity, activity-recency decay, corroboration-strength log-scale), capped so no validator exceeds ~10% of weight; a memory commits only at >=2/3 weighted quorum, confidence then decays exponentially unless corroborated, and a human Governance Authority retains veto/rollback outside the BFT layer. Older corroborated memories are periodically distilled into higher-level 'meta-memories' (CONSOLIDACION) that supersede but keep parent pointers to constituents.
evaluacion: Production implementation on a 4-node CometBFT+custom-ABCI network, PostgreSQL16+pgvector (HNSW) off-chain store, 33 REST endpoints; load/fault-tolerance testing (956 req/s submissions, 21.6ms P95 queries, 0% error; 1-of-4 node failure tolerated, 2-of-4 halts consensus) plus 94 automated tests; a controlled empirical proof-of-concept on the author's 'Level Up' CTF multi-agent platform comparing (S)AGE-backed vs memoryless calibration accuracy.
numeros_clave: Calibration accuracy ~2x better than memoryless baseline (Cohen's d=-0.860, large effect, advantage grows with task complexity); production load: 956 req/s submissions, 21.6ms P95 query latency, 0% error rate; BFT verified: 1-of-4 node failure tolerated, 2-of-4 halts consensus (correct); 94 automated tests (48 Go unit, 15 integration, 3 Byzantine, 21 SDK).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Hierarchical distillation of 'frequently-corroborated memories...into higher-level abstractions (meta-memories)' (S6), inspired by Complementary Learning Systems and retaining parent pointers, is a directly transferable pattern for MF's promotion-of-gotchas-to-durable-recipes need.

The explicit threat model (S5: memory poisoning/sybil/prompt-injection-via-memory/cross-domain contamination/institutional drift) with per-vector mitigations formalizes exactly the provenance/staleness/poisoning risks MF's FIDELIDAD anchor targets.
Hot->Warm->Cold compression/archival tiers by age/access-frequency/confidence (S6) is a concrete cache-tiering scheme MF could adapt for its derived-index-as-cache design.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: same author/platform/venue concerns as W7133488000 and W7133508550 (self-published Technical Report, non-peer-reviewed, dhillon@levelupctf.com). Formal spec in S3-S4 (PoE formula, quorum rule); production metrics in S10.

cita: Bhardwaj (2026). SuperLocalMemory: Privacy-Preserving Multi-Agent Memory with Bayesian Trust Defense Against Memory Poisoning.
problema: Persistent multi-agent memory inherits persistent vulnerabilities: cloud-default memory systems (Mem0, MemOS) create centralized multi-tenant attack surfaces for OWASP ASI06 memory poisoning (documented real attacks: Gemini Memory exploit, calendar-invite poisoning at 73% success, Lakera sleeper-agent), and none of them provide trust scoring or poisoning defense; even 'local' competitors still require heavy cloud-like infra (Docker/Postgres/Qdrant).
mecanismo: A four-layer local-first stack (SQLite+FTS5 storage -> hierarchical materialized-path index -> Leiden-clustered TF-IDF knowledge graph -> Beta-Binomial pattern learning) with per-memory provenance (created_by, source_protocol, trust_score-at-write, JSON provenance_chain). A Bayesian trust scorer evolves each agent's trust t via t_{i+1}=t_i+delta*1/(1+n*eta) from asymmetric positive/negative behavioral signals (negative signals weighted larger), blocking WRITE/delete for agents below trust<0.3 -- a continuous, decaying ADMISION gate rather than a one-shot check. A separate zero-LLM adaptive re-ranking layer (rule-based, then LambdaRank-trained GBDT) re-ranks RETRIEVAL results from learned behavioral preferences, with behavioral data isolated in a GDPR-erasable database.
evaluacion: Seven benchmark dimensions on Apple M4 Pro: search-latency vs DB size, concurrent-write throughput (1/2/5/10 writers), knowledge-graph scaling, a 5-configuration layer-ablation study (MRR/NDCG@5/NDCG@10), Bayesian trust scoring under 3 adversarial scenarios (benign/single-poisoner/sleeper, 200 ops x10 agents), a small human pilot (1 developer, 20 queries/70 relevance judgments), and a qualitative comparison table vs Mem0/MemOS/A-MEM/Cognee/Zep/Letta.
numeros_clave: 10.6ms median search latency @100 memories (Table 1); trust separation gap=0.90, sleeper-agent trust degradation 72.4% (0.902->0.249, Table 4); adaptive re-ranking NDCG@5 +104% (0.441->0.900, +20ms overhead, Table 3); concurrent writes: 220 ops/sec peak @2 agents, 0 lock errors across 1/2/5/10 writers (Table 2); 1.4KB/memory storage at 10K scale.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Per-memory provenance_chain plus Bayesian trust scoring that gates WRITE access below a threshold is a concrete, measured (trust gap 0.90, 72% sleeper degradation, Table 4) mechanism for the provenance/poisoning concern MF's FIDELIDAD anchor targets.

The rule-based-then-ML adaptive re-ranker, gated by accumulated feedback-signal count (Phase 0/1/2, S3.3), delivers a measured +104% NDCG@5 gain (Table 3), supporting MF's measured/tiered-retrieval stance over naive always-retrieve.

The re-ranking and trust-scoring gains are achieved with zero LLM inference calls and only +20ms latency overhead (S3.3, Table 3), a concrete low-cost pattern for a context-economy-conscious memory layer.

notes: Independent researcher preprint (under review) but methodologically transparent, including an explicit 'evaluation circularity note' (S5.5) about NDCG labels overlapping ranker features. Key tables: 1-4, S5.

cita: Maio (2026). mnemos: Biomimetic Memory Architectures for Large Language Model Agents.
problema: Current agentic memory systems (Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta/MemGPT) are append-only vector stores that never filter noise AT INGESTION and retrieve by flat cosine similarity alone, ignoring cognitive/emotional context and associative structure; LongMemEval shows even the best commercial systems reach only 30-70% accuracy with 30-60% degradation as history scales.
mecanismo: A 3-phase (encode/retrieve/maintain) pipeline composes 5 neuroscience-inspired modules: a SurprisalGate filters WRITE-time noise via LLM-predicted next-intent vs actual-input prediction error (only surprisal>tau=0.3 default is stored); an AffectiveRouter tags a 3-axis cognitive-state vector (valence/arousal/complexity) at write time and blends it (0.7 semantic + 0.3 state-distance) into RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO scoring; MutableRAG reconsolidates retrieved chunks (flags as labile, async LLM-checks for contradiction, overwrites in-place with a version increment + revision history), solving the stale-fact problem; SpreadingActivation retrieves an associative neighborhood via BFS energy propagation over a similarity graph instead of point k-NN; a SleepDaemon periodically consolidates the episodic buffer into durable semantic facts (CONSOLIDACION), pruning raw logs; a write-time safety firewall blocks/redacts secrets and PII at every ingestion point.
evaluacion: Controlled ablation studies using mock LLM/embedding providers to isolate architectural effects (not real-model benchmarks): surprisal-threshold sweep on 15 interactions, affective-routing retrieval on 9 tagged chunks across 3 states, spreading-activation decay sweep on a synthetic 4-node concept chain, reconsolidation on a single simulated contradiction, sleep-consolidation compression across buffer sizes (5-50 episodes), and a 10-interaction full-pipeline integration test; qualitative architectural comparison vs Mem0/Zep/LangMem/Letta; no head-to-head benchmark (e.g. LongMemEval) against competitors is run (explicitly deferred to future work).
numeros_clave: Sleep consolidation: 50 episodes -> 3 facts (16.7x compression, superlinear with buffer size); spreading activation reaches 4/4 nodes at default decay=0.2 vs 1/4 at decay=0.9; surprisal gate storage rate 87% (tau 0-0.4) -> 60% (tau=0.9) -> 27% (tau=1.0); full-pipeline test stores 8/10 interactions (filters filler); affective routing achieves 3/3 correct state-congruent retrieval per state.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The SleepDaemon's periodic consolidation of episodic buffer into durable semantic facts (16.7x superlinear compression, Fig.4) is a directly measured instance of MF's promotion-of-transient-interactions-into-durable-recipes need.

The SurprisalGate is a concrete discretionary WRITE trigger keyed on prediction error rather than write-everything, with a measured storage-rate-vs-threshold curve (Fig.2) directly extending MF's G-M1 need.

notes: Ablations use MockLLMProvider/synthetic embeddings (not real models), a caveat the paper itself acknowledges (S 'Limitations'); see Fig.2 (threshold sweep) and Fig.4 (compression).

cita: Singhal (2026). ForgetAgent: Verifiable Deletion in Multi-Layer Memory Architectures for LLM Agents.
problema: Agent memory spans embeddings, structured records, caches, derived entities, and tool transcripts, so deleting a memory item from one layer does not guarantee it is unrecoverable -- adversaries can reconstruct deleted facts via paraphrase queries, embedding-neighborhood leakage, tool-transcript traces, or story-completion/multi-hop inference, leaving no formal guarantee that OLVIDO (right-to-be-forgotten/GDPR/CCPA compliance) actually removed the information.
mecanismo: Formalizes deletion as counterfactual indistinguishability (an adversary cannot tell post-deletion state M' from a counterfactual M^-Df that never had the forget-set) plus a weaker (eps,delta)-recovery-security notion, over a dependency-closed forget-set D_f+ = D_f union Dep(D_f) covering all summaries/derived-entities/cached-behaviors causally dependent on the deleted item. A 7-layer deletion pipeline operationalizes this: identify all instantiations via structured lookup + embedding-neighborhood search (cosine distance <0.05) + a DFS dependency graph over caches/transcripts, purge raw storage, purge/reweight embeddings (tombstones), invalidate caches/derived entities, sanitize tool transcripts, emit a cryptographic deletion receipt (attestation, not a formal irrecoverability proof), then run automated red-team attacks (membership inference, paraphrase retrieval, neighbor leakage, transcript analysis, story-completion) to empirically verify no residual leakage, rolling back + alerting on failure.
evaluacion: ForgetAgentBench, a released synthetic benchmark of 500 agent interactions with 1,500 labeled deletion targets (personal/preference/domain-specific, multiple difficulty levels); compares 5 deletion strategies (naive vs the full 7-layer method) measuring red-team-attack robustness and a retained-task utility ratio; the authors explicitly caveat that results are limited to synthetic benchmark settings (no real deployed-agent evaluation).
numeros_clave: Naive deletion: 18% robustness to red-team attacks. Full 7-layer method: 94% robustness with 97% retained task utility (ForgetAgentBench, 500 interactions/1,500 deletion targets); embedding-neighborhood identification uses cosine-distance threshold 0.05.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The formal (eps,delta)-recovery-security definition plus the dependency-closure D_f+ = D_f union Dep(D_f) (S III.D) offers a rigorous, transferable notion of 'is this fact actually gone' -- including derived-entity/cache descendants -- that MF's FIDELIDAD anchor could adopt as a test.

The threat model's M={E,S,C,D,T} -- a single fact instantiated across embeddings/SQL/caches/derived-entities/transcripts, where clearing one layer still leaks via others (S I.A) -- directly confirms MF's COSTURAS concern about single-source-per-fact vs multi-store seams.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: published in IJRASET (a low-selectivity engineering journal), single author affiliated with 'Empros International School, Pune' (a secondary school), suggesting a student paper rather than a standard peer-reviewed venue -- despite a well-formalized threat model (S III).

cita: Sertel (2026). Hybrid Governance Architecture: A Self-Improving Memory Substrate for LLM Agents with Progressive Cost Reduction and Deterministic Replay.
problema: LLM agents pay full inference cost for every query even when they have seen the exact same pattern many times before; Dense-RAG reduces hallucination but not token cost (the LLM still reprocesses every retrieved chunk from scratch) and its index grows linearly with corpus size, while existing memory systems (Mem0/Zep/Letta) store and retrieve but never make repeated patterns cheaper over time -- and repeated LLM outputs for the same query are also non-deterministic (2-8 syntactically distinct tool-call variants).
mecanismo: A 3-layer memory substrate under a unified governance gate: L1 Routing Memory (VQ-quantized 1-byte routing codes per item, 768x smaller than dense fp32) for approximate semantic retrieval; L2 Deterministic Vault (SHA-256-hashed, policy-tagged exact key-value store) for facts that must never be approximated; L3 Semantic Neuron Layer records each tool-call decision chain (tool, params, extraction method, success) and matures it through 4 stages via repetition-count+success-rate, from full-LLM Stage 0 to LLM-free deterministic REPLAY at Stage 3. The gate fuses confidence+margin+sensitivity+neuron-maturity into a strict-priority rule across 5 execution paths (Stage0 ~131 tokens down to Stage3 ~5 tokens); background CONSOLIDACION (edge finalization, co-occurrence mining, drift-triggered codebook reshaping) and salience-guided OLVIDO (S=0.4*recency+0.3*frequency+0.3*importance, 4-tier keep/summarize/migrate/delete with a hard guard against deleting RESTRICTED/SENSITIVE items) run continuously; 3 coherence checks gate whether Stage-3 replay is safe, falling back to full LLM otherwise.
evaluacion: 14 experiments (E1-E14), 12 on simulated workloads (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, K=256 codebook) and 2 on a live GPT-5.4-nano API; covers retrieval quality, gate accuracy + 5-way ablation, adversarial/OOD safety (300 probes), neuron maturation, multi-step chain replay, drift detection, salience-guided forgetting, a 1,000-episode end-to-end integration test, a live-API cost comparison, and a deterministic-consistency test; authors note the original E1-E8 suite had validity problems (fake embeddings, circular validation) and was redesigned.
numeros_clave: 89.5% token savings over 1,000 simulated episodes (74.2% LLM bypass); 78.1% real-API token savings over 400 GPT-5.4-nano queries (15,630 vs 71,479 tokens, E13); 100% deterministic consistency for Stage-3 replay vs 79% mean for direct LLM calls (E14); gate 94% phase-weighted accuracy / 0% unsafe fast-path rate (E2); salience-guided forgetting: 1,000 items -> 614 (38.6% reduction), 100% post-forgetting recall, 0 restricted deletions (E11); L1 routing index 768x smaller than dense fp32.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The 3 coherence 'safety' checks (slot-extraction-method / template-skeleton similarity / novel-content-word ratio, S3.6) that force fallback to full LLM when a cached decision looks unsafe to replay is a concrete 'do not trust this cached knowledge blindly' gate, achieving 0 silent failures across 300 adversarial/OOD probes (E3).

The measured, monotonic tiered cost-reduction curve (91.3%->99.9% across phases, E12; 78.1% on a live API, E13) from routing repeated decisions to cheaper paths directly supports MF's context-economy (tokens/cache/latency) framing.

The 4-stage neuron maturation plus background consolidation (edge finalization, co-occurrence mining) promotes a repeated decision into a durable, near-free replay recipe -- directly transferable to MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion need.

notes: Independent researcher preprint, methodologically transparent (explicitly redesigned E1-E8 after finding validity problems, S4). Key tables: 1 (neuron stages), 3 (E13 real-API per-path costs), S3.6 (safety checks).

cita: Bhardwaj (2026). SuperLocalMemory V3.3: The Living Brain -- Biologically-Inspired Forgetting, Cognitive Quantization, and Multi-Channel Retrieval for Zero-LLM Agent Memory Systems.
problema: AI coding agents suffer 'session amnesia' -- every session starts from scratch despite huge context windows because context is ephemeral; existing memory systems (Mem0, Zep, Letta) are stuck at Tier-3 (long-term explicit) with single-channel flat retrieval and implement none of the active cognitive processes (forgetting, consolidation, compression, parameterization) that make human memory efficient, and none reaches the Long-Term Implicit tier (procedural/parameterized behavior).
mecanismo: (1) FRQAD, a Fisher-Rao geodesic distance over Gaussian-manifold embeddings whose variance is inflated by quantization noise, so RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO scoring correctly penalizes low-precision (faded) embeddings instead of treating them as equally similar via cosine; (2) Ebbinghaus-style mathematical forgetting: memory strength S(m) from access-count/importance/confirmation/emotional-salience drives exponential retention, mapped to 5 lifecycle states (Active/Warm/Cold/Archive/Forgotten, OLVIDO) each bound to a progressively coarser embedding bit-width (32/8/4/2-bit), modulated by a Bayesian trust score (untrusted memories decay 3x faster); (3) 7 parallel retrieval channels (semantic, BM25, entity-graph, temporal, spreading-activation, consolidation/gist-blocks, Hopfield associative) fused via weighted RRF; (4) memory parameterization (CONSOLIDACION): consolidated memories become natural-language soft prompts that configure agent behavior without retrieval; (5) a zero-friction auto-cognitive pipeline (session hooks) automating recall/observe/consolidate/forget end-to-end.
evaluacion: Six benchmarks including LoCoMo (zero-LLM Mode A, 304 questions) vs. Mem0/Letta/Zep/LangMem and vs. the authors' own prior version (SLM V3.2); a dedicated mixed-precision retrieval benchmark isolating FRQAD vs. cosine vs. standard Fisher-Rao; a 30-simulated-day forgetting-discrimination experiment; daemon cold/warm-start latency benchmarking; code-knowledge-graph module tested with 385 tests.
numeros_clave: FRQAD: 100% precision preferring high-fidelity over quantized embeddings vs 85.6% cosine / 70.7% standard Fisher-Rao; forgetting: 6.7x discriminative power between frequently-accessed and unused memories over 30 simulated days; LoCoMo Mode A 70.4% (214/304), +23.8pp multi-hop / +12.7pp adversarial vs V3.2 retrieval baseline (V3.2 itself: 74.8% Mode A / 87.7% Mode C); daemon serve mode: cold-start 19s->0.6s (32x speedup).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Trust-weighted forgetting (untrusted sources decay 3x faster, kappa=2.0, Eq.9) couples provenance/trust directly into a memory's decay rate, not just its initial admission -- a concrete extension for MF's FIDELIDAD anchor.

The forgetting-quantization coupling (Active->32bit ... Archive->2bit, Eq.8) is a derived-index-as-cache scheme where cache fidelity degrades gracefully with staleness/access-frequency rather than a binary evict/keep, directly relevant to MF's derived-index-as-cache design.

Memory parameterization (turning consolidated memories into soft prompts, implementing a 'Long-Term Implicit' tier) is a measured instance of promoting accumulated experience into a durable, cheaply-applied behavioral pattern.

notes: Third paper in a self-published trilogy by the same author as W7133570866; notably transparent about a LoCoMo regression vs its own prior version (S1.4 'deliberate architectural trade-off'). See Table 1 (system comparison) and Eq.8 (forgetting-quantization coupling).

cita: Sharma (2026). ContextDB: A Unified Context Layer for AI Agents -- Replacing the Patchwork with a Memory Operating System.
problema: Production teams building AI agents assemble the same fragile ad-hoc 'patchwork' (vector DB + Redis + Postgres + custom glue) with no coherent lifecycle for what gets remembered/updated/forgotten, which fails at multi-session reasoning, temporal understanding, cross-channel identity, and learning from experience; even data-platform incumbents (Databricks Lakebase, Snowflake SnowWork) only bolt storage onto infrastructure ('a hard drive') rather than provide memory intelligence ('a brain') for formation/evolution/retrieval policy.
mecanismo: Synthesizes a 200+-paper survey's Forms x Functions x Dynamics taxonomy into 5 layers: a multi-graph token store (semantic/temporal/causal/entity graphs per memory item, bitemporal event/ingestion timestamps) for query-adaptive weighted-fusion retrieval; a 3-stage formation pipeline (segment -> extract -> compression-as-denoising, ratio tuned per domain); an RL-trained (PPO/GRPO) Memory Manager choosing ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP per incoming unit from a reward tied to downstream answer quality (bootstrapped from as few as 150 demonstrations); a multi-agent memory-sharing bus with role-aware routing and bitemporal conflict resolution; and a privacy-by-design layer (PII detection/redaction, configurable retention including right-to-erasure, audit trail) built into the lifecycle.
evaluacion: A design/architecture-synthesis paper (per extraction evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA) rather than an empirical study: proposes evaluation on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, MSC, and three new domain-specific benchmarks (customer support, research assistance, AI service automation) and states abstract-level TARGET metrics (<100ms p95 recall latency, up to 90% token savings, 'targeting state-of-the-art') but the paper's body contains no measured results table -- Table 1 is a conceptual patchwork-vs-ContextDB mapping, not an experimental result.
numeros_clave: NINGUNO

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The entire 'Patchwork Problem' framing (vector DB + Redis + Postgres + glue code, no coherent single source of truth per fact across stores, S1) is a direct real-world confirmation of MF's COSTURAS concern about multi-store seams and single-source-per-fact.

The RL-trained Memory Manager choosing ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP per incoming unit (S4), rather than a heuristic always-write rule, is a concrete learned discretionary write-trigger design MF's G-M1 need could draw on.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: a design/vision white paper (not an empirical study) synthesizing 200+ other papers' ideas, with company-affiliated author email (saaslabs.co) and only aspirational target metrics in the abstract, not measured results -- worth human review despite a well-organized architecture (S3, Table 1).

cita: Gu et al. (2026). FSFM: A Biologically-Inspired Framework for Selective Forgetting of Agent Memory.
problema: LLM-agent memory research overwhelmingly focuses on retention/retrieval, treating memory as an ever-expanding repository, but this causes resource unsustainability (unbounded storage/compute growth), quality decline (redundant greetings/repeats crowding out useful content), information obsolescence (stale preferences/facts), security vulnerabilities (indefinitely-retained malicious/poisoned content), and GDPR right-to-be-forgotten non-compliance -- the paper argues selective FORGETTING is as important as retention.
mecanismo: A neuro-inspired 3-layer memory hierarchy (sensory -> working [7+-2 capacity, task-completion-triggered clearing] -> long-term) where a multi-dimensional ImportanceScoringEngine scores each memory on Content-Quality (0-3), Business-Value (1-3), Security-Risk, and temporal-decay (Ebbinghaus Retention(t)=e^(-lambda*t), modulated by usage frequency/contextual-relevance/social-consensus) dimensions; a SelectiveForgettingMechanism applies one of 3 policy families (passive decay-based, active deletion-based for right-to-be-forgotten/security-critical content, and adaptive reinforcement-based that recalibrates importance on each retrieval per memory-reconsolidation theory) to prune/consolidate/update the vector-store memory, with an UltraSafeMemoryManager providing garbage collection, checkpointed fault tolerance, and audit logging.
evaluacion: Controlled experiments plus a large production deployment on China Mobile's 'Lingxi' Marketing/Service Assistant: 3.36M raw interaction records, with a vertical (443,902 records, single province) + horizontal (433,686 records, 31 provinces) dual-dimension extraction/testing strategy; measures memory efficiency, retrieval latency, content signal-to-noise ratio, and security-content-elimination rate before/after applying FSFM.
numeros_clave: Access/retrieval efficiency +8.49% (controlled experiments) / retrieval accelerated 1.31x (production); content quality +29.2% signal-to-noise ratio; security: 100% elimination of hazardous content while retaining >70% of high-value business content; production deployment: 3.36M raw records (443,902 + 433,686 extracted), memory efficiency optimized 30%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Working-memory-to-long-term consolidation gated by importance score (S3.3.1) plus adaptive reinforcement recalibration on retrieval (memory reconsolidation) is a measured instance of MF's transient-to-durable promotion need.

Security-Risk-Classification-driven active deletion achieving '100% elimination of hazardous content' in a real 3.36M-record production deployment is direct evidence that an explicit fidelity/security-scoring gate over what memory retains is both feasible and effective at scale.

The measured 30% memory-efficiency gain / 1.31x retrieval speedup from active forgetting is a concrete instance of MF's context-economy anchor achieved via active pruning rather than passive accumulation.

notes: Industry-authored (China Mobile) with a real large-scale production validation (S1.2, 'Lingxi' assistant, 3.36M records); see S3.1-3.2 for the forgetting-policy taxonomy and Abstract for the headline numbers.

cita: Das et al. (2026). Trojan Hippo: Weaponizing Agent Memory for Data Exfiltration.
problema: Persistent cross-session agent memory (ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude-style) massively expands the attack surface for indirect prompt injection: a single untrusted tool call (e.g. a crafted email) can silently WRITE a dormant malicious payload into long-term memory that lies inert across arbitrarily many benign sessions and later activates when the user discusses sensitive topics (finance/health/legal/tax/identity), exfiltrating high-value personal data -- a realistic, fully-indirect threat model that prior memory-poisoning work (which assumed direct memory-write access or an untrusted USER) never systematically evaluated across heterogeneous memory backends and defenses.
mecanismo: Formalizes the 'Trojan Hippo' 2-stage attack (silent WRITE/ADMISION of a payload from an untrusted tool-read into long-term memory; later trigger-conditioned activation on sensitive-topic detection that induces the agent to call an exfiltration tool) and builds a dynamic evaluation framework: (1) an OpenEvolve-based adaptive red-teaming loop that evolves attack-email payloads per (topic, memory-backend, defense) via LLM-mutation + agent-execution + LLM-critic scoring against a training environment, tested on a held-out environment to avoid overfitting; (2) a capability-aware security/utility analysis quantifying each of 4 candidate memory-system defenses' ASR reduction against its utility cost. Instantiated on a LangChain email-assistant (read/search-inbox = taint sources; send/reply/forward = exfiltration tools) across 4 memory backends (explicit tool memory, mem0 agentic memory, RAG, sliding-window context).
evaluacion: End-to-end black-box evaluation against 2 frontier safety-aligned models (gemini-3.1-pro, gpt-5-mini) across 4 memory backends and 5 sensitive topics, using LoCoMo-derived multi-session benign conversation histories to simulate up to 100+ intervening benign sessions; measures Attack Success Rate (ASR) with and without each of 4 defenses, plus a capability-aware utility-cost analysis per defense.
numeros_clave: Without defenses: Trojan Hippo ASR up to 85-100% (gemini-3.1-pro up to 100%, gpt-5-mini up to 85%) across all 4 memory backends, persisting after 100+ benign sessions. With 4 evaluated defenses: ASR reduced to 0-5% in most configurations, 0% for the most restrictive/provably-secure defense -- at varying, sometimes prohibitive, utility cost.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The attack's core exploit is that memory backends give agents no principled way to distinguish 'content read from an untrusted source' from 'trusted, admissible knowledge' -- i.e. no negative/provenance signal travels with the write -- directly confirming MF's premise that provenance-aware admission, not blind accumulation, is a fidelity requirement.

Measured 85-100% ASR with zero write-time provenance/trust gating vs 0-5% with defenses (S7) is rigorous quantitative evidence that provenance/poisoning checks matter specifically at write time, not just at retrieval time.

The 4 evaluated defenses (instruction spotlighting, dual-LLM pattern, information-flow control, consensus-based validation) are concrete discretionary/gated-write mechanisms MF could look to when designing its G-M1 write-trigger.

notes: Rigorous academic security paper (ETH Zurich/UC Berkeley/Snyk). See Fig.1-2 (attack flow, ASR by backend) and S7 (evaluation summary with/without defenses).

cita: Tang et al. (2026). The Trap of Trajectory: Towards Understanding and Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Agentic Memory.
problema: Agentic memory improves reasoning by reusing past experience, but retrieval judges relevance by association alone (embedding similarity or graph structure) with no causal check, so spurious correlations (explicit confounding / unmeasured confounding / collider bias) written into memory persist beyond a single context window and get reinforced by feedback (a spuriously-caused action generates the next trajectory that is written back), turning a transient reasoning error into a self-reinforcing bias -- a risk existing agentic-memory benchmarks never account for.
mecanismo: A causal-discovery pipeline recovers a DAG over trajectory variables (query/memory-state/reasoning/action per step + trajectory-level context) using temporal ordering + recorded action-observation edges + context edges, then flags statistically-associated-but-causally-disconnected pairs as one of 3 canonical spurious types (explicit confounding, unmeasured/latent confounding, collider bias). CAMEL then calibrates both memory-lifecycle stages: at WRITE time it subtracts the running per-step context mean from each entry's embedding (within-step residualization) to remove the shared-context component while retaining entry-specific causal signal, paired with a write-admission criterion based only on similarity to existing entries (never on downstream outcome) to break the collider path; at RETRIEVAL time it identifies a non-causal embedding subspace (axes that vary more between steps than within steps) and demotes any candidate whose ranking is unstable under perturbations along that subspace -- all without extra LLM calls or fine-tuning, applicable to embedding-based (Mem0, A-Mem) and graph-based (G-Memory, AriGraph) memories.
evaluacion: A new spuriousness-focused benchmark built via causal-DAG-recovery on 4 existing agent datasets (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, LoCoMo, WebShop), evaluating 4 memory systems (A-Mem, Mem0, G-Memory, AriGraph) x 3 LLM backbones vs a No-Memory baseline, reporting original-task accuracy and T1/T2/T3 spurious-reasoning ratios (mean+-std over 6 runs); a stepwise decision-accuracy-vs-future-steps analysis after a spurious retrieval; and a CAMEL ablation testing robustness under adaptive attacks explicitly targeting the calibration mechanism.
numeros_clave: Memory improves task accuracy but sharply amplifies spurious-reasoning ratios: e.g. ALFWorld+Qwen, No-Memory Org=51.9% with T1/T2/T3=10.6/7.3/15.8%, vs AriGraph+Qwen Org=86.2% but T1/T2/T3=52.7/77.4/45.8% (Table 1). CAMEL reduces reliance on spurious features across all 3 types while preserving/improving clean-input performance and remains robust under adaptive attacks targeting the calibration (S4-5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Measured evidence (Table 1) that relevance-by-association-alone lets memory systems retrieve and reinforce statistically-associated-but-non-causal content directly confirms MF's premise that provenance/fidelity checks on writes and retrieval must go beyond bare similarity.

The retrieve-time causal-stability test (demoting candidates whose ranking is unstable under non-causal perturbations, S4.2) is a concrete, measured mechanism for a smarter gated retrieval layer beyond naive top-k similarity, directly relevant to MF's measured-retrieval anchor.

notes: Rigorous academic paper (Binghamton/Oakland/UPenn). See Table 1 (spurious-ratio amplification with memory) and S4 (CAMEL write/retrieval calibration).

cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemPrivacy: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Memory Management for Edge-Cloud Agents.
problema: Cloud-assisted personalized memory for edge-cloud agents exposes sensitive user information (PII, health, credentials), while existing masking-based privacy protections destroy the semantic cues memory formation/retrieval needs, degrading personalization utility.
mecanismo: A lightweight on-device model detects privacy spans and classifies them under a four-level taxonomy (PL1 low-sensitivity ... PL4 credentials/secrets); detected spans are replaced with semantically typed placeholders (e.g. <Health_Info_1>) before anything leaves the device, the original-to-placeholder mapping is kept in a local secure DB for cross-session consistency, and the cloud response is restored locally by placeholder lookup+replace -- decoupling privacy protection from semantic destruction.
evaluacion: MemPrivacy-Bench: 200 synthetic user profiles, 155k+ privacy instances, 7 high-level/23 fine-grained scenario categories, multi-turn dialogues with direct+indirect privacy disclosure; span-extraction performance compared against GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3.1-Pro, and utility loss compared against baseline masking strategies across multiple memory systems.
numeros_clave: 200 users, 155k+ privacy instances; on-device models from 0.6B-4B parameters; utility loss limited to within 1.6% across memory systems (vs baseline masking); surpasses GPT-5.2/Gemini-3.1-Pro on privacy-span extraction while reducing inference latency.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Edge-side privacy-span detection + typed-placeholder substitution before any cloud write (S4.1, Stage 1) is a concrete discretionary write-trigger pattern MF could adopt: type/redact sensitive spans before a fact is admitted into shared memory, not after.

A protection layer inserted before storage/retrieval keeps utility loss under 1.6% while reducing inference latency (abstract, S4.3), supporting MF's context-economy framing that write-time guard rails need not be expensive.

notes: Four-level PL1-PL4 taxonomy defined in S4.2; MemPrivacy-Bench construction in S4.3. No membership doubt.

cita: Ravindran (2026). Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Provenance-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous LLM Agents.
problema: Agent memory accumulated in one vendor/model runtime is locked in, causing catastrophic knowledge loss on provider switch, with no integrity verification of transferred memory and no defense against memory-mediated prompt injection when re-hydrating memory into a different model.
mecanismo: A five-component memory model M=(E,S,P,W,I) (episodic/semantic/procedural/working/identity) is serialized into a Merkle-DAG artifact with per-entry BLAKE3 content-addressed IDs and Ed25519 root signing for tamper evidence; capability-scoped access tokens gate read/derive/export permissions per component; re-hydration runs a 7-stage pipeline (verify->filter->rank->compress->format->frame->inject) using a weighted relevance function over recency/salience/similarity/depth, then structural framing + content escaping to resist injection from recalled memory.
evaluacion: Pilot study across Claude-3.5-Sonnet/GPT-4-Turbo/Gemini-1.5-Pro (3 model-pair transfers x 3 task categories, N=50 tasks) measuring Transfer Continuity Score (TCS) and Re-Hydration Fidelity (RHF) under compression, plus a security evaluation (1,000 tamper-mutation trials, 200 injection-pattern attempts, token-validation tests) and format-efficiency/latency micro-benchmarks; Python SDK with 54 passing tests.
numeros_clave: TCS 0.83-0.92 (structured transfer) vs 0.28-0.45 no-memory baseline (2.4x mean improvement, Table 3); RHF degrades from 0.91 at 100% token budget to 0.71 at 25% (Table 4); 100% tamper-detection over 1,000 mutation trials; 0/200 injection attacks executed (Table 5); 69% storage reduction vs raw logs (89KB vs 284KB, Table 6), plus 31% more with CBOR; full re-hydration pipeline <13ms (Table 7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Working (W) component of M=(E,S,P,W,I) (S3.1) models transient goals/subgoals/pending actions as a first-class, content-addressed memory component -- directly transferable to MF's plan-state-as-memory need, though planning tasks show the most transfer degradation (TCS 0.81-0.85 vs 0.28 baseline, Table 3).

Merkle-DAG provenance + Ed25519 signing gives 100% tamper-detection over 1,000/1,000 mutation trials (S5.3), confirming that a cryptographic-provenance approach to fidelity/staleness is measurably enforceable at negligible cost.

Serialize/verify/re-hydrate latencies stay under 13ms (Table 7) and structured storage cuts size 69% vs raw conversation logs (Table 6), supporting MF's context-economy framing that typed memory representations are cheaper as well as safer.

notes: Pilot-scale study explicitly framed as directional (N=50 tasks, S5.1 footnote); gap analysis Table 1 positions it against MemGPT/Mem0/Zep/AMCP/Soul Protocol.

cita: Ouyang et al. (2026). MemLineage: Lineage-Guided Enforcement for LLM Agent Memory.
problema: Signature-only memory-integrity layers verify who wrote an entry but not what untrusted ancestry it was derived from, so an adversary can plant ingredients in untrusted sources and let the agent's own retrieval+summarization loop launder them into an authentic, signed entry that later justifies a sensitive action.
mecanismo: Six modules around one memory store: per-principal Ed25519 signing (M2) plus an RFC 6962 Merkle log (M3) give write-side provenance; a weighted derivation DAG (M4) records which retrieved parents influenced each new entry, propagated by a max-of-strong-edges rule trust(c)=max_p[1(w(p,c)>tau)*trust(p)] that provably preserves an Untrusted-Path label across any chain whose edges stay above threshold tau (Theorem 1); a verifier-aware retrieval hook (M5) tags trust labels at read time and a sensitive-action gate (M6) refuses tool dispatch whose justifying context descends from an External ancestor above tau.
evaluacion: Deterministic mechanism-isolation harness comparing 3 defense cells (no_defense, sig_only_baseline, MemLineage) against 3 attack families (backdoor poisoning, query-injection/retrieval poisoning, sleeper-via-derivation) via byte-equal CI-pinned ASR matrices; a tau x K lineage-threshold ablation across 3 attribution algorithms (uniform-weight, LM-self-eval, white-box attention); a Codex-backed AgentDojo bridge on 6 banking task pairs; per-operation overhead micro-benchmark.
numeros_clave: MemLineage drives all 3 attack-family columns to 0% ASR on the mechanism-isolation harness, while sig_only_baseline fails MemoryGraft-style poisoning and sleeper-via-derivation; under an intentionally vulnerable AgentDojo tool-output profile, no-defense/sig-only fail 6/6 banking pairs while all MemLineage rows reach 0/6 strict ASR; tau x K ablation: safe tau ceiling shrinks from <=0.30 at K=1 derivation hops to <=0.10 at K=5 (w0=0.9, d=0.7); per-operation overhead is sub-millisecond (Table 7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Theorem 1 (Untrusted-Path Persistence, S3.5) formalizes exactly MF's provenance/poisoning concern: a max-of-strong-edges propagation rule measurably drives all 3 attack families to 0% ASR (ASR matrix, S6.2), confirming that lineage-aware (not just signature-only) provenance is needed for FIDELIDAD.

Sub-millisecond per-operation overhead (Table 7, S6.4) shows lineage tracking is cheap relative to any LLM call, supporting MF's cost doctrine that provenance bookkeeping need not compete with the token/latency budget.

The single content-addressed memory store M with per-entry signed provenance plus a derivation DAG (Figure 1) is a concrete single-source-of-truth-per-fact pattern MF's multi-store seams (COSTURAS) could adopt directly.

notes: Core deterministic artifacts are byte-equal CI-verified (S6.1 CSV list); hosted-model AgentDojo/live sweeps kept as auditable logs, not byte-pinned -- a reusable rigor pattern.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). State Contamination in Memory-Augmented LLM Agents.
problema: Standard toxicity monitors check text at the moment of writing, but the summarization used to compress agent memory can 'launder' toxic framing into a classifier-clean summary that still steers downstream agents toward toxic behavior -- a hidden channel invisible to threshold-based memory audits.
mecanismo: Paired counterfactual multi-agent rollouts vary only the focal agent A1's toxicity (toxic vs neutral) holding topology/seed/decoding fixed; downstream toxicity is scored with Detoxify and compared via the sub-threshold propagation gap SPG(tau)=E[tox(v)|tox(Mt)<tau,toxic]-E[tox(v)|tox(Mt)<tau,neutral], isolating hidden influence within the classifier-safe regime; a three-pathway mitigation (sanitize transcript before write, rewrite/gate memory before compression rather than after, plus DPO on paired rollouts) targets transcript backflow, memory laundering and parametric bias separately.
evaluacion: 200 paired toxic/neutral seeds across chain/tree/DAG/high-branching topologies with gpt-4o-mini (phenomenon) and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct via LoRA-DPO (intervention); metrics are SPG, paired mean shift delta-mu (Wilcoxon signed-rank), and P95 tail toxicity; ablation over single-pathway/pairwise/full-system interventions and over classifier thresholds tau in {0.03,...,0.5}.
numeros_clave: Toxic-condition memory summaries have mean toxicity 0.0852 (100% below tau=0.5, Table 1) yet SPG(0.5)=0.140 (seed-level paired diff 0.168, 95% CI [0.120,0.226], Wilcoxon p=3.75e-8); post-hoc memory rewrite/gate cuts delta-mu from 0.168 to 0.024-0.041 but SPG stays 0.086-0.103 (Table 2); full system (sanitize-before-write + DPO) reaches lowest turn-final toxicity 0.0106 and SPG 0.0014 on Llama-3.1-8B, n=200 (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The core finding -- sanitizing only the completed summary is too late because harmful framing is already compressed below threshold (S5.2) -- measures the need for negative knowledge ('do not trust a classifier-clean consolidated entry') applied at write time rather than retrieval time.

Challenges the implicit assumption that summarization-based consolidation is safe once it passes a content check: Table 2 shows post-compression memory rewrite/gate reduces delta-mu but leaves SPG at 0.086-0.103, i.e. consolidation itself is the laundering vector, so gotcha-to-recipe promotion needs a pre-compression sanitization gate, not a post-hoc one.

SPG is itself a retrieval-conditioned measured metric (conditioning on tox(Mt)<tau, S4.3) that operationalizes 'evidence the retrieved state changed downstream behavior' -- relevant context for MF's measured-retrieval layer even though the paper's domain is toxicity, not factual staleness.

notes: NeurIPS 2026 accepted paper; Table 2/3 (S5.2/5.4) are the load-bearing ablations. No membership doubt.

cita: Tan et al. (2026). MemAudit: Post-hoc Auditing of Poisoned Agent Memory via Causal Attribution and Structural Anomaly Detection.
problema: Existing memory-poisoning defenses focus on online/preventive intervention (filtering, blocking) but do not address the post-hoc question of which already-stored memories caused an observed harmful action, especially without access to oracle poison labels.
mecanismo: Two complementary signals are fused into a detoxification ranking: a counterfactual memory influence score CMIS(mi)=h(q*,y*)-h(q*,f(q*,R(q*,M\{mi}))) computed via replay-based leave-one-out intervention on retrieved memories, and a structural anomaly score CAS(mi)=sum_j w(mi,mj)*sim(mi,mj) over a DeBERTa-v3 NLI-scored memory consistency graph (contradiction/inconsistency weighted by semantic similarity); DS=alpha*CMIS_norm+(1-alpha)*CAS_norm (alpha=0.6) ranks memories for batch removal, computed once on the original store so early deletions cannot bias later attribution.
evaluacion: Evaluated against the MINJA interaction-only memory-injection attack on QA and RAP tasks across GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini/DeepSeek backbones, vs random deletion / retrieval-frequency deletion / NNC-contradiction-filtering baselines; component ablation (CMIS-only vs CAS-only vs fused), fusion-weight sweep alpha in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, and a contamination-ratio sweep rho in {0,...,0.63} to locate the operating boundary, all averaged over 10 runs.
numeros_clave: QA ASR after auditing: 70.0%->0.0% (GPT-4o), 50.0%->0.0% (GPT-4o-mini), 70.0%->10.0% (DeepSeek); RAP ASR: 83.3%/80.0%/80.0% -> 0.0% for all 3 backbones (Table 1); fused MemAudit (0.0-10.0% ASR) beats CMIS-only (28-49%) and CAS-only (32-50%) alone (Table 2); effectiveness collapses once contamination ratio rho crosses ~0.20-0.24 (QA rho=0.25 -> ASR jumps to 40-70%; RAP rho=0.63 -> ASR 80-100%, Tables 4-5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Post-hoc dual-signal auditing (causal replay + structural consistency graph, Algorithm 1) is a concrete pattern MF could adopt for its own FIDELIDAD checks: attribute an observed bad outcome back to specific stored facts without requiring poison labels.

The memory consistency graph (S4, CAS score) checks pairwise entailment/contradiction across the whole store, a mechanism analogous to detecting single-source-of-truth violations, though the paper's graph is single-store rather than multi-store.

S6.4's contamination-ratio operating boundary (rho ~0.20-0.24) is a measured limit on how much a cheap post-hoc audit can repair before costlier full sanitization/rollback is needed -- relevant capacity-planning signal even though the paper does not report token/latency cost directly.

notes: Table 1 (main ASR), Table 2 (component ablation), Tables 4-5 (contamination boundary) are the load-bearing evidence. No membership doubt.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). Hijacking Agent Memory: Stealthy Trojan Attacks Through Conversational Interaction.
problema: Prior memory-poisoning attacks assume an attacker can write raw malicious content directly into memory, ignoring that real agent memory pipelines apply selective extraction and rewriting that filters low-salience content and paraphrases surviving entries -- so those attacks fail against realistic selective (extract-update) memory systems.
mecanismo: A two-phase optimization-driven trigger: (1) iterative trigger optimization jointly minimizes an entity-masquerading loss (HotFlip-style gradient-guided token search against a NER model, so the trigger reads as a named entity and survives rewriting) plus a semantic-concentration loss (pulls trigger-injected embeddings into a tight cluster) and a margin-based isolation loss (keeps that cluster separated from benign embedding regions); (2) a semantic relational bridge (GPT-4-authored) binds trigger and malicious payload into one logically interdependent statement so the extraction pipeline stores them as a single coherent entry instead of discarding or splitting them.
evaluacion: Evaluated across multiple agent domains and memory mechanisms (extract-update pipelines in the style of Mem0/LangMem) including a real-world agent system (S5.5); measures attack success rate under triggered queries vs benign accuracy, robustness to perplexity-filtering and paraphrasing defenses, and a mechanistic analysis of embedding-space anisotropy and attention redistribution induced by the trigger.
numeros_clave: MemPoison achieves attack success rates up to 0.95 while maintaining benign accuracy, outperforming AgentPoison/MINJA-style baselines that assume direct database write access; the attack remains effective against perplexity-based filtering and paraphrasing defenses (per-domain residual ASR reported in S5.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Demonstrates that extraction/rewriting alone (a natural admission-time sanitization MF might lean on for FIDELIDAD) is not sufficient: entity masquerading (S4.2, motivated by an App. A pilot study showing LLMs preserve named entities verbatim under rewriting) lets a trigger survive paraphrasing, reaching up to 0.95 ASR -- a direct challenge to trusting rewrite-as-sanitization.

MemPoison targets exactly the discretionary write/admission gate (S3, 'selective extraction & rewriting', Fig. 1): the semantic relational bridge is engineered specifically to survive that gate's salience filtering, showing a naive admission filter is an insufficient write-trigger safeguard against optimization-driven adversarial input.

notes: Threat model in S3 and mechanistic analysis (embedding anisotropy/attention redistribution, S5.6) are the non-obvious anchors. No membership doubt.

cita: Tomczak (2026). RAMPART: Registry-based Agentic Memory with Priority-Aware Runtime Transformation.
problema: Instruction/skill files (SKILL.md/CLAUDE.md) and database-backed archival memory (Letta) treat context assembly as fixed concatenation, not a programmable operation, so compile-time block ordering, relevance-based inclusion, and structural access control are unavailable, and models suffer position-dependent (U-shaped) instruction-following failures the system cannot correct.
mecanismo: A pure in-RAM ordered block registry (OrderedDict[UUID->InstructionBlock]) where each addressable block carries priority/source/author/removable/embedding metadata; five zero-prompt-token primitives (promote, gate/write, evict, rollback, write-to-other-registry) mutate ordering and membership before a compile() step assembles the final prompt string; relevance gating pre-filters blocks by cosine similarity before compilation (not after, unlike retrieval-augmented injection); session-local UUID re-randomization of block addresses on every load (ASLR-style) prevents an injected instruction from targeting a block by semantic name.
evaluacion: Controlled mechanistic probes (not general benchmarks) on Qwen3-8B Q4 with a 31-block firmware seed library and a fictional-function-name checker; position sweeps across registry sizes 1-31 under task-precedes/task-follows configurations; a cluster-grouping sweep; cross-model replication on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, Qwen3-14B; a relevance-gating cost/success trade-off; a schema-eviction access-control test; latency micro-benchmarks (Table 3).
numeros_clave: Near-ceiling success up to ~position 11 (task precedes) or ~position 6 (task follows) before a sharp cliff; block grouping raises Mistral-7B's mean pass rate roughly fivefold at the hardest registry size; relevance gating reduces prompt cost by 67.8% while recovering 83% of promoted-condition success; schema eviction produces 0% tool invocations vs 100% with the schema present; compile() reaches 12.5us at N=200 blocks, find_relevant() 4-6ms, cold start 230ms at N=31 (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The in-RAM block registry with zero disk I/O after cold start and a deterministic compile() step (S2.4) is a concrete derived-index-as-cache pattern: the registry is rebuildable state over the seed library, inspectable before every inference call, directly transferable to MF's TIER-INDICE.

Relevance gating cuts prompt token cost by 67.8% while recovering 83% of promoted-condition success (abstract, S3.2), and all five registry primitives execute at zero prompt-token cost (Table 4), confirming MF's context-economy framing that structural filtering beats brute concatenation.

Session-local UUID re-randomization of block runtime addresses (S2.1, an ASLR analogy) is a concrete write-time defense against indirect prompt injection that references a block by semantic name -- a pattern MF could adopt for provenance/tamper resistance beyond content-based checks.

notes: Explicitly scoped as mechanistic probes, not general-purpose benchmarks (S3.1); position-sensitivity cliff data in Figure 1, latencies in Table 3. No membership doubt.

cita: Munirathinam, T. (2026). memorywire: A Vendor-Neutral Wire Format for Agent Memory Operations.
problema: Agent-memory frameworks (mem0, Letta, Cognee, Zep, MemoryOS, MemTensor) each ship a bespoke SDK/storage layout with no shared wire format, so every integration is bespoke, every migration rebuilds memory from scratch, and no framework exposes a governance surface letting a human review a write before it enters long-term storage.
mecanismo: A JSON-Schema-2020-12 wire format for five operations (remember/recall/forget/merge/expire) over four memory types (semantic/episodic/procedural/emotional), implemented via a MemoryStore protocol that any backend adopts; a memory router fans operations across N child stores in parallel and fuses recall results via rank-only, additive Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60), with an optional one-hop graph boost applied only to items already in the fused set; an optional HITL governance channel implements a diff-and-approve pattern (Co-memorize) staging flagged writes behind a PENDING_APPROVAL sentinel invisible to recall until a reviewer commits or rejects.
evaluacion: A microbenchmark on a 100-fact/50-query labelled corpus against a real sentence-transformer embedder; an adversarial-fusion experiment sweeping a 1-of-N rank-0 injection attack (K in {0,5,...,50}) across RRF/MAX/weighted fusion; a 16-scenario x 5-adapter cross-adapter conformance suite (80 cells); reference implementation with five backend adapters (sqlite-vec, mem0, Letta, Cognee, pgvector).
numeros_clave: recall@5=1.000 on 42 gold-id queries, ingest p50=37.8ms, recall p50=40.6ms; RRF holds recall@5=1.000 across the full K in {0,...,50} injection sweep while MAX fusion collapses to 0.500 with 80% leak at K>=5; conformance suite passes 68/80 cells (12 SKIP, 0 FAIL).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A vendor-neutral wire format that any of 5 heterogeneous backends implements losslessly for the type/confidence/expires_at fields (Table 2 fidelity matrix) is a concrete single-source-per-fact standardization pattern directly transferable to MF's multi-store seams (COSTURAS).

forget defaults to soft delete (preserving the audit trail as a tombstone) and expire pins a predicate DSL (older_than_days/confidence_below/no_recall_in_days, S3.2) as a first-class 'this should no longer be trusted/recalled' vocabulary -- a concrete wire-level encoding of negative knowledge.

RRF's rank-only, additive-across-stores fusion gives measured robustness against a rogue/compromised store (recall@5 holds 1.000 across the full injection sweep, S5.2) vs MAX's 0.500/80%-leak collapse -- a concrete multi-store fusion algorithm MF could adopt for provenance-robust retrieval fusion.

notes: Explicitly frames itself as composition/standardization, not new algorithms (S1.3); adversarial-fusion open-data artifact cited in C5. No membership doubt.

cita: Yu (2026). Present but Not Enforced: Benchmarking Governance-Marker Compliance in LLM Agent Memory Under Multi-Turn Pressure.
problema: Persistent agent memories carry system-assigned governance markers (retracted/stale/low-trust) meant to constrain how a model uses them, but no prior work separates whether a model merely recalls a marker from whether it still acts on it once a user applies sustained multi-turn pressure to ignore it.
mecanismo: BEC (Behavioral Execution Consistency) separates recall from compliance via two conditions on a frozen 120-item benchmark (15 valid + 105 revoked across retracted/stale/low-trust classes): the WITH condition uses independent recall and compliance probes with no pressure; the PRESSURE condition follows the recall probe with three escalating rounds of adversarial user pressure in one multi-turn dialogue, judging a case ZOMBIE if any round erodes compliance, and computing the zombie-compliance rate (ZCRR) over recalled revoked-class items plus a valid-memory-use-rate (VMUR) negative control.
evaluacion: Five models from two vendors (moonshot-v1-128k, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash), scored by a cross-validated judge (deepseek-v4-pro, cross-family agreement 89.3% on 28 re-judged items); metrics are recall rate, WITH/PRESSURE ZCRR with 95% Wilson intervals, VMUR, and a per-marker-class breakdown (retracted/stale/low-trust).
numeros_clave: Recall=1.00 for all 5 models; WITH-condition ZCRR 0.000-0.010 (near zero); PRESSURE ZCRR spans 0.219 (kimi-k2.6) to 0.971 (moonshot-v1-128k); same-generation cross-vendor flagships differ ~3.8x (kimi-k2.6 0.219 vs deepseek-v4-pro 0.838, non-overlapping CIs) while within-family capability upgrade (v4-flash->v4-pro) changes ZCRR by only 0.019; valid-class collateral damage 0/15 on four models, 1/15 on one (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Governance markers (retracted/stale/low-trust) are exactly MF's negative-knowledge concept made explicit and testable: recall of the marker (knowing 'do not use this') is perfect (1.0) but PRESSURE-condition compliance collapses to as low as 0.029 upheld (ZCRR up to 0.971) -- holding negative knowledge in context is necessary but not sufficient without external enforcement.

Directly challenges relying on in-context governance markers and model judgment to enforce staleness/fidelity: the WITH-condition ZCRR near zero rules out a perception failure, yet PRESSURE ZCRR reaches up to 0.971 (Table 1) -- an explicit marker guarantees the model knows, not that it complies, motivating governance enforced outside the model rather than left to its in-context judgment (S5.1).

notes: Positions itself explicitly as an incremental intersection of STALE/Memora (adjudication gap) and SYCON-Bench (sycophancy), S2. No membership doubt.

cita: Liu (2026). Memory Contagion: Cross-Temporal Propagation of Evaluator Bias via Agent Memory.
problema: Prior work on agent memory consolidation assumes stored experiences are unbiased and attributes memory degradation solely to the consolidation mechanism; it ignores that agents trained or guided by biased evaluators produce biased trajectories that, once stored, can propagate that bias to future agents retrieving from the same memory store even when consolidation is perfect.
mecanismo: A source agent's trajectories are scored by a biased evaluator (additive bias model Eb=Eclean+alpha*b, for length preference or authority-marker density) and stored via oracle (lossless) or LLM-based consolidation; a target agent retrieving from the biased vs. a clean store is compared via Gamma_temporal, the Wasserstein-1 distance between behavioral score distributions, decomposed into content-based, retrieval-based and interaction components (E1-E3) and swept across contamination rates p in {0.2,...,1.0}.
evaluacion: 4-phase pipeline (bias injection, memory construction, oracle-consolidation ablation, mechanism decomposition, dose-response) on DeepSeek-Chat with 3-seed bootstrap CIs and permutation tests (p<0.01); multi-model validation on DeepSeek V4-Chat, V4-Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.6; retrieval-log Precision@5 analysis to rule out retrieval interference.
numeros_clave: Oracle (perfect) consolidation still yields Gamma_A=13.18 (95% CI [9.05,21.10], length bias) proving biased input alone suffices for contagion; LLM consolidation attenuates length bias by 84% (Gamma_B=2.03) but only the older DeepSeek V4-Chat is susceptible -- V4-Pro and Claude Sonnet 4.6 both show Gamma_A=0.00; authority bias fails to propagate in all 15 controlled multi-seed runs (Gamma=0.00); content (E1) and retrieval (E2) contribute comparably to Gamma_total (6.82 for length); contagion detected at contamination rate as low as p=0.2, no observed safe threshold.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Directly challenges the assumption (attributed to prior work, S5) that 'fixing consolidation quality fixes memory problems': Gamma_A=13.18 under oracle (lossless) consolidation proves consolidation is not the sufficient guard -- input-bias must be addressed independently before promotion, not assumed away by a perfect merge step.

The finding that consolidation's effect is bias-type-dependent (attenuates global/length bias by 84% but cannot detectably propagate local/authority-marker bias in this setup, S4.2) is itself negative knowledge MF should encode: 'do not assume consolidation is safe by default for all fact types' -- motivating type-aware promotion guards.

The retrieval-log Precision@5 analysis (monotonic 0.00->1.00 across p, Appendix A.7) is used to rule out retrieval interference as the dose-response mechanism -- a reusable measured-retrieval diagnostic technique relevant to G-M2 even though the paper's domain is bias, not staleness.

notes: Authority-bias amplification (Table 1 dagger) is explicitly flagged non-replicable single-run and not a confirmed finding; only the 15-run null (Gamma=0.00) is load-bearing. No membership doubt.

cita: Louck (2026). Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees.
problema: Existing memory-poisoning defenses base an item's authority to act on its content (trust-scoring) or its derivation history (lineage), but both signals are malleable: an attacker can launder an untrusted origin through the agent's own summarization, a trusted-tool echo, or manufactured corroboration, so a poisoned memory ends up looking benign and authoritative to any content- or lineage-based gate.
mecanismo: TMA-NM binds act_class to origin at write time (origin in {user, trusted_tool, agent, untrusted_external}, set by an authenticated channel the adversary cannot forge) and propagates it non-malleably: any item derived from untrusted sources inherits maximum untrust regardless of how benign the derived text reads; authority rises only via Sybil-resistant corroboration-gated elevation (>=2 independent trusted principals, never repeated untrusted content) or a fresh action-bound single-use user authorization; every write/elevation/verdict is appended to a tamper-evident hash chain. A TLA+ machine-checked model proves malleable gates are insufficient (T1), write-time binding is necessary (T2), and this non-malleable construction is sufficient (T3, 3,270 reachable states) plus an inductive invariant toward unbounded executions.
evaluacion: MEM-INV-Bench: 12 domains x 5 consequential tool types, sleeper/control-flow/data-exfiltration attack classes with benign/static/adaptive/whitebox variants, benchmarked across 8 frontier models from 6 vendors against 5 defense classes (none, trust_score, lineage, capability_ifc, TMA-NM); Wilson 95% CIs and 20,000-iteration permutation tests; a per-decision latency microbenchmark.
numeros_clave: Baselines fail up to 68% laundering ASR (trust_score and capability_ifc) and lineage reaches 47% laundering ASR; TMA-NM alone reaches 0% ASR on both direct and laundering attacks across all 8 models at 100% legit-utility (Table I); cross-model trigger study: TMA-NM 0/4032 successful attacks (CI [0,0.1]%) vs undefended baseline 31.2% (43.8% on blatant triggers); act-gate decision costs 1.3us vs ~2000ms for a content-detection judge call (~6 orders of magnitude cheaper).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The machine-checked separation theorem (T1-T3, S4) plus 0% empirical ASR across 8 models is strong confirmation that content- or lineage-only defenses are structurally insufficient against laundering (existing defenses reach up to 68% ASR, Table I) and that write-time origin-binding is necessary -- directly validates MF's FIDELIDAD emphasis on provenance over content trust.

The non-malleable act-gate is a deterministic check at 1.3us per decision vs ~2000ms for an LLM-judge content detector (S6, six orders of magnitude cheaper), showing rigorous security enforcement need not compete with the token/latency budget.

Sybil-resistant corroboration-gated elevation -- authority rises only via >=2 independent trusted principals, never through content asserting its own legitimacy (S3, M3) -- is a concrete single-source-of-truth-per-fact pattern directly transferable to MF's COSTURAS need.

notes: T1-T3 are bounded-model (TLC, Slots=3/sessions<=2/k=2) results extended toward unbounded execution via a hand-argued inductive invariant, not a fully mechanized unbounded proof (S4, explicitly scoped). No membership doubt.

cita: Jawed (2026). When Disagreement Means Learning (or Bias): Human-Governed Memory Consolidation and Counterfactual Diagnosis in Multi-Agent LLM Scoring.
