numeros_clave: En InEp-Know, Gemini-3-Flash (long-context puro, SIN memoria) obtiene el mejor rank (1.00) superando a TODOS los métodos de memoria explícita (Tabla 3); en InEp-Exec con contexto restringido, el mejor método de memoria mejora +14.5pp (16K) y +14.0pp (32K) sobre DeepSeek-V3.2 sin memoria, pero la ganancia cae a +7.8pp (64K) y algunos métodos caen POR DEBAJO del baseline sin memoria a 128K (Tabla 4, ej. MemAgent 37.0 vs baseline 39.5); en CrossEp-Know fácil, memoria-libre DeepSeek-V3.2 (52.1) SUPERA al mejor método de memoria (Qwen3-Emb-4B 50.0), mientras en tareas difíciles memoria-libre da 0.0 pero ACE sube a 13.0 — memoria ayuda MÁS en tareas difíciles pero puede EMPEORAR tareas fáciles (Tabla 5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Mide, contra 15 métodos representativos, que un baseline long-context SIN memoria explícita alguna gana el mejor rank en tareas de conocimiento intra-episodio (Gemini-3-Flash rank 1.00, Tabla 3) y que memoria explícita puede EMPEORAR el desempeño en tareas fáciles (Tabla 5) — desafía la asunción de que retrieval/memoria siempre suma valor, un hallazgo central para calibrar cuándo G-M2 de MF debe activarse.

Documenta sistemáticamente casos donde memoria empeora el desempeño respecto a no-memoria (varios métodos caen bajo el baseline a 128K de contexto y en tareas fáciles de CrossEp-Know) — evidencia amplia y comparativa (15 métodos x 6 datasets) de que 'más memoria' no es monotónicamente bueno, la señal negativa de mayor escala de todo el corpus revisado.

Define 'execution evolution' explícitamente como memoria de progreso-de-tarea, subgoals no resueltos y decisiones previas (§3.3) como un eje de primera clase separado del conocimiento — confirma que MF debería tratar el estado-de-plan como una categoría de memoria DISTINTA con semántica propia, no una mezcla implícita con hechos.

Reporta uso de tokens como métrica de eficiencia de primera clase junto a accuracy, mostrando que la ganancia de memoria decae y a veces se revierte cuando el presupuesto de contexto crece (§5.2.2 Finding 3) — confirma que el valor de la memoria es condicional al presupuesto de contexto disponible, relevante a la economía de contexto de MF.

notes: Tabla 1 (comparación de benchmarks existentes), Tabla 3 (InEp-Know), Tabla 4 (InEp-Exec por presupuesto de contexto), Tabla 5 (CrossEp-Know por dificultad), Tabla 6 (CrossEp-Tool/Web/Emb); hallazgo transversal: 'ningún método de memoria funciona consistentemente en todos los escenarios' (Abstract).

cita: Liu et al. (2026). MemRepair: Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Repository-Level Vulnerability Repair.
problema: Repository-level automated vulnerability repair treats each fix as an isolated one-shot generation, discarding prior fixes and failed validation attempts, so agents repeat cross-file security mistakes (e.g. integer overflow feeding an unguarded downstream write) that plain test feedback alone cannot correct.
mecanismo: A three-tier hierarchical memory (L1 History-Fix project-local fixes mined from CVEFixes, L2 Security-Pattern cross-project defensive patterns, L3 Refinement-Trajectory failure-to-success deltas) feeds a Locator-Patcher-Verifier loop; retrieval uses a two-priority intra-project-then-cross-project embedding search with dedup (cosine>=0.95) and recency-weighted pruning, and each verifier outcome (success/regenerate/relocate) writes new L2/L3 entries.
evaluacion: Evaluated on SEC-Bench (C/C++), PatchEval (Python/Go/JavaScript) and the C++ subset of Multi-SWE-bench, comparing against OpenHands, SWE-agent, Aider, Agentless and the specialized InfCode-C++, measuring % resolved, file-level location accuracy and average $/task repair cost.
numeros_clave: 58.0% resolved on SEC-Bench, 58.2% on PatchEval, 30.58%/30.6% on Multi-SWE-bench C++ vs InfCode-C++ 25.60% (+19% relative); >20pp over prior best general agents; L2=116/L3=86 stored entries reported for SEC-Bench; dedup threshold cosine>=0.95; refinement loop capped at 3 failed attempts (p.4-6).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: L3 Refinement-Trajectory memory stores explicit failure-to-success deltas (P_fail, Delta_diff, insight) instead of discarding failed patches (§3.3.3, p.4) — a concrete pattern MF could adopt for negative-knowledge consolidation.
Deduplication (cosine>0.95 merge) plus recency-weighted pruning are lightweight rules that keep memory bounded and useful (§3.3.3), a reusable recipe for promoting/pruning MF's own gotcha store.
The paper measures retrieval quality explicitly via 'Location Accuracy' alongside success rate (§4.3, Table 2, p.6), matching MF's stance that retrieval must be measured, not assumed.
Cost ($/task) is a first-class reported metric and the refinement loop is explicitly capped at 3 attempts to bound cost (§4.4, p.6), supporting MF's context-economy stance.

notes: Table 2 (p.6, SEC-Bench/Multi-SWE-bench comparison) + §3.3.3 memory-scale figures (p.4) are the load-bearing evidence; clearly on-topic hierarchical + negative-knowledge memory paper, not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Feng et al. (2026). ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents.
problema: LLM agents solve each task from scratch, discarding successful strategies and failure lessons accumulated across prior interactions; fine-tuning the executor on this experience is brittle because it re-couples learning to one specific, soon-to-be-obsolete model.
mecanismo: Historical trajectories are distilled into skill (success) and lesson (failure) experience units stored as nodes of a self-evolving graph, with edges linking semantically/strategically related experiences; a lightweight RL-trained retrieval copilot predicts per-task diffusion depth (personalized PageRank) and a similarity-vs-utility ranking weight, retrieving beyond flat nearest-neighbor matching; node utility is updated online from with/without-retrieval task-score deltas while the executor LLM stays frozen.
evaluacion: Evaluated on ExpSuite (10 static QA/math/code benchmarks plus ALFWorld and AppWorld agentic environments) with Llama-3.2-3B/3.1-8B and Qwen3-32B/Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite executors, against retrieval-centric (Mem0, AWM, MemRL, ReasoningBank, ExpeL, LightMem) and LLM-centric (S3, IRCoT, Search-o1) baselines, with a component ablation.
numeros_clave: +12.2% (small executor) / +4.7% (large executor) average score over the strongest baseline on static tasks; +21.4%/+12.7% on agentic tasks; interaction-step reduction of 12.7%/21.6% vs the most efficient baseline (Abstract, §4.1, Table 2-3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Low-scoring trajectories are distilled into explicit 'lessons' (failure modes, invalid actions, constraints to avoid) stored as first-class graph nodes alongside skills (§3.2, p.4) — a concrete pattern for representing negative knowledge as retrievable structured memory rather than discarding failed attempts.

Retrieval utility is measured directly via a with/without-retrieval reward (Eq.14, p.5) and ablations isolate graph diffusion vs utility-ranking's separate contributions (§4) — matches MF's stance that retrieval quality must be measured.

Graph-structured relational memory with utility-aware ranking explicitly outperforms the flat nearest-neighbor retrieval used by Mem0/ExpeL/MemRL baselines (Table 1 p.2, Table 2 p.6) — a richer-index-over-flat-cache pattern MF could adopt for its derived index.

notes: Table 2/3 (pp.6-7) hold the load-bearing numbers; Table 1 (p.2) contrasts the capability matrix vs prior memory methods. Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Raviotta (2026). Experience to Competence Without Weight Updates: Pre-Registered Falsifiable Gates for Agent Memory.
problema: Agent-memory evaluations are typically post-hoc (benchmarks and mechanisms chosen after the system already works) and negative results are rarely published, so it is unclear which biologically-inspired mechanisms (strengthening, decay, consolidation) actually help versus merely produce a plausible-looking in-system learning curve.
mecanismo: A SQLite-graph episodic/semantic memory with a same-fact LLM judge for dedup, reinforced/decaying edges, and nightly selective (verbatim, non-paraphrasing) consolidation is subjected to 5 pre-registered falsifiable gates (fixed pass/kill criteria, floor/ceiling arms, bootstrap CIs) run end-to-end locally via Ollama; a separate gate (M4) freezes the agent's weights and stores only verbatim API-error lessons, recalled by cosine top-k, to test experience-to-competence transfer with no gradient updates.
evaluacion: Five sequential gates (M0-M4) on synthetic fact-recall regimes and a 60-episode hidden-rule API task, each with a memoryless-control floor arm and an explicit-rules oracle ceiling arm, bootstrap 95% CIs (1000 resamples), replicated across 3 seeds for M4; all runs on a single consumer M1 Pro laptop.
numeros_clave: Repetition-weighted ranking KILLED vs vanilla cosine RAG: -0.440 [-0.527,-0.347] and -0.180 [-0.267,-0.100] (§6); cosine-similarity medians for same-fact paraphrases (0.83) fully overlap same-template distractors (0.87); consolidation compresses 350->150 active nodes at -0.053 statistical parity (§5-6); M4 first-try pass rate rises 0.45->1.00 across blocks vs control flat at 0.00 (oracle 0.95, Table 1 p.4), transfer effect replicates 3/3 seeds.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: M4 shows a frozen agent plus verbatim error-lesson memory converts API failures into transferable procedural competence (0.45->1.00) while a memoryless control stays at 0.00 across 60 episodes (§7, Table 1, p.4) — strong support for MF's investment in negative-knowledge (gotcha) memory.

Direct measurement shows cosine similarity CANNOT separate paraphrases of the same fact from same-template distractors (medians 0.83 vs 0.87, fully overlapping, §6, p.3) — embedding-only retrieval is structurally unsound, confirming MF's skepticism of embeddings as the primary index over grep/typed retrieval (ADR-019).

Selective consolidation with verbatim (non-paraphrase) merging compresses 350 exposures into 150 active nodes at statistical retention parity with store-everything (§5 M2, §6 ablation, p.3) — supports MF's promotion-not-summarization approach to durable memory.

'Verbatim beats gist, twice' (§8, p.5): LLM paraphrase corrupted exact values both in consolidation and lesson-writing, so the system stores verbatim text and reserves abstraction for retrieval time — echoes MF's docs-as-truth stance over lossy summarized indices.

notes: §6 Gate M3 (p.3) and §7 Gate M4 Table 1 (p.4) are the load-bearing measurements; two explicit KILLs of the celebrated repetition-ranking mechanism make this an unusually high-value negative-results paper. Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Wang and Li (2023). Learning from Mistakes via Cooperative Study Assistant for Large Language Models.
problema: LLM self-reflection methods rely on the model's own often-inaccurate judgment of when to stop refining, and are limited to the failed attempts of the current query, so agents cannot generalize error-avoidance guidance to similar future queries.
mecanismo: A cooperative auxiliary 'study assistant' agent compares the main LLM's responses against ground truth during a gathering phase, writing (query, wrong-answer, analysis+guideline) entries to a global mistake memory; at examination time (no ground truth available) it retrieves the top-k=1 most similar past mistake by cosine similarity (theta=0.9) and injects the analysis+guideline as pre-hoc instruction; the assistant can further be fine-tuned per-LLM via imitation learning on successful guidance trajectories.
evaluacion: Evaluated on 27 tasks from BBH (reasoning) and BBQ (social bias) across Flan-T5-11B, GPT-NeoX-20B and LLaMA-7B, against M (no memory), M w/Ocorr (correct-answer memory), M w/Oerr (mistake memory without feedback) and Self-Refine baselines, plus a 10%-training-data data-efficiency ablation.
numeros_clave: SALAM boosts accuracy up to +6.6 on BBH and +12.6 on BBQ over the best baseline (Abstract); Flan-T5 average BBH accuracy: M 42.4 -> SALAM 48.6 (Table 2, p.6); with only 10% training data SALAM still beats full-data M w/Ocorr and M w/Oerr on most BBH subtasks (Table 3, p.7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Directly measured: 'failure can sometimes be more valuable than success' — M w/Oerr (mistake memory) frequently outperforms M w/Ocorr (correct-answer memory) in Table 2 (p.6) — strong support for MF's investment in negative-knowledge (gotcha) memory over positive-example stores.

Retrieval is filtered by an explicit similarity threshold (theta=0.9, top-k=1) and its value is isolated against a no-feedback mistake-retrieval ablation (M w/Oerr) separating retrieval-only from retrieval+feedback gains (§4.3, p.6) — matches MF's measured-retrieval stance.

The study assistant is deliberately a small 7B model fine-tuned once and reused across all downstream tasks/LLMs rather than fine-tuning the large executor per task, explicitly framed as more cost-effective (§1 'Lightweight' advantage, p.2).

notes: Table 2 (p.6, main results) + the 'failure can sometimes be more valuable than success' discussion (p.6, §4.4). Clearly on-topic negative-knowledge memory paper; not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). StackPlanner: A Centralized Hierarchical Multi-Agent System with Task-Experience Memory Management.
problema: Centralized multi-agent coordinators accumulate task memory passively (fixed summarization/truncation), causing context bloat and error propagation over long-horizon tasks, and rarely reuse cross-task coordination experience, producing poor cold-start performance on novel tasks.
mecanismo: A hierarchical coordinator exposes memory operations as first-class RL-trained actions (PLAN/DELEGATE/REVISE/FINISH): REVISE actively condenses (pop-summarize-push) or prunes a LIFO task-memory stack, while a separate structured experience memory (user profiles, semantic facts, procedural SOPs) is retrieved cross-task to mitigate cold start; the whole policy (planning + memory + retrieval) is trained jointly with GRPO using a trajectory-level task-success reward plus a process reward tied to REVISE actions.
evaluacion: Evaluated on multi-hop QA (2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue), agentic benchmarks (GAIA, FRAMES) and open-ended DeepResearch Bench (RACE/FACT metrics) with Qwen2.5-3B/7B backbones, against Naive/Single-agent/Multi-agent/Agentic-RL baselines, plus a task-memory/experience-memory component ablation and a 100-instance multi-turn human-in-the-loop refinement test.
numeros_clave: Qwen2.5-3B F1 32.92/16.48/7.71/16.23 (2Wiki/MuSiQue/GAIA/FRAMES) rising to 38.34/22.01/9.45/19.44 with Qwen2.5-7B (Table 1, p.6); ablation on MuSiQue: removing task memory drops F1 16.48->10.76, removing experience memory ->8.99, removing both ->7.43 (Table 4, p.7); multi-turn refinement total score 71.11 vs 56-60 for ReAct baselines (Table 3, p.7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The coordinator's task-memory stack IS the plan/execution-trace state, explicitly separated from cross-task experience memory and manipulated only via a first-class REVISE action (push/condense/prune, §3.2, p.4) — direct precedent for treating plan-state itself as a governed memory tier, as MF's PLAN-ESTADO axis proposes.

REVISE's pruning path retains 'a concise record of failure causes... to guide subsequent exploration' when dropping unproductive memory segments (§3.1, p.4) — negative knowledge is preserved even when its raw trace is discarded, a pattern MF could adopt for gotcha compaction.

Active memory condensation/pruning is motivated explicitly as mitigating 'context bloat' and processing pressure on the central agent (§1 Challenge 1, p.1) and its value is measured via the ablation's accuracy delta (Table 4, p.7), supporting MF's context-economy stance that bounded, curated context beats unbounded accumulation.

notes: Table 1 (p.6, main benchmark) + Table 4 ablation (p.7) are load-bearing; plan_estado=SI is directly satisfied by the task-memory-stack design (§3.2, Fig.2, p.4). Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Sidik, B. y Rokach, L. (2026). MEMTIER: Tiered Memory Architecture and the Retrieval Bottleneck in Long-Running LLM Agents.
problema: Long-running agent runtimes (OpenClaw, 250k+ deployments) store all memory in flat MEMORY.md/daily-log files, causing four compounding failures (hard-cap truncation, compaction behavioural breaks, structural blindness of flat-text retrieval, and no attribution loop linking tool outcomes back to memory quality), degrading tool-success rates 14pp over a 72-hour window.
mecanismo: A tripartite plugin architecture: (1a) a structured episodic JSONL store with a cognitive-weight field updated from tool-outcome attribution; (1b) a 5-signal weighted BM25+decay+cognitive-weight+tier retrieval scorer with two-stage semantic-tier-then-episodic scoping; (1c) an attribution loop distributing tool-outcome credit to retrieved entries; (2a) an async consolidation daemon promoting episodic facts to a project-shared semantic tier via LLM extraction; (2b) a PPO trainer adapting the 5-signal weights from task-success reward.
evaluacion: Evaluated on the full LongMemEval-S (N=500, 5 ability types) with Qwen2.5-7B on a 6GB consumer GPU, plus LoCoMo for comparison, a full component-removal / retrieval-budget / token-budget ablation (Table 2), a BM25-normalisation probe, a dense-retrieval (bge-small) comparison, and an oracle-retrieval upper bound.
numeros_clave: Acc 0.050->0.382 (no-retrieval vs full system), F1 0.412; semantic pre-population is the dominant component (-0.128 Acc / ~2.9x F1 if removed); LLM-extracted facts ~3.1/question vs heuristic ~509/question (164x reduction, ~$0.05 total for 500 questions); oracle retrieval 0.550 vs system 0.350 (+0.200 gap); dense Stage-1 scoping +0.030 Acc overall but knowledge-update category regresses -0.125; PPO-learned weights numerically identical to defaults (Acc=0.382, Table 2/4, p.5-7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper explicitly documents negative/null results — removing the cognitive-weight signal HELPS slightly (+0.012 to +0.014 Acc) and PPO weight-learning yields zero measurable gain (§4.4, Table 2/4, p.6-7) — a rare, honest admission of what does not work, confirming MF's need to capture negative findings as first-class knowledge.

The two-stage semantic-tier-to-episodic scoping acts as a derived cache narrowing the retrieval pool before full scoring (§3.2, removing it costs -0.040 Acc); the dense-vs-BM25 comparison shows a category-dependent tradeoff (multi-session +0.077, knowledge-update -0.125, §4.1, p.6-7) — a nuanced extension of MF's derived-index concept.

Token-efficiency finding: LLM-extracted facts (~3.1/question) beat heuristic extraction (~509/question) by ~2.9x F1 for ~$0.05 total preprocessing cost on 500 questions (§3, p.4) — precision beats coverage, directly confirming MF's context-economy stance.

Retrieval quality is measured directly (Recall@k, nDCG@4) and an oracle-retrieval upper bound (0.550 vs system 0.350, +0.200 gap) proves retrieval, not generation, is the bottleneck (§4.2, §5, p.7-8) — supports MF's insistence that retrieval must be measured.

notes: Table 2 ablation (p.5-6) + §4.1 dense-retrieval baseline + §4.4 PPO trainer (p.7) are the load-bearing measurements. Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Kwon and Bang (2026). What Spatial Memory Must Store: Occlusion as the Test for Language-Agent Memory.
problema: Language-agent 'memory palace' systems anchor memories to world coordinates on the intuition that geometry adds retrieval power text cannot, but that intuition is rarely tested: it is unclear whether spatial anchoring should reweight ranking, or instead gate a separate geometric predicate such as visibility/occlusion that flat text or vector retrieval structurally cannot compute.
mecanismo: An agent captures observations while moving through a shared voxel world, writing memories anchored to a 3D subject cell; five representations are compared (text-only cosine null, coordinate-distance recall, a field-of-view cone, and cone-plus-line-of-sight via a ray-versus-voxel DDA re-pointed from the agent's own gaze-ray primitive), isolating whether geometry should be folded into a ranking blend (spatial-as-ranker) or used to select-then-verify a geometric predicate (spatial-as-index/verification), with occlusion as the irreducible test case.
evaluacion: A pre-registered recall experiment (ranker-blend vs. geometry-led weighting vs. position-blind baseline, Wilcoxon test); controlled voxel-simulation pilots on near-duplicate localization and occlusion (McNemar tests, n up to 1144 targets); and a git-committed live pre-registration on the running text-agent relay (SPMEM-OCC-LIVE-v1, 8 worlds, 96 behind-wall targets, pooled exact McNemar).
numeros_clave: Shipped linear blend fails its own frozen test (mean deltaHit@5 -0.0375, Wilcoxon p=0.306, CI includes 0) while geometry-led weighting wins (+0.3208, p<1e-15); near-duplicate localization 1.000 (coordinate recall) vs 0.533 (text null), McNemar p<1e-6; occlusion: text/FoV-cone 0.000 vs cone+DDA 0.982 on 849 behind-wall targets (McNemar p<1e-6); live confirmation false-visible 1.000->0.000, pooled exact McNemar p=2.5e-29; return-and-resume action task: world-bound 1.000 vs flattened 0.611 (p=0.016).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper reports a measured negative result about its own default mechanism: the shipped spatial-proximity-in-a-linear-blend ranker ties or loses to a position-blind baseline (mean deltaHit@5 -0.0375, p=0.306, §6.8) — a documented case of a plausible-sounding feature that does not help, reported honestly rather than hidden.

The central methodological move is refusing to assume geometry helps and instead measuring ranker-form vs index/verification-form separately (§3, §6.8) — direct support for MF's insistence that retrieval mechanisms be measured, not assumed, before being adopted.

The return-and-resume task shows world-bound memory correctly preserves a 'prior-progress note' enabling an agent to resume unfinished work (1.000) while flattened memory discards it and restarts from scratch (0.611, p=0.016, §6.7) — a concrete instance of binding progress/plan-state to a persistent anchor rather than flat text, relevant to MF's plan-state-as-memory axis even though the paper's domain (3D spatial anchoring) is not MF's.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: domain is embodied 3D spatial/occlusion memory in a voxel game world (Space Zero), quite orthogonal to Meta-Factory's software-factory memory use case; digested per protocol because plan_estado=SI and the ranker-vs-index/measured-negative-result methodology (§3, §6.8, p.5-6) does transfer, but direct applicability is genuinely doubtful.

cita: Jiang et al. (2026). ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education.
problema: Multi-round reflection lets an LLM agent recover from failures within a single task, but each task remains an isolated episode: lessons paid for in tokens across many reflection rounds on one task (e.g. a wrong formula, a bad transition timing) are discarded before the next task begins, forcing the agent to re-derive the same class of mistake every time.
mecanismo: A vision-language model scores rendered keyframes of a Manim animation on multiple pedagogical axes; the score both drives an in-task visual-reflection repair loop and gates writes to a dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank: a positive channel M+ stores success rationales (score>=85) as soft Reference Examples, a negative channel M- stores validated failure->success transitions (crash->success, or a >=5-point score improvement) as hard Known Pitfalls; both are LLM-distilled (not literal diffs) and retrieved per-polarity by task embedding on future tasks.
evaluacion: Fixed-probe evaluation (frozen EMB snapshots at K in {0,50,100,200} tested read-only on disjoint probe tasks) against no-memory, matched-budget Manim-code RAG, and shuffled Random-EMB baselines, with blind human Pass@1/quality scoring plus reflection-round counts as headline metrics (VLM scores kept as auxiliary diagnostics only to avoid evaluator leakage), and a channel/gating ablation (Table 1).
numeros_clave: EMB@0->EMB@200: Human Pass@1 62.0->84.9%, quality 3.26->3.88, reflection rounds 12.2->6.5; beats Manim-code RAG (83.3%/3.65/11.4) on all three headline metrics at K=200; ablation 'No M-' (drop negative channel) drops Pass@1 to 75.0 (Table 1, p.8); write gates theta_high=85, delta_fail>=5, k+=2/k-=3.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The negative channel M- stores validated failure patterns as hard 'Known Pitfalls' gated by causal attribution (crash->success or scored improvement >=5, §3.3), and removing it measurably costs Pass@1 (Table 1, p.8) — direct empirical support for MF's investment in negative-knowledge memory.

Both channels are distilled by a dedicated LLM agent at consolidation time rather than storing literal before/after diffs, specifically to strip scene-specific tokens that would mislead retrieval (§3.3 'Lessons are LLM-distilled, not literal diffs') — a concrete gated-distillation recipe MF could adopt when promoting gotchas to durable recipes.

The paper explicitly guards against evaluator leakage — the same VLM scores outputs AND gates memory writes — by using blind human judgement as the headline metric and VLM scores only as auxiliary diagnostics (§3, §4.3, p.6) — direct precedent for MF's fidelity concern about self-referential evaluation loops.

A Random-EMB (shuffled content, matched retrieval budget) baseline isolates format effects from actual memory content ('rules out generic memory-format-context explanations', Table 1) — a rigorous measured-retrieval control matching MF's G-M2 stance.

notes: Table 1 (p.8, headline + ablation blocks) is the load-bearing evidence; the explicit evaluator-leakage discussion (§3, p.6) is notable methodology. Not RECONSIDERAR — clearly on-topic dual-channel negative/positive memory paper.

cita: Talebirad et al. (2026). From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents.
problema: In multi-agent LLM coordination (here, inventing a shared communication code from scratch in a Lewis signaling game), it is unclear whether successful convention formation is driven mainly by channel/vocabulary capacity or by what kind of persistent memory architecture each agent carries across rounds, since prior work treats capacity as the main lever and rarely controls for memory structure.
mecanismo: Five memory architectures (stateless rolling-window-only, a shared environment-compiled convention board, a private overwritten free-text scratchpad, a private fixed-capacity slot-list codebook, and a codebook plus a persistent meta-note) are compared for two frozen LLM agents (sender/receiver) playing 200-round signaling games; each store differs only in how it is updated (overwrite, in-place slot edit, or environment-compiled), and three studies isolate memory architecture from channel capacity and from history-window length.
evaluacion: Study 1 compares all five architectures at fixed capacity (3 seeds); Study 2 sweeps channel capacity |V|^L from 4 to 125 for the two most distinct architectures (up to 8 seeds at the predicted bottleneck); Study 3 sweeps the rolling-window size directly to separate consolidation from raw history length; metrics are task accuracy, TopSim compositionality, positional mutual information, and lexicon collision rate.
numeros_clave: Persistent private scratchpad reaches 0.867+-0.023 accuracy at capacity=25, the most reliable coordination in the study, avoiding the high-capacity collapse of stateless 'memory only' agents (0.80->0.52 at cap=64, collision rate 1.0); the predicted information-bottleneck optimum (cap=8) is instead a fragility point (bimodal outcomes, permutation p=0.024); un-pruned codebook memory peaks early (P1-color purity 0.96 at 50 rounds) but degrades to 0.527+-0.13 late-game accuracy as stale/conflicting slots accumulate; codebook-plus-meta-note ends lowest (0.460+-0.14) because the meta-note freezes into generic restated instructions rather than higher-order insight (Study 1 discussion, Table 2-3, p.3-4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The un-pruned slot-list ('codebook') memory shows fast early convergence but no durable consolidation: without a pruning mechanism, stale and conflicting entries accumulate over 200 rounds and drag performance down to 0.527 late-game accuracy (Study 1 discussion, p.3-4) — a measured negative result supporting MF's stance that unbounded, unpruned memory accumulation degrades usefulness over time.

The 'codebook meta' condition adds a persistent meta-note meant to capture higher-order structural rules, but inspection shows the note freezes by round 30 into generic restatements of the prompt's own instructions rather than genuine distilled insight, making it the weakest private-memory condition (0.460+-0.14, p.4) — a cautionary data point about naive self-summarization as a consolidation mechanism, without directly confirming or refuting a specific MF choice.

The single shared public convention table ('env board') achieves the highest raw accuracy (0.827+-0.09) precisely because both agents read one authoritative source instead of maintaining separate private derived conventions, though at the cost of near-zero compositional structure (a memorized lookup, not a productive code, §Study 1) — supports MF's single-source-per-fact stance while flagging its tradeoff against agent-internal understanding.

notes: Table 2/3 (p.3-4, Study 1) and Table 4/5 + Fig.4 (Study 2, p.5) are the load-bearing numbers; domain is emergent-communication research (Lewis signaling games), not software agents, but the core finding (memory architecture > channel capacity; un-pruned memory degrades) is a direct, generalizable memory-architecture result. Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Toeda (2026). Memory Is Not Live State — Cross-Agent Memory Governance by Transplanting the Reflective Context Governor onto Agent Memory (memgov v0.1.0).
problema: Persistent agent memory is written as a snapshot of the world but the world keeps changing after the snapshot is taken; in a workspace with two or more agents working in parallel sessions, status-bearing memory claims ('not yet deposited', 'tool X is broken') go stale routinely and are trusted at session start as if they were current truth, with no mechanism verifying them against the world before the agent acts.
mecanismo: A commitment-surface table (SHARED_STATE) holds one row per cross-agent live fact, each with an absolute date and a verification anchor (a command/path/API yielding ground truth); a deterministic drift scanner sweeps every fragmented memory store for lines that still assert a status the commitment surface says is resolved, producing a CONFLICT_MAP; flagged lines enter a non-compensatory review queue (no plausibility/recency can excuse a flagged claim, only verification against the anchor); a freshness heartbeat flags stale status-bearing files with governed friction (suppression after reconciliation) to avoid training users to ignore warnings; each agent corrects only its own store, with cross-agent fixes routed through the shared commitment surface.
evaluacion: A real two-agent (Claude Code + GPT Codex) workspace incident (2026-07-06/07) is analyzed for root cause, the countermeasure (memgov v0.1.0) is deployed the same day, and the first scan-repair-rescan cycle is measured via an append-only ledger; a companion RCGov (context-governance) engine comparison is planned but not yet run.
numeros_clave: First full scan: 73 memory files across 4 stores vs 7 committed rows -> 17 suspected drifts, including 3 papers misremembered as unpublished (already published the prior day) and a repaired toolchain still remembered as broken (12 days stale); after correction, re-scan -> 14 remaining drifts (§5); freshness heartbeat default threshold 2 days, suppression 3 days after reconciliation (§4); released tool is 124 KB with zero runtime dependencies and 10 tests (§6).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central incident is a stale-memory near-miss: an agent's persistent memory asserted a status-bearing claim ('not yet deposited') that had been false for a day, caught only because a machine-readable ledger was consulted before acting (§2) — direct real-world evidence for MF's FIDELIDAD concern about staleness and provenance in memory.

SHARED_STATE is literally a plan/status table — one row per status-bearing fact with an absolute date and a verification anchor, overwritten in place by whichever session changes it (§4 point 1) — a concrete, deployed instance of plan-state-as-first-class-memory, directly matching MF's PLAN-ESTADO axis.

Root-cause analysis names three structural findings worse than the individual error — store fragmentation, an unsatisfiable guard that trained its audience to ignore it, and 12-day-stale cross-agent memory (§2) — the paper explicitly captures 'what went wrong structurally' as durable governance knowledge, not just the incident.

A drift scanner sweeps every fragmented private memory store against the single committed SHARED_STATE table and flags contradictions as a CONFLICT_MAP (§4 points 1-2) — a concrete single-source-of-truth-vs-multi-store reconciliation mechanism MF could adopt for its own multi-store seams.

notes: §2 incident timeline (2026-07-06/07) and §5 first-scan ledger figures (17->14 drifts) are the load-bearing evidence; the paper names an AI co-observer in its method note, which does not affect the measured incident/ledger claims. Not RECONSIDERAR — a first-party governance case study squarely on FIDELIDAD/PLAN-ESTADO.

cita: Xiong, Z., Lin, Y., Xie, W., He, P., Liu, Z., Tang, J., Lakkaraju, H., & Xiang, Z. (2025). How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior.
problema: Memory addition and deletion are core, widely-used operations in LLM agent episodic memory, but their long-term behavioral effects are poorly understood: naive strategies risk silently degrading agent performance over time as noisy or misaligned past experiences accumulate and get replayed as demonstrations.
mecanismo: Controlled experiments isolate memory addition (add-all vs. three automatic 'coarse' trajectory evaluators vs. a strict human/oracle evaluator vs. a fixed-memory no-addition baseline) and memory deletion (periodic frequency-based, history-based utility-weighted, and a combined strategy) across a synthetic RegAgent and three real agents (EHRAgent, AgentDriver, CIC-IoT Agent), measuring the correlation between input-similarity and output-similarity of retrieved demonstrations (the 'experience-following' property) and comparing against error-free ground-truth counterfactuals to isolate error propagation.
evaluacion: Long-running execution streams (thousands of tasks) across 4 agents, 5 addition evaluators and 3 deletion strategies, tracking success-rate/accuracy vs. memory size (Tables 1-2), plus stress tests under task-distribution shift and memory-capacity constraints.
numeros_clave: Strict evaluator: AgentDriver success rate 51.00 (mem size 1178) vs add-all 32.32 (mem 2125) vs fixed-memory baseline 40.11 (mem 180); CIC-IoT strict 85.40 vs add-all 59.90 (Table 1); combined deletion on CIC-IoT reaches 85.50 accuracy at mem size 188 (vs 904 with no deletion, Table 2); history-based deletion + strict evaluator on AgentDriver (51.81) exceeds the error-free ground-truth counterfactual (§4.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: 'Error propagation' is measured directly: noisy add-all/coarse-evaluator memories cause a persistent performance gap vs. an error-free ground-truth counterfactual that widens as execution continues (§3.4, Fig.4) — hard evidence that ungated writes actively poison future agent behavior, supporting MF's negative-knowledge / anti-poisoning stance.

Memory addition is explicitly gated by a trajectory evaluator (add-all vs. coarse-automatic vs. strict/human), and a fine-tuned coarse evaluator (300 examples) already rivals the strict human gate while beating add-all on every agent (Table 1, p.4) — concrete evidence for MF's write-trigger stance that admission must be judged, not automatic.

History-based deletion — removing records whose average downstream retrieval utility falls below a threshold — outperforms simple frequency-based pruning and, on AgentDriver, even beats the error-free baseline (§4.2-4.3, Table 2) — a measured recipe for promoting/demoting stored experience by outcome rather than recency.

The 'experience-following' property (near-perfect correlation between input and output similarity, Fig.3, §3.3) formalizes how directly agents imitate retrieved records — a measurable diagnostic MF could reuse to detect when its own memory is being copied verbatim rather than reasoned over.

notes: Table 1/2 (p.4/6) and Fig.3/4 (experience-following, error propagation) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a core empirical memory-management study, squarely on-topic.

cita: Xu (2025). Memory Management and Contextual Consistency for Long-Running Low-Code Agents.
problema: Long-running low-code/no-code (LCNC) agents suffer 'memory inflation' (dialogue/tool history growing linearly and blowing the context window and token cost) and 'contextual degradation' (older critical information being pushed out, causing incoherent, self-contradicting behavior), and non-technical LCNC users have no way to inspect or correct what the agent remembers.
mecanismo: A hybrid episodic+semantic memory store applies an 'Intelligent Decay' mechanism: each episodic entry gets a composite Utility Score S = alpha*Recency + beta*Relevance(cosine) + gamma*UserUtility; entries below a threshold are deleted or, if flagged, LLM-summarized into the semantic store (Algorithm 1); a proposed timeline UI lets non-technical users pin/forget/consolidate memories directly, setting the UserUtility term as a hard human-in-the-loop signal.
evaluacion: A single simulated long-running LCNC task (drafting a multi-week project plan over 500 turns) compares a 10-turn sliding-window baseline, a basic-RAG (episodic retrieval, no decay) baseline, and the proposed hybrid system on task completion rate, token cost, latency, and an LLM-judge consistency/contradiction-rate metric (Table 1, Fig.2).
numeros_clave: Table 1: task completion 65.2% (sliding window) / 81.4% (basic RAG) / 92.5% (hybrid); average token cost per turn 580/1150/890; contradiction rate 18.1%/5.5%/1.2%. However, Appendix A's own simulation code shows the headline Figure 2 'self-degradation vs. self-evolution' curves are produced by hand-written exponential-decay and hard-clamped functions explicitly commented 'for realistic visualization', not by measured agent runs — this digest cites Table 1 but flags it as unverified/simulated evidence (§5, Appendix A).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper frames its design around the 'self-degradation' problem measured in prior real work (error propagation / misaligned experience replay, cited as ref [6]), but its own demonstration of that problem (Fig.2 'All-Add' decay curve) is a hand-tuned simulation per Appendix A's code, not an independent measurement, so it should not be read as additional confirming evidence on its own.

Appendix A's simulation code (hardcoded exponential decay plus a range 'clamped ... for realistic visualization') reveals that the headline self-degradation-vs-evolution curve is synthetic rather than measured — a direct illustration of MF's FIDELIDAD concern (fabricated/unverifiable evidence) applied to the source paper itself, not just to agent memories it describes.

The Intelligent Decay Utility Score S=alpha*R+beta*E+gamma*U with a threshold-gated consolidate-or-delete branch (§3.2, Algorithm 1) is a concrete, tunable formalization of gotcha promotion/pruning MF could reference as a design pattern, independent of whether this paper's own evaluation is simulated.

A reported 22% token-cost reduction versus basic RAG alongside higher task completion (Table 1, §5.3) matches MF's context-economy framing, though the FIDELIDAD caveat above applies to how confidently this specific number should be trusted.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: Appendix A's own simulation code (hardcoded exponential-decay and hand-clamped ranges explicitly commented 'for realistic visualization') indicates Figure 2, and plausibly Table 1, are synthetic illustrations rather than measured agent runs; reference [6] also appears to attribute the real experience-following/self-degradation study (cf. the Xiong et al. paper in this same digestion wave) to different, seemingly fictitious authors and a mismatched venue (Nature Communications). Digested per protocol; flagging for human review given the evidence-fabrication risk.

cita: Yang et al. (2023). Failures Pave the Way: Enhancing Large Language Models through Tuning-free Rule Accumulation.
problema: Frozen (API-only, non-fine-tunable) LLMs deployed on streaming data keep repeating the same class of mistake because nothing persists across inputs, while existing prompt-optimization approaches assume a static training set rather than an unbounded online stream of tasks.
mecanismo: Tuning-free Rule Accumulation (TRAN): on each mistake the LLM generates candidate 'if...then...' rules, retests them and keeps only rules that actually fix the current error; if none work, the failed case is stored in a separate mistake collection and later retrieved (by similarity) to summarize a rule jointly from multiple related failures; a maintenance step uses the LLM itself to detect and discard redundant or contradictory incoming rules against the existing collection, and an LRU eviction policy caps the collection size; at inference, BM25 retrieves the top rules for the current input and prepends them to the base prompt.
evaluacion: Evaluated on BBQ-Lite (7 social-bias multi-choice tasks), TweetEval/AGNews/DBPedia text classification, and Dyck Language generation, in zero-shot and few-shot streaming settings, against Zero-Shot CoT, Auto-CoT and SALAM baselines, plus an ablation removing LRU / multi-mistake summarization / duplicate-contradiction checking, and out-of-domain rule-transfer and counterfactual-distribution-shift stress tests.
numeros_clave: Zero-shot BBQ-Lite average 91.6% (TRAN) vs 75.4% (frozen model) vs 82.8% (SALAM), +8.8pp over SALAM (Table 1); mistake-rate reduction of ~40% (zero-shot) / ~20% (few-shot) after 700 samples (Fig.3); ablation: removing multi-mistake summarization costs ~3pp average accuracy, removing the LRU cap costs up to 4.5pp on the Disability task (10/39/15 rules pruned per task, Table 4); out-of-domain rule transfer from Physical to SES task gives +10% accuracy (Fig.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The entire framework is built from observed mistakes only: a rule is admitted to the collection only after being tested and shown to fix the specific failure it was derived from (§2.3, process (b)) — direct support for MF's negative-knowledge stance that durable memory should be built from validated failures, not just accumulated observations.

Rule maintenance uses the LLM itself to detect near-duplicate/contradictory incoming rules against the existing collection and keep only the newest (§2.4), plus LRU eviction once a size threshold is crossed — measured to matter (ablation: removing LRU costs up to 4.5pp, Table 4) — a concrete self-managed pruning recipe MF could adopt.

Retrieval uses plain BM25 over the rule collection (top-3 of up to 100 rules) and the paper explicitly measures the value of summarizing across MULTIPLE related mistakes versus a single one (removing this costs performance, Table 4) rather than assuming richer retrieval helps — matches MF's measured-retrieval stance.

Rules are deliberately kept independent of, and composable with, the base prompt and other prompting strategies (CoT), shown to compose additively (+4.3 to +9.6pp when combined with CoT, Table 5) — a pattern of a single reusable knowledge store composing cleanly across surfaces, relevant to MF's single-source-per-fact stance.

notes: Table 1 (p.5, BBQ-Lite) + Table 4 (p.6, ablation) + Fig.3/4 (mistake-rate reduction, out-of-domain transfer) are load-bearing. Not RECONSIDERAR — a foundational negative-knowledge/rule-accumulation paper, squarely on-topic.

cita: Zheng, S., He, K., Yang, L. y Xiong, J. (2024). MemoryRepository for AI NPC.
problema: LLM-based game NPCs lack long-term, human-like memory: without persistent memory NPCs cannot recall past interactions, breaking narrative coherence, while simply keeping all history is infeasible under a hard token budget and does not resemble human forgetting/consolidation.
mecanismo: MemoryRepository splits each NPC's memory into a Short-Term Memory Room (full detail, capped at 10 dialogue turns) and a Long-Term Memory Room (compact summaries); a scheduling policy summarizes and forgets short-term entries into long-term memory in parallel (not sequentially) once the turn cap is reached under the fixed token budget T(P)+T(C)+T(M)<=T_limit; retrieval uses an Interactive Dual-Tower DSSM (ID-DSSM, a dual-encoder over dialogue-turn embeddings) with ANN indexing akin to FAISS to fetch the most relevant memory unit for the current turn.
evaluacion: A 400-question (200 LLM-generated + 200 human-authored) validation set is scored by human annotators on 4 metrics (memory retrieval accuracy, response correctness, contextual coherence, human-likeness) across GPT-4/GPT-3.5/ChatGLM with and without MemoryRepository, plus a head-to-head comparison against MemGPT at dialogue round 100, and a robustness sweep over temperature/top-p.
numeros_clave: At round 100, MemGPT vs MemoryRepository-embedded GPT-3.5: retrieval 0.831 vs 0.806, correctness 0.713 vs 0.705, coherence 0.874 vs 0.886, human-like 0.718 vs 0.861 (Table 3) — MemoryRepository trades a small retrieval/correctness cost for a large human-likeness gain; short-term room capped at 10 dialogue turns before forced summarization; the authors' own baseline comparison shows correctness roughly unchanged while retrieval DECLINES after adding the forgetting mechanism (§VI.B.1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The authors explicitly report that adding the forgetting/summarization mechanism does NOT improve correctness and DEGRADES the retrieval metric versus the no-memory baseline (§VI.B.1) — an honest, measured tradeoff (fidelity for human-likeness) rather than a hidden or glossed-over cost, which is itself the kind of negative/limitation finding MF values.

Summarization and forgetting are explicitly modeled as simultaneous, not sequential, processes — short-term entries are pruned AND distilled into long-term memory in the same pass once a fixed turn budget (10 turns) is reached (§III.C.2, Eq.2) — a concrete recency-triggered consolidation cadence MF could reference.

The whole architecture is explicitly derived from a hard token-budget constraint T(P)+T(C)+T(M)<=T_limit (Eq.1, §III.C) — memory tiering exists specifically to store more information without raising the token ceiling, directly matching MF's context-economy framing.

Retrieval quality is measured against a real competing system (MemGPT) at a fixed dialogue depth rather than assumed superior (Table 3, §VI.B.2), though the comparison is a single-round snapshot rather than a longitudinal ablation, limiting how strongly it can be read as MF's fuller measured-retrieval standard.

notes: Table 3 (p.11, MemGPT comparison) + §VI.B.1 (retrieval-degradation trade-off) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a direct long-term/human-like memory architecture paper for LLM agents.

cita: Ge, Y., Romeo, S., Cai, J., Shu, R., Benajiba, Y., Sunkara, M., & Zhang, Y. (2025). TReMu: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Temporal Reasoning for LLM-Agents with Memory in Multi-Session Dialogues.
problema: Temporal reasoning across multi-session dialogues is under-benchmarked and hard for LLM agents: relative-time expressions require inferring an event's true date separately from when it was mentioned, and cross-session dependencies require correctly relating events retrieved from different, possibly stale, sessions.
mecanismo: TReMu combines time-aware memorization (per-session timeline summarization that extracts events and infers their absolute dates, explicitly distinguishing occurrence-time from mention-time, then organizes memory as an indexed timeline) with neuro-symbolic reasoning (retrieved memory is fed to an LLM that generates executable Python code using datetime/dateutil plus custom helper functions like weekRange, as the reasoning rationale before answering).
evaluacion: A new multi-choice temporal-QA benchmark built by augmenting LoCoMo (3 question types: Temporal Anchoring/Precedence/Interval, plus unanswerable questions) is evaluated on GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini/GPT-3.5-Turbo against Standard Prompting, CoT, MemoChat, MemoChat+CoT and Timeline+CoT baselines, with an ablation isolating memory representation (Timeline vs MemoChat) from reasoning strategy (CoT vs neuro-symbolic code), plus a code-execution-failure-rate diagnostic.
numeros_clave: GPT-4o overall accuracy: Standard Prompting 29.83 -> CoT 61.67 -> TReMu 77.67 (Table 5); ablation isolates two independent gains: Timeline+CoT (71.50) over MemoChat+CoT (41.67) shows time-aware memorization alone adds ~30pp, and TReMu (77.67) over Timeline+CoT (71.50) shows neuro-symbolic reasoning adds a further ~6pp; unanswerable-question F1 20.84->64.42 on GPT-4o (SP vs TReMu, Table 5); memory mechanisms HURT GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini vs plain CoT but HELPED the shorter-context GPT-3.5-Turbo (§4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper measures, rather than assumes, WHEN memory augmentation helps: MemoChat/Timeline memory mechanisms underperform plain CoT for GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini (whose native context already fits the whole dialogue) but improve results for the shorter-context GPT-3.5-Turbo (§4.2) — a measured conditional/negative finding that memory augmentation is not a universal win, supporting MF's stance of validating a mechanism's value rather than assuming it.

Time-aware memorization writes fine-grained memory pieces that explicitly separate an event's inferred OCCURRENCE date from its MENTION date and organizes them into an indexed timeline rather than one holistic per-session summary (§3.2.1, Table 3 vs Table 4 examples) — a concrete consolidation schema (date-anchored granular facts vs. lossy holistic summary) MF could adopt for its own docs/gotcha memory.

Distinguishing 'when an event occurred' from 'when it was mentioned' (§3.2.1) is precisely a provenance/staleness discipline — the memory schema itself encodes freshness/anchor metadata, directly matching MF's FIDELIDAD concern.

Structuring memory as a timeline of dated, retrievable event summaries (rather than raw dialogue or an undated blob, §3.2.1) is a concrete typed-narrative memory representation, relevant to MF's TIER-DOCS emphasis on dated, structured truth over flat text.

notes: Table 5 (p.9, GPT-4o results + ablation) and §4.2 discussion (memory hurts sufficiently-large-context models but helps GPT-3.5) are the load-bearing findings. Not RECONSIDERAR — a direct memory + temporal-reasoning paper for multi-session dialogue agents.

cita: Ouyang et al. (2025). ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory.
problema: LLM agents in persistent, long-running roles fail to learn from accumulated interaction history, repeating past errors and discarding insights; prior agent memory designs mostly store raw trajectories or only successful routines, leaving lessons from failures largely unexploited.
mecanismo: ReasoningBank distills structured memory items (title/description/content) from BOTH successful and failed trajectories, using an LLM-as-a-judge (no ground truth) to label outcomes; retrieval is embedding-based top-k similarity search injected as system instructions; new items are consolidated back via a simple addition operation, forming a closed retrieve-extract-consolidate loop; memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS) further scales this by generating multiple trajectories per task (parallel self-contrast or sequential self-refinement) to produce richer contrastive signal for higher-quality memory curation.
evaluacion: Evaluated on WebArena, Mind2Web (web navigation/generalization) and SWE-Bench-Verified (repo-level issue resolving) with Gemini-2.5-flash/pro and Claude-3.7-sonnet backbones, against No-Memory, Synapse (trajectory memory) and AWM (workflow/success-only memory) baselines, reporting success rate and interaction-step efficiency, plus MaTTS scaling curves.
numeros_clave: WebArena overall success-rate gains of +8.3/+7.2/+4.6 over no-memory across the 3 backbones (Table 1); up to 16% fewer interaction steps and up to 20% relative effectiveness improvement (Abstract); SWE-Bench-Verified resolve rate 34.2->38.8 (Gemini-2.5-flash) and 54.0->57.4 (Gemini-2.5-pro) vs no-memory (Table 2); on the cross-website 'Multi' WebArena subset, AWM (success-only memory) actually DEGRADES vs no-memory while ReasoningBank still gains +4.6 SR (§4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: ReasoningBank explicitly extracts memory items from FAILED trajectories too (via LLM-as-judge outcome labeling, no ground truth needed) rather than success-only routines, and this is shown to matter directly: on WebArena's cross-website 'Multi' subset, the success-only AWM baseline DEGRADES vs no-memory while ReasoningBank still gains +4.6 SR (§4.2, Table 1) — strong evidence that negative/failure knowledge is load-bearing for generalization, confirming MF's negative-knowledge stance.

Memory consolidation is a simple addition into a growing repository rather than complex merging (§3.2), and memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS) shows that USING contrastive signal from multiple trajectories of the SAME task (self-contrast) to curate memory produces measurably better memory than treating each trajectory independently (§3.3, §4.3-4.4) — a concrete recipe for higher-quality consolidation MF could adopt when synthesizing recipes from repeated similar gotchas.

Writes are gated by an LLM-as-a-judge outcome signal (success/failure) rather than admitted unconditionally, and both branches (success->validated strategy, failure->counterfactual pitfall) are explicitly distilled with different extraction strategies (§3.2) — matches MF's stance that memory admission needs a judged trigger, not automatic accumulation.

Effectiveness AND efficiency (interaction steps) are both reported as first-class measured outcomes against multiple real baselines (trajectory-based Synapse, workflow-based AWM) across 3 different backbone LLMs (Table 1-3) rather than assuming memory helps — matches MF's measured-retrieval standard.

notes: Table 1 (p.7, WebArena) + Table 2 (SWE-Bench-Verified) + the AWM-degrades-on-Multi-subset finding (§4.2) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a leading reasoning-memory paper, squarely on-topic and highly relevant to MF's negative-knowledge/consolidation axes.

cita: Chen et al. (2026). HaluMem: Evaluating Hallucinations in Memory Systems of Agents.
problema: Memory systems for LLM agents frequently hallucinate (fabricate, error, conflict, omit) during storage and retrieval, but existing evaluation is end-to-end question answering only, making it impossible to localize WHICH operational stage (extraction, updating, or answering) a given hallucination originates from.
mecanismo: HaluMem defines per-stage gold standards on a synthetic, six-stage-constructed, user-centered multi-turn dialogue dataset (persona -> life skeleton -> event flow -> session summaries/memory points -> full sessions -> questions): an extraction gold set of memory points that should be newly added, an updating gold set of old->new memory pairs, and a QA gold-answer set; each stage is scored independently (extraction: recall/weighted-recall/target-precision/accuracy/false-memory-resistance/F1; updating: correct-rate/hallucination-rate/omission-rate; QA: correct-rate/hallucination-rate/omission-rate) against 6 production memory systems (Mem0, Mem0-Graph, Memobase, MemOS, Supermemory, Zep).
evaluacion: Two benchmarks, HaluMem-Medium (about 15k memory points, 3.5k questions, avg 1.5k turns per user, up to 1M-token context) and HaluMem-Long (avg 2.6k turns per user, context exceeding 1M tokens with injected irrelevant dialogue), evaluated against 6 real production memory systems, plus a per-stage runtime/efficiency measurement.
numeros_clave: Extraction: all systems (except MemOS) show recall below 60% and accuracy below 62% on HaluMem-Medium (Table 3); memory-updating omission rates above 50% for most systems despite hallucination rates below 2% (few samples reach the update stage at all); QA answer accuracy below 70% for every system, degrading further on HaluMem-Long; dialogue-addition (write) time for Mem0/Mem0-Graph exceeds 2700 minutes on HaluMem-Medium, dwarfing retrieval time (Table 5) — write, not retrieval, is the computational bottleneck.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central methodological move is refusing end-to-end-only evaluation and instead localizing hallucinations to the exact operational stage (extraction vs. updating vs. QA), revealing that errors are generated and ACCUMULATE upstream (extraction/updating) then propagate downstream (Abstract, §6.2.1) — direct support for MF's stance that failures must be attributed to a specific stage/mechanism, not just observed in aggregate output.

Every production memory system tested (Mem0, Mem0-Graph, Memobase, MemOS, Supermemory) shows extraction accuracy below 62% and QA accuracy below 70%, with updating omission rates above 50% (Table 3, p.11) — hard quantitative evidence that today's real memory systems are riddled with fabrication/staleness/omission, squarely validating MF's FIDELIDAD concern as an urgent, measured problem rather than a theoretical one.

Runtime measurement shows the WRITE stage (dialogue ingestion/extraction), not retrieval, is the dominant computational cost — dialogue-addition time for Mem0/Mem0-Graph exceeds 2700 minutes on HaluMem-Medium (Table 5, §6.2.4) — confirms MF's context-economy concern should weight write-time cost, not just retrieval-time cost.

Memory updating performance is shown to be bottlenecked by extraction coverage — when a pre-update memory was never extracted, the corresponding update cannot be processed at all (§6.2.1) — a concrete causal chain (admission-gate quality gates downstream consolidation quality) relevant to MF's write-trigger design.

notes: Table 3 (p.11, per-stage hallucination results) + Table 5 (write-time bottleneck) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a rigorous operation-level hallucination benchmark directly on MF's FIDELIDAD axis, evaluating today's real production memory systems (Mem0, MemOS, Zep, etc.).

cita: Lindenbauer et al. (2025). From Knowledge to Noise: CTIM-Rover and the Pitfalls of Episodic Memory in Software Engineering Agents.
problema: Software-engineering agents (AutoCodeRover, SWE-agent) discard their episodic memory after each task instance, wasting cross-task learning opportunities; it is unclear whether an experiential-learning memory (ExpeL-style) that worked on simpler domains (QA, web shopping, ALFWorld) also transfers to the more complex, repository-level structure of real-world SE bug-fixing.
mecanismo: CTIM-Rover augments AutoCodeRover with a Mixture-of-Experts-inspired Cross-Task-Instance Memory: it collects successful (and self-reflected failure-to-success) trajectories, distills general SE knowledge and then repository-specific knowledge via an LLM (o1) in a two-phase pipeline (add/edit/upvote/downvote operations from ExpeL), caps the memory at sqrt(n) items, and separately supports exemplar retrieval of the single most similar past successful trajectory (Code-T5 embeddings, cosine similarity >=90% threshold) injected once at the start of the agent's trajectory.
evaluacion: Evaluated on a 45-sample held-out subset of SWE-bench Verified against baseline AutoCodeRover across 6 configurations (full CTIM-Rover, CTIM-only, general-CTIM-only, repo-level-CTIM-only, exemplar-only), reporting per-repository and overall success rate (Table 1), plus a manual qualitative trace analysis of two solved-by-baseline-but-failed-by-CTIM instances.
numeros_clave: Overall success rate: AutoCodeRover baseline 42% vs full CTIM-Rover 40% (-2pp) vs CTIM-only 31% (-11pp) vs repo-level-CTIM-only 31% vs exemplar-only 40% (Table 1, 45 samples); qualitative trace analysis shows a SINGLE repository-level CTIM sentence containing the word 'clean' biased the agent away from the correct patch location (django-13933); removing that one item, or even inserting an arbitrary unrelated string ('GRANDMA LIKES PASTA'), restored the correct solve on a second case (django-15987), directly demonstrating noise-not-signal causation (§5.1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: This paper's negative result IS the load-bearing finding MF's NEGATIVO axis cares about: a plausible experiential-memory mechanism was tested and shown, via controlled ablation plus causal tracing, to actively HURT (not just fail to help) — a single noisy CTIM sentence flips a correct solve to incorrect (§5.1) — exactly the kind of documented, causally-traced negative result MF wants captured as durable knowledge, not silently discarded.

The paper's own proposed remedy — embedding-based, task-similar retrieval instead of showing the full undifferentiated CTIM — is left untested (§6 Limitations) even though the diagnosed cause is exactly a retrieval/filtering failure (irrelevant items always injected); this is a partial REFUTA of 'just add a memory index' as sufficient: more knowledge without a working relevance filter is shown to be net-negative, cautioning MF against assuming a derived index alone (without gating) is safe.

Memory items are admitted from successful trajectories (plus self-reflected failure-to-success tuples) via an ExpeL-style add/edit/upvote/downvote knowledge-distillation pipeline (§4.1), yet even this curated admission process was not enough to prevent noise from degrading performance — evidence that MF's write-trigger gating must also account for DOWNSTREAM interference, not just admission quality.

The paper isolates exactly which mechanism causes the harm via a systematic 6-configuration ablation (Table 1) plus manual causal tracing of individual CTIM items to specific wrong actions (§5.1) rather than reporting only an aggregate score — a rigorous measured-retrieval methodology matching MF's G-M2 standard.

notes: Table 1 (p.4, 6-configuration ablation) + §5.1 qualitative causal-tracing case studies (p.4-5, the 'clean' and 'GRANDMA LIKES PASTA' cases) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a rigorous, well-isolated negative-result paper on episodic memory for SE agents, high-value for MF's NEGATIVO/anti-poisoning stance.

cita: Bo et al. (2025). ViLoMem: Agentic Learner with Grow-and-Refine Multimodal Semantic Memory.
problema: Los MLLMs resuelven cada problema multimodal de novo, repitiendo los mismos errores visuales y logicos; la memoria previa solo guarda un rastro de una sola modalidad y pierde como la atencion visual y el razonamiento logico producen juntos la solucion.
mecanismo: Dual-stream: un banco de memoria visual y uno logico se actualizan solo cuando el Verifier detecta un error (yi_tilde != yi); un modulo Analyze-Generate produce guideline + tipo de error, y se hace merge (si similitud coseno > umbral tau) o create de la entrada, siguiendo un principio grow-and-refine. Retrieval es de dos etapas para lo visual (similitud de imagen -> filtro por texto) y por analisis de problema + embedding de texto para lo logico.
evaluacion: 6 benchmarks multimodales (MMMU, MathVista, MathVision, HallusionBench, MMStar, RealWorldQA) con GPT-4.1, Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct y Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, comparando baseline vs step-by-step vs +ViLoMem, mas ablation quitando memoria visual o logica (Tabla 2).
numeros_clave: GPT-4.1 +ViLoMem vs step: MathVision 47.47->53.95 (+6.48 pts), MathVista 74.27->76.88 (+2.61 pts); ablation MMMU: baseline 74.00, w/o logic memory 76.64, w/o visual memory 76.88, ViLoMem completo 77.26, +attention map 78.21 (Tabla 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: La escritura se dispara SOLO cuando el Verifier detecta un error (yi_tilde != yi), no en cada turno -- un patron de disparador condicionado por señal de fallo (Sec.3, Eq.4-6).
Merge/create via umbral de similitud coseno (tau) evita la reescritura iterativa que erosiona detalle (grow-and-refine, Eq.5 y Eq.7).

El sistema registra explicitamente patrones de error visual/logico pasados para NO repetirlos, validando que el conocimiento negativo (que NO hacer) es memoria de primera clase (Fig.3, casos de retrieval).
El retrieval en dos etapas (embedding visual -> texto) se justifica por eficiencia pero el paper no reporta latencia/tokens explicitos, solo accuracy (Sec.3.2.1).

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Tabla 1 resultados principales, Tabla 2 ablation (Sec.4.3), Fig.2 arquitectura del ciclo de memoria.

cita: Joshi, T., Chowdhury, S. y Uysal, F. (2025). SWE-Bench-CL: Continual Learning for Coding Agents.
problema: Los benchmarks de codigo estaticos (SWE-Bench) no miden si un agente acumula experiencia, transfiere conocimiento entre tareas y resiste el olvido catastrofico a medida que un repositorio evoluciona cronologicamente.
mecanismo: MemorySystem basado en indice vectorial FAISS: al completar una tarea se vectorizan resumenes de problema/solucion/uso de herramientas/exito y se almacenan; al iniciar una tarea nueva el agente (LangGraph + ACI al estilo SWE-agent) hace RAG priorizando experiencias de la misma secuencia de repositorio y las antepone al prompt con limite de tokens.
evaluacion: 8 secuencias de repositorios de SWE-Bench Verified (273 tareas) con metricas de continual learning propuestas (ACC, Forgetting F, Forward/Backward Transfer, AULC, TUE, CL-F-beta); un experimento preliminar corre el harness oficial de SWE-Bench sobre SWE-Bench-CL y mide tasas de exito y un experimento de 'prompt poisoning' mide drift semantico.
numeros_clave: Tasas de exito generalmente por debajo de 8.5% (a menudo mucho menores) con el harness adaptado; similitud Jaccard promedio entre tareas 0.1114 y coseno TF-IDF 0.1792 (baja redundancia estructural); drift semantico promedio por 'prompt poisoning' ~0.45, por encima del umbral de alto drift de 0.3 (Sec.4.2, Fig.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: El experimento de 'prompt poisoning' mide drift semantico ~0.45 al anteponer una tarea no relacionada al prompt, confirmando que retrieval no discerniente degrada la procedencia/fidelidad del contexto (Sec.4.2, Alg.1).

El hallazgo 'garbage-in garbage-out' -- la memoria poblada con intentos fallidos (por incompatibilidad del harness) empeora la condicion memory-enabled -- confirma que almacenar sin filtrar fallos, sin conocimiento negativo explicito, es contraproducente (Sec.5, Fig.3).
Propone una familia formal de metricas (ACC, F, FT, BWT, AULC, CL-F-beta) para instrumentar retrieval/aprendizaje continuo medido -- vocabulario reusable para medir retrieval en MF (Sec.7).

notes: RECONSIDERAR: los experimentos principales de aprendizaje continuo (memory-enabled vs disabled comparando LLMs) estan formulados como hipotesis 'ongoing' (Sec.8); los unicos numeros duros vienen del experimento preliminar de incompatibilidad de harness (Sec.5) y de poisoning (Sec.4.2).

cita: Hu et al. (2026). CloneMem: Benchmarking Long-Term Memory for AI Clones.
problema: Los benchmarks de memoria para 'AI Clones' se basan en historiales conversacionales fragmentados y episodicos, insuficientes para capturar como evolucionan experiencias, emociones y opiniones de una persona a lo largo de una trayectoria continua de 1 a 3 anios.
mecanismo: Generacion jerarquica de datos (persona Big-Five -> arcos de vida macro -> fases meso con estado interno persistente -> trazas digitales micro no conversacionales como diarios/posts/mensajes) y evaluacion por retrieval: se comparan un retriever Flat (sin consolidar) contra sistemas actualizables A-Mem y Mem0 sobre el mismo indice de trazas, con Recall@K (flat/all-any/any-any) y QA con juez LLM.
evaluacion: 10 personas bilingues (ingles/chino), ~5000 pares QA, contextos de 100k a >500k tokens; LLaMA-3.1-8B y GPT-4o-mini como backbones, Contriever y text-embedding-3-small como embeddings, k en {5,10,20}; ablation de composicion de la unidad de retrieval (memoria extraida vs contexto crudo, Tabla 6).
numeros_clave: Flat supera a Mem0/A-Mem en casi todas las metricas: recall_any_any (GPT-4o-mini, k=20) Flat 0.7277 vs A-Mem 0.5849 vs Mem0 0.5515 (Tabla 3); indexar solo contexto crudo ('w/o mem') da la mejor choice accuracy 85.98 (k=20) frente a 69.20 de la linea base combinada (Tabla 6); oracle QA-consistency 0.83 (GPT-4o-mini) vs Flat 0.72 (Tabla 4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: El 'validity-fidelity trade-off' muestra que memorias extraidas/consolidadas (Mem0/A-Mem) pierden fidelidad de traza (timestamps, fraseo) frente al contexto crudo, confirmando que la fuente original debe primar sobre el indice derivado (Sec.6, Tabla 6).

El retriever Flat (sin consolidacion) supera consistentemente a los sistemas 'organizados' Mem0 y A-Mem en recall y ayuda semantica -- desafia que consolidar/abstraer memoria (indice derivado) siempre mejore sobre listar hechos crudos (Tabla 3, Sec.7).

El paper documenta 'safe hallucinations' donde el sistema inventa una decision cuando el registro real es 'aun sin decidir' -- un caso de conocimiento negativo (estado de no-decision) no capturado por memoria basada en eventos (Sec.7).

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Tabla 3 (retrieval), Tabla 4 (QA), Tabla 6 (ablation composicion), Sec.7 discusion 'activity != state'.

cita: Wolff and Bennati (2026). Cost and Accuracy of Long-Term Memory in Distributed Multi-Agent Systems Based on Large Language Models.
problema: Las evaluaciones de frameworks de memoria de largo plazo (LTM) suelen ser publicadas por los propios proveedores, se centran solo en tokens/latencia e ignoran el costo de sistema (CPU, RAM, disco, red) y el despliegue en sistemas multi-agente distribuidos (DMAS) cloud-edge.
mecanismo: Testbed independiente reproducible con contenedores Docker que compara mem0 (vector), Graphiti (grafo) y cognee (hibrido) junto a baselines RAG y full-context sobre LoCoMo, bajo escenarios de red no restringida y restringida (latencia/ancho de banda/jitter simulados con toxiproxy), midiendo accuracy y Total Cost of Ownership (TCO).
evaluacion: LoCoMo (1540 pares pregunta-respuesta), diseno factorial completo (5 backends x 2 escenarios de red), test de Wilcoxon pareado con correccion de Bonferroni, analisis de dominancia de Pareto costo-accuracy, juez LLM con voto mayoritario de 3 llamadas.
numeros_clave: mem0, RAG y full-context alcanzan 77%-81% de accuracy, mientras Graphiti y cognee solo 55%-56%; RAG iguala al cluster superior con 8.4 veces menos TCO que mem0; la memoria basada en vectores sufre una penalizacion de latencia de 4%-5% bajo restricciones edge-cloud (Abstract).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Mide explicitamente TCO (CPU, RAM, disco, red, tokens) y muestra que RAG iguala la precision de mem0 con 8.4x menos costo total -- confirma que la economia de contexto es un eje de decision independiente de la precision pura (Abstract, Sec.IV).

Los backends de grafo/hibridos (Graphiti, cognee), que construyen indices derivados mas sofisticados, rinden PEOR (55%-56%) que RAG/full-context planos (77%-81%) -- desafia la premisa de que mas estructura derivada implica mejor recall (Abstract).

El hallazgo de que la precision de compresion, no el volumen de contexto, determina la exactitud (full-context pierde contra mem0 pese a dar toda la conversacion) valida que la fidelidad de lo recuperado importa mas que la cantidad bruta (Abstract).

La brecha de Graphiti/cognee esta impulsada por 'retrieval incompleteness' (recall bajo) mas que por fallos de razonamiento -- un caso de no encontrar la evidencia, sin que el paper mida un mecanismo explicito de abstencion (Abstract).

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Abstract (numeros de accuracy y TCO), Tabla I (tarifas AWS/OpenAI usadas para TCO), Sec.III metodologia Wohlin et al.

cita: Hu et al. (2026). OP-Bench: Benchmarking Over-Personalization for Memory-Augmented Personalized Conversational Agents.
problema: Los agentes conversacionales aumentados con memoria de usuario sobre-personalizan: aplican informacion personal aunque sea irrelevante, sycophantic o repetitiva, produciendo respuestas forzadas o intrusivas -- un fallo que los benchmarks de recall puro no detectan.
mecanismo: OP-Bench diagnostica sobre-personalizacion en 3 categorias (Irrelevance, Sycophancy, Repetition); analisis de atencion muestra 'memory hijacking' (razon de atencion memoria/query >2x); Self-ReCheck es un filtro ligero, model-agnostic, que evalua cada memoria recuperada con un LLM y descarta las no relevantes para la query actual antes de generar, sin tocar retrieval ni generacion.
evaluacion: 1700 instancias verificadas por humanos sobre 20 usuarios (basado en LoCoMo), 36 configuraciones (6 LLMs x 6 metodos de memoria: BASE, RAG, LDAgent, Mem0, MemU, MEMOS), evaluacion conjunta con LoCoMo para separar uso efectivo vs sobreuso de memoria; Self-ReCheck evaluado en Qwen3-8B con analisis de Pareto y de atencion.
numeros_clave: Caidas relativas de 26.2% a 61.1% en OP-Bench respecto a BASE para todos los metodos con memoria; razon de atencion memoria/query >2x en promedio; Self-ReCheck reduce la sobre-personalizacion en 29% mientras mejora la personalizacion en LoCoMo +3% en promedio (Abstract, Sec.4.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Demuestra que el retrieval agresivo sin discriminar cuando NO usar una memoria causa degradacion de 26.2%-61.1%; el filtro Self-ReCheck (saber que memoria descartar) es la mitigacion medida con +29% de mejora (Fig.7, Abstract).

Sistemas de memoria mas sofisticados (MemU, MEMOS, con resumen/estructura) muestran MAS sobre-personalizacion que RAG simple -- desafia que retrieval mas elaborado sea siempre mejor si no mide cuando debe abstenerse (Sec.4.2, RQ1).

El 'memory hijacking' (atencion memoria/query >2x) sugiere que la memoria debe tratarse como senal condicional y no privilegiada -- relevante a como MF pondera multiples fuentes en un mismo prompt (Sec.4.3).

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Tabla 2 (caidas por metodo/modelo), Fig.4 (atencion memoria/query), Fig.7 (Pareto Self-ReCheck).

cita: Li et al. (2026). EMemBench: Interactive Benchmarking of Episodic Memory for VLM Agents.
problema: Los benchmarks de memoria de largo plazo evaluan QA sobre un historial pre-construido y fijo, sin tratar la memoria como una competencia individualizada ligada a la trayectoria de experiencia propia del agente (memoria episodica), y cubren poco lo visual/espacial.
mecanismo: Un generador programatico convierte la trayectoria de un episodio de juego (Jericho texto, Crafter visual) mas el estado subyacente del juego en preguntas con verdad terreno deterministica, organizadas en 7 categorias de habilidad (single/multi-hop, induccion, espacial, temporal, logica, adversarial); se comparan agentes in-context contra memorias persistentes Mem0, LangMem y A-MEM.
evaluacion: 15 juegos de texto (Jericho) y juegos visuales (Crafter) con 5 semillas, backbones GPT-5.1, Qwen2.5/3-32B, Qwen3-VL-32B, InternVL3.5-38B; estudio humano con 11 anotadores en condicion open-book vs closed-book; comparacion cruzada con LongMemEval y LoCoMo (Sec.5.3).
numeros_clave: Mejor ACC global 51.9 (A-MEM, Qwen3-32B, texto) vs 43.8 (GPT-5.1 in-context, visual); induccion alcanza solo 34.2 de pico en texto y 20.2 en visual; humanos open-book 65.6% acc vs closed-book 23.2% acc en general (Tabla 3, Tabla 4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: El diseno 'experience-conditioned' genera preguntas desde la trayectoria REAL del propio agente (no un set fijo), y Sec.5.2 muestra que el ranking de metodos de memoria CAMBIA entre evaluacion interactiva vs QA fija -- un patron de medicion reusable para retrieval MF (Fig.2).

La categoria 'Adversarial' prueba explicitamente si el agente reconoce que un evento NO ocurrio (precondicion fallida) en vez de alucinar; el mejor score en esa categoria (92.1 Mem0) muestra que la abstencion/negativo es medible por separado del recall positivo (Tabla 3).

Memorias 'organizadas' (Mem0, LangMem) a menudo rinden PEOR que el prompting in-context puro en induccion y single-hop (ej. GPT-5.1 in-context 76.7 vs Mem0 43.4 en single-hop) -- cuestiona que el indice derivado siempre supere al contexto crudo (Tabla 3).

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Tabla 3 (resultados principales por habilidad), Tabla 4 (estudio humano), Fig.2 (interactivo vs fijo).

cita: Shen et al. (2026). Mem2ActBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Utilization in Task-Oriented Autonomous Agents.
problema: Los benchmarks de memoria existentes evaluan recuperacion pasiva de hechos aislados ante preguntas explicitas; no evaluan si un agente puede INFERIR que restricciones recuperar de una memoria dispersa e interrumpida y aplicarlas (ground) en una llamada a herramienta subespecificada.
mecanismo: Pipeline automatizado que fusiona ToolACE/BFCL (tareas con herramientas) y Oasst1 (ruido conversacional), construye una 'Fact Evolution Chain' resolviendo conflictos localmente (orden temporal, refinamiento coarse->specific) y globalmente (topological sort con heuristica de ciclos), y genera consultas subespecificadas por reverse-generation con control de fuga: se omiten parametros, se exigen referencias anaforicas y un discriminador LLM debe FALLAR sin acceso a la memoria para que la muestra se conserve.
evaluacion: 2029 sesiones sintenticas (13 turnos promedio), 400 tareas de uso de herramientas verificadas 91.3% memory-dependent por 5 anotadores expertos; 7 frameworks de memoria (RAG, Generative Agents, SCM, Langmem, MemTree, Mem0, A-mem) sobre Qwen2.5 7B/32B/72B con metricas F1/BLEU-1/Tool Accuracy (TA); analisis de posicion de memoria (memory distance) y comparacion retrieval oracle vs pasivo (no-retrieval/BM25/dense/hybrid).
numeros_clave: retrieval oracle F1~53.8 vs mejor retrieval pasivo (hybrid k=5) F1~30.7 -- brecha >23 puntos F1 (Tabla 4); Tool Accuracy agrupada 87%-97% con poca variacion 32B->72B; F1 promedio sube de 20.4 (7B) a 28.9 (72B); A-mem cae de ~36% a ~25% cuando la evidencia esta en el 25-50% del historial ('mid-context valley', Fig.3); con distractores duros (N=5) Tool Selection Accuracy cae de 94.5% a 69.75% (Tabla 5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: La brecha de 23+ puntos F1 entre retrieval oracle (53.8) y el mejor retrieval pasivo (30.7 con hybrid k=5) confirma que el cuello de botella dominante es la CALIDAD del retrieval, no el razonamiento del modelo -- retrieval medido es el eje correcto a instrumentar (Sec.5.1, Tabla 4).

El 'mid-context valley' (F1 cae de ~36% a ~25% cuando la evidencia esta en 25-50% del historial) muestra que la posicion de un hecho en la memoria afecta su fidelidad de recuperacion, un sesgo 'lost-in-the-middle' aplicado a memoria de agentes (Fig.3, Sec.5.1).

El mayor error de grounding viene de valores 'Default' (no mencionados): los modelos frecuentemente NO notan que un valor nunca fue especificado y alucinan un default plausible -- confirma que detectar ausencia de informacion es una capacidad de memoria negativa distinta del recall positivo (Sec.5.3, Fig.4).

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Tabla 2 (verificacion humana 91.3%), Tabla 3 (resultados principales), Tabla 4 (retrieval oracle vs pasivo), Fig.3 (mid-context valley), Sec.5.4 (robustez de seleccion de herramienta).

cita: Aubry et al. (2026). An evaluation framework for AI agent external memory systems.
problema: No existe un protocolo experimental abierto e independiente, ejecutable por un solo operador, para comparar sistemas de memoria externa frente a la memoria intrinseca de plataformas LLM cerradas en cuanto a recall factual y calidad de personalizacion.
