El eje Y (retrieval atomico -> asociacion relacional -> sintesis evolutiva sobre actualizaciones/conflictos) es una taxonomia graduada y medida de dificultad de retrieval-razonamiento, trasladable a auditar si un indice responde busquedas simples vs multi-hop vs revision-de-estado.

Muestra que la memoria basada en texto (captions como indice derivado mas barato sobre imagenes) pierde de forma confiable detalles visuales finos necesarios para preguntas X3-X4 (Sec.4, hallazgo de tradeoff) -- evidencia medida de que un indice derivado barato puede ser INSEGURO como sustituto de la fuente cuando esta es de alto ancho de banda (imagenes), desafiando la suposicion de que un indice comprimido siempre es un sustituto adecuado de la fuente.

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Fig.2 (ganancia caption-a-multimodal), Fig.3 (taxonomia de dos ejes), Sec.3.1 (filtros bypass/caption/dificultad), Fig.5 (heatmap por metodo).

cita: Yang et al. (2026). GroupMemBench: Benchmarking LLM Agent Memory in Multi-Party Conversations.
problema: Los sistemas de memoria de agentes y sus benchmarks actuales estan construidos para interacciones diadicas de un solo usuario, dejando sin medir tres propiedades de la memoria GRUPAL: dinamica de grupo mas alla de chats 1:1 concatenados, seguimiento de creencias ligado al hablante (la misma consulta de distintos usuarios puede requerir respuestas distintas), y vocabulario adaptado a la audiencia (jerga especifica de rol impulsada por Teoria de la Mente).
mecanismo: No es un sistema de memoria (operaciones=NA); sintesis de conversaciones multi-parte fundamentada en grafo (grafo tipado de dominios/topicos/fases/usuarios/mensajes, generacion por muestreo de rutas channel-post/threaded-reply/cross-project-bridge) condiciona cada mensaje en personas por usuario y audiencia objetivo; pipeline adversarial Solve-Judge-Refine liga cada pregunta a un usuario preguntante especifico en 6 categorias (multi-hop, actualizacion de conocimiento, ambiguedad de termino, razonamiento implicito-de-usuario, temporal, abstencion), aceptando una pregunta solo si un baseline de retrieval competente falla en resolverla; se benchmarquean sistemas de memoria disenados para el caso diadico (Mem0, MemGPT, A-Mem, HippoRAG, Hindsight) mas baselines RAG en este entorno multi-parte.
evaluacion: Accuracy juzgada por GPT-5 por categoria en 4 dominios (Tecnologia/Salud/Manufactura/Finanzas), mas ejes de eficiencia (costo de ingesta en USD, almacenamiento en disco en GB) reportados como tradeoff desempeno-eficiencia (Fig.4).
numeros_clave: El mejor sistema (Hindsight) alcanza solo 46.0% de accuracy promedio; knowledge-update cae a 27.1% (Hindsight 17.76%) y term-ambiguity a 37.7%; un baseline simple BM25 (43.22% promedio) iguala o supera a la mayoria de los sistemas de memoria dedicados (Mem0 25.73%, MemGPT 28.15%); la abstencion se mantiene alta en todos los metodos (>75-82%, Tabla 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: La abstencion es la UNICA categoria donde casi todos los sistemas puntuan alto (>75%, Tabla 2) precisamente porque no requiere modelar estructura/hablante -- confirma que 'saber que no se sabe' es comparativamente facil/barato de implementar de forma confiable, mientras el recall positivo ligado al hablante (knowledge-update, term-ambiguity) es donde los sistemas realmente fallan.

Identifica que los sistemas de memoria diadicos heredan user_id como un NAMESPACE AISLADO que separa almacenes en vez de un atributo semantico que condiciona extraccion/retrieval, y resuelven conflictos SOBRESCRIBIENDO en vez de preservar creencias coexistentes atribuidas a distintos hablantes (Sec.2) -- evidencia directa de que la costura 'un hecho, una fuente' se rompe cuando multiples fuentes legitimas (hablantes) pueden sostener creencias validas distintas simultaneamente.

Reporta costo de ingesta (USD) y almacenamiento (GB) como eje explicito de eficiencia junto a accuracy (Fig.4, Tabla 1), pero el hallazgo central del paper es el colapso de accuracy, no una recomendacion orientada a costo -- contexto relevante sin fuerza direccional.

Un baseline simple de retrieval lexico BM25 (43.22% promedio) iguala o SUPERA a la mayoria de sistemas de memoria activa (Mem0 25.73%, MemGPT 28.15%, A-Mem 35.10%, Tabla 2) en este entorno multi-parte mas exigente -- desafia la suposicion de que pipelines de extraccion/consolidacion activa son estrictamente mejores que el retrieval lexico crudo cuando el entorno exige preservar procedencia (quien dijo que).

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Tabla 2 (accuracy por categoria/metodo), Fig.4 (tradeoff desempeno-eficiencia), Sec.2 (supuestos estructurales que rompen sistemas diadicos).

cita: Kim, T., Francois-Lavet, V. y Cochez, M. (2026). Short-Term-to-Long-Term Memory Transfer for Knowledge Graphs under Partial Observability.
problema: En RL bajo observabilidad parcial con memoria simbolica de grafo de conocimiento, la mayoria de enfoques no modela explicitamente la decision de transferencia de corto a largo plazo (que hecho observado conservar vs descartar antes de insertarlo en memoria persistente de capacidad limitada).
mecanismo: Formula la transferencia como un problema de decision de valor neuro-simbolico: cada tripleta RDF observada recibe una decision binaria keep/drop mediante Q-learning por-item con parametros compartidos (maneja cardinalidad variable del buffer de corto plazo), representaciones via GNN (GCN/R-GCN/StarE-GNN) sobre el grafo de memoria, y una actualizacion TD practica que empareja items entre pasos consecutivos con cardinalidad distinta (matching estocastico por orden aleatorio); politicas de transferencia local (por-item) vs global (pooled) y con input solo-corto-plazo vs contexto completo.
evaluacion: Benchmark RoomKG (grid 7x7, 49 cuartos, 100 pasos/episodio) con capacidad de memoria de largo plazo=128; comparacion contra baselines simbolicos con anotaciones temporales (Novel-Only, Always-Transfer, Random-Transfer p=0.5) y baselines neuronales end-to-end (LSTM, Transformer); ablacion de encoders GNN (GCN/R-GCN/StarE-GNN) x modos de politica (Local-Full/Local-STM/Global-Full/Global-STM); analisis comportamental de decisiones keep/drop paso-a-paso sobre 560 decisiones de transferencia en episodios held-out.
numeros_clave: La mejor configuracion (GCN + Local-STM) alcanza 38.920+/-3.090 en test vs 31.960+/-1.255 del mejor baseline simbolico (Novel-Only, +6.96 puntos) y vs 11.800+/-3.187 (Transformer) y 7.600+/-2.332 (LSTM, +27.12 y +31.32 puntos respectivamente, Tabla 1); analisis conductual: (agent, at_location, room) se conserva 98/100 veces, hechos de ubicacion de objetos consultados se conservan 58/60 veces, mientras que enlaces de direccion norte/sur/este/oeste se descartan 332/400 veces (keep rate global 0.40).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: La politica aprendida de keep/drop (Sec.5.2) descarta sistematicamente el 83% de los enlaces de direccion norte/sur/este/oeste (332/400) mientras retiene casi siempre la posicion del agente y los hechos consultables -- un mecanismo explicito, interpretable y AUDITABLE de decidir que NO vale la pena conservar en memoria persistente, aprendido por señal de recompensa de tarea, no por heuristica de recencia/frecuencia.

El diseno de Q-learning por-item con parametros compartidos (Sec.3.2) trata la decision de escritura a largo plazo como una decision de VALOR aprendida por cada hecho candidato (no un umbral fijo ni un juicio LLM binario) -- disparador de escritura discrecional entrenado end-to-end contra el desempeno downstream real (QA correctness).

Opera bajo una capacidad de memoria de largo plazo estrictamente fija (K=128) y muestra que la politica de transferencia APRENDIDA supera a heuristicas simbolicas (LRU/MRU) exactamente porque optimiza que conservar bajo ese presupuesto duro (Tabla 1) -- confirma que decidir bien QUE escribir importa mas, bajo presupuesto fijo, que simplemente escribir todo y podar despues.

notes: Ancla de evidencia: Tabla 1 (resultados train/test por variante), Sec.5.2 (analisis de keep/drop 560 decisiones, Fig.2). Estudio de mecanismo enfocado (n=5 seeds, un solo benchmark RoomKG) -- RECONSIDERAR (validez externa limitada, los propios autores lo describen como mechanism-validation study, no un barrido amplio de benchmarks).

cita: Yan et al. (2026). Evo-Attacker: Memory-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool Attacks on LLM-MAS.
problema: LLM-MAS implicitly trust tool-return outputs; existing tool attacks are domain-specific or rely on static templates, so they fail to generalize across architectures/tasks/tool-schemas and cannot plan coherent multi-step interventions (long-horizon credit assignment).
mecanismo: Builds a dynamic Attack Memory that archives full trajectories (task context + tool-call/modification/perturbed-return tuples) only when an episode ends in a VERIFIED system failure (outcome-gated write/admission). At attack time a deliberative Retrieve-Reflect-Modify policy queries the memory by semantic similarity, decides ATTACK/CONTINUE/NOOP, and crafts the perturbed tool return; the whole pipeline is optimized end-to-end with Attack-Flow GRPO, which broadcasts the terminal outcome reward to every intermediate reasoning token.
evaluacion: 3 LLM-MAS architectures (Flat/Chain/Hierarchical) x 6 benchmarks (HumanEval, MAB.code, MAB.research, DeepResearchBench, WebArena, WebShop) vs baselines (Forced Output, InjecAgent, Web Fraud, Prompt Infection); ablation on retrieval/reflection/RL-training components; sensitivity sweeps over attack budget, reflection depth, retrieved-memory count; stealthiness measured against 5 LLM-based detectors.
numeros_clave: Ablation (Table2, full pipeline vs w/o component): Code TS degrades from 55.2(w/o RT)/49.9(w/o RF)/52.5... to 40.9 full; Research 51.0->40.1; Web 36.9->26.0 (w/o RL is the most severe drop). Main results: WebArena SR degradation up to -18.8pp (flat arch) vs InjecAgent's -9.2pp.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The NoOp control decision (S3.2) preserves the intervention budget by refusing to act when retrieved memories are insufficient or the context is unsuitable -- MF could adopt this as a negative-knowledge gate that skips known-unproductive retrieval instead of a blind re-attempt.

Attack Memory only admits an episode after a VERIFIED successful outcome (S3.1: 'an interaction episode terminates with a verified system failure'), an outcome-gated write trigger MF's own write-admission decision could mirror.

Ablation Table 2 measures retrieval's marginal contribution directly (removing retrieval degrades attack success across all three domains), confirming that retrieval quality is worth measuring rather than assumed.

notes: Table 1 (main results) + Table 2 (ablation, S4.3) + Figure 2 (S4.4 sensitivity) on arXiv 2605.25389.

cita: Tummalapenta and Addanki (2026). Memory Architectures for Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL: A Benchmark and Empirical Study.
problema: Text-to-SQL is evaluated almost entirely single-turn, yet real analyst workflows are multi-turn with anaphoric follow-ups; it is unknown whether frontier LLMs degrade without explicit memory, which memory-architecture components (working/episodic/semantic) actually help, and at what marginal cost.
mecanismo: EnterpriseMem-Bench: 300 sessions/1400 turns built deterministically from 3 live enterprise DBs (BIRD financial, SEC EDGAR, Northwind), each turn flagged memory-critical iff it needs a state_update from a prior turn. Five memory conditions form a three-way ablation isolating working-memory window size, episodic retrieval, and semantic-schema augmentation as independent effects; a per-turn Memory Benefit Score (MBS) normalizes each condition's execution accuracy against the stateless baseline.
evaluacion: 5 frontier models (GPT-5 mini, GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6) x 5 memory conditions x 3 datasets, 35,000 turn evaluations; execution-accuracy metric (result-set equality) plus MBS per turn depth; reasoning-configuration parity controls between GPT and Claude.
numeros_clave: Stateless (A) yields 15-19% EX% across all 5 models, collapsing to 0% by turn 3 on memory-critical questions; working memory (B) recovers to 75-86%. Claude Sonnet 4.6 underperforms Sonnet 4.5 on SEC EDGAR by 17.2pp at B, 29.0pp at C, 33.1pp at D (Opus 4.6 reaches 99.2% at D, no regression).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Finding that episodic and semantic memory layers 'frequently negative' marginal effects (S1 abstract) confirms MF's stance that adding memory-architecture complexity is not free and must be measured, not assumed to help.

The three-way ablation (window size vs episodic retrieval vs semantic augmentation, S5.1) is exactly the kind of measured-retrieval-layer decomposition MF's G-M2 need calls for, isolating which memory component earns its cost.

The reproducible Sonnet-4.6-vs-4.5 regression on SEC EDGAR (17-33pp, Fig.3) that 'survives extended reasoning' shows model-family/generation choice can silently degrade memory-dependent fidelity independent of the memory architecture itself, a confound MF should not assume away.

notes: Table 6 (RQ1 stateless collapse) + Fig.3/S6.2 EDGAR regression + S5.1 three-way ablation design, arXiv 2605.26394 (JPMC applied study).

cita: Garg et al. (2026). MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems.
problema: Existing memory benchmarks report aggregate QA accuracy and treat memory systems as black boxes, making it impossible to attribute an incorrect answer to a specific stage (summarization, storage, or retrieval) of the memory pipeline.
mecanismo: Formalizes any memory system as three composable operations (summarize, store, retrieve) and constructs 5 diagnostic datasets across 4 tasks (Conditional-Facts Easy/Hard, Coexisting-Facts, Persona-Retrieval, Long-Hop), each adversarially designed to isolate one failure mode; an LLM-as-judge classifies every graded memory into storage/summary/retrieval/reasoning check outcomes using get_all_memories() as ground truth.
evaluacion: Evaluates 4 open-source memory systems (Mem0, A-MEM, SimpleMem, StructMem) sweeping retrieved-memory count k=4..20, varying the internal test-taker/summarizer model strength (gpt-4.1-mini, haiku-4.5, gpt-5.4-mini, gemini-3.1), and measuring the accuracy-vs-tokens-per-memory tradeoff per task.
numeros_clave: Human validation: gpt-5-mini scores 98% answer-correctness and 98.4% error-type-classification accuracy on 100 manually graded examples. Scaling k or model strength yields marginal or negative gains (architecture-bound, not model-intelligence-bound); StructMem excels on causal tasks but collapses on Coexisting-Facts while Mem0 shows the opposite pattern.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: MemFail's decomposition into summarize/store/retrieve failure modes (S3.2) is exactly the localization MF needs to attribute a wrong answer to WHICH memory stage failed rather than treating memory as a black box.

S6 Q3 shows performance does NOT monotonically improve with more tokens per memory -- for retrieval-bottlenecked tasks larger memories 'pollute the embedding space' and hurt retrieval, challenging any assumption that richer/verbose entries are strictly better.

S6 Q1 measures retrieval success rate as a function of k directly (Figure 1) and shows scaling k yields marginal returns when summarization is the real bottleneck, confirming retrieval quality must be measured per task not assumed to scale with k.

Architecturally distinct systems (graph-based StructMem vs Mem0) show OPPOSITE failure signatures on the same task, suggesting no single-store design dominates -- relevant evidence for MF's multi-store seam decision.

notes: Task taxonomy S3.2 + Table 1 architecture comparison + S6 Q1-Q4 findings (Figures 1-3), arXiv 2605.26667.

cita: Yang, X. (2026). Memoria: A Cognitive-Fidelity Memory Architecture for AI Agents.
problema: Conversational AI memory is evaluated almost exclusively on retrieval accuracy, which optimizes systems to retain low-arousal routine facts human memory is designed to forget; companion AI instead needs 'cognitive fidelity' -- behavioral alignment of what is retained/forgotten with human memory dynamics, a target no existing system (Mem0, MemGPT, LightMem, A-MEM) pursues.
mecanismo: A four-phase pipeline (Encoding->Tagging->Consolidation[SWS+REM]->Transformation) governed by a state-driven (not timer-driven) dual-layer tracker (behavioral ACTIVE/RESTING/SLEEP + mood valence/arousal); unified power-law strength S(t)=s0*(1+t)^-d with arousal-gated decay exponent d(a); write depth (deep/normal/shallow s0) gated by a cheap residual-arousal check that only invokes an LLM on divergence >=0.3; consolidation gated by a 3-factor priority score; retrieval scored by a 5-factor weighted sum; each retrieval opens a prediction-error-gated reconsolidation window (stabilize/update/extinguish) with eventual garbage collection.
evaluacion: Two-track evaluation: Track A fits power-law vs exponential decay to human retention data and measures the arousal-gated retention gap; Track B benchmarks the full pipeline vs a naive RAG baseline on 300 LongMemEval-S pairs; plus a 10-mechanism neuroscience-coverage audit of Mem0/MemGPT/LightMem/A-MEM.
numeros_clave: Track A: power-law fit R2=0.954 vs exponential R2=0.295; arousal-gated decay yields a 24pp retention gap at 30 days (1.56x strength ratio, high- vs low-arousal). Track B: Memoria 27.6% vs naive-RAG 26.1% on 300 LongMemEval-S pairs (1.5pp gap, within noise), with a 5.7pp advantage on preference questions. Mechanism audit: existing systems cover 1-3/10 mechanisms vs Memoria's 10/10.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Phase 4's garbage collection (physically deletes facts once S(t)<0.03) and the prediction-error-gated 'extinguish' action (S3.5) implement principled forgetting as a first-class operation, a concrete negative-knowledge/decay mechanism MF's own forgetting policy could mirror.

The state tracker is explicitly state-driven not timer-driven and mood-tracking 'requires zero LLM calls' absent divergence (S3.7), confirming MF's economy-of-context stance that not every tick should invoke the model.

Encoding depth (how strongly something is written) is gated by a residual-arousal check that only invokes an LLM when the keyword heuristic and predicted mood diverge by >=0.3 (S3.2) -- a cheap discretionary write-trigger MF could adapt beyond the emotional-salience use case.

Track B (S5) shows the full cognitively-faithful pipeline scores only 1.5pp above naive RAG on LongMemEval-S; the paper argues retrieval-accuracy benchmarks are the wrong target for fidelity, challenging any assumption that a more elaborate/faithful architecture must also win standard retrieval benchmarks.

notes: Table 1 mechanism-mapping + Table 3 parameter provenance + S5 Track A/B results, single-author arXiv preprint June 2026.

cita: Tian et al. (2026). Joint Agent Memory and Exploration Learning via Novelty Signals.
problema: Effective exploration in open-ended agentic environments requires memory to distinguish exhausted from unseen behaviors, but latent-memory compression lacks reliable step-level supervision (no ground truth for what a memory vector should encode), while retaining raw history is too costly over long trajectories.
mecanismo: JAMEL jointly trains a latent-memory compressor (a frozen VLM's EOS hidden state per observation-action step, aligned via a learned linear projector into the policy's embedding space as a soft prefix) and an exploration policy, using a persistent, deterministic novelty signal (JS code-coverage delta) as the sole supervisory reward; training data is collected via rejection sampling that keeps only the prefix up to the last positive-novelty step (a natural curriculum), 24k samples across 86 web apps.
evaluacion: ScaleWoB benchmark (96 web apps, 86 train/10 held-out), 50-step sessions, cumulative-coverage-reward metric, vs closed-source ReAct-text/vision (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, full history) and open-weight GUI agents (MAI-UI-8B, Mobile-Agent-v3.5); token-consumption comparison over 500 eval steps; per-app breakdown plus a qualitative failure-mode case study.
numeros_clave: Main results (Table1): JAMEL 20.7 avg reward vs MAI-UI 8.4, Mobile-Agent-v3.5 5.9, ReAct-text 19.9, ReAct-vision 20.9 (trails by only 0.2). Token cost (Table2): JAMEL uses 1,061,103 total input tokens (2,122.2/step) vs 2.76x (Mobile-Agent-v3.5), 2.81x (MAI-UI), 17.85x (ReAct-text), 21.92x (ReAct-vision) more.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Novelty reward is defined precisely as NOT re-triggering a previously-visited state (S3.3, rt=1[C(t)>C(t-1)], persistent, never re-fires) -- an explicit negative-knowledge signal that rewards genuinely new behavior over recall of the known, close to MF's re-derivation-over-recall stance.

Table 2 measures token consumption directly and shows JAMEL's single-token-per-step latent memory uses 2.76-21.92x fewer tokens than baselines retaining full/pruned explicit history, confirming compact memory representations pay off measurably in context cost.

Memory writes are gated entirely by an external, deterministic, annotation-free novelty signal (code-coverage delta, S3.3) rather than an LLM judgment call -- a cheaper write-trigger design MF could consider when a deterministic proxy for 'new information' exists.

notes: Table 1 main results + Table 2 token cost + S4.3 per-app analysis (Fig.3) + Pinduoduo case study, arXiv 2606.01528.

cita: Xu et al. (2026). When Should Memory Stay Silent: Measuring Memory-Use Boundaries in Memory-Augmented Conversational Agents.
problema: Existing memory evaluations measure retrieval accuracy and downstream task utility but ignore whether integrating retrieved sensitive memory into a response is WARRANTED by the current turn -- a distinct 'memory-use boundary' problem, separate from both privacy leakage and retrieval accuracy.
mecanismo: RBI-Eval: a controlled probe set (2,400 single-turn cases, 10 personas) pairing benign current-turn prompts with prior sensitive-disclosure history; compares model responses across no-memory / full-context / 3 retrieval-memory conditions (Mem0, A-Mem, MemU) using a condition-blind LLM judge scoring 4 dimensions (sensitive-history integration, relationship-maintenance agreement, affective intensity, assistant centrality) via an absolute Boundary Separation Score (BSS); decomposes risk into retrieval-exposure vs generation-time-integration stages with matched control conditions isolating sensitivity-specific effects from general personalization.
evaluacion: 4 base LLMs (Claude-Sonnet-4.6, GPT-5.4-mini, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.5-9B) x 5 memory conditions (no-mem, full-context, Mem0, A-Mem, MemU); paired diagnostics + control-condition ablations (neutral-relevant, boundary-policy, oracle/irrelevant-sensitive, transparent-vector) + retrieval-exposure decomposition (target-hit rate vs integration-if-hit rate).
numeros_clave: Sensitive-history-integration BSS drops from ~99.7-99.9 (no-mem) to 17.0-30.3 under memory access: GPT-5.4-mini drops only 8.9-26.6pp vs 51.1-82.9pp for Claude/DeepSeek/Qwen (Table1). Retrieval-time filtering cuts exposure-and-use risk ~71-84% vs full-context, but integration-if-exposed stays 66.7-94.9% once retrieved (Fig.4). Boundary-policy instruction restores DeepSeek BSS from 28.3 to 99.9 (Table2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The core finding is that retrieval+relevance is NOT sufficient -- a memory can be true, stored, and topically relevant yet still not WARRANTED for the current turn (S3.3), a distinction MF's own retrieval/write gating could adopt as an explicit filter beyond similarity.

S3.4/Fig.4 shows retrieval-time filtering reduces exposure risk by 71-84% but generation-time integration-if-hit stays 66.7-94.9%, confirming fidelity/provenance controls are needed at BOTH the store/retrieve layer and the consumption layer, not one alone.

The study is a measured decomposition of retrieval-exposure vs generation-time use (Fig.4, target-hit vs recall-if-hit rates) rather than an aggregate accuracy number, directly confirming MF's ADR-019 stance that retrieval must be measured per-stage, not assumed.

S4 argues memory governance 'should not collapse storage, retrieval, and use into one switch' and proposes lightweight per-turn warrant signals -- a seam MF could adopt between what is stored and what is exposed/used per interaction.

notes: Table 1 (BSS by model x condition) + Table 2/3 controls + Fig.4 exposure-vs-integration decomposition, arXiv 2606.06055.

cita: Omri et al. (2026). Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads.
problema: Agent memory systems (flat retrieval, LLM-mediated extraction, consolidating fact stores, agentic control flows) are evaluated only on downstream accuracy, leaving their system-level cost behavior (construction vs retrieval vs generation) entirely uncharacterized despite drastically and asymmetrically redistributing compute cost across the write and read paths.
mecanismo: A four-axis taxonomy (construction, storage, retrieval, mutability) classifies 10 representative systems into 4 paradigms (long-context, flat RAG, structure-augmented RAG [append-only/consolidating], agentic control flow); a phase-aware profiling harness attributes API telemetry (tokens, calls) and hardware telemetry (GPU utilization, VRAM, HBM bandwidth, energy) to construction, retrieval, and generation phases on the same monotonic timeline.
evaluacion: MemoryAgentBench (4 competencies: accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, selective forgetting) + MemoryArena (multi-session freshness-latency); measured on LongMemEval_S_* (5 samples ~360K tokens history, 300 queries) under remote (OpenAI API) and local (vLLM on H100) construction regimes across an LLM ladder (Qwen3-32B/14B/8B/1.7B).
numeros_clave: Table3 (Qwen3-32B, 300 queries): accuracy ranges 20.0% (MIRIX) to 47.0% (BM25); end-to-end energy spans 26.7x, from BM25's 582 kJ to Letta's 15,429 kJ; per-correct-answer energy from BM25's 4,128 J floor to A-Mem 116,116 J and MIRIX 144,629 J (28-47x premium). Fig.2: Mem0 answers a query in <0.1s vs ~38s for a long-context (GPT-4.1-mini) baseline.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central contribution is a measured cost taxonomy (Table3, Fig.3/4: tokens, GPU energy, latency per phase) showing costs invisible to accuracy metrics span 26.7x in energy and 2 orders of magnitude in per-query latency, directly confirming MF's stance that context economy must be measured per design choice, not assumed.

The paper documents that 'maintenance is weak or absent' in most current systems -- memory accumulates indefinitely with no freshness/pruning policy (S2.1) -- an explicit gap MF's own forgetting/negative-knowledge design should not repeat.

Table 1's taxonomy shows storage substrates range from a single raw-context buffer to multi-store DBs coupling lexical/vector/graph/structured metadata (MIRIX, Letta) -- directly informing MF's single-store-vs-multi-store seam tradeoff with a measured cost consequence.

Fig.2 explicitly measures per-query retrieval+generation latency and accuracy jointly across 10 systems rather than reporting accuracy alone, confirming MF's stance that retrieval must be measured (cost AND quality) not assumed.

notes: Table 1 taxonomy + Table 3 end-to-end cost + Fig.2-4 (phase breakdown, energy-per-correct-answer), arXiv 2606.06448 (Stanford/MIT/KU Leuven).

cita: Asawa et al. (2026). Continual Learning Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI Systems in Real-World Stateful Environments.
problema: No high-quality benchmark exists to measure whether AI systems genuinely improve through sequential online experience (continual learning), distinct from recall/QA benchmarks; existing memory evaluations conflate learning with static base-model capability.
mecanismo: CL-Bench: 6 expert-validated domains with discoverable latent structure (schema conventions, opponent strategies, codebase layout) shared across sequential instances, some with concept drift requiring re-learning; introduces a 'gain' metric (gt = r_sf_t - r_sl_t, stateful minus stateless reward on the SAME instance) to isolate the causal contribution of accumulated state from base capability, plus cross-task normalization against an external stateless reference.
evaluacion: Frontier models (Claude Opus 4.7/Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro/3 Flash, GPT-5.4) x continual-learning systems (full-context ICL, ICL Notepad, Mem0, ACE playbook, Claude Code, Codex) averaged over 5 rollouts/task; measures normalized reward, normalized gain, and USD cost per system.
numeros_clave: Table1: full-context ICL+Sonnet4.6 ranks #1 (22.3% norm. reward, 25.4% norm. gain, $30.4/run); ACE (dedicated memory playbook) ranks 9th by gain (8.6%) despite the highest cost ($62.8/run); Mem0+GPT-5.4 ranks 4th (15.1% reward, 20.2% gain, $18.3). Naive ICL occupies 3 of the top 5 ranks by gain.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Central finding is that dedicated memory-management systems (Mem0, ACE) underperform naive full-context ICL on the gain metric (Table1) despite far higher cost, directly challenging any MF assumption that adding an explicit memory/consolidation layer necessarily improves online learning over just keeping context.

The gain-vs-cost figure plots normalized gain against USD cost per system and shows ACE's $62.8/run buys LESS gain than $30.4 ICL, confirming MF's stance that memory-architecture cost must be measured against the gain it actually produces, not assumed proportional.

The gain metric (S4.2, gt=r_sf-r_sl on the SAME instance) is a rigorous measured-memory-value construction MF could adopt directly: it isolates the causal contribution of accumulated state from base-model capability, rather than reporting raw accuracy.

The Database Exploration task's concept-drift variant (Fig.1, a schema migration mid-task) explicitly tests whether a system detects and discards STALE past experience rather than blindly reusing it, confirming MF's fidelity/staleness concern is a real, measured failure mode (frontier systems are shown 'rigid in early, incorrect beliefs').

notes: Table 1 rankings + Fig.5 learning curves + Fig.1 Database Exploration concept-drift illustration, arXiv 2606.05661 (Berkeley/Snorkel AI/Wisconsin).

cita: Biswas (2026). COMA: Adaptive Context Budget Management for Memory-Augmented RAG via Query-Aware Zone Allocation, Memory-Conditioned Retrieval, and Cognitive Memory Consolidation.
problema: RAG systems treat context assembly as concatenate-then-truncate with no allocation policy across competing zones (system prompt, working memory, retrieval, episodic history, scratchpad); retrieval is conditioned only on the query, ignoring what the agent already knows; and memory management (promotion/eviction/decay) relies on hand-crafted rules that cannot adapt.
mecanismo: COMA combines (1) a Query-Aware Context Budget Allocator that partitions the token budget across 5 zones via calibrated heuristic profiles conditioned on query complexity/task type/memory state (with a pluggable neural-replacement interface); (2) a Memory-Conditioned Retriever extending Maximal Marginal Relevance to penalize candidates already covered by working memory (score = rel(c,q)*(1-lambda*max cos(c,m))); (3) a Three-Tier Cognitive Memory (sensory/working/long-term) with Ebbinghaus-inspired exponential-decay retention and a 4-operation consolidation engine (extract/consolidate/merge/decay-sweep).
evaluacion: GPT-4.1-mini vs naive-RAG/fixed-allocation/no-memory ablations on (i) a real 10-paper research corpus with LLM-as-judge scoring (relevance/groundedness/completeness/conciseness/recall) and (ii) 3 synthetic multi-turn scenarios (20 turns, 50 docs, planted facts) using 4 new metrics (ContextWaste, MemoryRecall@K, RedundancyScore, ContextEfficiency).
numeros_clave: Real-corpus (Table IV): COMA uses 99,585 tokens vs Naive RAG's 158,233 (37.1% reduction), recall accuracy 1.000 vs 0.500, relevance 0.923 vs 0.910, but lower groundedness 0.464 vs 0.687. Synthetic (Table V): ContextEfficiency 3.725-4.031 vs 0.738-0.747 for Naive RAG (5.4x gain); MemoryRecall@20 = 1.000 vs 0.000 for memory-less baselines; ContextWaste 0.489-0.493 vs 0.650 (24.2% reduction).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central measured result is a budget-allocation policy across 5 competing context zones (Table I) that cuts real-corpus token usage by 37.1% while improving recall (Table IV), confirming MF's stance that context economy across write/retrieve/scratch zones is a first-class, measurable design axis.

The Memory-Conditioned Retriever (Eq.1) penalizes retrieving chunks ALREADY covered by working memory, an explicit 'don't re-fetch what you already know' negative-knowledge filter that directly reduces token waste (RedundancyScore), a pattern MF's retrieval layer could adopt.

The four-operation consolidation engine (Extract/Consolidate/Merge/Decay-sweep, S3.E) with an explicit similarity-threshold merge step (mu=0.85) that prevents 'semantic fragmentation over long conversations' is a concrete, parameterized promotion-to-durable-memory mechanism MF's own consolidation design could mirror.

The paper's own honest limitation (S6) that COMA's lower groundedness score reflects a judge-protocol mismatch (penalizing correct memory-sourced citations as ungrounded) is a cautionary note for MF about how retrieval/fidelity evaluation harnesses must account for cross-turn provenance, not just single-turn chunk citation.

notes: Table I allocation profiles + Table IV real-corpus results + Table V synthetic benchmark + S3.E consolidation engine, single-author preprint (IIT Kharagpur), Harvard Dataverse release.

cita: Chen and Cheng (2026). Learning What to Remember: A Cognitively Grounded Multi-Factor Value Model for Agentic Memory.
problema: Forgetting/consolidation decisions in agentic memory are made at consolidation time, BEFORE the future query is known, yet production systems rank memories by query-similarity (a retrieval-time signal) or recency, both mis-specified for the governing triage decision of what to keep under a fixed memory budget.
mecanismo: A learned multi-factor value V(m)=sum(wi*fi(m)) over 7 cognitive-psychology-grounded factors (emotional intensity, goal relevance, value alignment, self/user relevance, task utility, reliability, usage history); weights are fit by a gradient-free hill-climb optimizer against a downstream objective (gold-evidence retention). The single scalar V(m) uniformly drives encoding depth (4 tiers), a forget score (age and retrieval-count combined with a 1/V(m) resistance term), and retrieval rank, replacing three separately hand-tuned rules. The key methodological move separates 'oracle' goal-relevance (computed against the held-out future query, measuring retrieval) from 'blind' goal-relevance (a query-agnostic session-topic centroid, measuring true forgetting).
evaluacion: A synthetic confound study (60 train/60 test cases with planted value-alignment/self-relevance confounds) plus real LongMemEval-S (479/500 usable cases, oracle vs blind regimes, keep-fraction sweep kappa in [0.1,0.5]) vs uniform-weight/single-factor/recency baselines; an MLP ablation over the same factors tests linear vs nonlinear capacity; all experiments CPU-only, no API calls.
numeros_clave: LongMemEval blind regime (keep 30%, 479 cases): learned multi-factor value retains 0.770+/-0.011 gold evidence vs uniform 0.657, best single factor (self-relevance) 0.518, recency 0.368, goal-only 0.286 (near 0.30 chance floor); oracle regime saturates at 0.993 (goal-only alone reaches 0.979), exposing the retrieval-vs-forgetting metric artifact. Synthetic confound study: learned weighting retains 1.00 vs uniform 0.62, single-factor policies 0.00.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central methodological claim is that scoring goal-relevance against the FUTURE evaluation question ('oracle') saturates retention (~0.98) and looks like a forgetting win, but this 'measures retrieval, not forgetting' -- directly challenging any MF benchmark that scores its own forgetting/consolidation policy using knowledge unavailable at write time.

A single learned scalar V(m) drives encoding depth, forget-risk, AND retrieval rank (fig.1, S3.2) replacing three separately-tuned rules, a unifying write/forget/retrieve trigger design MF's own memory gate could adopt instead of independent heuristics per operation.

Table1's 'reliability' factor (provenance heuristic: user-stated > model-stated) is learned to carry the largest weight (0.64) in the blind regime on real data, empirically confirming MF's provenance/fidelity concern is a measurably dominant signal for what should durably survive consolidation.

The entire evaluation reproduces CPU-only with zero API calls (S6, local sentence-transformer embeddings + gradient-free optimizer over 7 scalars), a concrete demonstration that a useful memory-value signal need not cost an LLM call per item, confirming MF's economy-of-context stance.

notes: Table 3 oracle-vs-blind LongMemEval results + Fig.2/3 + Table 2 synthetic confound study, arXiv 2606.12945 v2.

cita: Liu et al. (2026). StreamMemBench: Streaming Evaluation of Agent Memory for Future-Oriented Assistance.
problema: Existing memory benchmarks test dialogue recall or task-behavior improvement in isolation using synthetic/scripted evidence, leaving untested the full streaming trajectory from real egocentric observations to evidence use in an initial task, feedback incorporation, and follow-up reuse in a later related task.
mecanismo: StreamMemBench builds evidence anchors from EgoLife egocentric lifelog segments (an anchor agent extracts user-specific evidence plus two task queries per anchor; a review agent filters for no-leak/necessity/naturalness); evaluation runs a chronological trajectory (initial task -> response -> user feedback -> post-feedback response -> memory commit -> follow-up task -> response) scored by four metrics: Fidelity (evidence preserved in the memory delta), Initial Evidence Use (IEU), Feedback Incorporation (FI), Follow-up Reuse (FUR).
evaluacion: 2 retrieval baselines (RAGraw, RAGext) + 6 memory systems (Mem0, EverMemOS, A-Mem, MemOS, MemoryOS, MemSkill) x 2 backbones (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Gemini-3-Flash) on 8,107 evidence anchors / 16,214 queries from 3,347 EgoLife segments; temporal-drift analysis across stream position (early/mid/late); a 5-way lifecycle-failure taxonomy; storage/latency/token-cost measurement per segment.
numeros_clave: Table2 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash): A-Mem's highest FUR is 64.98 with 100% Fidelity; MemOS has high FI (77.25) but near-collapsed FUR (2.94) despite 67.97 Fidelity -- a large Fidelity-minus-FUR gap. Table3 per-segment cost: compact systems (EverMemOS 502B, Mem0 569B, MemOS 658B) vs raw/linked (RAGraw 8044B, MemoryOS 8286B); token cost ranges 5.34k (RAGext) to 38.57k (A-Mem)/38.48k (MemoryOS).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Evidence anchors explicitly retain 'a long-term preference, plan, commitment or capability' (S3.1) and generate activity-planning-type task queries, confirming plan-state is one of the first-class memory contents whose future reuse this benchmark measures, directly relevant to MF's plan-state-as-memory need.

The 5-way lifecycle-failure taxonomy (Formation/Initial-use/Feedback-incorporation/Correction-consolidation/Evidence-use-persistence failure, Fig.4) is a concrete template for diagnosing WHERE a memory pipeline silently drops information, a negative-knowledge-style failure attribution MF's own memory gate could adopt.

The central finding -- 'systems with perfect or high Fidelity can still have much lower IEU and FUR' (S4.2), e.g. MemOS 67.97 Fidelity but 2.94 FUR -- directly confirms MF's fidelity concern that storage/retention alone does not guarantee correct future use, a distinct failure mode from staleness or poisoning.

Table3 shows storage, latency, and token cost do NOT move together (e.g. A-Mem is token-expensive at 38.57k/segment despite moderate latency), confirming MF's stance that context economy must be measured on multiple independent axes, not a single proxy.

notes: Table 2 main results + Table 3 storage/latency/token cost + Fig.3 temporal-drift curves + Fig.4 failure taxonomy, arXiv 2606.14571.

cita: Long et al. (2026). MemTrace: Probing What Final Accuracy Misses in Long-Term Memory.
problema: Memory benchmarks aggregate accuracy over independent question rows/episodes, hiding how a SINGLE fact behaves as conditions change (aging, question type, evidence present/missing/conflicting); pooled scores cannot show that a system answering a fact's current state correctly may still fail on its trajectory or under a false premise.
mecanismo: MemTrace uses the 'knowledge point' (a single typed user fact) as the unit of measurement; each fact is probed along 3 controlled dimensions -- memory age (8 chronological checkpoints), question type (current/historical/trajectory), evidence condition (present/missing/conflicting) -- scored on Gist accuracy/Verbatim completeness/Response type, plus a failure-attribution protocol (oracle-with-gold-evidence vs retriever-reach-vs-use replay) distinguishing unreachable from reachable-but-unused evidence.
evaluacion: 13 memory-system configurations across 4 paradigms (long-context: Qwen3.5-35B/Gemini-3-Flash/GPT-5-nano; RAG: BM25/text-emb-3-small/Qwen3-Emb/HippoRAG-v2; external-memory: Mem0/SimpleMem/REMem/AMem; agentic: MIRIX/Mem-T) on 835 knowledge points/20 users, expanded to 15,422 question rows and 200,453 scored answers (built from HaluMem-Medium).
numeros_clave: When systems fail, gold evidence was retrievable ~10x more often than missing (dominant bottleneck = evidence USE not retrieval). Saturated trajectory Gist collapses for long-context models: Qwen3.5-35B 49.0%(fresh)->6.7%(saturated), GPT-5-nano 38.4%->6.5%. Boundary-safe systems (Mem0 99.3% boundary abstention) barely resolve conflicts (Mem0 conflict Gist 14.6%). Oracle-evidence lift on hard failure subsets: +65.6 to +85.0 percentage points (Fig.5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's headline finding is that when systems fail, the evidence was retrievable ~10x more often than missing -- 'improving memory depends on using reachable evidence, not on more storage or retrieval' -- directly challenging any MF assumption that better retrieval/storage is the main lever, when evidence-USE is the dominant bottleneck.

The failure-attribution protocol (oracle-on-hard-failures + reach-vs-use replay, S3.4/Fig.5) is exactly a measured decomposition of retrieval-reach vs generation-use, directly confirming MF's stance that retrieval quality must be isolated and measured, not inferred from end accuracy.

Table4/Fig.4 shows boundary-safe systems (Mem0, AMem, REMem) that correctly abstain on missing evidence (94-99%) nonetheless fail to correct FALSE-PREMISE (conflict) probes (14.6-35.1% Gist), confirming MF's fidelity concern that safe abstention and active conflict-resolution are separate capabilities a memory system can have one without the other.

Trajectory questions (how a fact changed over time) require connecting MULTIPLE stored states with correct temporal order, not a single lookup (S4.2), evidence that a derived/cached index needs to preserve state history and ordering, not just the latest value, to support trajectory-style queries.

notes: Table 3 memory-maintenance by question type + Table 4 conflict/boundary profile + Fig.4/5 diagnostics, arXiv 2606.17328.

cita: Yang, D. (2026). Control-Plane Placement Shapes Forgetting: An Architectural Study of Agent Memory Across Thirteen System Configurations.
problema: Production memory failures are predominantly FORGETTING failures (rotated credentials still recommended, GDPR-deleted records still surfacing) rather than recall failures, yet every existing memory benchmark scores only recall; the control plane (supersede/release/purge) is largely untested, and it is unknown WHERE in the pipeline an LLM should sit to recover which forgetting failure modes.
mecanismo: ForgetEval decomposes forgetting into 5 structural families (supersession, decay, amnesia, purge, drift), scored by deterministic substring match (no LLM judge in the eval loop) across a 1000-case template suite plus a 385-case adversarial layer (10 attack categories: prefix_collision, cross_lingual_identifier, compound_fact, etc.); a 6-method Adapter Protocol (3 mandatory recall primitives + 3 optional mutation primitives with honest N/A scoring) lets heterogeneous memory stores be compared apples-to-apples; compares 13 system configurations spanning 6 placement regimes for WHERE the LLM sits (no-deletion/deterministic/vec-only/inscribe-time-LLM/KG-abstraction/mutation-time-hook).
evaluacion: 13 system configurations (Lethe, Mem0, LangGraph/LangMem, MemPalace + LLM-hook and inscribe-time variants) on the 385-case adversarial suite + 1000-case template suite; cross-evaluation on the Memora benchmark (150 questions/10 personas) to test axis-complementarity; 10-annotator IAA + cross-family LLM-judge audit + 77-case external-authored replication subset; embedder-swap ablation.
numeros_clave: Deterministic systems cluster 62.9-68.3% overall on the 385-case suite; a mutation-time LLM hook lifts non-primitive-existence cases (n=345) by +22.6 to +24.1pt (70.1-70.7% -> 93.3-94.2%), headline overall 91.7-93.2%, at ~$0.17/385-case run, mutation latency ~2.3s/case vs 64-191ms/case deterministic. MemPalace: 0/385 on ForgetEval-Adv (no deletion primitive) but 60/150 (40%) on Memora recall-heavy benchmark (axis-flip).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Central claim is that 'production failures are predominantly forgetting failures... yet existing memory benchmarks measure only recall', directly challenging any MF assumption that a well-measured retrieval/recall layer is sufficient; forgetting/deletion is shown to be an independent, under-tested axis (MemPalace: 0/385 forgetting despite 60/150 recall).

The paper's core architectural finding is WHERE the LLM sits relative to the recall vs control (mutation) plane determines which forgetting failure modes recover (S1, Fig.2): inscribe-time LLM fixes canonicalization but not intent-aware deletion, mutation-time hook fixes both -- a concrete placement lesson for where MF should put its own write/forget-trigger LLM calls.

The mutation-time-hook lift (91.7-93.2% overall) costs only ~$0.17/385-case run and ~2.3s/case (mutations only) while leaving the recall hot path LLM-free and unchanged, confirming MF's stance that a targeted, narrowly-scoped LLM call (not a blanket one) can buy large capability gains cheaply.

The five forgetting families (supersession/decay/amnesia/purge/drift) and identifier-canonicalization attacks (cross-script, prefix-collision) are exactly staleness/provenance failure modes MF's FIDELIDAD concern targets, empirically shown recoverable only by specific architectural placements, not by recall quality.

notes: Table 2 385-case adversarial results + Table 3 Memora axis-flip cross-eval + Fig.2 placement regimes, arXiv 2606.15903 v2.

cita: Ma et al. (2026). MEMPROBE: Probing Long-Term Agent Memory via Hidden User-State Recovery.
problema: Memory evaluation relies on downstream task success, which is a weak diagnostic: a memoryless agent achieves near-perfect task success, so task completion cannot distinguish good memory formation from none, and the memory ARTIFACT itself (what durable user state got written and remains recoverable) is left unaudited.
mecanismo: MemProbe treats memory as a post-interaction auditable artifact: 50 simulated users each carry a hidden 31-dimension taxonomy-anchored user-state bank (skill/knowledge/episodic/self-model/assistance-preference); leak-controlled tasks (indirect design + anti-fishing critic) elicit evidence without naming the target; after the trajectory, each hidden dimension is reconstructed from the memory store under two read modes -- full-store dump_all (probes whether evidence was ever WRITTEN) vs top-k retrieve (probes whether it is REACHABLE) -- scored by an LLM judge against ground truth (category-balanced recovery score B); a 3-stage failure-attribution pipeline (task-design / disclosure / elicitation-vs-strictness) localizes where recovery loss occurred.
evaluacion: 5 memory systems (nomem, longctx_full, amem/A-Mem, mem0/Mem0, memt/Mem-T) across 50 simulated users x 31 dimensions (1,550 recovery targets), measuring task-completion rate, preference score, turns, reconstruction score B (full-store vs top-k), and memory footprint.
numeros_clave: All systems saturate task completion at 99.87-99.94% INCLUDING nomem (no memory at all); reconstruction B stays moderate: full-store 0.611-0.624 for amem/mem0/longctx_full vs 0.000 for nomem, dropping to 0.465-0.540 under top-k retrieval. Episodic-memory category is hardest across all systems (0.242-0.451 full-store/top-k) vs assistance-preference easiest (0.721-0.773).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The headline finding is that task success and memory formation are DISTINCT capabilities -- a memoryless agent (nomem) attains near-perfect task success (99.935%) yet 0.000 reconstruction, directly challenging any MF assumption that downstream task/behavioral success is a valid proxy for whether durable memory was actually formed.

The dual full-store-vs-top-k read protocol (S3.1) is precisely a measured decomposition of write-side vs read-side failure, confirming MF's stance that retrieval must be measured SEPARATELY from whether information was ever captured, not conflated into one aggregate score.

The paper identifies 'retrieval-aware consolidation' as the major bottleneck: systems capture raw interaction but 'seldom distill it into compact user state' (S1) -- capacity and retrieval tuning alone cannot fix what only a better WRITE/consolidation policy can, challenging any MF assumption that a good retriever compensates for a weak consolidation step.

Table3 shows EPISODIC memory (binding an event to its context and consequence) is the hardest category to recover across every system (0.242-0.451) versus stable preferences (0.721-0.773), confirming MF's fidelity concern that different memory TYPES have measurably different durability and cannot be treated as a single undifferentiated store.

notes: Table 2 main results + Table 3 category breakdown + S3.5 failure-attribution pipeline, arXiv 2606.24595 (preprint, UIC/KU Leuven/UCSD).

cita: Wang (2026). MemDelta: Controlled Baselines and Hidden Confounds in Agent Memory Evaluation.
problema: Agent memory system evaluations conflate the memory ARCHITECTURE with confounded changes in the language model, embedding model, or retrieval pipeline, so it is unclear what a reported 'memory gain' is actually measuring.
mecanismo: MemDelta is a controlled protocol that varies exactly one component at a time (retrieval quality, embedding choice, base-model behavior, write-path cost) while holding the rest of the pipeline fixed (7 strategies: no-memory, random-RAG, full-context, self-memory scratchpad, MiniLM-RAG, cloud-embedding-RAG, Mem0 extraction, on LongMemEval-S), with paired McNemar significance tests and explicit write-path cost accounting (LLM calls, wall-clock, dollars) per strategy.
evaluacion: LongMemEval-S (500 questions, 6 types, 3 model families: GPT-4o-mini/Claude Sonnet/Gemini 2.5 Flash); 6 controlled pairwise comparisons isolating each confound; matched-instance cost-accuracy audit of Mem0 vs verbatim RAG on 88 instances.
numeros_clave: Verbatim RAG (MiniLM) matches full-context GPT-4o-mini (47.2% vs 49.8%, p=0.34), but the ranking reverses per model: Sonnet gains +31pp from RAG (63% of full-context queries refused) while Gemini gains +14pp from full context. A single embedding swap (MiniLM->cloud) shifts accuracy +6.2pp (p=0.004) and flips Mem0-vs-RAG: Mem0 beats MiniLM-RAG by +11pp but loses to cloud-RAG by -1.2pp. On 88 matched instances, Mem0 (72.7%) ties cloud RAG (73.9%, p=1.0) at 50x the write-path cost.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's core demonstration is that a reported '+11pp memory architecture gain' (Mem0 vs RAG) was ENTIRELY an embedding confound that reverses to -1.2pp under a single component swap, directly challenging any MF claim attributing an observed gain to a memory-architecture decision without holding embeddings/model/cost fixed.

The matched-instance audit shows Mem0 ties verbatim RAG (72.7% vs 73.9%) at 50x the write-path cost (1,000+ LLM calls, $0.50+, ~120min vs $0.01/instance), confirming MF's stance that write-path cost must be reported alongside accuracy before crediting an architecture with a gain.

The recommended protocol (report a named-embedding RAG baseline, include random retrieval, test >=2 model families, disclose embedding-swap sensitivity, report write-path cost) is a direct, actionable methodology for how MF should measure its own retrieval layer to avoid confounded conclusions.

The Sonnet case study (63% of full-context queries explicitly refused despite the answer being present in the 115K-token context, dropping to 41% at 47K tokens) shows apparent 'memory failure' can actually be a model-specific long-context attention failure unrelated to the memory system, confirming MF should separate storage/retrieval fidelity from generator behavior when diagnosing failures.

notes: Table 3 main results + Table 5 embedding ablation + Table 6/7 matched cost-accuracy audit, arXiv 2606.29914.

cita: Filatov (2026). RPR-Memory: Decomposing Retrieval, Policy, and Reasoning in Persistent Memory Systems.
problema: Persistent-memory benchmarks reduce evaluation to one aggregate score, hiding WHERE a system fails: missing evidence (retrieval), wrong exposed state (read-time policy), or failed composition (reasoning), so an apparent 'memory failure' cannot be localized or fixed.
mecanismo: RPR-Memory decomposes persistent-memory pipelines into three diagnostic layers (Retrieval R+, read-time Policy, Reasoning A+) via a per-(system,query) 2x2 matrix (R+A+/R+A-/R-A+/R-A-) and three hard probes (compositional-chain, version/supersession, temporal-window) run through a common six-primitive interface (write/read/search/update/forget/consolidate) wrapping 37 heterogeneous architectures; a controlled 3-arm causal intervention (original / write-time-supersession-only / read-time query-conditioned router) on one in-house semantic-fact store isolates whether a 'memory failure' is fixable at write time or read time.
evaluacion: 37 memory architectures (35 in-house + Mem0 v2.0.2 + HippoRAG v2.0.0a4) on 3 hard probes (chain n=50/51q, version n=50/152q, temporal n=50/150q) under a fixed local llama3.1:8b composer; a post-freeze temporal ladder + 6-participant human pilot comparing strict vs semantic EM; external-only sensitivity check; controlled write/read-time intervention with pre-registered falsification bound.
numeros_clave: Retrieval saturates before correctness: chain R+=0.977 but P(A+|R+)=0.377; temporal R+=0.968 but P=0.314 (between-window subtype collapses to P=0.027 despite R+=0.987). Version-resolution causal core: adding write-time supersession lifts current-state update correctness from 0.000 to 0.680 but breaks history-sensitive exact match (0.816->0.355); only a query-conditioned read-time router recovers both. Human pilot: between-window rows move from 0.000 strict to 0.967 semantic EM, while the model stays at 0.078 even with oracle-filtered candidates.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central methodology, a per-axis R+/P(A+|R+) matrix that separates retrieval success from post-retrieval correctness (Table3/Fig.2), is exactly the measured, decomposed retrieval evaluation MF's G-M2 need calls for, showing retrieval can saturate (R+=0.977) while conditional correctness stays low (0.377), which an aggregate score would hide.

The version-resolution finding that 'read-time state exposure is a separate, repairable layer' distinct from write-time supersession gives MF a concrete architectural distinction between what to STOP writing (superseded facts) vs what to FILTER at read time, informing a negative-knowledge/staleness design that need not conflate the two.

The causal intervention shows write-time supersession ALONE creates a seam conflict: fixing current-state correctness (0.000->0.680) actively BREAKS history-sensitive exact match (0.816->0.355) in the same store, challenging any MF assumption that a single write-time policy can serve both current-state and historical-lookup needs without a read-time query-conditioned split.

The paper shows a system can achieve high aggregate exact match (0.816) while stale-hit leakage is 1.000 and current-state update correctness is 0.000 (the 'motivating paradox'), directly confirming MF's fidelity/staleness concern that aggregate accuracy can mask complete failure on the specific state-resolution behavior a query needs.

notes: Table 3/4/5 retrieval-vs-correctness decomposition + Table 8 human-pilot temporal ladder, arXiv preprint 2026-07-01, independent researcher.

cita: Xiang et al. (2026). MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory.
problema: Existing memory benchmarks evaluate only whether memories are correctly stored, retrieved, or updated, ignoring how retrieved memories influence downstream reasoning; this overlooks 'memory-induced sycophancy', where agents over-align with outdated or inapplicable historical user beliefs at the cost of factual accuracy or objective reasoning.
mecanismo: MemSyco-Bench defines 5 task categories: 3 where memory should be SUPPRESSED (Objective Fact Judgment, Contextual Scope Control, Memory-Evidence Conflict) and 2 where memory should be SELECTED/USED correctly (Valid Memory Selection, Personalized Memory Use), built via a 4-step pipeline: memory-decision schema construction, question instantiation with target vs memory-misleading answers, long-term dialogue simulation embedding memory cues naturally, and multi-stage quality validation (semantic relatedness, memory-use boundary, failure direction).
evaluacion: Preliminary studies establish that memory snippets induce sycophancy and that existing benchmarks' errors are retrieval-driven; main experiments evaluate 7 memory systems (NaiveRAG, Mem0, A-Mem, LightMem, MemGPT, MemoryBank, SuperMemory) x 2 backbones (Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash) across the 5 tasks, reporting Accuracy plus Sycophancy Rate / Memory-Use Metrics.
numeros_clave: Preliminary: adding a misleading memory snippet drops DeepSeek-V4-Flash's objective accuracy from 56.1% to 40.2% and raises sycophancy rate from 24.3% to 52.3%. Existing benchmarks are retrieval-dominated: R-/A- accounts for 47.4-66.1% of errors vs R+/A- only 5.8-13.7% (Fig.3). Main results (Qwen3-8B, Objective Fact Judgment): No-Memory 49.12% Acc vs memory-system settings 26.00-36.00% (all WORSE); Contextual Scope Control sycophancy rate for Mem0/LightMem hits 51.00/79.67% vs Full-Dialog baseline 40.33%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Existing memory benchmarks' errors are dominated by retrieval failure (R-/A- = 47.4-66.1%) while post-retrieval misuse (R+/A-) is rare (5.8-13.7%) in THOSE benchmarks, yet on MemSyco-Bench's own tasks memory systems actively WORSEN accuracy vs a no-memory baseline, challenging any MF assumption that solving retrieval is sufficient once post-retrieval reasoning is also measured.

Central finding is that current memory systems (Mem0, A-Mem, LightMem, MemGPT, etc.) 'do not reliably mitigate memory-induced sycophancy' and often move sycophancy rate in the WRONG direction relative to a no-memory/full-dialog baseline (Table1), directly challenging any MF assumption that adding a memory layer is safe by default without an explicit mechanism to suppress inapplicable retrieved memory.

The five-task taxonomy cleanly separates 'memory should be suppressed' (objective facts, scope, evidence-conflict) from 'memory should be selected/used' (valid-selection, personalization) as DISTINCT decision problems (S3.2), a seam MF's own retrieval/generation-gating policy could adopt to decide per-query whether a retrieved memory should influence the answer at all.

The R+/A+ vs R+/A- vs R-/A- error-attribution protocol (S2.2, Fig.3) used to show existing benchmarks are retrieval-dominated is itself a measured decomposition of retrieval success from generation-time correctness, confirming MF's stance that retrieval and post-retrieval use must be measured as separate axes.

notes: Fig.2/3 preliminary studies + Table 1 main results (5 tasks x 7 memory systems x 2 backbones), arXiv 2607.01071 v2, work-in-progress (Xiamen/Jilin).

cita: Roth et al. (2024). Pairing Analogy-Augmented Generation with Procedural Memory for Procedural Q&A.
problema: LLMs struggle to synthesize disparate pieces of information into a coherent procedure for unfamiliar/specialized domains (not well-represented in training data); plain RAG retrieves generic text passages rather than adapting analogous prior PROCEDURES (input/output/ordered-steps) via structural/relational similarity to a new task.
mecanismo: Analogy-Augmented Generation (AAG): a procedural memory store holds procedures (input, output, ordered steps) as dense 768-d embeddings (all-mpnet-base-v2), written once and retrieved by cosine similarity; a query generator decomposes the input query into up to N=4 HyDE-style sub-questions to retrieve K=3 analogous procedures per sub-question; an answer generator filters/synthesizes each retrieved analogy into a Q&A context; an iterative LLM-critic self-refinement loop (up to T=3 cycles) edits the draft procedure until no further edits are suggested.
evaluacion: LLM-based pairwise evaluation (10 calls/sample, position-debiased, majority vote) vs Zero-Shot/Few-Shot/RAG/ReAct baselines on LCStep (unfamiliar domain, 276 LangChain-tutorial procedures) and RecipeNLG (familiar domain, 10k-recipe subset); corroborated by a blind human study on RecipeNLG (50 examples, 3-6 raters/pair); full ablation removing each of the 3 AAG components (query generator, answer generator, critic refinement) in all permutations; also surveyed on CHAMP (math) in the appendix.
numeros_clave: Table1 pairwise vs RAG: AAG wins 69.64% / loses 12.50% (LCStep); wins 85.70% / loses 7.60% (RecipeNLG). Vs ReAct: AAG wins 98.21% (LCStep) / 97.65% (RecipeNLG). Blind human study on RecipeNLG (50 examples): AAG preferred in 56% of instances vs RAG preferred in 16% (28% tie). Ablation vs NO-answer-generator: AAG wins only 39.28%/loses 39.28% on LCStep (near-tie, component matters less there) but wins 58.45%/loses 26.20% on RecipeNLG (component matters clearly there).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Procedural memory stores structured (input,output,steps) objects retrieved by embedding similarity and then ADAPTED via analogy rather than copied verbatim (S4.1-4.3); the composability property (two procedures chain into one) lets stored steps be recombined, a derived-index pattern MF could adopt for procedural playbooks distinct from factual retrieval.

The full ablation (Table1, removing query-generator/answer-generator/critic in all permutations, scored by pairwise LLM judging) isolates each pipeline component's marginal contribution rather than reporting only end-to-end task success, confirming MF's stance that a retrieval/analogy mechanism's value must be measured component-by-component -- and the ablation shows the answer-generator's contribution is domain-dependent (near-tie on LCStep, clear on RecipeNLG), not uniformly load-bearing.

notes: Table 1 pairwise win/loss/tie (LCStep + RecipeNLG) + S5.5 human study (56% vs 16%) + S5.6 ablation permutations, arXiv 2409.01344 (2024, EMNLP-era; older cohort than the corpus's typical 2026 papers but on-topic for procedural memory).

cita: Kong et al. (2025). MapAgent: Trajectory-Constructed Memory-Augmented Planning for Mobile Task Automation.
problema: LLM-based mobile GUI agents lack real-world knowledge of specific apps, causing hallucinations and ineffective planning because they cannot remember prior interactions with an app and must re-explore it from scratch each time.
mecanismo: A trajectory-based memory mechanism (WRITE) uses an MLLM to summarize each page of a trajectory (description, key UI elements, action path, label) into a page chunk, vectorized and stored per-app in a Milvus database; coarse-to-fine planning schedules subtasks to apps then retrieves top-k=3 similar pages by cosine similarity to augment the LLM Planner; a dual-LLM (Decision-maker + Judge) executor tracks task progress via short-term memory across steps.
evaluacion: Evaluated on real Android devices (Xiaomi 14, ADB) with GPT-4o on SPA-Bench (340 tasks, single/cross-app, EN/ZH) and the CHOP dataset (60 tasks, 3 difficulty levels), compared against AutoDroid, AppAgent, MobileAgentV2, SeeAct and M3A, plus per-step time/token-cost measurement.
numeros_clave: SPA-Bench single-app success 0.627 EN/0.553 ZH vs M3A 0.640/0.447; cross-app 0.350/0.350 vs M3A 0.200/0.100; CHOP overall 0.800 EN/0.700 ZH vs best baseline 0.700/0.633; cost $0.040/step at 14.6s vs M3A $0.092/step at 19.3s.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the dual-LLM Judge maintains an explicit natural-language task-progress state (evaluation/progress/next-action, Eq.8-9) fed back into the Decision-maker each step, a concrete plan-state channel MF could adapt for tracking sub-goal completion.

coarse-to-fine retrieval (top-k=3 cosine similarity over page vectors, Eq.5) is measured end-to-end against 5 real baselines and drives the success-rate gains, supporting MF's bet on a measured retrieval layer over ad-hoc context stuffing.

Fig.3 explicitly plots mean token-cost-per-step (USD) and mean time-per-step, showing MapAgent reaches a better accuracy/cost trade-off than heavier baselines, external evidence for treating cost as a first-class metric.

notes: Numbers from Table 1/2 (SPA-Bench/CHOP results) and Fig.3 (cost-vs-time scatter); ablation Table 3 (memory+Judge) referenced in text.

cita: Fang et al. (2025). Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory.
problema: LLM agents suffer from brittle procedural memory that is either manually hand-engineered as prompt templates or entangled in static model parameters, so there is no systematic, learnable way to build, retrieve and update reusable procedural knowledge across trajectories.
mecanismo: Build (WRITE) distills past trajectories into fine-grained step-by-step Trajectory memories and higher-level Script abstractions (or their combination, Proceduralization), stored as raw trajectory text (DOCS-ARCHIVOS) and retrieved via query- or keyword-based (AveFact) vector matching (VECTOR); Update applies dynamic add (ADMISION), validation-filtering, reflexion and dynamic-discarding (OLVIDO) strategies (ACTUALIZACION) that periodically consolidate the memory bank as new experience arrives.
evaluacion: Evaluated on TravelPlanner and ALFWorld with GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-sonnet and Qwen2.5-72B backbones; ablations on memory granularity (Table1), retrieval key strategy (Table2), online update strategy (vanilla/validation/reflexion, Fig.3), and cross-model transfer (GPT-4o memory reused by Qwen2.5-14B).
numeros_clave: Proceduralization raises ALFWorld test success from 42.14% (no memory) to 87.14%/77.86% with GPT-4o; reflexion-based update beats the 2nd-best update strategy by +0.7 points and cuts 14 steps by the final trajectory group; transferring GPT-4o's memory to Qwen2.5-14B raises task completion by ~5% and cuts avg steps by 1.6.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the dynamic Update module (validation-filtering + reflexion + discarding, §4.3) directly measures which consolidation strategy best promotes successful trajectories into durable memory, supporting MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion design.

reports step-count reduction as a measured efficiency proxy for token/latency savings (Fig.1, Table1) — a cheap pattern MF could reuse to track context economy without instrumenting raw token counters.

the Validation/Adjustment update strategies (§4.3) explicitly guard against stale or erroneous memory entries by filtering to only successful trajectories, evidence for MF's anti-drift/staleness discipline.

notes: Numbers from Table 1 (Build ablation), Fig.3 (update-strategy reward/steps curves), Fig.5b (cross-model transfer), §4.2-4.4.

cita: Han et al. (2025). LEGOMem: Modular Procedural Memory for Multi-agent LLM Systems for Workflow Automation.
problema: Multi-agent LLM workflow-automation systems (an orchestrator delegating to specialized task agents) remain stateless and transactional — each task is solved from scratch discarding prior experience — and no prior procedural-memory work addresses the placement/allocation problem specific to multi-agent coordination.
mecanismo: An offline construction phase (WRITE) distills successful trajectories into full-task memories (task description + high-level plan) and subtask memories (agent-specific tool traces), indexed by dense-embedding vector stores (VECTOR) per orchestrator and per task-agent; at inference three retrieval/allocation variants (vanilla, Dynamic just-in-time, QueryRewrite) allocate full-task memory to the orchestrator and subtask memory to each task agent (role-aware, MULTIAGENTE placement).
evaluacion: Evaluated on OfficeBench (300 multi-app office tasks, 148 train/152 test, 3 difficulty levels) across LLM-only (GPT-4o), Hybrid (GPT-4o orchestrator + GPT-4o-mini agents), and SLM-only (GPT-4o-mini) teams, against No-memory/Synapse/AWM baselines, with ablations on memory placement (orchestrator vs agent vs both) and retrieval variant.
numeros_clave: LEGOMem improves overall task success rate by +12.61%, +12.72%, +13.38% absolute over memory-less LLM/Hybrid/SLM teams respectively; Hybrid team + LEGOMem-QueryRewrite reaches 50.22% success, surpassing the memory-less full-LLM team's 45.83%; in the task-agent-only memory setting, Dynamic/QueryRewrite beat vanilla by 4-5% for Hybrid teams.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the orchestrator dynamically regenerates the next subtask from current state and can re-plan on stalled progress (§3.1.1, Algorithm 1) — an explicit plan/re-plan state machine MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor could reuse.

Table2's placement ablation shows orchestrator memory and per-agent subtask memory are distinct, single-purpose stores whose separate placement (not one shared blob) drives most of the gain, evidence for single-source-per-fact allocation across roles.
three retrieval strategies (vanilla/Dynamic/QueryRewrite) are measured head-to-head on OfficeBench (Table2) rather than assumed, supporting MF's insistence on a measured retrieval layer.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main results) and Table2 (placement/retrieval ablation), §4.2 Main results.

cita: Cao et al. (2025). Remember Me, Refine Me: A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution.
problema: Existing procedural-memory frameworks follow a 'passive accumulation' paradigm — memory is a static append-only archive that is never adapted to new contexts nor pruned of harmful entries, so the experience pool degrades into a mixture of valid insights and toxic noise over time.
mecanismo: Multi-faceted distillation (WRITE/ADMISION) extracts success-pattern, failure-analysis and comparative-insight experiences from sampled trajectories, validated by an LLM judge and deduplicated before being embedded (VECTOR) by usage-scenario; context-adaptive reuse retrieves top-K by cosine similarity then reranks and rewrites experiences for the new task (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); utility-based refinement (CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION) tracks per-experience retrieval-frequency and utility, selectively adding only successful trajectories and pruning entries whose utility/frequency ratio falls below a threshold.
evaluacion: Evaluated on BFCL-V3 (150 test tasks) and AppWorld (168 test-normal tasks) with Qwen3-8B/14B/32B backbones, reporting Avg@4 and Pass@4 against No-Memory, A-Mem and LangMem baselines, plus ablations on extraction granularity (trajectory- vs keypoint-level, Table2) and on addition/reflection/deletion components (Table3).
numeros_clave: Qwen3-8B+ReMe(dynamic) beats No-Memory by 8.83% Avg@4 / 7.29% Pass@4 on average across benchmarks; on AppWorld Qwen3-8B rises from 14.97% (no memory) to 24.70% Avg@4 / 42.06% Pass@4; keypoint-level extraction (44.50/65.77) beats trajectory-level (43.00/60.00) on BFCL-V3 for Qwen3-8B (Table2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: utility-based deletion (Eq.1, §3.4) explicitly measures which memories to keep vs prune based on a retrieval-utility ratio, directly supporting promotion/demotion of gotchas into durable recipes.

ablation Table3 shows selective addition (only successful trajectories) outperforms full addition (which also distills failures) because failure-derived entries introduce noise, evidence memory must guard provenance/quality rather than just accumulate.

the abstract's memory-scaling claim (small Qwen3-8B+ReMe beats larger memory-less Qwen3-14B) is framed as a compute-efficiency argument relevant to MF's context-economy lens, though token/latency cost itself is not directly measured.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main BFCL-V3/AppWorld results), Table2 (granularity ablation), Table3 (component ablation).

cita: Wang et al. (2026). EffiSkill: Agent Skill Based Automated Code Efficiency Optimization.
problema: LLM-based code-efficiency optimization methods operate instance-by-instance (one-shot rewriting, retrieved exemplars, or search-based rewriting) and never distill reusable optimization knowledge, so recurring slow-to-fast transformation mechanisms are re-discovered per task rather than captured once and reused across tasks.
mecanismo: Stage I (offline WRITE/CONSOLIDACION) mines large-scale slow/fast program pairs into structured traces, abstracts them into signatures, hybrid-clusters (TF-IDF + embeddings) and distills each cluster into a documented 'Operator Skill' or higher-level 'Meta Skill' card stored as a skill-card file library (DOCS-ARCHIVOS); Stage II applies the library execution-free at inference — diagnosis, skill retrieval (3 candidate sets, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO), plan composition (2-3 plans per bundle) and candidate generation, without any runtime execution feedback.
evaluacion: Evaluated on EffiBench-X (623 tasks, Python and C++ subsets, execution-based runtime measurement) with GPT-5-mini and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct backbones, against prompting/retrieval/search-based baselines including SBLLM, using a public/private test split for candidate ranking and final correctness/efficiency scoring.
numeros_clave: Improves optimization success rate over the strongest baseline by 3.69-12.52 percentage points across settings: +12.03pp (C++) and +4.98pp (Python) with GPT-5-mini; +12.36pp (C++) and +8.67pp (Python) with Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Operator/Meta Skill cards (Fig.2) are explicit typed narrative documents (skill_id, triggers, transformation steps, pitfalls) mined offline and reused as ground truth at inference, a concrete pattern for MF's typed-docs-as-truth Tier-1.

Stage I explicitly clusters and merges near-duplicate mined traces (TF-IDF cosine merge threshold 0.8, §3.2) into a compact skill library, direct evidence for promoting scattered instance-level lessons into durable, deduplicated recipes.

the execution-free inference design (no runtime candidate-execution feedback loop, §2.1) trades a larger offline mining cost for near-zero per-task inference compute, a pattern relevant to MF's context-economy tradeoffs.

notes: Numbers from Abstract and §4 (EffiBench-X results per language/backbone); skill-card structure in Fig.2, §3.2 mining pipeline.

cita: Cheng et al. (2026). Mem2Evolve: Towards Self-Evolving Agents via Co-Evolutionary Capability Expansion and Experience Distillation.
problema: Existing self-evolving agent frameworks treat experience-accumulation and capability-creation (new tools/expert agents) as isolated processes: experience-centric methods stay bounded by a fixed pre-defined toolset, while capability-centric methods create new assets from scratch with no experiential guidance, causing unstable, non-replicable capability growth.
mecanismo: A dual-memory design couples Asset Memory (agent bank + tool bank, structured records combining role/expertise text and executable tool code — HIBRIDA) with Experience Memory (title/context/use-cases/distilled-knowledge records, WRITE); forward inference recruits from Asset Memory by similarity or creates new tools/agents on-demand guided by retrieved experience (ADMISION + RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, MULTIAGENTE recruitment of expert agents); backward evolution runs an LLM-judge trajectory evaluation, a self-correction/test-validation loop before persisting new assets (FIDELIDAD), then reflects to distill success/failure lessons and merges them into Experience Memory (ACTUALIZACION/CONSOLIDACION).
evaluacion: Evaluated across 6 task categories and 8 benchmarks (GAIA, ALFWorld, WebShop, TravelPlanner, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, AIME24/25) with GPT-5-chat, against naive-LLM, experience-centric (DyLAN, EvoAgent, AFLOW, DSPy) and capability-centric (Alita, AgentVerse, AutoAgents, SwarmAgentic) baselines, plus an ablation removing Tool Creation / Expert-Agent Creation / Experience Distillation (Table3).
numeros_clave: Mem2Evolve reaches 70.24% avg Pass@1 across 8 benchmarks, beating naive-LLM by 18.53%, experience-centric best (AFLOW) by 11.80%, capability-centric best (Alita) by 6.46%; on GAIA it gains +57.84% Pass@1 over a minimal-toolset baseline; ablation shows removing Tool Creation causes the largest drop (-10.28%), removing Expert-Agent Creation -1.72%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: backward evolution explicitly promotes only validated, test-passing assets and reflected lessons into persistent memory (§3.3.2-3.3.3), a direct instance of consolidating transient trial outcomes into durable recipes.
new tools/agents must pass an LLM-synthesized test suite (Valid(mnew,ct), Eq.8) before being merged into Asset Memory, guarding against poisoning the capability store with unreliable assets.

splitting memory into a typed Asset Memory (tools/agents) versus Experience Memory (lessons) with distinct schemas (Eq.1-4) is a concrete multi-store seam design MF's COSTURAS anchor could compare against.

notes: Numbers from Table2 (main 8-benchmark Pass@1) and Table3/§5.1 (ablation: -10.28%/-1.72%).

cita: Lin et al. (2026). Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses.
problema: Automating coding-agent harness engineering (system prompt, tools, middleware, skills, memory) is hard because the action space is heterogeneous, raw trajectories bury actionable signal in millions of tokens, and edit effects are hard to attribute, so harness improvement remains a manual, ad-hoc craft that struggles to keep pace with rapidly advancing base models.
mecanismo: Three observability pillars close the loop: component observability exposes seven harness component types (including long-term memory) as explicit versioned files so edits are revertible (WRITE); experience observability (Agent Debugger) distills millions of raw trajectory tokens into a layered, drill-down per-task evidence corpus an Evolve Agent can consume (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); decision observability pairs every edit with a self-declared falsifiable prediction in a change manifest, verified against the next round's task-level outcomes — edits that fail their prediction are reverted at file granularity (OLVIDO) while validated ones are committed via git (ACTUALIZACION).
evaluacion: 10 AHE iterations on the full 89-task Terminal-Bench 2 (GPT-5.4 high, ~32h), compared against human-designed harnesses (OpenCode, Terminus-2, Codex) and self-evolving baselines (ACE, Training-Free GRPO); cross-benchmark transfer to SWE-bench-verified (500 tasks) and cross-model transfer to 5 alternate base models, plus a per-component ablation (memory/tools/middleware/prompt) isolating where the gain lives.
