numeros_clave: AHE lifts Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 from 69.7% (seed) to 77.0%, beating Codex (71.9%), ACE (68.9%) and TF-GRPO (72.3%); on SWE-bench-verified it reaches the highest aggregate success (75.6%) while using 12% fewer tokens than the seed and 32%/21% fewer than ACE/TF-GRPO; cross-model transfer yields +5.1 to +10.1pp gains across 3 alternate model families; component ablation shows tools/middleware/long-term-memory each beat the seed alone while the system-prompt-only swap regresses.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: component observability represents every editable harness piece (prompt, tools, middleware, skills, long-term memory) as an explicit file at a fixed mount point with one git commit per edit (§3.1), a concrete instance of typed, versioned narrative-as-truth close to MF's Tier-1 anchor.

reports tokens/trial explicitly (Table2) and shows the evolved harness cuts aggregate tokens by 12-32% versus baselines on a transfer benchmark, external evidence that memory/tool design measurably affects context economy.

decision observability attaches a self-declared, falsifiable prediction to every edit that the next round's task-level outcomes must confirm or the edit is reverted at file granularity (§3.3), a concrete provenance/verification mechanism MF could adopt against silent drift.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (Terminal-Bench 2), Table2 (SWE-bench-verified transfer), Fig.3 (cross-model transfer), Table3 (component ablation, §4.4.1).

cita: Song et al. (2026). SkillOps: Managing LLM Agent Skill Libraries as Self-Maintaining Software Ecosystems.
problema: LLM agent skill libraries accumulate 'skill technical debt' over time — redundant, stale, interface-mismatched, or unvalidated skills that don't break any single task locally but degrade future retrieval, composition and execution reliability; existing skill-based agents only handle task-time retrieval/repair and ignore library-time maintenance.
mecanismo: Each skill is represented as a typed Skill Contract (precondition/operation/artifact/validator/failure-modes) linked into a Hierarchical Skill Ecosystem Graph via typed dependency/compatibility/redundancy/alternative edges (WRITE); a Task-Time loop retrieves and stitches skills through dependency/compatibility constraints with local repair (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); a Library-Time loop scores five health dimensions per skill (utility, redundancy, compatibility, failure-risk, validation-gap), propagates risk along dependency edges, then applies typed maintenance actions merge (CONSOLIDACION), retire (OLVIDO) and repair/add-validator (ACTUALIZACION) — nearly rule-based, near-zero LLM cost at library time.
evaluacion: Evaluated on ALFWorld with a 200-2000 skill library built from 229 curated SkillsBench skills plus synthetically degraded variants (six technical-debt patterns), against ReAct, LLM_Skill_Planner, Hybrid_Retrieval, GoS_Style and SkillWeaver baselines on GPT-4o-mini; measures standalone task success, plug-in lift over each baseline, task-time token-cost delta, and library-scale/ablation studies.
numeros_clave: SkillOps_Full reaches 79.5% success on ALFWorld (200-skill library), +8.9pp over the strongest baseline (LLM_Skill_Planner 70.6%); as a plug-in it lifts Hybrid Retrieval by +2.90pp, BM25 by +1.00pp, Dense by +1.12pp; at 2000 skills SkillOps leads the next-best baseline by >31pp; maintenance is token-neutral-to-beneficial (24/35 cells decrease, largest -3.95%) with nearly zero library-time LLM calls.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the Library-Time Loop explicitly scores utility/redundancy/failure-risk/validation-gap per skill and applies merge/retire/repair actions between tasks (Algorithm2), directly measuring the value of promoting/demoting entries rather than passively accumulating them.

typed Skill Contracts require an explicit Validator field and flag a 'validation gap' when missing (§2), and CGPD propagates upstream risk to catch structurally-sound-looking skills that inherit failure risk — direct evidence for provenance/staleness guarding as a first-class memory dimension.

Table3 explicitly measures task-time token deltas after maintenance (mostly neutral-to-negative) and states the rule-based maintenance pass uses near-zero library-time LLM calls, external evidence that memory-management overhead can be kept near-zero.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (standalone), Table2 (plug-in delta), Table3 (token cost), §5.2 (library-scale stress test).

cita: Fan et al. (2026). Resource2Skills: Distilling Executable Skills from Human-Created Resources for Software Agents.
problema: Existing skill libraries for software agents are hand-written, text-centric, or derived only from an agent's own traces, leaving rich human-created multimodal resources (tutorial videos, repos, articles) largely untapped, even though procedural know-how for creative/commercial software is often best conveyed through demonstration rather than static text.
mecanismo: An offline construction operator distills multimodal resources into typed multimodal skill-wiki entries (structured text, code, visual examples, metadata, provenance — HIBRIDA) organized in a domain-specific hierarchical taxonomy, passing quality gates for dedup/completeness/executability/safety (WRITE/ADMISION); at inference a two-stage MetaBrowse retrieves candidates via BM25 over name/tags/applicability/taxonomy-path then an LLM selects a subset to compose (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); when the offline pool lacks coverage, the same construction operator is invoked online as a controlled gap-filler.
evaluacion: Evaluated across 7 authoring domains (Web/Excel/Reaper/PPT/Blender/CAD/UE5) and 4 model backbones (GPT-5.5/5.4/5.4-mini/5.4-nano) against no-skill agents and two off-the-shelf harnesses (ClaudeCode-H, Codex-H), plus ablations on skill-pool scale, wiki organization vs flat text, source mix, and offline-vs-online acquisition, and a blinded human A/B study.
numeros_clave: w/ Skills beats w/o Skills in all 28 main-aggregate model-domain cells, averaging 56.8% vs 45.0% (+11.9pp), and beats the stronger off-the-shelf harness in 26/28 cells; UE5 gains +30 to +40pp; online acquisition adds only +0.7pp on standard tasks but +21.6pp (41.2%->62.8%) on a novel-capability stress test; performance saturates near 200 skills; hierarchical wiki beats flat text by 2.5-8.2pp.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: each skill is a typed multimodal entry with structured text/code/visual fields plus explicit provenance/metadata organized in a domain taxonomy (§3.1), a pattern for combining a typed narrative record with non-text evidence that MF's Tier-1 docs-as-truth could generalize toward.

the hierarchical taxonomy path is used as a first-class retrieval signal alongside name/tags/applicability (§3.3), evidence that organizing a single source of truth by domain structure (not a flat blob) materially narrows and sharpens retrieval.

a domain-specific predicate enforces five acceptance checks (completeness, traceable provenance, deduplication, modality consistency, structural executability) before a distilled candidate enters the wiki (§3.2), guarding the memory store against low-quality or unverifiable entries.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main comparison), Table2 (offline/online acquisition), Table3 (source-mix ablation), Fig.a (scaling).

cita: Wang et al. (2023). VOYAGER: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models.
problema: LLM-based embodied agents in open-ended environments (Minecraft) are not lifelong learners: they cannot progressively propose their own tasks, acquire and reuse skills across long horizons, or avoid re-deriving the same routines from scratch, so they plateau and cannot compound capability over time.
mecanismo: An automatic curriculum (LLM-generated, state-conditioned) proposes progressively harder tasks; an iterative prompting loop generates executable JavaScript programs, incorporating environment feedback and execution errors across rounds until an LLM self-verification module confirms task completion, at which point the verified program (WRITE/ADMISION of only successful skills) is added to an ever-growing skill library indexed by the embedding of its natural-language description (HIBRIDA: code + vector index); composable, reusable skills (CONSOLIDACION, since complex skills are built on simpler stored ones) are retrieved by similarity for future tasks.
evaluacion: Evaluated in MineDojo/Minecraft against ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT on tech-tree mastery, exploration (unique items discovered), map coverage, and zero-shot generalization to a new world with cleared inventory; ablations remove curriculum, skill library, and each feedback type.
numeros_clave: VOYAGER discovers 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer distances, unlocks tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster (wooden), 8.5x (stone), 6.4x (iron) than baselines, and is the only method to unlock the diamond tool tier (1/3 runs); removing the skill library causes a plateau in later exploration stages; removing self-verification drops discovered items by 73%; GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 for code generation yields 5.7x fewer unique items.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the automatic curriculum conditions its next proposed task on the agent's running list of completed/failed tasks and current world state (§2.1), an explicit plan/progress-state record fed back into planning, direct precedent for MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor.

only self-verified successful programs are committed to the skill library, and complex skills are explicitly built by composing simpler stored ones (§2.2), a canonical example of promoting validated experience into durable, reusable recipes.
the paper reports prompting-iteration counts as an efficiency proxy (Table1/2) rather than tokens/latency directly, relevant context for MF's cost lens but not a direct cost measurement.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (tech tree), Table2 (zero-shot generalization), Fig.9 (ablation studies).

cita: Wang et al. (2023). LDM2: A Large Decision Model Imitating Human Cognition with Dynamic Memory Enhancement.
problema: Standard few-shot prompting for LLM decision-making agents relies on fixed, manually crafted example prompts that cannot generalize to complex or unseen situations and cannot be updated with environment feedback once fixed, so the agent's decision quality is capped by whatever examples were chosen upfront.
mecanismo: A memory-formation stage (WRITE) decomposes human demonstration trajectories into standard state-action tuples (goal, LLM-summarized history, observation, action) clustered by LLM-generated goal/observation indices and stored as batch memories (DOCS-ARCHIVOS); at inference the most relevant tuples are retrieved (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) via the goal/observation index to build a dynamic prompt; a memory-refinement stage runs LLM-guided tree exploration to generate multiple candidate decision processes, compares the best-reward path against a memory-only 'ground' path, and adds (ADMISION) the valuable sub-trajectory after the key divergence point back into memory.
evaluacion: Evaluated on WebShop (500 test instructions, score + success rate) and ALFWorld (134 test games, success rate) with GPT-3.5-turbo, against Standard few-shot, ReAct and Reflexion baselines, comparing initial memory (LDM2-In) vs refined memory (LDM2-In+Re) against a human-expert upper bound.
numeros_clave: On WebShop, LDM2 reaches score 71.8 / success-rate 40.8% with initial memory and 72.4 / 41.6% after refinement, versus Standard 62.7/29.6%, ReAct 67.1/39.6%, Reflexion 68.4/40.2% (human expert 82.1/59.6%).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the LLM-summarized historical information hτ explicitly tracks 'the decision stage it has reached' to guide future actions (§3.2), a lightweight plan-state summary distinct from raw history that MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor could reuse.

memory refinement compares an explored best-reward decision path against the memory-only ground path and back-fills only the valuable divergent sub-trajectory into memory (§3.3), a targeted consolidation pattern (add only the delta that beat the baseline) rather than bulk logging.

batching trajectories (batch size 50-100) to keep each memory shard within context length is a pragmatic context-budget workaround (§3.2) relevant to MF's economy lens though not measured as a cost metric.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (WebShop score/SR); ALFWorld results follow in §5 (not fully captured at read cutoff, but WebShop numbers ground evidencia_tipo).

cita: Roth et al. (2024). Pairing Analogy-Augmented Generation with Procedural Memory for Procedural Q&A.
problema: LLMs struggle to synthesize disparate pieces of information into a coherent multi-step plan for procedural tasks in specialized or unfamiliar domains (e.g. a library newer than the model's training cutoff), and standard few-shot/RAG retrieval surfaces noisy or insufficiently related examples when the query wording doesn't match stored procedures.
mecanismo: A procedural-memory store embeds whole linear procedures (input/output/ordered-steps, WRITE) built from a formal chain-graph representation and retrieved via K-nearest cosine similarity (VECTOR); a query generator decomposes the goal into a high-level outline and rewrites it into up to N=4 sub-questions (HyDE-style), each retrieving and being answered against K analogical procedures by an answer-generator LLM (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); an iterative LLM self-critic then revises the composed answer for up to T=3 cycles before returning the final procedure.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LCStep (a new LangChain-tutorial dataset chosen because it postdates the test LLM's training cutoff), RecipeNLG, and CHAMP, via LLM-based pairwise comparison against Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, RAG and ReAct baselines (plus a blind human study on RecipeNLG), with a full ablation removing the query generator, answer generator, and critic refinement in all combinations.
numeros_clave: AAG wins over RAG in 69.64% of LCStep pairwise comparisons (loss 12.50%, ties 17.86%) and 85.70% of RecipeNLG comparisons (loss 7.60%); a blind human study on RecipeNLG found 56% preferred AAG recipes vs 16% RAG (28% tie); removing the query generator (NO QG) drops the AAG-win rate to 71.43%/80.05% (still positive but reduced).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the ablation study (Table1, NO QG/NO AG/NO CR rows) measures exactly how much each retrieval/analogy component contributes to output quality via pairwise LLM and human evaluation, direct external evidence for treating retrieval design as a measured layer rather than an assumed one.

query rewriting into sub-questions before searching the vector memory (§4.2, HyDE-style) is a derived/cached intermediate representation built purely to sharpen retrieval, a pattern relevant to MF's TIER-INDICE derived-index-as-cache anchor.

inference-time cost of the multi-query, multi-cycle refinement pipeline is only briefly addressed (appendix reference) rather than being a first-class measured axis in the main body read, relevant context but not a strong signal either way.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (LLM pairwise evaluation) and §5.5 (human study, RecipeNLG).

cita: Wang et al. (2024). Agent Workflow Memory.
problema: LM-based web-navigation agents integrate only a fixed set of examples via training or in-context learning, so they lack robustness to changes in task context or environment and cannot learn from their own past successes and failures across a session to disentangle reusable task routines from increasingly complex tasks.
mecanismo: An LM-based induction module abstracts reusable 'workflows' (an NL description plus a step trajectory) from one or more agent experiences (WRITE), deliberately generalizing example-specific values into placeholders so routines transfer across instances; workflows are added to the agent's text memory (ADMISION) either offline (induced once from all training examples before test time) or online (streamed per test task, keeping only workflows from LM-judged successful trajectories, CONSOLIDACION), and complex workflows are built by composing/extending previously induced simpler ones.
evaluacion: Evaluated on WebArena (812 tasks, 5 websites, execution-based evaluation, online AWM) and Mind2Web (1000+ tasks, 200+ domains; offline + online AWM), against BrowserGym, SteP (human-written workflows), AutoEval, MindAct and Synapse baselines with GPT-4/GPT-3.5, plus cross-template/cross-website/cross-domain generalization splits.
numeros_clave: AWM improves WebArena overall success rate to 35.5% (+12.0 absolute / 51.1% relative over BrowserGym, and 7.6% relative over SteP's human-written-workflow baseline) while using ~2.0 fewer steps per task than BrowserGym and 40.8 fewer than AutoEval; on Mind2Web offline AWM reaches 4.0-8.9% relative and 0.4-2.8 absolute step/task success rate gains over Synapse/MindAct, driven mainly by +5.0-9.0 element-accuracy gains; cross-website/domain margins widen to 8.9-14.0 absolute points as the train-test gap grows.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the online setting only turns a completed trajectory into a workflow when an LM-judged evaluator marks it successful (§2.3), and later workflows explicitly reuse/extend earlier simpler ones (Fig.6), a direct example of promoting validated experience into durable, composable recipes.

AWM is measured head-to-head against retrieval of raw concrete examples (Synapse) and shows abstracted workflows beat concrete-example retrieval by +5.0 element accuracy (§3.2.1), external evidence that WHAT gets retrieved (abstracted vs raw) is a measurable design axis, not an assumed one.

reports steps-to-solve as an efficiency metric alongside success rate, showing AWM needs ~2.0 fewer steps than BrowserGym and 40.8 fewer than an evaluation-heavy baseline (§3.1.1), external evidence that memory-guided planning reduces interaction/token cost.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (WebArena), Table2 (cross-template), Table3 (Mind2Web offline), §3.1.1/§3.2.1.

cita: Jiang et al. (2024). Long Term Memory: The Foundation of AI Self-Evolution.
problema: Current LLMs are static, 'average' foundation models trained once and frozen at inference, so they cannot progressively personalize to an individual's or organization's long-tail data or continually improve from accumulated interactions without full retraining, which the authors argue requires a first-class Long-Term Memory (LTM) layer to enable inference-time 'self-evolution.'
mecanismo: LTM is proposed as a repository of refined, retained interaction data (WRITE) built and updated per specialized agent in a multi-agent architecture (MULTIAGENTE, the OMNE/AutoGen-based framework), where individual agents distill and store personalized knowledge that is periodically consolidated (CONSOLIDACION) into a shared collective memory model and updated in real time (ACTUALIZACION) as new interactions accumulate; retrieval combines RAG-style in-context retrieval with LoRA fine-tuning to locally update the model with LTM data (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) instead of always retraining all parameters.
evaluacion: Primarily a position/technical report; empirically grounds the LTM framework with an OMNE multi-agent system evaluated on the GAIA benchmark (400+ QA tasks) using GPT-4o + o1-preview with a scene-router deciding local-vs-web-tool solving, plus a cited Synthesis-Step-by-Step (S3) ablation on NLP task performance.
numeros_clave: Omne (the LTM-based multi-agent framework) achieved 1st place on the GAIA test set (40.53%) and 2nd place on the validation set (46.06%); a cited Synthesis-Step-by-Step (S3) ablation on smaller models' errors reports NLP task gains of up to 15.17%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: describes per-agent, cortical-column-like memories that are periodically merged into a shared LTM collective (§3.1, §6.3), external evidence for consolidating distributed transient experience into a durable shared store.

the OMNE architecture assigns each specialized agent its own memory slice, later integrated into a unified memory model (§6.3.1), a concrete multi-agent multi-store seam design relevant to MF's COSTURAS anchor.

the GAIA result (1st place, 40.53% test) is a genuine measured retrieval/tool-use benchmark, but the surrounding LTM framework (Sections 1-5) is argued conceptually rather than ablated against a no-LTM baseline, offering only partial support for MF's insistence on a measured retrieval layer.

notes: Numbers from §6.3.4 GAIA benchmark (Omne, 40.53%/46.06%) and the cited S3 ablation (up to 15.17% NLP gains).

cita: Liao et al. (2025). ReflecTool: Towards Reflection-Aware Tool-Augmented Clinical Agents.
problema: Clinical LLM agents are typically restricted to one narrow clinical scenario with a small fixed toolset, so they cannot generalize to a realistic, holistic evaluation across the diverse types of clinical data (images, EHRs, text, multi-document) and lack a mechanism to learn how to select and use domain-specific tools well from limited demonstrations.
mecanismo: An optimization stage lets the agent solve a small training subset with a clinical toolbox, self-reflects on each first attempt against the ground truth to produce a suggestion and a refined second trajectory, and only stores the refined trajectory in long-term memory when it succeeds (WRITE/ADMISION); successful vs. failed action usages are additionally compared to distill tool-wise experience per tool/action type (CONSOLIDACION); at inference the agent retrieves BM25-similar successful cases from memory (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) and applies the accumulated tool-wise experience via one of two verification methods -- iterative refinement or candidate selection -- to improve each tool call.
evaluacion: Evaluated on the newly introduced ClinicalAgent Bench (CAB, 18 tasks across 5 clinical dimensions) with Qwen2-7B/72B backbones against LLM/MLLM baselines and agent baselines (COT, ReAct, CRITIC, Reflexion), plus ablations removing long-term memory and tool-wise reflection, and a study of optimization-step count and verification size.
numeros_clave: ReflecTool surpasses the strongest agent baseline (Reflexion) by at least 3 points on CAB with both Qwen2-7B/72B, and surpasses the base LLMs by more than 10 points; ablation shows removing reflective long-term memory costs ~4 points (refinement) / ~7 points (selection) of average CAB performance (Table3); Candidate Selection already beats Iterative Refinement by ~4.5 points (62.5 vs 58) even before any optimization steps.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the ablation in Table3 isolates long-term memory and tool-wise action-level experience as separate levers and measures their individual contribution (removing memory alone costs ~4-7 points), direct evidence that consolidating validated trajectories into durable per-tool experience pays off measurably.

BM25-based case retrieval from long-term memory (Eq.5) is directly compared against no-memory ablations and against Reflexion's non-memory self-reflection, isolating retrieval's specific contribution to task success on a real benchmark.

the study of optimization-step count and verification size (Figs.3-4) trades more memory/compute for accuracy but is framed as a quality lever rather than a first-class token/latency cost measurement, relevant context but not a strong signal for MF's cost anchor.

notes: Numbers from Table2 (main CAB results), Table3 (ablation), Fig.3/4 (optimization-step and verification-size studies).

cita: Raman et al. (2025). REMI: A Novel Causal Schema Memory Architecture for Personalized Lifestyle Recommendation Agents.
problema: Personalized LLM lifestyle-assistant agents give generic, population-level advice because they cannot integrate a user's own multimodal life-event data into their reasoning, and even when they retrieve personal facts they surface correlations without an explainable causal chain linking a recommendation back to the user's own history.
mecanismo: A personal causal knowledge graph (nodes = life events/habits, weighted causal edges) serves as persistent long-term memory that is incrementally updated with new events (ACTUALIZACION, WRITE); a causal-reasoner module maps the query onto graph nodes via dual-encoder embedding similarity (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO), performs n-hop Graph-of-Thought/Tree-of-Thought causal traversal with LLM-based path scoring and counterfactual node-removal checks, followed by an LLM self-reflection validation pass (FIDELIDAD guard) before handing the validated causal factors to a schema-based planner that instantiates a matching plan template with the user's specifics, all glued together by an LLM orchestrator required to cite the causal trace and retrieved memory in its final explanation.
evaluacion: Evaluated qualitatively/quantitatively on 28 personal lifestyle scenarios (Gemini-2.0-Flash as orchestrator LLM) against a Memory-Only-LLM baseline (RAG-style, no causal reasoning) and an Ablated-CSM baseline (causal graph traversal but no schema planner), using two new embedding-similarity-based metrics: Personalization Salience Score (PSS) and Causal Reasoning Accuracy (CRA).
numeros_clave: On the afternoon-fatigue scenario REMI scores PSS 0.92/1.0 and CRA 0.60/1.0; across the 28 scenarios both baselines reach PSS 0.68-0.82 (comparable to REMI) but the memory-only baseline scores 0.0 CRA on every prompt while Ablated-CSM scores 0.2-0.6 CRA inconsistently, versus REMI's 0.4-0.8 CRA in every case.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: an LLM self-reflection loop revalidates each candidate causal factor before it informs planning, and a counterfactual verification step checks that a plan step actually severs the causal link it targets (§4.2.5, §4.3.3), a concrete grounding/staleness check on inferred memory before it is acted upon.

the system pairs a structured causal graph (in-memory networkx) with a separate FAISS vector store over unstructured logs (§4.4.1), a two-store seam design (structured causal facts vs semantic recall) relevant to MF's COSTURAS anchor.

Causal Reasoning Accuracy is measured against a Memory-Only (retrieval-only) baseline that scores 0.0 CRA on every prompt (§6), directly isolating what plain retrieval misses versus a measured causal-reasoning layer.

notes: Numbers from §6.1 (scenario walkthrough, PSS/CRA) and §6.3-7 (aggregate 28-scenario comparison).

cita: Wang and Chen (2025). MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents.
problema: Existing LLM agent memory systems store all history in a single flat, text-centric store (or a pure knowledge graph) with no routing into specialized memory types, so they retrieve inefficiently, fail on multimodal (image-heavy) input, and have no abstraction layer to keep storage bounded as raw screenshots or documents accumulate.
mecanismo: MIRIX routes incoming multimodal input into six typed memory components (Core, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural, Resource, Knowledge Vault) via a Meta Memory Manager that dispatches to six specialized Memory-Manager agents (MULTIAGENTE) which write and update (WRITE/ACTUALIZACION) their own memory type in parallel while deduplicating; Core Memory triggers a controlled rewrite when over 90% full (CONSOLIDACION-by-compaction); at query time an Active Retrieval mechanism first infers a topic from the query, then pulls top-K entries per memory type via embedding/BM25/string match (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO), tagging results by memory-type source for grounding (FIDELIDAD).
evaluacion: Evaluated on a new ScreenshotVQA benchmark (5,000-20,000 high-resolution screenshots per user, 3 users) against RAG and long-context baselines, and on the LOCOMO long-conversation benchmark (Chat Agent restricted to retrieved memory only, no raw transcript) against existing memory-system baselines.
numeros_clave: MIRIX achieves 35% higher accuracy than the RAG baseline on ScreenshotVQA while cutting storage by 99.9%, and a 410% improvement over long-context baselines with 93.3% less storage; on LOCOMO it reaches 85.38% overall accuracy, 8.0 points above the best existing method.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the six typed memory schemas (Core/Episodic/Semantic/Procedural/Resource/Knowledge-Vault, §3.1) each define explicit typed fields (e.g. event_type/summary/details/actor/timestamp for Episodic) rather than a flat text blob, a concrete instance of typed narrative memory MF's Tier-1 anchor could model closer to.

routing input to one of six specialized memory managers rather than one shared store (§3.3) is the paper's central design bet, and it is what drives both the accuracy gains and the 99.9% storage reduction, direct evidence for single-source-per-fact-type multi-store routing over a monolithic memory.

the headline ScreenshotVQA result explicitly pairs an accuracy delta with a storage-reduction delta (35% accuracy up, 99.9% storage down) rather than reporting accuracy alone, external evidence that a well-typed memory layer can jointly improve quality and cost.

notes: Numbers from §1 (main results, ScreenshotVQA and LOCOMO); memory schemas detailed in §3.1.

cita: Wong et al. (2026). Confucius Code Agent: Scalable Agent Scaffolding for Real-World Codebases.
problema: Production-scale coding agents on massive repositories need both long-context reasoning (localizing and reasoning across dispersed modules without exceeding context limits) and long-term memory (accumulating reusable patterns and failure modes across sessions), but existing research-grade scaffolds use flat interaction histories or ad-hoc truncation/retrieval that silently drop important state, while production-grade systems trade away extensibility and interpretability.
mecanismo: A hierarchical, file-system-based working memory (a tree of Markdown documents with metadata tags) lets the orchestrator write/read/edit/delete state during a session (WRITE); an Architect Agent triggers adaptive context compression when the context nears a threshold, summarizing older turns into a structured plan (goals/decisions/errors/open TODOs) that replaces the raw history while keeping a rolling recent window (CONSOLIDACION+OLVIDO of raw turns, ACTUALIZACION of the compressed plan); separately, a note-taking agent distills each session's trajectory into persistent cross-session Markdown notes, explicitly including 'hindsight notes' for failures (errors, stack traces, abandoned strategies) that a later session retrieves (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) to avoid repeating the same mistake; a meta-agent automates a build-test-improve loop (MULTIAGENTE) that synthesizes and refines the orchestrator/tool configuration itself against a test set.
evaluacion: Evaluated on SWE-Bench-Pro (731 tasks) and SWE-Bench-Verified (500 tasks) across Claude 4/4.5 Sonnet, Claude 4.5 Opus and GPT-5.2 backbones against SWE-Agent, Live-SWE-Agent, and Anthropic/OpenAI's own proprietary scaffolds under identical repositories and tools; ablations isolate context management (hierarchical memory + compression) and meta-agent-learned tool-use versus a naive tool-use baseline.
numeros_clave: CCA reaches Resolve@1 59.0% on SWE-Bench-Pro with GPT-5.2 (vs OpenAI's own 56.0%) and 54.3% with Claude 4.5 Opus (vs Anthropic's own 52.0%); a weaker Claude 4.5 Sonnet + CCA (52.7%) beats a stronger Claude 4.5 Opus + Anthropic's proprietary scaffold (52.0%); ablation on a 100-example subset shows disabling context management drops Resolve@1 from 48.6% to 42.0% (Claude 4 Sonnet) and disabling advanced tool-use drops it from 51.6% to 44.0% (Claude 4.5 Sonnet).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: context compression explicitly replaces older raw turns with a structured plan (goals, decisions made, open TODOs, critical error traces, §2.2.1/Fig.3) that persists across turns as the agent's working state, a direct, measured instance of MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor (ablation shows disabling it costs ~6.6pp Resolve@1).

the note-taking system explicitly records 'hindsight notes' for compilation errors, exceptions, and abandoned strategies indexed by error signature so a later session retrieves the known fix instead of rediscovering it (§2.2.2), a direct implementation of negative-knowledge/re-derivation-avoidance memory.

the ablation table (Table2) isolates context-management and tool-use contributions to Resolve@1 on a matched subset, quantifying that scaffolding (memory/orchestration), not raw model capability, is a primary, measured determinant of quality under fixed compute.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main SWE-Bench-Pro results) and Table2 (context-management/tool-use ablation, §3.2-3.3).

cita: Gaurav et al. (2025). CodeMem: Architecting Reproducible Agents via Dynamic MCP and Procedural Memory.
problema: Vanilla CodeAct agents suffer probabilistic instability, redundant re-derivation of already-solved logic, inability to retain user feedback across sessions, and context drift during long multi-step workflows, making them unreliable for repetitive real-world tasks.
mecanismo: CodeMem couples Dynamic-MCP tool discovery (search_functions/load_functions, JIT schema loading) with a Python sandbox (execute_code) and a procedural-memory bank: validated Python functions are frozen via register_skill after a trial-and-confirm phase, letting future sessions execute (Texecute) instead of re-plan/re-write/re-debug; write_todos externalizes plan state as an anchor against context truncation.
evaluacion: LLM-as-judge (Gemini 2.5 Flash) scores full agent trajectories (tool calls, sandbox code, stdout/stderr, side-effects) over a curated dataset of 25 multi-step agentic tasks (difficulty 1-5, 2-8 chained tools) across three backbone models.
numeros_clave: Table 2: Gemini 3 Full 96% min correctness / 7.00 avg calls / 100.48s P50 latency / 2.02M tokens; Claude 4.5 Sonnet 79% / 6.96 calls / 71.38s / 2.61M tokens; GPT-5 Chat 68% / 2.80 calls / 14.75s / 0.49M tokens.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: write_todos externalizes a Pending->In-Progress->Completed checklist outside the chat history so the agent recovers exact plan position after a sandbox crash or context truncation (SS5.4/SS6.5) -- a concrete pattern for MF's plan-state memory.

register_skill freezes a validated Python function into a permanent library only after an explicit trial+user-confirmation phase (SS5.2), a discretionary promotion trigger MF's CONSOLIDACION could adopt.

SS3.3 and Table 2 show standard tool-calling context grows O(N) with steps while CodeMem stays O(1) (data stays in sandbox RAM, not the LLM context), and reuse collapses Ttask to ~Texecute -- supports MF's context-economy thesis.

notes: Table 2 (SS7.3) anchors the quantitative claims; Fig.2 diagrams the architecture; case study in SS6 (Outlook-OneDrive) grounds register_skill/write_todos mechanics.

cita: Li et al. (2026). Experience-Evolving Multi-Turn Tool-Use Agent with Hybrid Episodic-Procedural Memory.
problema: Multi-turn tool-use agents face shifting decision contexts where full-trajectory reuse is too context-specific to transfer and tool-only graphs ignore dialogue/environment context, leaving experience reuse either coarse-grained or context-blind.
mecanismo: H-EPM builds a state-annotated tool-transition graph from accumulated trajectories: edges encode procedural transition weights (frequency + efficiency) and attach episodic summarized-state annotations (via an autonomous state-summarization tool) between tool nodes; at inference the agent adaptively chooses episodic recall (state-summary similarity) vs. procedural exploitation (edge weight) for next-tool selection, and the same graph biases RL rollout exploration toward historically successful tool transitions (memory-guided GRPO).
evaluacion: Inference-time evaluation on 4 multi-turn tool-use benchmarks (tau-Bench Telecom, tau2-Bench Retail, ToolSandbox, ACEBench) against retrieval, ReasoningBank, and tool-graph baselines across multiple backbones (GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4o, Qwen3); RL evaluation integrates H-EPM into GRPO rollout vs. base GRPO and AgentEvolver on tau-Bench Retail (Qwen3-4B-Instruct).
numeros_clave: Abstract: up to 50%+ inference-time gains over baselines and up to 40%+ improvement on out-of-distribution RL tasks; gains reported as more pronounced for weaker backbones (GPT-4.1-mini benefits more than GPT-4.1/GPT-4o).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The POMDP formulation tracks interaction history h_t and compact state summaries s_t across turns (SS3-4.1) as decision context, not an explicit plan/task-state artifact -- relevant context but no direct MF-style plan-state memory design.

Edge weights blend transition frequency with an efficiency term w'(tau_t,tau_t+1) (SS4.2) that continuously reweights procedural routines by successful trajectories, offering a graph-based consolidation mechanism MF could adapt for promoting recurring gotchas to durable recipes.

Efficiency-aware edge weighting (SS4.2) explicitly penalizes tool overuse by rollout-step count, aligning with MF's context-economy concern that recall must weigh cost/latency, not just semantic similarity.

notes: Table 1 reports per-benchmark/per-backbone inference gains; Table 3 reports RL gains vs GRPO/AgentEvolver; Fig.1-2 diagram graph construction and adaptive retrieval (SS4.2-4.3).

cita: Liu et al. (2025). Unifying Dynamic Tool Creation and Cross-Task Experience Sharing through Cognitive Memory Architecture.
problema: LLM agents struggle to adapt to novel tasks because tool-creation approaches build tools from scratch without reusing past experience, while experience-sharing approaches transfer trajectories but lack integrated tool creation -- fragmenting adaptive, cumulative learning.
mecanismo: SMITH organizes memory into procedural (Mproc, static system prompts/behavior), semantic (Msem, human-crafted tool examples/demonstrations) and episodic (Mep, embedded successful trajectories) components; tool creation is an iterative sandboxed code-generation loop until success feedback, and cross-task reuse retrieves top-k semantically-similar episodic/semantic experiences via dense-sparse hybrid retrieval (text-embedding-3-large + Splade, RRF fusion) to condition the next action; a curriculum-learning module reranks tasks via an ensemble of proxy agents' difficulty re-estimation.
evaluacion: GAIA benchmark (165 validation tasks, levels 1-3) with a multi-agent planner/developer-tester workflow, 3-path sampling with LLM-as-a-judge (o4-mini) consensus voting, compared against tool-creation (Alita) and experience-sharing (Memento) SOTA baselines, plus ablations removing curriculum learning, episodic memory sharing, and cold-start demonstrations.
numeros_clave: 81.8% Pass@1 on GAIA (vs Alita 75.2%, Memento 70.9%); ablation Table 3: -10.3% w/o curriculum learning, -13.9% w/o episodic memory sharing, -21.8% w/o cold-start demonstrations.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: plan_estado=SI per extraction, but SMITH's planner/developer-tester loop (SS4, Fig.1) tracks sub-plan execution implicitly through the outer loop rather than an explicit persisted plan-state object -- adjacent but not a direct plan-state memory design.

Ablation Table 3 measures episodic memory sharing contributing +13.9% and cold-start demonstrations +21.8%, empirically confirming that consolidating and reusing prior successful trajectories/tools materially improves task success -- supports MF's consolidation thesis.

SMITH's tri-partite Mproc/Msem/Mep hierarchy (SS3.3, Eq.7-8) keeps each memory type in a distinct store retrieved through one consistent interface, illustrating a multi-store-with-single-retrieval-seam design relevant to MF's COSTURAS question.

notes: Table 1 (GAIA main results) and Table 3 (ablation) anchor the numbers; Fig.4 shows the temporal shift from semantic to episodic memory reliance across curriculum progression.

cita: OPPO AI Agent Team, LV-NUS lab (2025). MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems.
problema: Self-evolving agent memory systems rely on manually engineered, static architectures: while agents can accumulate experience within a fixed memory pipeline, the memory architecture itself cannot meta-adapt to diverse task domains, leaving performance misaligned whenever a task's memory affordances differ.
mecanismo: MemEvolve runs a bilevel (dual) evolution: an inner loop lets the agent populate an empty memory under a fixed candidate architecture Omega=(Encode,Store,Retrieve,Manage) across a batch of trajectories; an outer loop's diagnose-and-design meta-evolution operator F Pareto-ranks candidates on (performance,-cost,-delay), selects top-K parents, diagnoses architectural bottlenecks per component from trajectory replay, and generates new (E,U,R,G) variants -- grounded on EvolveLab, a modular codebase re-implementing 12 prior memory systems (Voyager, ExpeL, AWM, G-Memory, Memp, etc.) under one interface.
evaluacion: Evaluated on four agentic benchmarks (GAIA, WebWalkerQA, xBench-DeepSearch, TaskCraft) atop frameworks SmolAgent and Flash-Searcher, comparing MemEvolve-evolved architectures against the 12 EvolveLab baselines and testing cross-benchmark/cross-LLM transfer of memory architectures evolved on TaskCraft.
numeros_clave: Improves frameworks such as SmolAgent and Flash-Searcher by up to 17.06%; memory architectures evolved on TaskCraft show 2.0-9.09% gains when transferred to unseen benchmarks/backbones (abstract); Table 2 lists per-benchmark Pass@1 across 20+ agent frameworks (e.g., Flash-Searcher GPT-5-mini 81.18% GAIA avg.).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Manage(G) component explicitly performs consolidation/abstraction/forgetting (SS3.2) and is itself meta-evolved by diagnose-and-design (SS4.2) -- a self-improving consolidation policy MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could draw from.

The outer-loop fitness vector explicitly includes token cost and latency alongside task performance (Fj=(Perf,-Cost,-Delay), SS4.1) and Pareto-ranks candidates on this tradeoff, directly confirming MF's context-economy framing of memory design.

EvolveLab's modular (Encode,Store,Retrieve,Manage) decomposition (Table1, SS3.2) treats the retrieval index/store as a swappable, evolvable derived layer rather than fixed ground truth, echoing MF's Tier-3 derived-index-as-cache framing.

notes: Table 2 (main cross-framework/cross-benchmark results) and Table 1 (12 EvolveLab baselines taxonomy) anchor the numbers; Fig.3 diagrams the dual inner/outer evolutionary loop (SS4.1-4.2).

cita: Gaurav et al. (2025). Synthesizing Procedural Memory: Challenges and Architectures in Automated Workflow Generation.
problema: The mechanism for autonomously synthesizing procedural memory 'from a blank slate' is underexplored: agents must transition from passive tool-users to active workflow architects, but four structural bottlenecks -- Discovery, Verification, Decomposition, Scaling -- block reliable automated skill generation.
mecanismo: The paper proposes: (1) Dynamic MCP search/load_functions for O(1) tool discovery instead of O(N) prompt injection; (2) a 'Probe' methodology -- sample with strict pagination, print raw structure to stdout, then lock the schema -- to avoid hallucinated data shapes before writing final code; (3) Linear State Anchoring via write_todos as an external program-counter, replacing search-tree decomposition (LATS) for linear workflows with intrinsic LLM reasoning; (4) production-hardening via asyncio concurrency and external persistence (SQLite/Sheets checkpoints) plus idempotent operations for scaling.
evaluacion: Single high-fidelity qualitative case study (Outlook-to-OneDrive cross-service orchestration workflow) with an illustrative HumanEval/83 comparison contrasting a LATS/GPT-4 'reflection trap' against modern intrinsic-reasoning (GPT-5) derivation; no formal quantitative benchmark table.
numeros_clave: Illustrative, not benchmarked: naive sequential processing of 1000 emails ~33 minutes vs. concurrent asyncio.gather ~2 minutes (SS5.1); case study probe reports 'Fetched 7 emails with attachments' as schema-locking evidence (SS3.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: write_todos as 'Linear State Anchoring' (SS4.3) is explicitly proposed as an external Program Counter surviving context flush/truncation, directly extending MF's plan-state-as-memory need (P13) with a concrete decouple-plan-from-context pattern.

The 'Probe' methodology (SS3, sample->inspect stdout->codify) is a structural anti-hallucination discipline that grounds tool-response schemas in observed reality before code generation, a concrete pattern for MF's FIDELIDAD anchor (grounding/provenance against poisoning by invented structure).

SS2.1/2.4 quantify tool-schema injection as O(N) context cost vs. O(1) retrieval-based discovery, and SS5.1 shows async concurrency dropping a 1000-email workflow from ~33min to ~2min -- both confirm MF's context/latency economy framing.

notes: Case study spans SS2-5 (Outlook/OneDrive running example, companion to CodeMem W4417531516); Fig.1 (HumanEval/83 comparison) is the only figure with concrete numbers; evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA confirmed -- no formal benchmark table found in the PDF.

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory.
problema: Current memory-based agents rely on passive semantic-similarity retrieval that cannot distinguish high-utility experiences from noisy-but-similar ones, while fine-tuning the backbone to internalize experience is costly and prone to catastrophic forgetting -- leaving no tuning-free way to exploit runtime feedback for retrieval quality.
mecanismo: MemRL structures episodic memory as Intent-Experience-Utility triplets and formalizes retrieval as a value-based decision process (Memory-MDP): a Two-Phase Retrieval first recalls a semantically-similar candidate pool via cosine similarity/threshold, then re-ranks by a composite score blending normalized similarity and a learned Q-value; Q-values are updated online via a Monte-Carlo/TD rule from environmental reward (success/failure), while the backbone LLM stays frozen -- learning happens entirely in the retrieval policy over memory, not in model weights.
evaluacion: Runtime-learning and transfer evaluations on four benchmarks (HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, LifelongAgentBench OS/DB) against RAG, Self-RAG, Mem0 and MemP baselines under a frozen-backbone setting, reporting Success Rate and Cumulative Success Rate over 10 epochs, plus ablations on the Q-weighting factor lambda and cross-task vs single-task retrieval scope.
numeros_clave: Runtime learning: MemRL beats strongest baseline MemP by +3.8% avg CSR (up to +6.2% on ALFWorld/OS); Transfer: +2.8% avg SR (+5.8% ALFWorld); ablation shows lambda=0.5 is optimal Q-weighting (Fig.5); cross-task retrieval beats single-task Reflexion-style baseline on OS (+9.0%) and ALFWorld (+5.1%), Table 3.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: MemRL empirically shows pure cosine-similarity retrieval (lambda=0) plateaus and retrieves 'functional distractors' (SS5.3.2 ablation), while augmenting with a learned utility (Q-value) signal from environmental feedback yields robust gains -- confirms MF's G-M2 stance that retrieval must be MEASURED (grounded in outcome-based signal), not semantic similarity alone.

MemRL optimizes retrieval policy without weight updates to avoid fine-tuning compute cost (SS1), but reports no explicit token/latency accounting for the memory itself -- relevant context for MF's context-economy thesis without direct confirmation/refutation.

Utility (Q-value) updates via Monte-Carlo/TD rules (Eq.3-4, SS4.3) continuously reweight which stored experiences are worth reusing based on environmental feedback, offering a quantitative consolidation mechanism (vs. MF's qualitative gotcha-to-recipe promotion) worth considering for CONSOLIDACION.

notes: Table 1 (runtime) and Table 2 (transfer) anchor the CSR/SR numbers; Fig.5 shows the lambda ablation; Table 3 isolates cross-task vs single-task retrieval scope (SS5.3.3).

cita: Guo et al. (2026). EET: Experience-Driven Early Termination for Cost-Efficient Software Engineering Agents.
problema: SE agents resolve GitHub issues via multi-round LLM iterations whose conversation-history context grows super-linearly ('token snowball'), and agents often keep iterating on hopeless or already-solved issues, wasting substantial monetary/API cost without improving resolution rate.
mecanismo: EET distills each historical issue-resolution trajectory into a structured experience object (concise issue abstraction, compressed execution_summary, pass-only evaluation, plus a confidence/confidence_reason retrospective) retrieved via TF-IDF similarity above a threshold; at inference it augments patch generation with dual-milestone (code-modification, test-execution) confidence checks that trigger early termination, and independently scores each generated patch (confidence vs. two thresholds) to stop redundant patch-selection iterations early.
evaluacion: SWE-bench Verified (500 real GitHub issue tasks) across three SE agents (Agentless, Mini-SWE-Agent, Trae Agent) x two backbones (GPT-5-mini, DeepSeek-V3.2), compared against Turn-control and a Naive-EET (raw-trajectory RAG) baseline; experience mined from a deduplicated 207-task subset of SWE-bench Lite; RQ1-3 ablations isolate experience injection vs. early termination.
numeros_clave: Table 1/3: EET cuts total cost 19.3%-55.1% (avg 31.8%) with <=0.2% resolution-rate loss (even +2.7% avg gain), vs. -10.7% resolution rate for Turn-control at -41.4% cost; reduces API calls/input/output tokens by avg 20.8%/29.9%/25.1%; early-termination fires on avg 11.3% of issues (Table 2); confidence>90 patches show 63.6-92.6% pass rate vs 8.7-13.8% for confidence<40.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table 1/3 directly measures per-issue cost/token/API-call reduction from experience-guided early termination (avg -31.8% total cost, negligible performance loss), a strong quantitative confirmation of MF's context/cost-economy thesis.
Experience objects are written only from successfully validated trajectories (evaluation_result=pass, SS3.1), an outcome-gated write trigger MF's G-M1 (discretionary write) could adopt directly.

EET stores one experience-object-per-issue in a single TF-IDF-indexed base retrieved by the issue description (SS3.1) -- a single-source-per-fact design relevant to MF's COSTURAS question, though not explicitly framed as a multi-store seam problem.

notes: Table 1 (RQ1 main cost/performance results), Table 2 (early-termination rate), Table 3 (RQ2 baseline comparison) anchor the numbers; confidence-calibration analysis in Appendix M grounds the reliability claim (SS5.1).

cita: Biswal et al. (2026). AgentSM: Semantic Memory for Agentic Text-to-SQL.
problema: Agentic Text-to-SQL systems on realistic enterprise schemas (Spider 2.0) repeat identical exploration steps across queries on the same database, rigidly apply one-size-fits-all strategies regardless of task, and exhibit high run-to-run variance -- inflating cost/latency and destabilizing accuracy at scale.
mecanismo: AgentSM builds a structured trajectory store: synthetic exploration questions are generated offline per schema and executed to produce dense exploration traces; trajectories are step-classified (exploration/execution/validation) and re-formatted as LLM-annotated Markdown with semantic headers; at inference the planner retrieves the single most-similar prior trajectory segment (same database, top-1 by question similarity) to skip redundant schema exploration, while frequently co-occurring tool pairs are fused into composite tools (e.g., get_ext+get_ddl -> local_exploration) to shorten trajectories.
evaluacion: Spider 2.0 / Spider 2.0 Lite benchmark (547 enterprise-scale multi-dialect Text-to-SQL tasks); ablation on a 20-question sample compares no-trajectory vs. naive raw-trajectory vs. structured Markdown/JSON trajectory formats, measuring average steps and execution accuracy.
numeros_clave: State-of-the-art 44.8% execution accuracy on Spider 2.0 Lite; reduces average token usage by 25% and trajectory length by 35% vs. SOTA; Table 1 ablation: raw/naive trajectories give NO improvement (22.62 steps/25% acc, same as no-trajectory) while structured Markdown trajectories cut steps to 16.50 and raise accuracy to 50% (JSON: 15.12 steps/50%).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table 1 is a direct, measured demonstration that raw/unstructured trajectory dumps give ZERO benefit while typed, structured (Markdown/JSON) trajectory representations cut steps ~33% and lift accuracy 2x -- confirms MF's TIER-DOCS thesis that typed narrative beats raw log dumping as ground-truth memory.
Reported 25% token reduction and 35% trajectory-length reduction (abstract) via trajectory reuse and composite-tool fusion directly supports MF's context-economy framing.

Composite tools (SS3.3) mine consistently co-occurring tool pairs across historical trajectories and freeze them into a single reusable action, an automated consolidation-of-routine pattern MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could adopt.

notes: Table 1 (SS3.2 trajectory-structure ablation) is the key mechanism-validating number; Fig.2 (repeated-exploration measurement on Spider 2's firebase DB) and Fig.4 (composite-tool mining) anchor the motivating opportunities in SS2.1.

cita: Mi et al. (2026). Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution.
problema: GUI agents on long-horizon, cross-app tasks suffer context amnesia from limited context windows, and existing memory paradigms either rigidly couple high-level intent to entire fixed low-level trajectories (breaking under dynamic layout changes) or statically accumulate outdated/toxic trajectories with no mechanism to purge them.
mecanismo: DMS decomposes trajectories into independent reusable (Precondition,Goal)-tagged sub-plan units with their dense action trajectory, retrieved via dual-factor (precondition x goal) cosine-similarity matching; a survival value S(mi) combines log-diminishing reuse utility, sigmoid temporal decay (with usage-extended half-life) and a Bayesian reliability penalty from verification failures, pruned via an Elbow-method cutoff on the ranked utility curve; an epsilon-mutation mechanism lets the agent re-attempt a sub-task from scratch and overwrite the stored trajectory in-place if the new one is shorter/more efficient, while a Beta-Binomial Bayesian risk score suppresses historically failure-prone plans.
evaluacion: AndroidWorld benchmark (116 tasks x 20 real apps, millions of parameterized variants) across four general-purpose MLLM backbones (Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, GLM-4.5V, Seed1.6-VL) comparing PA-Lite baseline vs. DMS-PA-Lite, plus a 5-round memory-reuse-rate and success/stability(SRR)-over-rounds analysis.
numeros_clave: Table 1: DMS-PA-Lite reaches 66.4% success with Qwen2.5-VL-72B (+25.4pp over PA-Lite baseline), avg gains of +18.0% success rate and +33.9% execution stability across 4 backbones while reducing task latency (e.g. -4.75% for Qwen2.5-VL); memory reuse rate climbs from ~12% (round1) to >30% (round5), stabilizing at a 30-36% structural ceiling (Fig.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The composite survival value explicitly penalizes 'toxic priors' via temporal decay + a Bayesian reliability penalty driven by post-execution verification failures (SS3.2.3), a concrete staleness/poisoning-mitigation mechanism relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor.

epsilon-Mutation triggers in-place evolutionary overwrite of a stored trajectory only when a re-attempt proves shorter/more efficient (SS3.2.2), a concrete promotion-of-better-recipe mechanism MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could draw from.

DMS reports consistent task-latency reductions alongside accuracy gains (Fig.1, abstract) by replaying verified sub-trajectories instead of re-generating them, confirming MF's context/latency-economy framing.

notes: Table 1 (main AndroidWorld results) and Fig.4 (memory-reuse-rate heatmap over 5 rounds) anchor the quantitative claims; SS3.2.3 formalizes the survival-value pruning law.

cita: Mi et al. (2026). Skill-Pro: Learning Reusable Skills from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents.
problema: LLM agents re-derive solutions from scratch even in recurring situations because episodic-memory approaches merely retrieve past cases as 'history books' requiring inference-heavy re-reasoning at decision time, producing computational redundancy and unreliable long-horizon execution -- while parametric fine-tuning to fix this is costly and forgets.
mecanismo: Skill-Pro formalizes a Skill-MDP where procedural memory is a pool of explicit Skills omega=(activation-condition, execution-procedure, termination-condition); Non-Parametric PPO evolves the pool without weight updates via Semantic Gradients (per-trajectory hindsight-attribution feedback on each Skill component, batch-aggregated into a natural-language update direction that revises the Skill) filtered by a PPO-style trust-region Gate (a clipped importance-ratio/advantage verification functional under the frozen LLM policy admitting only candidates with positive expected advantage), plus online score-based pruning (advantage-per-invocation) that removes non-positive-score or duplicate Skills to keep the pool compact.
evaluacion: ALFWorld and TextArena benchmarks; in-domain, cross-task (out-of-distribution/higher-difficulty), and cross-agent (heterogeneous LLM backbones: Gemma-3-4B, Qwen3-32B, LLaMA-3.3-70B) reuse-rate and performance evaluation vs. RAG, ExpeL, A-MEM, AWM, G-Memory, ReAct, CoT baselines, plus ablations on Semantic Gradients / PPO Gate / online scoring.
numeros_clave: Table 1: Skill-Pro reuse rate 0.925 (in-domain)/0.825-0.90 (cross-task)/0.85-0.875 (cross-agent) vs best baseline RAG 0.349/0.44-0.47; storage cost 816 total stored tokens vs 40510-391706 for baselines (>50x compression); Table 2: ALFWorld success 0.90 (train)/0.909 (OOD) vs best baseline AWM 0.70/0.90.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Non-Parametric PPO's Semantic Gradient + PPO Gate (SS4.1-4.2) is a formalized, verifiable procedure for revising and admitting a refined Skill into the pool only if it passes a trust-region advantage test -- a rigorous consolidation/promotion gate MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could adopt beyond ad hoc gotcha-to-recipe promotion.

Table 1 shows Skill-Pro's procedural memory footprint (816 total stored tokens) is 50-500x smaller than episodic/insight/workflow baselines (40510-391706 tokens) while achieving higher reuse and task success (Table 2) -- a strong confirmation of MF's context-economy thesis that typed procedural memory beats raw episodic accumulation.

The Skill pool acts as a small, evolvable derived index over raw interaction trajectories (SS3.4-4.3) rather than the ground truth itself, echoing MF's Tier-3 derived-index framing, though the paper doesn't discuss staleness/rebuild relative to a Tier-1 source.

notes: Table 1 (SS5.2, reuse rate + storage/execution cost) and Table 2 (task performance) anchor the quantitative claims; Fig.2 diagrams the Skill-MDP + Non-Parametric PPO pipeline (SS4).

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval.
problema: LLM self-correction/code-optimization methods (TextGrad-style textual gradient descent) are stateless first-order optimizers: each run starts from scratch, ignoring past debugging experience and the 'semantic curvature' of the error landscape, causing inefficient zig-zagging and excessive token consumption to converge.
mecanismo: TextBFGS maintains a Hessian-Proxy Case Base of (gradient, operator) tuples -- historical error/feedback descriptions paired with the abstract correction operator that resolved them -- and retrieves top-k operators by error-similarity (not surface problem-similarity, unlike REMO) using the previous step's gradient as a 'semantic momentum' query; a single LLM call (One-Pass Update) simultaneously diagnoses the current error (<GRADIENT>), generates/reuses a correction operator (<OPERATOR>) and revises the code (<IMPROVED>); successful updates are retained back into the Case Base (Retain), forming a self-evolving Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain CBR loop.
evaluacion: HumanEval-Hard (45 tasks) and MBPP-Hard (117 tasks) filtered subsets from EvalPlus where the base model (Qwen3-235B-A22B) initially scores 0 on Pass@1; compared against TextGrad, TextGrad-Momentum, a no-Case-Base ablation (TextBFGS w/o CB), and TextBFGS-REMO (problem-similarity retrieval reproduction), including a cross-domain vs. in-domain Case-Base-source transfer experiment.
numeros_clave: On MBPP-Hard, Case Base integration lifts Plus pass rate from 58.12% (Momentum) to 78.63% (+20.51pp, Table 2); cross-domain transfer: TextBFGS (error-based retrieval) holds 74.36% Plus pass using a HumanEval-sourced case base to solve MBPP, vs. TextBFGS-REMO (problem-based retrieval) collapsing to 58.12% on the same cross-domain transfer (+16.24pp gap, Table 3 vs 4); One-Pass update reduces computational cost by ~50% vs standard multi-step methods (SS3.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: TextBFGS deliberately indexes cases by error/gradient (not by surface problem text) as the single retrieval key (SS3.3, Eq.6), and this key choice is shown empirically to determine cross-domain transfer (Table 3 vs 4) -- a concrete lesson for MF's COSTURAS question of what the single source-of-truth key for a fact/lesson should be.

Table 2's ablation (Case Base integration: +20.51pp Plus pass rate on MBPP-Hard vs. Momentum-only) empirically confirms that retaining and reusing successful correction operators (a consolidation loop, SS3.5 Retain) materially improves outcomes over transient/no memory -- supports MF's CONSOLIDACION thesis.
SS3.4 reports the One-Pass fused diagnosis+operator+revision step cuts computational cost ~50% vs standard multi-step correction pipelines, confirming MF's context/latency-economy framing.

notes: Table 1/2 (HumanEval-Hard/MBPP-Hard ablations) and Table 3/4 (cross-domain vs in-domain retrieval) anchor the numbers; Fig.2 visualizes the TextGrad vs TextBFGS optimization-trajectory difference (SS3.2).

cita: Mokssit, Ravi, Nie, Kim & Liu (2026). FHIR-AgentEval: A Modular Sandbox for Benchmarking Clinical LLM Agents with an Evaluation of Memory-Augmented Configurations.
problema: LLM agents translating natural-language clinical requests into structured FHIR API operations are unreliable for realistic appointment-management/genetic-testing workflows (prior work shows a steep drop from read-only Q&A to multi-step write/action tasks), with strategic failures like incorrect tool selection and resource-type confusion, and no rigorous sandboxed benchmark existed to measure whether memory helps.
mecanismo: FHIR-AgentEval provides 43 modular tasks against a resettable HAPI FHIR R4 server with deterministic + soft (LLM-judge) validators; agents (LangChain ReAct/GPT-4.1-mini, capped 15 iterations) are evaluated in 5 configurations varying access to an on-demand FHIR-specs MCP server and a Reflexion-inspired long-term-memory MCP server, whose micro (per resource/operation tip) and macro (task-level strategic) reflections are distilled offline by a GPT-4.1 evaluator + o4-mini reflector from training-task trajectories and indexed in a dual FAISS store (semantic for macro, structured-metadata exact-match for micro).
evaluacion: Four experimental settings (seen variations; unseen variations; paraphrased prompts; held-out tasks) across five agent configurations (baseline, +specs, +memory no-specs-training, +memory specs-trained, +memory specs-trained+specs), measuring task success rate (mean +/- SD over 3 runs), variance decomposition (same-prompt/within-task/between-task), failure-mode flags, tool-call counts and token usage.
numeros_clave: Best memory configuration (Memory specs-trained+FHIR specs) beats baseline by +22.5% (Exp.1) and +27.9% (Exp.2); on held-out tasks (Exp.4) best memory config (no-specs-training) reaches 60.6% overall success, +9.1% over baseline (abstract); memory-enhanced configs show lower total variance (2503-2643 vs 2879-2905 squared pp for baselines) driven by reduced between-task variance (42-49% vs >54%).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The ablation across 5 configurations isolates that memory (not raw spec access alone) is what reduces strategic failures like incorrect tool selection/resource-type confusion (Discussion, Fig.7-8) -- a measured demonstration that retrieval mechanism/content matters more than mere context availability, aligning with MF's G-M2 measured-retrieval stance.

Reflexion training distills micro (operation-level tips) vs. macro (task-level strategic) reflections from execution logs offline (SS Reflexion training process), a two-granularity consolidation scheme MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could adopt for promoting gotchas at different scopes.

Memory-augmented configurations consistently show HIGHER median token usage than baseline (Fig.10) despite better success/stability -- relevant context for MF's context-economy tradeoff (accuracy vs. token cost), without a clear net-favorable verdict either way.

notes: Held-out-task results (Exp.4, Discussion) and variance-decomposition analysis (Fig.6) anchor the quantitative claims; failure-mode taxonomy (Fig.7-8: incorrect tool selection/order, resource-type confusion) grounds the qualitative mechanism claims.

cita: Xie et al. (2026). MEMO: Memory-Augmented Model Context Optimization for Robust Multi-Turn Multi-Agent LLM Games.
problema: Multi-turn, multi-agent LLM game evaluations exhibit substantial run-to-run variance because small early deviations compound across turns and are amplified by multi-agent coupling, biasing win-rate estimates and destabilizing model rankings across repeated tournaments; static or single-batch prompt optimization cannot adapt to rare, decisive states that recur across game rounds.
mecanismo: MEMO couples tournament-based context evolution (TrueSkill Bayesian skill rating with a conservative lower-confidence-bound score to select/discard candidate contexts across self-play generations) with a persistent memory bank Bmem that distills structured typed insights from sampled trajectory reflections and reconciles them via CRUD-style Add/Remove/Edit merge operations (conflicting insights mutually removed, similar ones merged/generalized); a prioritized replay buffer resamples rare/decisive game-state prefixes (inverse-frequency priority) to improve coverage, and the highest-scoring evolved context is reinjected as inference-time priors for future rounds.
evaluacion: Five text-based games from TextArena/SPIN-Bench (negotiation, imperfect-information, perfect-information categories) with GPT-4o-mini and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct backbones, compared against static prompting (baseline, CoT, ToT), prompt optimization (TextGrad, MIPRO, GEPA) and RL self-play (UnstableBaselines, SPIRAL) baselines using mean win rate and relative standard error (RSE) across 3 optimization runs plus a module ablation (Tournament/Memory/Replay) and cross-task transfer analysis.
numeros_clave: MEMO raises mean win rate from 25.1% to 49.5% (GPT-4o-mini) and 20.9% to 44.3% (Qwen-2.5-7B) using 2,000 self-play games (19x fewer than RL's 38,000); lowest RSE 6.4% vs MIPRO's 12.4%; ablation Table 3: mean win rate 23.8% (prompt-opt alone) -> 34.2% (+Memory, +10.4) -> 48.1% (Tournament+Memory, +24.3) -> 50.2% (+Replay, +26.4); output-token cost 91K vs MIPRO 354K / GEPA 113K (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Ablation Table 3 isolates that Memory alone contributes the largest single jump (+10.4pp) and Tournament+Memory jointly (+24.3pp) dominates Tournament-only (+3.3pp) or Replay-only gains -- a direct measured confirmation that MF's CONSOLIDACION (retained, merged insights) is the dominant lever, not exploration alone.

The memory bank's Add/Remove/Edit merge rule (SS3.2) explicitly detects and deletes CONTRADICTORY insights (both sides removed) rather than storing conflicting facts side-by-side, a concrete single-source-of-truth reconciliation policy relevant to MF's COSTURAS anchor.

Table 1 shows MEMO uses ~91K output tokens vs 354K (MIPRO) and 113K (GEPA) while matching/beating their win rates, and needs 19x fewer self-play games than RL -- a strong confirmation of MF's context/sample-economy thesis.

notes: Table 2 (main win-rate/RSE results) and Table 3 (module ablation) anchor the numbers; Fig.1 visualizes the stability-vs-win-rate and sample-efficiency comparisons; Table 4 tests cross-game generalization of learned context.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). VeriAgent: A Tool-Integrated Multi-Agent System with Evolving Memory for PPA-Aware RTL Code Generation.
problema: LLM-based RTL (Verilog) code generation focuses mostly on functional correctness while overlooking Power/Performance/Area (PPA) physical-design metrics, and existing systems use EDA-toolchain feedback only shallowly (single-round), lacking any long-term optimization memory to accumulate and refine knowledge across design iterations.
mecanismo: VeriAgent runs a closed-loop multi-agent workflow (Programmer, Correctness, PPA agents + EDA tools) where a Memory Manager extracts structured memory nodes (trigger condition, natural-language guidance, metadata) from execution trajectories into three types -- Rule Memory (general design constraints), Structure Memory (code-pattern-to-optimization mappings), EDA Signal Memory (PPA-signal-to-optimization mappings); before each generation step an LLM semantically matches context against stored triggers to activate top-K relevant nodes injected into agent prompts, and after each task an LLM-based Decide module inserts/refines/discards each candidate memory node against the top-K most-similar existing nodes (Algorithm 1).
evaluacion: VerilogEval (Machine/Human tracks, pass@1/5/10) and RTLLM v1.1 (functional) / v2.0 (PPA, via Yosys+OpenROAD NanGate45 synthesis) benchmarks with GPT-4o and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview backbones, compared against training-based SOTA (CraftRTL, ChipSeek-R1, etc.) and training-free direct prompting, plus an ablation removing Memory / Tool Feedback / PPA Analyzer and pairwise PPA win-rate vs VeriPPA/ChipSeek-R1.
numeros_clave: VeriAgent(Gemini-3-pro) reaches 97.9% pass@1 VerilogEval-Machine / 98.1% Human / 100% RTLLM Syn@5; RTLLM v2.0 relative PPA score 8.539 (Gemini-3) / 5.119 (GPT-4o) vs original=1.0, ChipSeek-R1=2.196; ablation Table 3: removing Memory drops PPA score from 5.119 to 3.839 (GPT-4o) and 8.539 to 6.541 (Gemini-3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Ablation Table 3 shows removing the memory mechanism alone drops the PPA score from 5.119 to 3.839 (GPT-4o) and 8.539 to 6.541 (Gemini-3) -- a clean, isolated measurement confirming that consolidating optimization experience into reusable memory nodes materially improves outcomes, supporting MF's CONSOLIDACION thesis.

Memory nodes are explicit (trigger, guidance, metadata) typed structures activated via LLM semantic matching against triggers (SS2.3.2), not raw log retrieval -- a derived, typed index layer over raw EDA tool output relevant to MF's TIER-INDICE/TIER-DOCS framing.

Three parallel memory types (Rule/Structure/EDA Signal) are each triggered and retrieved through one shared Memory Manager interface (Fig.1), illustrating a multi-typed-but-single-manager seam relevant to MF's COSTURAS question, without discussing cross-type conflict resolution explicitly.

notes: Table 1 (functional correctness) and Table 2 (PPA scores per design) anchor the primary numbers; Table 3 (component ablation) isolates the memory contribution; Fig.1 diagrams the closed-loop multi-agent + Memory Manager architecture (SS2).

cita: Rana et al. (2026). Oblivion: Self-Adaptive Agentic Memory Control through Decay-Driven Activation.
problema: Memory-augmented LLM agents rely on 'always-on' retrieval and 'flat' undifferentiated memory storage, causing high interference (needle-in-a-haystack degradation as stores grow) and unnecessary latency/cost, and typically resort to hard deletion rather than graceful, reversible forgetting to manage context limits.
mecanismo: Oblivion decouples memory control into a read path and a write path over a hierarchical memory (L1 Dynamic Procedural cluster index, L2 timestamped Semantic facts, L3 Preemptive Episodic entries): the Decayer gates retrieval by an uncertainty score (LLM-judge + embedding similarity) and computes an Ebbinghaus-inspired exponential retention score Rt(c)=exp(-nt(c)/St(c)) per cluster (utility+frequency-modulated stability, decay temperature T) so unused clusters fade in accessibility (never deleted) while frequently-used ones decay slowly; when triggered, the Activator decomposes the query into a DAG of sub-queries for targeted L2/L3 retrieval; on the write path a Recognizer performs credit assignment (which memories actually contributed to the response) and a Memory Manager reinforces only those clusters' utility, implementing decay-driven (not deletion-driven) forgetting.
evaluacion: LongMemEval (500 human-curated multi-session QA questions, Oracle vs. noisy-S settings) and GoodAI-LTM (33 dynamic long-horizon interaction tests, Isolated/2K/32K/120K memory-span settings) across 4 backbones (Phi-4-mini, Qwen3-30B-A3B, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini) vs. direct (LME-RFT/FullCtx) and memory (EverMemOS/BeyondPrompts) baselines, plus a memory-hierarchy ablation (L1/L2/L3 combinations) and a computational-efficiency (token/latency/cost) analysis.
numeros_clave: LongMemEval-S GPT-4.1-mini: Oblivion 90.60% avg accuracy vs LME-RFT-direct 89.00% and EverMemOS-memory 81.27%; GoodAI-LTM GPT-4.1-mini 120K: Oblivion 6.70 solved scenarios vs FullCtx 6.42; token cost reduced 73% (120K) and 67% (32K) vs FullCtx (Table 4); hierarchy ablation Table 3: full L1+L2+L3 stack (M5) reaches 90.60% (LongMemEval-S) / 8.41 (GoodAI-LTM 2K) vs single-layer 86.40%/6.14.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Oblivion reframes forgetting as decay-driven REDUCED ACCESSIBILITY rather than deletion (SS2.2-2.3: memories 'never deleted from D, preserving reactivatability') -- directly relevant to MF's NEGATIVO anchor if MF also treats non-recall as a graded signal rather than binary erase, though Oblivion's target is efficiency/interference, not explicit negative-knowledge capture.

Table 4 measures 73%/67% token-cost reduction at 120K/32K memory spans via uncertainty-gated (not always-on) retrieval while improving/matching accuracy -- a strong quantitative confirmation of MF's context-economy thesis that gating retrieval by need beats always-on recall.

L2 Semantic Memory stores timestamped facts specifically to resolve 'world drift' (temporal inconsistency, prioritizing currently-valid facts over outdated ones, SS2.1) -- a concrete staleness-resolution mechanism directly relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor.

notes: Table 1 (LongMemEval) and Table 2 (GoodAI-LTM) anchor main results; Table 3 isolates the L1/L2/L3 hierarchy contribution; Table 4 anchors the token/latency/cost tradeoff; Fig.2 visualizes the Ebbinghaus decay/reinforcement curves (SS5.1).

cita: Wu et al. (2026). LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues.
problema: Existing agent-memory benchmarks mostly evaluate personalized user-chat histories, short traces, or indirect downstream task success, leaving open whether memory systems can directly internalize environment-specific experience (interface affordances, state dynamics, workflows, recurring failure modes/gotchas) the way an 'experienced colleague' would across a genuinely long (25M-115M token) multi-trajectory haystack.
mecanismo: LME-V2 formalizes memory as a context-gathering task with Insert(trajectory)/Query(question) APIs over a haystack of up to 500 trajectories; the paper's own baseline AgentRunbook-R maintains three separate LLM-controller-queried knowledge pools (raw state-observation slices, state-transition events, high-level strategy/gotcha notes) retrieved via multi-stream dense queries, while AgentRunbook-C instead stores raw trajectories as files and invokes an augmented coding-agent (with workflow docs, memory manifests, helper inspection scripts) to search/inspect/assemble evidence at query time, trading latency for accuracy.
evaluacion: 451 manually curated questions (five memory abilities: static state recall, dynamic state tracking, workflow knowledge, environment gotchas, premise awareness) over web-agent trajectories from WebArena/WorkArena, in Small (100-trajectory/25M-token) and Medium (500-trajectory/115M-token) haystack tiers, comparing a simple RAG baseline, AgentRunbook-R, an off-the-shelf Codex coding-agent baseline, and AgentRunbook-C, measured by answer accuracy and query latency; pilot studies test frontier-LLM parametric-knowledge-only performance and oracle-trajectory upper bounds.
numeros_clave: Simple RAG: 40.1% overall accuracy; AgentRunbook-R: 57.8%; off-the-shelf Codex coding agent: 69.3% accuracy but ~182s/query (6.9x slower than AgentRunbook-R); AgentRunbook-C: best overall 72.5% accuracy while 32% faster than Codex; frontier LLMs with no trajectory context reach only up to 14.1% best-model accuracy (Fig.4), confirming questions are not answerable from parametric knowledge alone.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: AgentRunbook-R's separate 'procedure and hint note pool' explicitly consolidates trajectory-level notes into reusable typed workflow/gotcha knowledge (SS4.1), and the pilot study shows raw long-context prompting or slices alone underperform structured notes (Fig.4: 59.6% oracle-trajectories vs 82.5% oracle-slices+notes) -- confirms MF's TIER-DOCS thesis that typed narrative beats raw log dumping.

AgentRunbook-C achieves the best accuracy (72.5%) while being 32% faster than the raw coding-agent baseline (69.3% at 182s/query) purely from added scaffolding (workflow doc, manifests, helper scripts) -- directly supports MF's context/latency-economy thesis that structuring the retrieval interface (not just having more compute) is the lever.

The benchmark's central finding -- that a naive RAG baseline (40.1%) is dramatically outperformed by structured multi-pool retrieval (57.8%) and coding-agent-based evidence assembly (72.5%) -- is a MEASURED demonstration that retrieval design/mechanism, not mere embedding similarity, determines memory quality, aligning with MF's G-M2 stance.

notes: SS5 main results (RAG 40.1% / AgentRunbook-R 57.8% / Codex 69.3% / AgentRunbook-C 72.5%) and Fig.4 pilot studies anchor the numbers; Table 1 situates LME-V2's scale (25M-115M tokens) against prior benchmarks; Fig.5 diagrams both AgentRunbook variants (SS4).

cita: Choi et al. (2026). PREPING: Building Agent Memory without Tasks.
problema: Agent memory construction methods (offline from curated demonstrations, or online from post-deployment interactions) both require target-environment task experience that is unavailable for a newly connected environment, leaving a 'cold-start gap': the agent has no procedural memory when it first needs it, exposing users to early failures during online construction.
mecanismo: PREPING separates a construction-time Proposer memory (tracks prior synthetic-practice history, tool/workflow coverage imbalance, and grounded-environment facts observed during execution) from deployment-facing Solver memory: a Proposer generates synthetic tasks conditioned on Proposer memory (coverage-seeking, environment-grounded, avoiding redundancy), a Solver executes them producing trajectories, and a Validator scores feasibility+completion; only Validator-approved (feasibility=5) task-trajectory pairs are distilled (reflector-curator style, ACE-inspired) into Solver memory, while ALL outcomes (including rejected/infeasible ones) update Proposer memory to steer future proposals away from repeated failure modes -- an asymmetric write-gate separating what shapes practice from what becomes deployed procedural guidance.
