evaluacion: AppWorld (stateful app tasks, Test-Normal/Test-Challenge splits), BFCL v3 (function calling: Base/Long-Context/Missing-Parameter/Missing-Function), and MCP-Universe (Repository/Financial/3D/Browser categories); compared against pre-task baselines (Base no-memory, Direct-Memory-from-docs, Random/Guided free-form Exploration) and task-informed reference methods (ACE-Offline, ACE-Online), plus a component ablation (Validator gating / environment info / practice history) and a warm-start experiment (PREPING+ACE).
numeros_clave: PREPING improves average score over Base by 17.1pp (AppWorld), 19.3pp (BFCL v3), 5.4pp (MCP-Universe) with zero target-task experience, exceeding ACE-Offline on AppWorld (72.2 vs 69.0 avg) and near/surpassing ACE-Online on BFCL v3; PREPING+ACE warm-start improves AppWorld from 71.3 to 76.3 avg; deployment cost 2.99x lower on AppWorld and 2.23x lower on BFCL v3 than ACE-Online when frozen; ablation Table 2: disabling Validator+Env-Info+Practice-History drops AppWorld score from 83.7/70.2 to 47.8/26.8.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Validator's feasibility=5 threshold is an explicit, outcome-gated write trigger deciding what enters Solver memory (SS3.4), while a SEPARATE asymmetric channel (Proposer memory) absorbs ALL outcomes including rejects to steer future practice -- a two-tier write-discipline MF's G-M1 (discretionary write) could adopt: gate the durable store, but still learn from rejects elsewhere.

Proposer memory explicitly records failure/infeasibility reasons for REJECTED tasks (not just successes) to prevent future proposals from repeating the same failure modes (SS3.3) -- a concrete negative-knowledge mechanism (what NOT to try again) relevant to MF's NEGATIVO anchor, even though F does not flag NEGATIVO for this paper.

Frozen pre-task memory reduces deployment-time cost by 2.99x (AppWorld) and 2.23x (BFCL v3) vs. online memory construction (ACE-Online) by avoiding per-task memory-update calls -- a direct confirmation of MF's context/cost-economy thesis for WHEN to write vs. defer.

notes: Table 1 (main pre-task vs task-informed results) and Table 2 (component ablation) anchor the numbers; Table 3 and Fig.3 show the PREPING+ACE warm-start cold-start mitigation; Fig.1 (right) visualizes tool-coverage-vs-tested-tasks curves.

cita: Jin et al. (2026). SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents.
problema: GUI agents on multi-step tasks are limited by constrained context windows (losing early critical information, causing error accumulation across long horizons) and by static policies trained on fixed datasets that cannot reuse past successful strategies or adapt to dynamic layout/environment changes.
mecanismo: SE-GA's Test-Time Memory Extension (TTME) maintains a hierarchical memory M=(M_EPI, M_SEM, M_EXP): episodic memory is a sliding-window (horizon H) buffer of recent action transitions; semantic memory stores abstract interaction rules retrieved by cosine similarity of instruction embeddings; experiential memory stores raw trajectories plus reflective summaries retrieved via a hybrid intent+visual-similarity score, all three contexts concatenated into the agent's input at each decision step. Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution (MASE) then trains on this TTME-collected data in two stages: Grounding SFT (behavior cloning on memory-augmented context) followed by GRPO-based Self-Evolution Training with token-level importance ratios, adaptive clipping, a hierarchical format+accuracy reward, and a Hindsight Goal-Shifting mechanism that relabels prefix subsequences of FAILED trajectories as successes for whatever alternative sub-goal they actually achieved, converting failures into usable supervision.
evaluacion: ScreenSpot (grounding), AndroidControl-Low/High and GUIOdyssey (step-wise type/grounding/success-rate), and AndroidWorld (online dynamic generalization), using Qwen2.5-VL-7B as backbone, compared against 15 baselines (closed-source VLMs, generalist open-source VLMs, specialized GUI agents like UI-TARS/OS-Atlas/Aguvis), plus implicit ablation of TTME components and the Hindsight Goal-Shifting mechanism.
numeros_clave: 89.0% avg success on ScreenSpot (vs UI-TARS-72B 88.4%, OS-Atlas 82.5%); 75.8% success rate on AndroidControl-High (abstract); AndroidControl-Low: SR 88.6% (vs UI-TARS 91.3%), grounding 92.5% (best in Table 2); significant AndroidWorld generalization gains reported (abstract, dynamic online benchmark).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: plan_estado=SI per extraction; TTME's episodic memory (M_EPI) is a sliding-window transition history tracking CURRENT task progress (SS4.1.1), functioning as an implicit plan/state tracker rather than an explicit persisted plan-state artifact distinct from raw interaction history.

MASE's Hindsight Goal-Shifting mechanism (SS4.2.2) relabels FAILED trajectory prefixes as successes for whichever sub-goal they actually achieved, converting otherwise-discarded experience into reusable training/memory signal -- a concrete failure-to-recipe promotion pattern relevant to MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor.

Three memory types (episodic/semantic/experiential) are retrieved by three DIFFERENT similarity mechanisms (recency window, text-embedding cosine, hybrid intent+visual) and simply concatenated into one prompt (SS4.1), illustrating a multi-store/multi-key design relevant to MF's COSTURAS question without an explicit single-key reconciliation policy.

notes: Table 1 (ScreenSpot) and Table 2 (AndroidControl/GUIOdyssey) anchor the numbers; abstract reports AndroidWorld and AndroidControl-High headline figures not fully tabulated in the read excerpt; SS4.2 formalizes MASE's two-stage GRPO training with Hindsight Goal-Shifting (Eq.17).

cita: Ye, C., Liu, Y., Wang, Y., Yu, H., Zhao, Y., Liu, G., McAuley, J. y You, J. (2026). Auto-Dreamer: Learning Offline Memory Consolidation for Language Agents.
problema: Existing language-agent memory systems couple fast per-session acquisition and slow cross-session consolidation into a single online update, so they cannot discover recurring patterns, abstract reusable procedures, resolve contradictions, or prune redundant entries across sessions.
mecanismo: Two-timescale design: a fixed local append-only writer records typed entries per session; a learned offline consolidator (GRPO-trained, Qwen3-14B) performs a bounded tool-use rollout over a selected working region R (search/inspect/get-source-trace), treating R as read-only provenance-grounded evidence and synthesizing a replacement set S that supersedes R (region rewriting), rewarded by downstream task utility plus a counterfactual-masking term that credits load-bearing entries and penalizes redundant ones.
evaluacion: Continual-memory deployment and fixed-bank consolidation on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and WebArena, benchmarked against 10 baselines across 7 families (Reflexion, ExpeL, AWM, Memp, ReasoningBank, Mem0, LightMem, Mem-alpha, UMEM), reporting success rate, AUC and active memory-bank token size, plus ablations isolating region rewriting and the counterfactual reward.
numeros_clave: ScienceWorld 41.1% SR (+7pts vs UMEM 34.1%) with 12x smaller memory bank than the strongest baseline; ALFWorld 60.2% SR with 6x less memory; WebArena 52.3% SR leading all baselines; fixed-bank ALFWorld 72.7% acc using only 634 tokens vs Memp 927 / ReasoningBank 3,221.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A learned offline consolidator achieves large measured token compaction (12x/6x, Table 1) while improving task success, a concrete write-side lever for MF's context-economy goal.
Region-rewriting replace-semantics (§4.1: old entries persist only if re-synthesized into S) is a directly adoptable pattern for promoting transient gotchas into durable recipes.
Consolidation is provenance-grounded (re-readable source trajectories linked from every entry, Fig.1), supporting MF's stance that consolidated memory must stay traceable to source.

notes: Numbers anchored in Table 1 (continual deployment + fixed-bank panels) and §4.1-4.3 (region-rewriting formalism, Eq.1-2); Fig.2 gives the full architecture.

cita: Bi et al. (2025). Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents.
problema: LLM-based agents lack a posteriori mechanisms to acquire procedural knowledge after deployment; a priori written SOPs are incomplete (humans learn by observation, not documentation), cannot enumerate all edge cases, and go stale as web interfaces change.
mecanismo: PRAXIS writes a state-action-result tuple after every action in real time: pre-action environment state, agent internal state/goal, action taken, post-action environment state. Retrieval (Alg.1) jointly matches environment-state similarity (IoU + length overlap) to select a top-k candidate set, then re-ranks by internal-state embedding similarity and a threshold, injecting matched exemplars into the action-selection node of the Altrina web agent.
evaluacion: REAL web-browsing benchmark (11 site replicas, 112 tasks) across five VLM backbones (Llama4, Qwen3-VL, Gemini2.5 Flash, GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5), measuring accuracy, best-of-5 accuracy, reliability (success rate over 5 repeats) and steps-to-completion, with an ablation over retrieval breadth k.
numeros_clave: Average accuracy 40.3%->44.1% with procedural memory; best-of-5 53.7%->55.7%; reliability 74.5%->79.0%; steps-to-completion 25.2->20.2; accuracy rises monotonically then plateaus as retrieval breadth k grows (Fig.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Retrieval is a measured joint state+goal similarity policy with an explicit breadth-k ablation (Fig.3, §4.4), a concrete alternative measured-retrieval design MF could compare against ADR-019's stance.
The write trigger is every single action step (append-only, real time, §3.2), an aggressive discretionary-write baseline MF's G-M1 design could be measured against.

notes: Fig.1-3 and Table 1-2 (REAL benchmark, per-backbone deltas) anchor the numbers; Altrina is an industry proprietary agent (formerly Tessa), single benchmark family.

cita: Omelchenko, I. y Strukov, V. (2025). Reflective memory architecture for adaptive planning in hierarchical LLM agents in virtual environments.
problema: Storing the complete interaction history for LLM-based planning agents overflows the context window, raises computational cost and planning latency, and degrades attention performance, so agents need a bounded inter-episode memory mechanism.
mecanismo: A Reflective Memory System evolves a typed set of RULE memory elements (content + importance score, init 0.5) via LLM-generated CRUD-like operators (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/CONFIRM) applied every k episodes by a larger reflecting LLM (Qwen3:30b); importance is updated by an exponential moving average from DELETE/CONFIRM signals, and elements below a threshold are pruned, while a smaller planner LLM (Qwen3:8b) consumes the surviving rules.
evaluacion: Ablation across 9 memory configurations (no memory, episodic-only, offline reflection, three unstructured-reflection variants, structured Reflection every 2/5 episodes, manual expert instructions) in the Minigrid ColoredDoorKey environment, measured by task accuracy, cumulative reward, steps-per-episode and planning duration/cost.
numeros_clave: Structured Reflection E-2 reaches accuracy 0.99 (reward 0.7353, 29.29 steps) vs the no-memory baseline's 0.68 (reward 0.4994, 52.06 steps), matching or exceeding the Manual-Instructions upper bound (0.99, reward 0.7345) (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: CRUD reflection operators with importance-score decay and pruning (§3.3) empirically beat naive full-history accumulation, supporting MF's promotion-of-gotchas-to-recipes consolidation design.
The paper explicitly measures Planning Duration as a function of memory size (Table 1's step/latency metrics), backing MF's concern that unbounded memory growth raises inference cost.

notes: Table 1 (9-config comparison) and §3.3 (CRUD operator equations) anchor the numbers; single small environment (Minigrid) and niche student-thesis venue (Karazin Kharkiv bulletin) -- RECONSIDERAR generalizability of the ablation.

cita: Lin et al. (2026). MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation.
problema: Prior automatic-skill systems (Voyager, AutoSkill, EvoSkill, SkillGen, Anthropic Agent Skills) cover only part of the skill lifecycle: they lack structured per-skill memory, unit-test-driven evaluation/refinement, or handle long-horizon context poorly, leaving skills as static, unvalidated artifacts.
mecanismo: MUSE unifies five lifecycle stages -- creation, memory, management, evaluation, refinement -- around a built-in skill_create tool invoked inside the agent's ReAct loop: new skills are packaged as SKILL.md+scripts/tests/resources, gated by a create->evaluate->register loop that runs unit tests/sandbox checks and triggers a Refiner on failure; multi-level memory adds skill-level per-skill .memory.md notes atop short-term (compressed) and long-term (persistent) memory; management does catalog-based retrieval, merging of overlapping skills and pruning of unused ones.
evaluacion: SkillsBench (75-task, 4 super-domains, Docker-graded verifiers) and SkillLearnBench (100-instance continual-skill benchmark), compared against Hermes, Codex and Claude Code (all GPT-5.5-backed), with/without human- or self-authored skills, plus a cross-agent transfer experiment and a run-to-run stability analysis.
numeros_clave: SkillsBench human-skill average 59.67% (+12.72pp lift); self-created-skill accuracy 53.42% vs Codex 47.52% and Claude Code 44.27%; self-created skills beat human skills on the covered subset (85.24% vs 81.17%); transfer to Hermes reaches 51.90% (exceeds Hermes+human 48.02%); SkillLearnBench human/self-created 72.0%/48.0%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The skill-management stage's merge/prune/refine over a growing skill bank (§3.2) is a directly transferable pattern for promoting durable, testable procedures in MF.
The structured context manager provides adaptive compression with cross-session state persistence for long-horizon tasks (§3.4), directly relevant to treating plan/task state as first-class memory.
Skills are unit-test/sandbox-gated before registration (create->evaluate->register loop, §3.2), confirming MF's stance that consolidated artifacts need a validation gate against drift.

notes: SkillsBench Fig.1/Table 2-3 anchor the accuracy numbers; §3.4 (context manager, cross-session state) anchors the PLAN-ESTADO claim; skill format follows Anthropic's Agent Skills spec (§3.2).

cita: Liu et al. (2026). MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs.
problema: Existing agentic memory systems typically adapt only the memory bank or its prompt text while keeping the surrounding memory-construction-retrieval (MCR) pipeline fixed after deployment, so they struggle with heterogeneous task-specific failure modes and drift out of alignment as the bank evolves.
mecanismo: MemPro treats the entire MCR pipeline (both prompts and executable code) as the evolution target, maintaining a version tree of runnable pipeline implementations with per-node evaluation logs; an Evolving Agent iteratively selects a promising node, diagnoses recurring failure modes from the logs, and expands it via a sequence of EDIT/DEBUG/TERMINATE actions (failure-mode-guided edit-debug refinement) to produce an improved child pipeline version, which is then evaluated on a held-out training split.
evaluacion: LongMemEval, LoCoMo, HotpotQA (56K/224K/448K context lengths) and NarrativeQA, compared against static agentic memory baselines (Mem0, A-MEM, MemoryOS, LightMem, GAM, etc.) and prompt-only evolution (GEPA, MetaMem), with an ablation removing code-level edits, the version tree, and iterative expansion.
numeros_clave: MemPro-15 LongMemEval avg 79.00 vs best baseline GAM 72.40 (gpt-4o-mini); LoCoMo avg rises 79.48->84.93 from MemPro-5 to MemPro-15; HotpotQA avg F1 66.72 vs GAM 61.50; ablation removing code-level edits drops LoCoMo score from 84.93 to ~74.83 (Fig.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Evolving the whole MCR pipeline as one runnable, versioned artifact (rather than only its data store) is a pattern relevant to MF's single-source-per-fact / multi-store-seams question.

The paper claims a 'favorable performance-cost trade-off' (abstract, Fig.1 iteration curve) but reports no explicit token/latency ablation table, so it is context without a hard cost number for MF to act on.

notes: Table 1-2 (main benchmark results) and Fig.3 (ablation, w/o Code drops ~10pts) anchor the numbers; version-tree evolution operates over executable pipeline code, not memory content itself.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). Learning to Retrieve: Dual-Level Long-Term Memory for Text-to-SQL Agents.
problema: Memory retrieval for interactive text-to-SQL agents either uses fixed similarity heuristics that ignore downstream utility, or single-horizon dynamic retrieval trained only from sparse terminal rewards at the episode level, mismatching interactions where useful memory differs between initial planning and local, state-conditioned execution.
mecanismo: MERIT maintains two memory banks: episode-level memory (full trajectories + distilled insights) retrieved via embedding candidates plus an RL-trained (PPO) selector trained on terminal reward for global strategy, and turn-level memory (state-signature-indexed state-action-observation snippets) retrieved via a second RL-trained selector; because turn-level retrieval lacks direct outcome labels, a lightweight Process Reward Model (SFT+GRPO on teacher rubrics) scores retrieved-memory utility per turn and supplies dense PPO rewards.
evaluacion: BIRD-Interact (in-domain, Phase1/Phase2, READ/WRITE task splits) against no-memory, static-retrieval (BM25, cosine similarity, TopicK) and dynamic-retrieval (Memento, MemRL) baselines, plus zero-shot transfer to Spider2-Snow and ablations on component removal, retrieval breadth (pass@k) and retrieved-memory count.
numeros_clave: MERIT overall success 33.01% Phase1 / 22.17% Phase2 (best baseline TopicK/Memento reach 27.17%/16.00% and 29.00%/18.83%); lowest avg turns 7.84 (Phase2) vs No-Memory 8.93; Spider2-Snow transfer 69.29% vs No-Memory 66.00%; removing episode-level memory drops Phase1 success to 23.50% (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A dense Process-Reward-Model score, not embedding similarity alone, drives turn-level retrieval training (§5.3), reinforcing MF's ADR-019 stance that retrieval quality should be measured/learned, not assumed.
MERIT lowers average interaction turns relative to no-memory and every baseline (Table 1), evidence that better-targeted dual-horizon retrieval reduces operational cost, not just improves accuracy.

notes: Table 1 (BIRD-Interact Phase1/2) and Table 2 (Spider2-Snow transfer) anchor the numbers; the episode-vs-turn dual-horizon split is the key differentiator vs the single-horizon Memento/MemRL baselines.

cita: Zhao et al. (2026). Neural Procedural Memory: Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering.
problema: Explicit textual procedural memory (RAG-style workflows/insights) causes a text-action disconnect: agents comprehend retrieved instructions but fail to consistently act on them, since procedural knowledge is inherently ineffable and lossy once compressed into discrete tokens.
mecanismo: Neural Procedural Memory (NPM) extracts dual-granularity contrastive experience (inter-trajectory: failed vs successful runs; intra-trajectory: degenerate vs effective steps within one failed run) into per-layer hidden-state representations; at inference it retrieves the top-K most similar historical tasks, synthesizes a task-specific steering vector from the retrieved contrastive pairs, and additively injects it into the residual stream at a target layer during generation, training-free and without consuming context-window tokens.
evaluacion: ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld and BabyAI with MiniCPM3-4B and Qwen3-4B/8B backbones, compared against No-Memory, explicit-text baselines (Insights, Workflows), other implicit-steering baselines (CAA, Mass-Mean), a Hybrid (NPM+Workflows) condition, plus PCA and cosine-similarity representational analyses of the extracted vectors.
numeros_clave: Qwen3-8B average score rises 30.63->36.32 with NPM vs CAA 22.79 / Mass-Mean 31.89; Hybrid (NPM+Workflows) reaches avg 41.89 (ALFWorld 66.42%, ScienceWorld 31.89); on WebShop/Qwen3-4B NPM scores 48.00, exceeding explicit Workflows' 45.73 (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper argues procedural knowledge represented as opaque activation-space steering vectors (not typed textual docs) outperforms text-based memory (§1, Table 1), challenging MF's Tier-1 'docs=truth, typed narrative' design for procedural facets specifically.
Implicit steering matches or beats explicit textual memory while consuming zero context-window tokens (§4.2), supporting MF's context-economy stance that not all memory needs to occupy the prompt.

Retrieval is a measured top-K historical-task similarity step that feeds vector synthesis (§3.3), an alternative measured-retrieval design operating over activations rather than text/embeddings of docs.

notes: Table 1 (4 benchmarks x 3 backbones) and Fig.4-5 (PCA/cosine-similarity structure of steering vectors) anchor the numbers; a genuinely different representation modality (activation space, not text or vector DB).

cita: Zhao et al. (2026). Parametric Skills.
problema: Textual in-context skills are bottlenecked by the model's ability to comprehend and follow complex instructions in long contexts, and existing text-space skill-evolution methods remain decoupled from the underlying model's own learning.
mecanismo: A hypernetwork converts a textual skill (via a frozen text encoder) into LoRA-adapter parameters in a single forward pass, requiring no gradient updates and no context tokens at deployment; it is trained via skill-reconstruction pretraining (full/prefix/section-completion self-supervised objectives) then skill-exploitation fine-tuning on single/multi-turn trajectories, supports merging multiple parametric skills via rank-concatenation of LoRA factors, and includes a self-evolving loop (generate text skill -> verify -> revise -> recompile to parameters) with a continual variant that EMA-merges accepted task skills into one global parametric skill.
evaluacion: Six complex SWE subtasks judged by DeepSeek-V4-Flash (LLM judge), BERTScore and F1 against In-Context, SHINE and No-Skill baselines; a 529-task multi-skill-merging benchmark; self-evolution on HumanEval (up to 5 rounds) with an online continual-merging variant.
numeros_clave: ParametricSkills averages +6.44 LLM-judge points over In-Context (64.09 vs 57.65), beating No-Skill (50.21) and SHINE (48.48); rank-concat merge avg-judge 60.12 vs single-skill 58.27; self-evolution raises HumanEval pass rate from 75.00% (base parametric skill, 123/164) to 84.76% (139/164).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The skill still lives once as text and is recompiled into parameters only on demand (Fig.1), an alternative single-source-of-truth pattern where the compiled artifact is never itself the source of record, relevant to MF's multi-store-seams question.
The continual-learning variant EMA-merges accepted per-task parametric skills into one global skill (§3.4), a concrete consolidation mechanism operating in parameter space rather than text.

Self-evolving skills are still authored/revised as text and only compiled to parameters after verifier acceptance (§3.4), so provenance stays anchored in an inspectable textual artifact even though execution is parametric.

notes: Table 1 (six SWE subtasks) and Table 3 (HumanEval self-evolution) anchor the numbers; representacion=PARAMETROS is the differentiator vs typical text/vector memory stores.

cita: Zhou et al. (2026). ToM-SWE: User Mental Modeling for Software Engineering Agents.
problema: Coding agents operate statelessly session-to-session and lack mechanisms to infer and track evolving user intent, goals, preferences and constraints, especially under underspecified instructions, causing wasted effort and misaligned output.
mecanismo: A dedicated theory-of-mind (ToM) agent runs alongside the primary SWE agent, maintaining a three-tier external hierarchical memory (raw session storage; per-session user-model analysis; an aggregated overall cross-session user model). The SWE agent calls consult_tom in-session to receive user mental-state suggestions, and update_memory after each session to trigger the ToM agent's tiered update workflow (analyze_session then initialize/update the overall user model).
evaluacion: Ambiguous SWE-bench and a newly introduced Stateful SWE-bench (500 instances, 15 synthetic developer profiles, LLM user simulator) against CodeAct and RAGCodeAct baselines across 3 backbones, plus a 3-week/17-developer/209-session in-the-wild deployment study and a cost-overhead analysis.
numeros_clave: Stateful SWE-bench: ToMCodeAct 59.7% resolved vs CodeAct 18.1% (Claude Sonnet 4, +41.6pp); Ambiguous SWE-bench 63.4% vs 51.9%; user-satisfaction score 3.62 vs 2.57 (+41%); 86% of 174 ToM suggestions across 209 sessions accepted/partially accepted; ToM overhead ~16% of the SWE agent's average cost.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The three-tier hierarchical external memory (raw session / per-session model / overall model, Fig.2) separating raw evidence from a distilled narrative is directly analogous to MF's typed-doc-tiering design.

After-session consolidation aggregates per-session user models into the overall model only via an explicit LLM-driven update/initialize action (not passive accumulation), confirming MF's stance that promotion to durable memory should be a deliberate step.

The paper reports ToM overhead as roughly 16% of the SWE agent's average cost (§5.3) without a directional verdict on whether that overhead is acceptable, leaving it context rather than confirming or refuting a cost stance.

notes: Fig.4 and Table 1-2 (benchmark results) plus the cost Pareto-frontier figure (§5.3) anchor the numbers; the 3-week/17-developer field study (86% acceptance) is the qualitative evidence.

cita: Jayanti and Han (2026). Enhancing Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Context-Aware Server Collaboration.
problema: Traditional MCP keeps servers stateless and forces every coordination step through a central LLM that must hold the full context/state in its window, causing high latency, repeated inference calls, and context loss between steps in multi-agent workflows.
mecanismo: CA-MCP introduces a Shared Context Store (SCS) that the central LLM seeds once with an initial plan (goals, constraints, execution outline); MCP servers then become autonomous stateful reactors that read/write the SCS directly to coordinate intermediate state and outputs, without repeated round-trips to the central LLM, which only re-engages at the end to summarize the accumulated context into a final response.
evaluacion: TravelPlanner (500 queries: execution time, completeness, BERTScore, ROUGE-L, LLM-call count) and REALM-Bench Wedding Logistics P5 (goal/constraint satisfaction, makespan, coordination score, LLM calls), comparing Traditional MCP vs CA-MCP with paired significance tests.
numeros_clave: TravelPlanner: execution time 41.99s->13.52s (67.8% faster, paired t-test p=1.6e-137); completeness 0.764->1.000; LLM calls 5->2 (60% reduction); REALM-Bench: makespan 330->180 min (45.5% shorter), execution time 8.52s->2.26s (73.5% faster), LLM calls halved 2->1.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Shared Context Store persists intermediate task/plan state (goals, constraints, execution outline) written once by the planner LLM and read/updated by servers throughout execution (§2), a direct instance of plan-state as first-class shared memory across agents.

Replacing per-server private context with one shared blackboard-style store (single source of truth for task state) empirically halves LLM calls while improving completeness (Table 2-3), supporting MF's single-source-per-fact stance over duplicated per-agent stores.

Measured wall-clock/latency and LLM-call reductions (67.8%/73.5% faster, Fig.2-3) evidence that centralizing shared state, instead of re-sending full context each step, is a concrete context-economy lever.

notes: Table 2 (TravelPlanner) and Table 3 (REALM-Bench) anchor the numbers; small-scale paper (anonymous GitHub repo, only 2 benchmark tasks, authors explicitly note no hardware/parallelism controls in Limitations) -- RECONSIDERAR generalizability.

cita: Anderson (2026). The AI Codebase Maturity Model: From Assisted Coding to Fully Autonomous Systems.
problema: Teams adopting AI coding tools plateau at ad-hoc 'prompt and review' without a systematic framework for progressing toward more autonomous, trustworthy AI-driven development, and existing maturity models define levels by autonomy alone rather than by the feedback infrastructure that makes autonomy safe.
mecanismo: A 6-level maturity model (Assisted -> Instructed -> Measured -> Adaptive -> Semi-Automated -> Fully Autonomous) defined by feedback-loop topology: each level encodes human judgment into durable artifacts (instruction files -> metrics/tests -> self-tuning configs -> proposal pipelines -> a multi-agent fleet with a distributed work ledger 'Beads' for claiming work plus a workload governor that adapts cadence to backlog), validated by a 4-month practitioner case study and a reference multi-agent implementation (Hive).
evaluacion: 4-month longitudinal practitioner case study on KubeStellar Console (36+ cataloged feedback loops mapped to ACMM levels) plus initial production-deployment evidence for the Hive Level-6 reference implementation, including specific bug-fix case studies.
numeros_clave: 91% code coverage across 12 shards; 74 CI/CD workflows, 32 nightly test suites, 36+ cataloged feedback loops; bug-to-fix under 30 minutes and feature-to-implementation under 60 minutes, 24/7; Case A external bug fixed/merged in 3 hours (624 additions across 7 files); Case B user-misunderstanding response in 10 minutes.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Level 6's Beads distributed work ledger lets agents claim/track work-in-progress state to prevent duplicate effort, and an adaptive workload governor tracks backlog state (SURGE/BUSY/QUIET/IDLE) to set cadence, both concrete instances of plan/task state as first-class shared memory.

The model's central thesis, that each level's capability must be encoded into a durable artifact (instructions -> tests -> configs -> policy files) rather than held only in a human's head or the model's context, directly supports MF's promotion-of-gotchas-to-recipes stance.

The paper's headline lesson (Level 3 section) is that flaky/non-deterministic tests erode the trust required for autonomous merges, reinforcing MF's concern that memory/automation artifacts need reliability guarantees, not just presence.

notes: Table 1-2 (level/feedback-loop inventory) and the Case A/B examples anchor the numbers; single-practitioner, self-authored experience report (IBM Research, written with Claude Code assistance per its own disclosure), not peer-reviewed -- RECONSIDERAR given the n=1, self-reported nature of the evidence.

cita: Jiang et al. (2026). KRCA: An Efficient Root Cause Analysis System in Hyper-Scale Microservice Systems via Agentic AI.
problema: Root-cause analysis in hyper-scale (200,000+ service) microservice systems is bottlenecked by extreme dynamism (no time budget for model retraining) and massive scale (400+ metrics per service), pushing LLMs into a 'lost in the middle' hallucination failure mode when reasoning directly over raw anomalous-metric sets.
mecanismo: A 3-stage pipeline: (1) API-level drilldown recursively scores/prunes downstream APIs by failure-rate/latency correlation to isolate suspicious services; (2) anomalous metrics are mapped onto a generic 4-type causal skeleton (External/Internal/Dependency/KPI) to instantiate a high-recall initial causal graph without expensive statistical causal discovery; (3) a multi-agent framework (Main Agent plus domain Sub Agents) refines the graph via a three-tiered memory (Working, Factual, Experiential) that retrieves similar historical failure cases and reasoning insights through a weighted composite RAG scheme to support evidence-based verification and self-reflection.
evaluacion: 300 real-world production failures at Kuaishou, measured by AC@1/AC@3 accuracy for root-cause service localization and failure-type classification against baselines (incl. RCA-Agent), an ablation removing drilldown / skeleton-graph / multi-agent / tiered-memory / using naive RAG, and 6+ months of live production deployment.
numeros_clave: KRCA AC@1 0.88 (service localization) / 0.79 (failure-type classification), beating strongest baseline RCA-Agent by >=31/32 absolute points; production deployment reduces average diagnosis time by 77.3% over 6+ months, processing 2,000+ alerts/day; ablation shows disabling Tiered Memory or replacing it with Naive RAG both cause consistent AC@1/AC@3 drops (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: An ablation explicitly measures that a naive flat-similarity RAG underperforms the structured tiered-retrieval scheme (Table 2, w/ Naive RAG row), direct evidence that retrieval DESIGN, not just presence, is measurably load-bearing, reinforcing ADR-019.

The three-tiered memory (Working/Factual/Experiential) separating live working state from durable factual/experiential knowledge, refreshed via self-reflection after each case, is a production-proven tiering pattern MF could examine.
Production deployment reports a 77.3% reduction in diagnosis time over 6+ months at 2,000+ alerts/day, hard evidence that a well-designed retrieval-augmented memory reduces operational cost at scale.

notes: Table 1 (main AC@1/AC@3 results) and Table 2 (ablation, w/o Tiered Memory / w/ Naive RAG rows) anchor the numbers; Fig.6 describes the three-tiered Working/Factual/Experiential memory architecture.

cita: Sun et al. (2026). OpsMem: Dual-Memory Reasoning with Cross-Memory Resonance for Failure Diagnosis.
problema: LLM-based failure diagnosis needs iterative evidence acquisition guided by operational experience, but existing agentic-reasoning methods suffer long-horizon instability over linear context while knowledge-augmented (RAG) methods retrieve operational experience statically, without continuously aligning it to the evolving diagnostic state.
mecanismo: OpsMem maintains two graph-structured memories: a short-term memory (STM) capturing the current incident's evolving belief state (symptoms/evidence/hypotheses linked by derive/refine/support/refute edges) and a long-term memory (LTM) of cross-incident patterns/cases/procedures. Cross-Memory Resonance (signal coupling -> pattern activation -> memory propagation) activates the LTM subgraph most relevant to the current STM at every round, jointly conditioning a multi-agent diagnosis loop (Central Agent plans, Expert Agents acquire/analyze evidence, STM is updated); after resolution, a multi-agent consolidation module (MetaAgent + memory agents) proposes CREATE/DELETE node operations to distill the solved incident back into the LTM.
evaluacion: 120 real-world Huawei microservice failure incidents, LLM-as-a-Judge (Match/Relevant on a 3-point scale) across three seed LLMs, against ReAct, GoS, and GoS+VectorRAG/GraphRAG/LinearRAG baselines, with an ablation removing STM/LTM/CMR/LTM-consolidation and a sequential-window self-evolution study.
numeros_clave: OpsMem improves Match by 6.66-25.00 points and Relevant by 3.33-13.33 points over the strongest baseline per seed LLM (e.g. Qwen3.5-27B: Match 78.33 vs GoS+LinearRAG 53.33, Relevant 85.83 vs 72.50); ablation shows removing LTM causes the largest drop (Match 78.33->30.83); self-evolution study shows growing gains vs a fixed-LTM variant across four incident windows (+0/+3/+1/+5 Match).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The short-term memory is an explicit graph-structured belief state of the current diagnostic task (symptoms/evidence/hypotheses with derive/refine/support/refute relations, §III-A), a concrete instance of plan/task state as first-class memory that is read/updated every reasoning round.

An ablation directly measures that removing Cross-Memory Resonance (state-aware LTM activation) hurts performance versus always retrieving generically (Table II, w/o CMR row), evidence that state-conditioned retrieval design is measurably load-bearing, reinforcing ADR-019.

A dedicated multi-agent consolidation module (MetaAgent reviews CREATE/DELETE proposals before merging, §III-D) gates promotion of solved-incident experience into durable long-term memory, and the self-evolution study (Table III) shows this measurably compounds over time -- confirming MF's deliberate-promotion stance.

notes: Table I (main results, 3 seed LLMs) and Table II-III (ablation, self-evolution windows) anchor the numbers; Fig.5 shows a worked case study of cross-memory resonance on a real incident.

cita: Huang, Z., Gutierrez, S., Kamana, H. y MacNeil, S. (2023). Memory Sandbox: Transparent and Interactive Memory Management for Conversational Agents.
problema: LLM-powered conversational agents manage conversational memory (summarization, selective storage, retrieval) entirely behind the interface, so users lack any affordance for viewing or controlling what the agent remembers, producing a poor mental model and conversational breakdowns when the agent's and the user's understanding of 'what was said' diverge.
mecanismo: Memory Sandbox reifies conversational history as draggable, editable 'memory objects' in a 2D-canvas UI: users can toggle a memory object's visibility (hide/show what the agent 'sees'), edit or delete an object to refine or remove context, add new objects to supplement context, select and summarize a group of objects into a new distilled object, and drag-copy objects by reference across separate conversations/agents to share context between them.
evaluacion: A design-probe system (Next.js + GPT-3.5-turbo) presented with a walkthrough of its interaction affordances and discussed qualitatively against explainable-AI and common-ground literature; the authors explicitly defer formal user studies of efficacy/trade-offs to future work.
numeros_clave: NINGUNO

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Treating each memory entry as an inspectable, editable object that a human can view/edit/delete directly (§2.1-2.3) is an early, direct precursor of MF's 'docs=truth, typed and human-legible' stance, applied to conversational memory instead of project docs.

The paper's core motivation is that a hidden memory-management strategy causes a 'poor mental model' and breakdowns for the user (§1); making memory state transparent and directly manipulable is presented as the fix, supporting MF's concern that opaque memory erodes trust/provenance.

Summarization is a user-triggered, selective operation over chosen memory objects rather than an automatic background process (§2.4), an alternative human-in-the-loop consolidation trigger MF could consider alongside fully automated promotion.

notes: This is an HCI design-probe/vision paper (CHI-style short paper, 2023) with only a system walkthrough and no quantitative evaluation (evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA only, hence numeros_clave=NINGUNO); the earliest paper in this batch (predates most cited memory-system work it inspired).

cita: Jiang et al. (2026). RepLLM: Toward Automatically Reproducing Network Research Results.
problema: Reproducing network-systems research code from papers is hard because open-source implementations are rare (only ~38% of SIGCOMM/NSDI papers over the past decade ship code) and general-purpose multi-agent code-generation frameworks suffer excessive redundant token consumption, ambiguous task allocation, and lack verification/error-recovery when generating long, interdependent multi-file codebases.
mecanismo: RepLLM coordinates four specialized agents (Content Parsing, Architecture Design, Code Generation, Audit & Repair) through an explicit file-system-backed Shared Memory: a dedicated shared_memory directory holding structured JSON ground-truth artifacts (paper.json, appendix.json) that is excluded from LLM prompts by default, governed by a rule-based read-write protocol under a stateless LLM-API interface (no dialogue history carried across calls). The Architecture Design Agent decomposes the target system into a DAG of operational steps with explicit I/O interfaces (the reproduction plan) stored in Shared Memory, and a sandbox-isolated hierarchical refinement loop (static analysis then execution-trace-driven debugging) iteratively repairs the generated code.
evaluacion: Evaluation on representative SIGCOMM/NSDI network-systems papers against SOTA system-level LLM code-generation frameworks (e.g. Claude Code CLI, broadcast-style multi-agent baselines), measuring compile-readiness, logical correctness and fidelity of reproduction against official implementations plus token consumption.
numeros_clave: Reproduces 95% of the original benchmarks within approximately two hours; reduces token consumption by up to 10% vs SOTA baselines; contrasted against a reported >10 million tokens for Claude Code CLI to generate a thousand-line codebase (Section 2.3.2); only 38.05% of SIGCOMM/NSDI papers over the past decade ship open-source code (motivating statistic).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Architecture Design Agent's DAG-of-operational-steps decomposition, with explicit per-step I/O interfaces stored in Shared Memory and consumed by later agents (Section 3.1.2), is a concrete plan-state artifact treated as first-class shared memory across the pipeline.

An explicit filesystem-backed Shared Memory (paper.json as ground truth, isolated from ordinary prompts) rather than implicit per-agent context or broadcast is exactly MF's single-source-per-fact stance, and the paper attributes its token-efficiency gains directly to this design versus AutoGen-style broadcast (Section 2.3.2).

Reports up to 10% token-consumption reduction vs SOTA baselines and contrasts this against a reported >10M-token cost for a naive multi-agent baseline (Claude Code CLI) on a 1K-LOC codebase, hard evidence for MF's context-economy stance.

notes: Abstract and Section 2.3.2/5.2 (Shared-Memory design and token-consumption comparison) anchor the numbers; pdftotext produced OCR/encoding syntax-error noise on this PDF but the main prose was recoverable.

cita: Chen et al. (2025). Multi-LLM Orchestration for High-Quality Code Generation: Exploiting Complementary Model Strengths.
problema: In single-LLM code-generation pipelines, no one model dominates across all programming languages, algorithmic problem categories, or generation/debugging/refinement stages, so committing to one fixed model throughout the pipeline leaves measurable code-quality gains unexploited.
mecanismo: PerfOrch decomposes generation into four agents (Categorization, Generation, Debugging, Refinement); the Generation, Debugging and Refinement agents each consult their own Memory module, an offline-profiled ranking matrix indexed by (programming language, algorithmic category), to select the top-k=5 candidate LLMs most suitable for that specific stage/task at runtime, applying stage-specific acceptance criteria and correctness-preserving rollback if a chosen model's attempt fails.
evaluacion: HumanEval-X and EffiBench-X (2,500 problems, 5 languages) with 5 LLMs, comparing PerfOrch against single-model pipelines (PerfCodeGen-GPT-4o), majority voting, and exhaustive multi-model evaluation; a preliminary 3-model study (Tables 1-3) establishes the per-stage/per-category routing premise, and Memory built solely on HumanEval-X profiling is evaluated zero-shot on the unseen EffiBench-X benchmark.
numeros_clave: PerfOrch average pass@1 97.19% (HumanEval-X) / 95.83% (EffiBench-X), +1.22 to +14.58pp over the strongest single-model pipeline; per-stage pairing reaches 98.17%/85.98% (Python/Rust) vs majority voting 97.56%/84.76%; category-aware routing adds +2.43pp on Rust (88.41% vs 85.98%); execution time improved for 61-90% of solved problems with mean speedups 4.7-29.9%, at roughly half the token cost of exhaustive multi-model evaluation.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Each agent's Memory is a per-(language,category) ranking matrix built from OFFLINE profiling and consulted, not re-derived, at runtime to pick which model to trust for a given task -- an alternative measured-retrieval pattern operating over model-performance priors rather than documents.

PerfOrch matches the refinement coverage of exhaustive multi-model evaluation 'at roughly half the token cost' (abstract) and bounds overhead via a top-k=5 candidate pool chosen from a measured plateau (Section 6.2 sensitivity analysis), concrete evidence that a small measured cache beats brute-force redundancy.

The ranking Memory is described as 'updatable as new models/versions become available' (Section 3.2), but the paper does not evaluate an online-consolidation mechanism, so this is a stated design intent rather than measured evidence.

notes: Tables 1-3 (preliminary 3-model study) and the abstract's headline numbers (97.19%/95.83% pass@1, 4.7-29.9% speedups) anchor the figures; 'Memory' here is model-performance-ranking metadata, not task/user knowledge -- a narrower notion of memory than most other papers in this batch.

cita: Fang et al. (2025). MLZero: A Multi-Agent System for End-to-end Machine Learning Automation.
problema: End-to-end multimodal AutoML agents lack automated data perception (forcing hard-coded preprocessing) and, when relying solely on parametric knowledge, hallucinate code or use outdated ML-library APIs; their performance further degrades when managing long, convoluted domain knowledge without efficient memory mechanisms.
mecanismo: MLZero pairs a perception module (file-grouping/perception, task-perception and ML-library-selection agents) with dual memory: semantic memory is built OFFLINE by summarization and condensation agents into queryable, condensed per-library knowledge indices, then retrieved at each iteration conditioned on the current error context to supply targeted guidance; episodic memory maintains a chronological record of prior code, execution logs, retrieved knowledge and error context per iteration, distilled by an error-analyzer agent into a concise error summary plus fix suggestion, feeding an iterative coder-executer loop until success or a max-iteration limit.
evaluacion: MLE-Bench Lite (21 Kaggle competitions) and a new Multimodal AutoML Agent Benchmark (25 datasets, diverse modalities) against AIDE, DS-Agent, AutoKaggle and Codex CLI, with ablations removing external knowledge (semantic memory, -ext) and episodic memory (-epi), plus a compact 8B-LLM robustness variant.
numeros_clave: MLE-Bench Lite: 86% success rate / avg rank 1.43 vs AIDE 81%/2.36, with 6 gold + 2 silver medals; Multimodal benchmark: success rate 0.92 (+263.6% vs the best baseline), avg rank 2.42; the compact-8B variant still reaches 45.3% success / rank 5.14, beating other agents' full-size configurations (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Semantic memory is explicitly built OFFLINE (summarization+condensation agents) as a derived, queryable index over library documentation/tutorials, then retrieved per-iteration, a clean instance of MF's derived-index-as-cache (Tier-3) pattern.

Episodic memory explicitly distills raw execution history into a concise error-summary-plus-fix-suggestion rather than replaying full logs, stated to reduce token consumption while preserving problem-solving effectiveness (Section 3.3), directly supporting MF's context-economy stance.

An ablation explicitly measures the contribution of external-knowledge retrieval (-ext) and episodic memory (-epi) to end-to-end success rate (Table 1), evidence that retrieval/memory presence is measurably load-bearing rather than assumed.

notes: Table 1 (25-dataset Multimodal AutoML benchmark, -ext/-epi ablation columns) and the MLE-Bench Lite medal counts anchor the numbers; industry paper (AWS/Amazon authors) with a fully public benchmark and repository.

cita: Tablan et al. (2025). Smarter Together: Creating Agentic Communities of Practice through Shared Experiential Learning.
problema: The shift to agent-centric software development is eroding human developer knowledge-sharing communities (falling participation in peer repositories), while AI coding agents remain siloed and amnesiac -- each session, user, or provider starts a fresh, isolated learning loop with no equivalent shared 'community of practice' to draw on.
mecanismo: Spark is a shared, multi-agent-writable experiential memory layer with three subsystems: a knowledge base (seeded by indexing raw developer documentation across text/embedding modalities), a retrieval agent (an 8-step workflow: intent analysis -> search-strategy planning -> recall of past experiential traces -> documentation retrieval -> recommendation generation -> citation -> best-practice synthesis -> contextualized response) combining vector search, lexical search and experiential-trace matching, and a continuous multi-epoch experiential-learning loop that captures every agent interaction as a structured 'trace,' clusters and curates traces into generalizable knowledge patterns each epoch, and redistributes that curated knowledge to future agents facing similar problems.
evaluacion: DS-1000 (1000 Python data-science problems from StackOverflow, 7 libraries) with three codegen backbones (Qwen3-Coder-30B, Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5-Codex) compared NO-SPARK vs WITH-SPARK (one epoch of synthetic experiential-trace ingestion), judged by an independent LLM (Gemini 2.5 Pro) on a 5-point code-quality scale across correctness/completeness/code-quality/practicality, plus a separate helpfulness-band evaluation of Spark's recommendations.
numeros_clave: WITH-SPARK raises mean code quality for all three backbones (Fig.1); a 30B open-weights model boosted by Spark matches the code quality of a much larger SOTA model; Spark recommendation helpfulness reaches up to 98.2% in the top-two of five qualitative bands; knowledge base seeded with approximately 34,000 documentation blobs.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A continuous multi-epoch curation loop (feedback -> knowledge extraction -> memory-augmented learning -> next epoch, Section 3.2) that clusters raw interaction traces into generalizable 'curated knowledge' distinct from the raw traces themselves is a directly transferable pattern for promoting gotchas into durable recipes.

Spark is explicitly framed as a SHARED cross-agent/cross-user memory versus today's siloed single-user provider- or user-managed memory stores (Sections 2.1-2.2), a concrete alternative to per-agent private stores directly engaging MF's single-source/multi-store-seams question.

The paper does not detail how conflicting or stale curated knowledge is reconciled or aged out across a large multi-agent contributor base, leaving MF's provenance/staleness/poisoning concern for a genuinely shared memory largely unaddressed by the evaluation.

notes: Fig.1 (code quality by backbone) and Section 4.4-4.5 (helpfulness bands, 98.2% figure) anchor the numbers; industry paper (The Memory Company / Moonsong Labs) evaluated only with SYNTHETIC experiential traces from one LLM (Section 4.1) rather than real multi-agent/multi-user community usage -- RECONSIDERAR how far the 'shared community' claim is validated versus a single-epoch synthetic proxy.

cita: Lu et al. (2025). ViDove: A Translation Agent System with Multimodal Context and Memory-Augmented Reasoning.
problema: Multimodal video subtitling/translation agents must fuse visual, audio and textual cues coherently across long documents, but most LLM-based MT systems only handle text and lose domain/visual context across chunks.
mecanismo: A short-term memory Ms (per-video-chunk translation history, visual/audio cues) and long-term memory Ml (domain knowledge, web knowledge via Tavily) are implemented over LlamaIndex; three collaborating agents (Translator, Proofreader, Editor) write, consolidate and retrieve from M during multi-agent post-editing.
evaluacion: Evaluated on DoveBench (17h human-annotated long-form video) and BigVideo using BLEU/BLEURT/SubER/SubSONAR/sCOMET against Gemini-2.5-Flash, Qwen-2.5-Omni, VideoCaptioner and Whisper+DelTA, plus an ablation removing domain memory, vision and the proofreader agent.
numeros_clave: vs strongest baseline Whisper+DelTA: +28.8% BLEU, +58.9% BLEURT, -15.5% SubER (DoveBench); ablation Table 2: full ViDove BLEU 15.84 vs w/o domain memory 14.86 vs w/o Proofreader 13.56 (sharpest drop).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The ablation (Table 2, Sec 5.4) measures retrieval-relevant memory components (domain memory, vision) directly against BLEU/SubER, confirming MF's practice of gating memory design on measured retrieval outcomes.
Long/short-term memory split reduces re-processing cost of prior chunks (Sec 3.5.1) but no explicit token/latency numbers are reported, so it is only weak context for MF's cost lens.

notes: Ablation numbers at Table 2 (Sec 5.4, single-column DoveBench subset); main comparison Table 1 (Sec 5.3).

cita: Yan et al. (2025). General Agentic Memory Via Deep Research.
problema: Ahead-of-time (AOT) static memory precompresses agent history offline and is inevitably lossy and inflexible to unforeseen, fine-grained downstream requests at retrieval time.
mecanismo: A duo design follows just-in-time compilation: a Memorizer writes a lightweight memo per session while keeping the full trajectory in a page-store; a Researcher performs iterative plan/search/reflect deep-research (vector, BM25 and ID-based tools) over the page-store guided by the memo to build a task-specific context at runtime, trained end-to-end via RL.
evaluacion: Benchmarked on LoCoMo, HotpotQA (56K/224K/448K), RULER-128K and NarrativeQA against memory-free (long-LLM, RAG) and memory-based baselines (A-Mem, Mem0, MemoryOS, LightMem), with ablations on search tools, module isolation, output format and offline/online efficiency timing.
numeros_clave: HotpotQA-56K F1: GAM 64.07 vs best baseline LightMem 37.30; module ablation (Table 3) 'memory without research' collapses to avg F1 27.50 vs full GAM 53.18; efficiency (Table 5) GAM total time 69.32s at 56K vs A-mem 210.26s, though costlier online than Mem0 (37.57s) or LightMem (5.13s).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The 'memory without research' ablation (Table 3, Sec 3.5) shows a precomputed static memory alone underperforms sharply, confirming MF's stance of treating any derived/compressed index as a cache and re-deriving/searching over ground truth rather than trusting it standalone.

Table 5 (Sec 3.6) measures offline-build vs online-serve latency directly, giving a concrete cost/accuracy tradeoff curve (GAM slower online than Mem0/LightMem for higher F1) relevant to MF's context-economy lens, without forcing a specific MF decision.

notes: Ablation tables 3 (module isolation) and 5 (efficiency) in Sec 3.5-3.6; ranked accuracy tables 1-2 in Sec 3.2-3.3.

cita: Fiorini et al. (2025). Episodic Memory in Agentic Frameworks: Suggesting Next Tasks.
problema: Scientific-workflow agentic frameworks need to recommend plausible next steps without relying on hallucination-prone pre-trained LLM guesses or costly fine-tuning on scarce proprietary workflow data.
mecanismo: An Episodic-Memory (EM) Agent intercepts user instructions, compiles the executed trajectory into a ProvLake/W3C-PROV workflow, retrieves similar past workflows via tree matching plus embedding similarity of leaf steps from a workflow database, and asks an LLM to suggest next tasks from the retrieved and current workflows; a '\save' command explicitly writes the current workflow back into episodic memory.
evaluacion: Demonstrated qualitatively (no quantitative benchmark) on a Materials-Science PFAS-hazard-assessment crew built with BeeAI, using illustrative execution traces (with vs without a retrievable similar workflow) with similarity threshold T=0.65 and up to 10 retrieved workflows.
numeros_clave: similarity threshold T=0.65; max 10 retrieved workflows per query (Sec 3, implementation paragraph); no quantitative accuracy/latency figures are reported (evidence is CUALITATIVA).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The core mechanism stores past executed workflows (ordered task sequences) as plan-state memory and matches the in-progress workflow against them to suggest next steps (Sec 2, Fig. 1b) -- a concrete pattern MF could adopt for plan-state-as-memory.

Retrieval uses a fixed similarity threshold and tree matching (Sec 2) but is validated only through illustrative examples, not a measured benchmark, so it is weak (qualitative-only) evidence for MF's retrieval-measured discipline.

notes: Only qualitative demonstration (Figs. 3-4, Sec 3); RECONSIDERAR -- evidence is illustrative-only, no quantitative retrieval or task-suggestion accuracy is reported.

cita: Zou et al. (2026). Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems.
problema: Text-mediated multi-agent collaboration re-encodes each agent's reasoning into natural language, which is lossy relative to the model's internal representations and imposes heavy token and latency costs on system-level reasoning.
mecanismo: Each agent autoregressively generates 'latent thoughts' as last-layer hidden states instead of decoding text, and a shared latent working memory (concatenated layer-wise KV caches, with a training-free linear alignment operator) transfers this state losslessly to the next agent, replacing token-level write/read of memory with continuous-representation write/read across agents.
evaluacion: Evaluated on 9 benchmarks (math/science reasoning, commonsense, code generation) across 5 backbones (Qwen3 4B/8B/14B, Llama3 3B/8B) under sequential and hierarchical MAS designs, against single-model and text-based MAS (TextMAS, vLLM-optimized) baselines.
numeros_clave: up to +14.6% accuracy, 70.8%-83.7% fewer output tokens, and 4x-4.3x faster end-to-end inference vs TextMAS (Sec 4.1); e.g. Qwen3-14B sequential MedQA: 80.7% acc with 86.6% fewer tokens and 4.3x speedup over TextMAS (Table 1-2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Measured 70.8-83.7% token reduction and 4-4.3x speedup from replacing textual inter-agent memory with shared latent KV-cache state (Fig. 1, Table 1-2) is a concrete mechanism MF could borrow for internal, non-human-facing agent-to-agent handoffs to cut context/token cost.

Theorem 3.3 (Sec 3.2) proves the latent transfer is information-lossless relative to text hand-off, a fidelity argument that is internal to the model rather than about human-auditable provenance, so it only weakly bears on MF's fidelity/staleness concerns.

notes: Complexity/expressiveness proofs in Appendix B (Theorems 3.1, 3.3, 3.4); main efficiency numbers Fig. 1 and Tables 1-2, Sec 4.1-4.2.

cita: Liao et al. (2026). From Atom to Community: Structured and Evolving Agent Memory for User Behavior Modeling.
problema: Single, unstructured summary memories for user-behavior modeling conflate multi-dimensional interests, suffer interest-forgetting from naive overwriting, and cannot exploit collaborative signals from similar users under sparse interaction data.
mecanismo: STEAM decomposes user preferences into fine-grained atomic memory units (content, embedding, linked interactions, community link); relation extraction plus 2-hop BFS groups semantically similar memories across users into communities summarized as prototype memories (graph representation), and reflection-triggered consolidation (merge overlapping memories) or formation (new memory unit) evolve memory over time.
evaluacion: Evaluated on three real-world recommendation datasets (Amazon CDs, Clothing, MovieLens-100k, 100 sampled users) via NDCG@{1,5,10} recommendation accuracy, user-simulation fidelity (F1) against GPT-3.5/AFL, diversity metrics (ILD/Entropy/DS), and an ablation removing atomic memory units (AMU), consolidation (MC) or community construction (CC).
numeros_clave: overall NDCG improvement of +5.74% over the best baseline (Table 2); ablation on CDs (Table 5) NDCG@10: full STEAM 0.5982 vs w/o AMU 0.5765, w/o MC 0.5886, w/o CC 0.5906.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The consolidation-vs-formation evolution mechanism (Sec 3.4, Table 5 ablation) gives a concrete, measured pattern for merging overlapping memories into refined units, which MF's gotcha-to-recipe consolidation could adopt directly.

Table 5's ablation isolates the retrieval-relevant community-construction component and measures its NDCG contribution (0.5906 vs 0.5982 full), confirming MF's discipline of gating structure on measured retrieval gains rather than assumed benefit.

notes: Ablation Table 5 (Sec 4.5); main NDCG comparison Table 2 (Sec 4.2.2).

cita: Charoenwet et al. (2026). AgenticSCR: An Autonomous Agentic Secure Code Review for Immature Vulnerabilities Detection.
problema: Pre-commit secure code review of 'immature' (incomplete, context-dependent) vulnerabilities is poorly served by noisy rule-based SAST tools and by standalone LLMs that lack repository context and explicit tool use.
mecanismo: A detector-validator subagent chain writes curated SAST rule knowledge (CodeQL-derived, CWE-mapped JSON) into the detector's semantic memory and a CWE-tree knowledge base into the validator's semantic memory; the detector localizes/explains vulnerabilities from a diff-centric view of the repo, and the validator recalls the CWE tree to filter false positives from the detector's candidate comments.
evaluacion: Evaluated on SCRBench, a curated repository-aware human-annotated line-level immature-vulnerability benchmark, against a static LLM baseline and SAST tools, with an ablation toggling security knowledge (SAST/CWE) in the detector and validator subagents versus a 'Vanilla Agentic' baseline.
numeros_clave: 17.5% of comments correctly localized/relevant/typed, +10.6 absolute points over the static LLM baseline while producing only 32% as many comments; ablation: full security-knowledge config raises absolute localization/relevance rate by +10.2 points over Vanilla Agentic with 81% fewer comments; abstract cites >=153% relative improvement in correct comments over the static-LLM baseline.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Grounding the detector/validator in curated documentary knowledge (SAST rule JSON, CWE tree, Sec 3.4.1) rather than relying on the LLM's implicit pretrained knowledge measurably improves precision, confirming MF's docs-as-verified-truth principle.

The ablation (Sec 1, contributions) directly measures the retrieval/use of security knowledge against localization+relevance rate, aligning with MF's requirement that retrieval value be measured, not assumed.

notes: Ablation numbers reported in abstract/introduction (Sec 1); SCRBench described in Sec 2-3.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). E-mem: Multi-Agent Based Episodic Context Reconstruction for LLM Agent Memory.
problema: Prevalent memory preprocessing compresses complex sequential dependencies into rigid pre-defined structures (embeddings, graphs), causing 'destructive de-contextualization' that severs the logical/causal integrity needed for deep, long-horizon System-2 reasoning.
mecanismo: A master agent delegates to multiple SLM-based assistant agents, each holding an uncompressed raw episodic context segment (sliding-window chunks with overlap) plus a lightweight routing summary; a multi-pathway router (global narrative alignment, vector semantic association, BM25 symbolic trigger) activates relevant assistants, which re-experience and reason within their raw context to produce temporally-anchored evidence that the master aggregates and reconciles by timestamp.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo and streaming HotpotQA (400/800/1600 documents) against Long-Context windowing, RAG, A-Mem, Mem0, MemoryOS, LightMem and GAM, with ablations on routing pathways, number of activated chunks, and master/assistant backbone scaling, plus a hallucination analysis on LoCoMo's adversarial subset.
numeros_clave: E-mem overall F1 54.17 (GPT-4o-mini) / 57.04 (Qwen2.5-14B) on LoCoMo, +8.86%/+6.63% over best baseline GAM (Table 1); Multi-hop F1 49.15 vs GAM 38.94 (Qwen); token cost reduced by over 70% vs baselines (abstract).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central claim -- that compressing history into embeddings/graphs is 'destructive de-contextualization' that loses provenance and sequential integrity -- and its measured gains from reconstructing raw context instead (Table 1) directly extend MF's fidelity/staleness concern with a concrete dual raw+summary architecture.

Reporting >70% token-cost reduction while preserving raw context via routed reconstruction (Sec 1, abstract) is a relevant cost data point, though not broken down per operation for MF's specific context-economy needs.

notes: Ablation on routing pathways and activated chunks in Fig. 3 / Sec 4.4; hallucination analysis Table 4 (Sec 4.3).

cita: Dong et al. (2026). KernelBlaster: Continual Cross-Task CUDA Optimization via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reinforcement Learning.
problema: Agentic CUDA-kernel optimization workflows typically treat each optimization task independently, so they cannot aggregate knowledge across tasks, causing biased sampling and forcing the agent to rediscover effective strategies from scratch for every new kernel or GPU generation.
mecanismo: A Memory-Augmented In-Context RL (MAIC-RL) loop treats the agent's Knowledge Base as its mutable 'policy parameters': a State Extractor derives a profiling-based performance signature per kernel, a State/Optimization Selector retrieves and weighted-samples (state, optimization, score) entries from a Persistent CUDA Knowledge Base, a Lowering Agent applies and profiles the change, and PolicyEvaluation/PerfGapAnalysis/ParameterUpdate agents write the resulting natural-language performance-gap analysis back into the Knowledge Base as a textual-gradient update.
evaluacion: Benchmarked on KernelBench Levels 1-3 against PyTorch eager mode, torch.compile, the IREE compiler, and the agentic AI CUDA Engineer baseline, using NCU-profiler cycle counts and application-level timing.
numeros_clave: geometric-mean speedups over the PyTorch baseline of 1.43x (KernelBench Level 1), 2.50x (Level 2), and 1.50x (Level 3) (abstract); motivating case: FlashAttention-2 ported to H100 dropped ~47% in performance before hardware-aware redesign (Sec 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The PolicyEvaluation/PerfGapAnalysis/ParameterUpdate chain (Sec 3) explicitly consolidates raw trial-and-error experience -- successes AND failures -- into structured, reusable Knowledge-Base entries, a close technical-domain analogue to MF's promote-gotchas-to-durable-recipes consolidation pattern.

The framing of ICRL as far more sample-efficient than weight-updating RL or from-scratch search (Sec 2, In-Context RL discussion) is a relevant cost argument for MF's context-economy lens, though no direct token/dollar figures are reported for the memory operations themselves.

notes: Knowledge Base construction and consolidation loop in Sec 3 (Fig. 3-6); speedup results Sec 4 / abstract.

cita: Li et al. (2026). OpenSage: Self-programming Agent Generation Engine.
problema: Existing Agent Development Kits require humans to manually design agent topology, tools and memory, limiting the scalability and generalizability of constructed agents, and their static sub-agent structures discard informative states after each execution.
mecanismo: OpenSage gives the LLM itself tools to create/manage sub-agents (topology), write and register new tools, and read/write a hierarchical graph memory -- a Neo4j-backed short-term execution graph and a long-term project graph -- through a dedicated memory agent that supports both graph-based and embedding-similarity retrieval and can add, modify or delete nodes/edges, i.e. explicit write, consolidation and forgetting operations.
evaluacion: Evaluated on Terminal-Bench 2.0, CyberGym and SWE-Bench Pro (plus LoCoMo in an appendix) against agents built with SOTA ADKs (Google/OpenAI/Claude ADK, OpenHands, LangChain), with ablations isolating the contribution of agent-topology, tooling, and memory design (full agentic memory vs a Mem0-style graph vs no memory).
numeros_clave: SWE-Bench-Pro-Python resolved rate (Sec 4.4 memory ablation): full agentic memory 59.0% vs Mem0-graph 56.4% vs no-memory 56.2%; OpenSage vs the expert-designed Agentless baseline on the same 266-instance subset: 59.0% resolved (Sec 4.2); agent-topology ablation on a 300-instance CyberGym subset shows a large gap between the full configuration and NoFeature variants (Fig. 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Sub-agent state, including 'resuming execution from a specific point in time' (Sec 3.4), is persisted as long-term/short-term graph memory that downstream sub-agents build upon -- a concrete pattern for treating in-flight task/plan state as first-class memory that MF could adopt.

The memory agent's search-then-add/modify/delete workflow over the long-term graph (Sec 3.4, 'so that only non-redundant, relevant knowledge is persisted') is a directly measured (Sec 4.4 ablation) consolidation mechanism MF's own consolidation lens could reuse.

notes: Memory-design ablation Sec 4.4 (Fig. 5); topology/tooling ablations Sec 4.2-4.3 (Fig. 3); plan_estado=SI reflects the resumable sub-agent execution state described in Sec 3.4.

cita: Hu et al. (2026). Pancake: Hierarchical Memory System for Multi-Agent LLM Serving.
problema: Existing vector-database memory backends assume static or batch-oriented indexes, so the highly dynamic, small-batch, interleaved search/insert/delete pattern of real agentic memory workloads makes approximate-nearest-neighbor search a dominant and growing share (up to 82-99%) of end-to-end serving cost as memory size grows.
mecanismo: A three-level (L0/L1/L2) cache-inspired index promotes and evicts vectors based on per-agent access patterns modeled as finite-state machines; a hybrid graph unifies multiple agents' coarse indexes into a single traversal instead of per-agent traversal, with per-cluster agent-specific access records for fine search; and GPU-CPU coordinated index management (insertion buffers, asynchronous transfers) lets hotspot clusters be updated and searched without full re-caching, all exposed via a Python API for scoped Insert/Update/Delete/Search across shared and per-agent memory partitions.
evaluacion: Throughput/latency benchmarks on realistic multi-agent workloads (compatible with Mem-GPT, LangChain, LlamaIndex), measuring end-to-end speedup and the share of total runtime spent on memory operations as memory size scales from 1K to 8M items, plus GPU-vs-CPU search microbenchmarks.
numeros_clave: over 4.29x average end-to-end throughput improvement vs existing memory libraries (abstract); memory-operation time share cut to an average of 3.2% at large scale, down from baselines reaching over 82-99% of total execution time (Sec 1); GPU vector search over 3x faster than CPU once cluster size >=512 vectors (Fig. 8).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Figures 1 and 8 directly measure memory-operation time as a share of total serving cost across memory sizes and hardware placements, hard evidence for MF's context/latency-economy lens that raw retrieval-index cost must be engineered, not assumed cheap.

Figure 2's multi-agent example explicitly Inserts/Deletes a shared task Plan object (P) as a first-class memory item across agent scopes, illustrating plan-state-as-memory, though the paper's own contribution and evaluation target index performance rather than plan semantics.

notes: plan_estado=SI corresponds to Fig. 2's Task-Planner-agent example (Insert(P,3) / Delete(P,2)); throughput numbers in abstract and Sec 1; scaling figures Sec 3.

cita: Mao et al. (2026). Joint Optimization of Multi-agent Memory System.
problema: Memory systems built as multi-agent construction+retrieval pipelines are usually optimized one agent at a time under a single shared global reward, which ignores inter-agent dependencies and co-adaptation and gives ambiguous credit assignment, limiting collaboration quality.
mecanismo: CoMAM models the extraction-agent -> profile-agent -> retrieval-agent memory pipeline as a sequential Markov Decision Process and jointly trains all agents end-to-end with GRPO, combining each agent's local task reward (evidence coverage, profile-quality score, retrieval precision/coverage) with an adaptively-weighted share of the shared global answer-correctness reward, where weights come from an NDCG-based consistency score between each agent's local-reward ranking and the global-reward ranking across sampled trajectories.
evaluacion: Evaluated on PersonaMem (32K/128K/1M context) and LongMemEval against no-memory (Base, RAG), prompt-based memory (CAM, MemoryBank, A-Mem) and RL-based memory baselines (Mem1, Memory-R1, GAM), with ablations removing each agent, disabling per-agent training, comparing single vs heterogeneous policies and independent vs end-to-end RL, and comparing credit-assignment schemes.
numeros_clave: PersonaMem accuracy gains of +8.5% (32K) to +16.7% (128K) over the best baseline (Table 1); LongMemEval F1 62.17 vs best baseline GAM 51.75 (Table 2); ablation (Table 3): removing any of the 3 agents drops accuracy from 0.64/0.70/0.66 (full) to as low as 0.51-0.57, and leaving one agent untrained costs 2-8% accuracy.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The per-agent ablation (Table 3) measures exactly how much each specialized construction agent (extraction, profile) contributes and how much its optimization matters, confirming MF's discipline of gating any consolidation-like role on measured, not assumed, contribution.

Retrieval-agent contribution and joint-vs-independent optimization of retrieval are directly ablated (Table 4-5) against downstream QA accuracy, aligning with MF's requirement that retrieval value be measured rather than assumed.

notes: Ablation tables 3-5 (Sec 5.3-5.5); main comparisons Table 1 (PersonaMem) and Table 2 (LongMemEval).

cita: Park (2026). Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents: Formal Belief Revision Semantics for Versioned Memory Architectures.
problema: Agent-produced outputs (beliefs, code, documents, decisions) accumulate without systematic versioning or provenance tracking, so multi-agent pipelines lack a principled way to know which belief/output is current, why it changed, and what downstream conclusions depend on it.
mecanismo: Kumiho is a property-graph memory with immutable versioned revisions, mutable tag pointers, and typed dependency/provenance edges addressed via hierarchical URIs; updates are AGM-compliant belief-revision operators (e.g., a Supersedes edge creates a new revision rather than an in-place overwrite, satisfying Success/Consistency/Relevance while explicitly rejecting the Recovery postulate); an async consolidation pipeline (dual Redis working-memory + Neo4j long-term graph, hybrid full-text+vector retrieval) runs with published-item protection, circuit breakers and dry-run validation, and an AnalyzeImpact operation traverses typed edges to propagate belief changes to dependent conclusions.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo (official token-F1 metric) and LoCoMo-Plus (Level-2 implicit-constraint recall) against Graphiti/Zep, Mem0, A-Mem, Letta, Hindsight and MAGMA, plus an automated AGM-compliance test suite (49 scenarios, 7 postulates) and ablations of consolidation enrichments (prospective indexing, event extraction) and answer-model cost/accuracy trade-offs.
numeros_clave: LoCoMo 0.447 four-category F1 (n=1540, highest reported on retrieval categories) with 97.5% adversarial refusal accuracy (n=446), overall F1 0.565 (n=1986); LoCoMo-Plus 93.3% judge accuracy (n=401) vs best published baseline Gemini-2.5-Pro 45.7%; prospective indexing + event extraction eliminated a >6-month recall-accuracy cliff (37.5% to 84.4%); 100% pass rate on the 49-scenario AGM-compliance suite; total run cost approx. $14 for 401 entries on GPT-4o-mini.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The near-perfect 97.5% adversarial refusal, explained as 'the memory graph contains no fabricated information, so there is nothing to hallucinate from' (abstract), is a measured instance of MF's provenance/staleness concern, confirming that versioned, provenance-tracked memory materially reduces hallucination risk versus flat overwrite.

The formal, AGM-grounded rejection of the Recovery postulate (Sec 7.3: a superseded belief is not silently recoverable, only reachable via explicit opt-in) is a concrete design MF's own derived-index-as-cache model could adopt when specifying what 'superseding a fact' must guarantee.

notes: Formal AGM correspondence and Recovery-postulate rejection in Sec 7; empirical results Sec 15.2-15.3, 15.7; architectural comparison Table 1.

cita: Chang et al. (2026). MemCollab: Cross-Model Memory Collaboration via Contrastive Trajectory Distillation.
problema: Memory built from one agent's own reasoning trajectories entangles task-relevant knowledge with that model's reasoning style/biases, so naively transferring it to agents with different backbone models in heterogeneous deployments can degrade rather than help performance.
mecanismo: For each training task, trajectories are collected from multiple heterogeneous-backbone agents; a preferred (correct or strongest-model) trajectory is contrasted against each unpreferred one by the strongest model, distilling (violation pattern, reasoning invariant) discrepancies into normative 'enforce X; avoid Y' memory entries tagged with the producing/failing agent's identity; at inference, task-aware then model-aware retrieval filters the shared bank to entries matching the query's task category and involving the target agent before ranking by relevance and injecting the top-p entries into the prompt.
evaluacion: Evaluated on MATH500, GSM8K, MBPP and HumanEval with Qwen2.5-7B/32B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct backbones against Buffer-of-Thoughts, Dynamic Cheatsheet, same-model memory, naive cross-model memory transfer, and self-contrast memory baselines, with ablations on retrieved-entry count, retrieval strategy, and a three-model heterogeneous-source robustness check.
numeros_clave: Qwen2.5-7B + MemCollab raises MATH500 from 52.2% (vanilla) to 67.0% and MBPP from 47.9% to 57.6% (Table 1); naive cross-model transfer (w/ Memory(32B) applied to the 7B agent) instead DEGRADES MATH500 to 50.6% and HumanEval to 34.1% vs vanilla 52.2%/42.7%; top-3 retrieved memories (p=3) found optimal, with performance dropping beyond a task-dependent threshold (Fig. 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The measured finding that naively pooling one backbone's memory as a universal source for a different agent DEGRADES performance (Table 1, 'Direct cross-model memory transfer can degrade performance') is hard evidence for MF's single-source/no-blind-multi-store discipline: memory must be scoped to its valid consumer, not shared blindly.

Distilling contrastive (violation, invariant) pairs into normative 'enforce/avoid' constraints (Sec 2.2) is a concrete consolidation mechanism -- turning disagreement between multiple executions into a durable, reusable rule -- that MF's gotcha-to-recipe consolidation lens could adopt directly.

notes: Ablation on retrieved-entry count Fig. 3 (Sec 3.4); main comparison Tables 1-2 (Sec 3.1-3.2).

cita: Mayank and Nath (2026). Orchestrating Intelligence: A Framework for Dynamic Task Decomposition and Role Specialization in Multi-Agent Generative AI Systems.
problema: Prior multi-agent LLM frameworks rely on static role assignment, brittle ad hoc inter-agent communication, no shared persistent memory across agents, and no principled mechanism for reconciling contradictory outputs from independent agents.
